Adults with IHCA at a tertiary university hospital were identified, and archived serum samples collected within 48 h before the event were analyzed.

title: Entinostat plus exemestane for hormone receptor-positive advanced breast cancer: long-term overall survival results from the EOC103A3101 randomized controlled trial
creator: Jiani Wang, Qingyuan Zhang, Xichun Hu, Tao Sun, Wei Li, Quchang Ouyang, Jingfen Wang, Zhongsheng Tong, Min Yan, Huiping Li, Xiaohua Zeng, Changping Shan, Xian Wang, Jian Zhang, Yue Zhang, Liang Zhang, Hongyan Shang, Binghe Xu
description: The addition of entinostat, a histone deacetylase inhibitor, to exemestane has demonstrated improved progression-free survival (PFS) in hormone receptor-positive (HR + ), human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HER2-) advanced breast cancer (ABC) following endocrine therapy failure in the EOC103A3101 randomized trial (NCT03538171). This study reports long-term overall survival (OS) results.

title: Genetic and environmental influences on educational disparities in adult weight change: an individual-based pooled analysis of 11 twin cohorts
creator: Alvaro Obeso, Gabin Drouard, Aline Jelenkovic, Emanuela Medda, Corrado Fagnani, Virgilia Toccaceli, Antti Latvala, Sari Aaltonen, Sarah E. Medland, Scott D. Gordon, Jooyeon Lee, Soo Ji Lee, Joohon Sung, Hyojin Pyun, Glen E. Duncan, Dedra Buchwald, Juan R. Ordoñana, Juan F. Sánchez-Romera, Eduvigis C
description: IntroductionEducational attainment (EA) is negatively associated with body mass index (BMI), but less is known about the association between EA and adult BMI change. We analysed the role of genetic and environmental factors in the associations between EA and BMI trajectory components over adulthood.

title: Integrating machine learning and geospatial technologies for spatio-temporal analysis of urban expansion and land use transformation in Gambella Town, Ethiopia
creator: Kanenus Fufa Dararo, Goanar Jal Dup, Weyesa Merga Chemeda, Shankar Karuppannan
description: Rapid urbanization and the associated expansion of built-up areas are transforming land resources, ecosystem functions, and the spatial structure of cities. Distinguishing urban growth, urban expansion, and urban sprawl is essential for understanding the processes and patterns of urban transformation and supporting sustainable urban planning.

title: Conserved genetic and antigenic profiles of Pf12 and Pf41 in asymptomatic Plasmodium falciparum carriers in Tanzania
creator: Fadhila Fitriana, Wang-Jong Lee, Hyun-Young Sim, Hojong Jun, Jadidan Hada Syahada, Fauzi Muh, Se Jin Lee, Sunghun Na, Kyu Joon Lee, Joo-Won Nam, Eun-Taek Han, Jim Todd, Alphaxard Manjurano, Winifrida Kidima, Ernest Mazigo, Jin-Hee Han
description: Plasmodium falciparum remains a major cause of mortality in malaria-endemic regions, and strain-specific immunity limits vaccine efficacy. The 6-cysteine proteins Pf12 and Pf41 are proposed blood-stage vaccine candidates, yet their diversity and antigenicity in asymptomatic carriers are poorly defined. Genetic variation and natural selection pressure were analyzed in 172 P. falciparum isolates from asymptomatic individuals in Tanzania.

title: Retraction: Transcription Regulation of HYPK by Heat Shock Factor 1
creator: The
description: being used to represent different experimental conditions: The left and right Fig 2D AcH4 panels. The left and right Fig 2D AcH4 panels. The left Fig 2D RNA polymerase II panel in [1] and the Fig 2C RNA polymerase II panel in [2].

title: Seasonal and environmental patterns of naturally occurring parasitoids with potential to attack the invasive pest Drosophila suzukii in the Andes
creator: Déborah Fischbein, Mónica Daniela Germano, Andrés Santiago Martínez, Julian Mensch, Marcelo Eduardo Kun, Andrea Cardozo, Verónica Chillo
description: Landscape complexity shapes insect spatiotemporal population dynamics and trophic interactions. In this context, understanding seasonal and environmental patterns of potential resident natural enemies of novel polyphagous herbivores, such as the globally invasive fruit fly pest Drosophila suzukii, is fundamental for developing effective landscape-scale pest management strategies.

title: Increased temperature selects for antibiotic resistance genes in a model aquatic ecosystem
creator: Emma Bousquet, Sabine Favre-Bonté, Thibault Meyer, Concepción Sánchez-Cid
description: There is a rising concern that temperature increases associated with climate change might select for antibiotic-resistant bacteria (ARB) and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in aquatic ecosystems, although the extent of this phenomenon remains unknown. This study aimed to determine whether increased temperatures induce ARG selection and modify the transcriptional response in a model aquatic ecosystem using an omics approach.

title: Cerebrospinal fluid and dural accumulation of α-synuclein impairs CNS clearance in Parkinson’s disease
creator: Taylor J. Stevenson, Luca Vinnell, Samuel J.C. McCullough, Daniel X. Flyger, Blake Highet, James A. Wiseman, Ben Watkin, Kate Hitpass Romero, Victoria F. Low, Amy M. Smith, Angela Wu, Dahna M. Fong, Natasha L. Grimsey, Birger V. Dieriks, Clinton P. Turner, Deborah Young, Maurice A. Curtis, Richard L
description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Impaired waste clearance and chronic inflammation are emerging contributors to Parkinson’s disease pathogenesis. Here, Stevenson et al. show that aggregated α-synuclein at CNS borders promotes TNF-driven meningeal inflammation and impairs CNS clearance, identifying these tissues as potential therapeutic targets. Introduction

The central nervous system (CNS) relies on specialized clearance pathways to remove metabolic waste and maintain neurological health (Kim et al., 2025; Kipnis et al., 2025; Rustenhoven and Kipnis, 2022).

title: Dynamic Changes in Serum Glial Fibrillary Acidic Protein Levels Predicts Early Neurological Deterioration After Intravenous Thrombolysis in Minor Stroke
creator: Jie Zhou, Yang Qu, Reziya Abuduxukuer, Peng Zhang, Ting Wang, Jian‐Hua Gao, De‐Wang Pan, Zhi‐Mei Yuan, Chun‐Ying Li, Li‐Ping Chen, Jin‐Hua Chen, Ji‐Liang Gu, An‐Ying Wang, Li‐Gang Jiang, Liang Liu, Yong‐Fei Jiang, Chun‐Fei Wang, Yan Jia, Hong Xin, Chun‐Li Jiang, Ying‐Bin Qi, Xue‐Feng Hu, Song Li, Ha
description: ObjectiveMinor strokes may be associated with early neurological deterioration (END) and disabilities. The objective was to investigate the role of serum glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) levels in predicting END.MethodsData originated from a multicenter cohort study conducted prospectively. ΔGFAP was calculated as the ratio of post‐thrombolysis GFAP at 24 h to baseline GFAP.

title: Electronic and steric effects of phosphine ligands on the linear regioselectivity of propylene methoxycarbonylation
creator: Chao Kong, Qin Zhong, Dinghua Liu, Boyang Liu
description: The propylene methoxycarbonylation is a potential atom-economical reaction for the synthesis of butyrate esters, which minimizes wastewater discharge and alleviates subsequent separation difficulties. However, to the best of our knowledge, the mechanism of this reaction has not been thoroughly investigated, and the regioselectivity enhancement remains challenging.

title: Ungulate geophagy maintains termite mound habitat heterogeneity and increases internal mound temperature
creator: Stein R Moe, Cathrine Glosli, Ole Gunnar Støen, Paul Okullo
description: Savannas are globally important ecosystems and unique in supporting abundant and diverse populations of wild large mammals. Mound building fungus-farming Macrotermitinae are key determinants of savanna structure and function. Termite colonies are sensitive to shade, and their lifetime reproductive success is substantially reduced in forests compared to open savanna areas.

title: Multiplexed CRISPRi reveals a transcriptional switch between KLF activators and repressors in the maturing neocortex
creator: Ryan W Kirk, Liwei Sun, Ruixuan Xiao, Erin A Clark, Sacha B Nelson, Joshua Corbin, Ryan Kirk, Liwei Sun, Ruixuan Xiao, Erin A Clark, Sacha B Nelson
description: A critical phase of mammalian brain development takes place after birth. Neurons of the mouse neocortex undergo dramatic changes in their morphology, physiology, and synaptic connections during the first postnatal month, while properties of immature neurons, such as the capacity for robust axon outgrowth, are lost.

title: Prediction of soil shear strength using hybrid machine learning approaches for performance and interpretability analysis
creator: Muhammad Suliman, Maaz Khan, Touqeer Ali Rind, Farhan Ullah, Sabila Khan, Zafar Mahmood
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Shear strength of soil plays an essential role in geotechnical properties affecting construction stability. Conventional laboratory testing for determining soil shear strength is often expensive and time-consuming. Therefore, machine learning (ML) methods were employed to predict soil shear strength using geotechnical parameters compiled from previously published literature based on investigations conducted at the Le Trong Tan Geleximco project in western Hanoi, Vietnam.

title: On the origin of Earth’s Universal BioConsciousness
creator: Akbota Tleuberdinova
description: The origin of consciousness remains one of the oldest problems in both science and philosophy. Several emerging theories provide new perspectives on the origin and evolution of consciousness, including Cellular Basis of Consciousness (CBC) theory and the Cognition-Based Evolution (CBE) theory.

title: Real-world decision support in hospitality using pessimistic multi-granulation roughness of cubic intuitionistic fuzzy soft sets
creator: Asma Bibi, Shahida Bashir, Muhammad Shabir, Rabia Mazhar, Muhammad I Syam, Rizwan Gul
description: Traditional fuzzy and rough set models usually have a hard time in providing sufficient ambiguity, hesitancy, and partiality to information that is common in actual hospitality decision-making. In order to overcome these problems, this paper suggests a new decision-support model that is built upon pessimistic multi-granulation rough sets combined with cubic intuitionistic fuzzy soft relation.

title: Abstracts of the ICARE 2026 80th SIAARTI National Congress
creator: Unknown
description: f Medical and Surgical Sciences, Fondazione Policlinico Agostino Gemelli, Rome, Italy Correspondence: F. Scialanga Journal of Anesthesia, Analgesia and Critical Care 2026, 6(1):A1 Background Aspiration pneumonia is a significant complication in anaesthesiology, associated with increased perioperative morbidity. Despite adherence to standard preoperative fasting guidelines1, aspiration risk is not completely abolished, particularly in patients with impaired gastric emptying.

title: Correction: LncRNA H19 promotes the differentiation of bovine skeletal muscle satellite cells by suppressing Sirt1/FoxO1
creator: Xiaochun Xu, Shengyue Ji, Weili Li, Bao Yi, Hengxin Li, Hongfu Zhang, Wenping Ma
description: suppressed the differentiation of bovine tibia skeletal muscle (sk-muscle) satellite and C2C12 cells. a The immunofluorescence results for C2C12 cells and satellite cells on day 4 of differentiation. b The silencing efficiency of pLenti-H19. Cells with pLenti-NTC were the negative control and wild-type cells were the blank control (control).

title: Machine learning guided processing, microstructure and coercivity mapping in M type strontium hexaferrite
creator: Harshit Nashier, Anuja Dhingra, Rajesh Kumar, O. P. Thakur, Raghvendra Pandey
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). M-type hexaferrites are technologically important rare-earth-free permanent magnets in which coercivity (Hc) emerges from a strongly coupled and non-linear interplay between processing conditions, microstructural evolution, and intrinsic magnetic parameters. Here, we develop an experimentally grounded, physics-informed machine-learning framework by studying the multidimensional influence of processing parameters (processing temperature and time), microstructural descriptors (grain size), and intrinsic magnetic properties (saturation magnetization (Ms) and magnetocrystalline anisotropy constant (K1)) on Hc.

title: A randomized, double-blind, controlled study on the efficacy of an oral dietary supplement containing fish oil, ASU and phytotherapeutic extracts in canine osteoarthritis
creator: Angela Palumbo Piccionello, Valentina Riccio, Sara Sassaroli, Antonio Tredanari, Felice Ciabocco, Margherita Galosi, Mario Fordellone, Giacomo Rossi, Nicola Pilati, Fabrizio Dini
description: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a common musculoskeletal disorder in canines, characterized by discomfort, lameness, and reduced mobility. Because of the inconsistent efficacy of available treatments, and that a definitive resolution can be achieved only in a small number of cases, OA remains a major challenge in veterinary orthopedics.

title: Regioselective epoxidation of a polyunsaturated fatty acid by a vanadyl complex with redox-active ligands
creator: Andrew G. Hill, Tiffany Y.-C. Tang, Christina M. Knight, Kaitlyn S. Engle, Maximilian G. Bernbeck, Jake D. Soper, Aditi Das
description: Reaction of docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) with the oxovanadium complex [(Phisq)(Phibq)V(O)Cl] produces exclusively 19,20-epoxydocosapentaenoic acid (19,20-EDP). Computations reveal that the observed regioselectivity is not attributable to thermodynamics. New vanadyl analogs [(dippisq)(dippibq)V(O)Cl] and [(dippisq)2V(O)] were synthesized and showed no selectivity in DHA epoxidation.

title: Strategic resource allocation for malaria elimination in endemic settings: a systematic review of cost-effectiveness evidence
creator: Misra Helma Firdaus, Dina Syazana Ho Imran, Sharifa Ezat Wan Puteh, Tam Jenn Zhueng, Mohd Hafizi Abdul Hamid, Zulkarnain MD Idris, Mohd Rizal Abdul Manaf
description: IntroductionMalaria remains a significant global health burden, especially in endemic regions where efficient use of limited resources is critical. Economic evaluations provide essential evidence to guide strategic resource allocation and optimise intervention outcomes. This systematic review synthesises recent evidence (2018–2025) on the cost-effectiveness of malaria prevention and treatment interventions in endemic settings.

title: Demographic and regional disparities in concurrent respiratory and renal failure mortality: a CDC WONDER analysis, 1999–2024
creator: Iftikhar khan, Ibrahiem Azeem Ajaz, Asma Chaudhary, Mirha Imran Khan, Rida Khan, Fnu Urooba, Nadia Siddiqui, Waqas Ali, Arham Khalid, Muhammad Sarim Azad Khan, Hamza Asif, Ahmed Saleem, Syed Nosherwan Ali, Aisha Chaudhary, Nawras Fashafsheh, Shankar Biswas
description: Concurrent respiratory and renal failure carries exceptionally high mortality, yet population-level trends remain understudied. We analyzed temporal trends and demographic disparities in US mortality for this dual-organ failure from 1999 to 2024. We analyzed mortality data via CDC WONDER for deaths citing both respiratory (J96) and renal failure (N17–N19). Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 persons were extracted.

title: No Female Germline Stem Cells Were Identified by Advanced Dual Recombinase‐Based Lineage Tracing System
creator: Yang Gao, Zhiming Shen, Xiuhong Cui, Min Chen, Mengyue Wang, Kui Liu, Fei Gao, Hongmei Wang
description: Whether female germline stem cells (fGSCs) exist in postnatal mammalian ovaries has been debated for decades. Since the fGSCs were first reported in 2004, a large number of studies have been conducted using different approaches. However, the persistent controversy surrounding the results has caused confusion among many researchers and clinicians.

title: Bioinformatic pipeline to identify potential therapeutic targets with subsequent isolation and characterization of novel human anti- DDR1 antibodies
creator: Divya Agrawal, Stephen M. Mahler, Anurag S. Rathore, Martina L. Jones, Jessica C. Mar, Lucía F. Zacchi
description: Breast cancer remains a major global health challenge, driving the need for safer and more effective targeted therapies. This study aimed to systematically identify therapeutic targets for breast cancer using an integrated bioinformatics approach and to generate novel human monoclonal antibodies against an identified potential target followed by characterization.

title: Theory of mind and executive functions in sighted children of blind parents
creator: Joanna Wysocka, Maciej Haman, Karolina Golec, Agnieszka Pluta
description: IntroductionPrevious research indicates that during infancy, children of blind parents demonstrate greater communicative flexibility compared to peers raised by sighted parents. The present study aimed to examine whether such experience may influence executive functions and theory of mind at later stages of development.

title: Association Between Dynamic Changes in the Sling-Pubis Gap and Urinary Symptoms After Tension-Free Vaginal Tape Surgery: Protocol for a Prospective Observational Pilot Study
creator: Yaman Degirmenci, Ceren Efe Sayın, Annette Hasenburg, Gilbert Georg Klamminger, Amy Schwartz
description: BackgroundStress urinary incontinence (SUI) is one of the most common pelvic floor disorders in women and is frequently treated surgically using midurethral sling procedures. Despite the high success rates of these procedures, postoperative voiding dysfunction remains a clinically relevant complication that may negatively affect patient satisfaction and quality of life. The underlying mechanisms are multifactorial and not completely understood.

title: Development and operation of a 100 W wave energy converter for persistent ocean observation
creator: Curtis J. Rusch, Erik Hammagren, Joe Prudell, Zhe Zhang, Jim Thomson
description: Much of the existing literature for wave energy converters focuses on devices tailored to grid-scale performance. In this paper, we present the development of TigerRAY, a small, blue-economy scale wave energy converter, designed to generate 100 W in fetch limited waves.

title: Neurostimulation device infection control in China and the United States: a comparative analysis using the MCS framework
creator: Xiaohan Qin, Lanfang Chen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Neurostimulation devices, including deep brain stimulation (DBS) and spinal cord stimulation (SCS) systems, have transformed treatment for neurological disorders and chronic pain. However, device-related infections remain a critical challenge with global incidence rates of 3–7%. This narrative review introduces the Mechanism-Clinical-System (MCS) framework to comprehensively evaluate infection control practices in China and the United States, integrating evidence from 2020 to 2025.

title: Morphological identification of fungi associated with preharvest spoilage of sweet orange (Citrus sinensis L.) fruit in Bilo Nopha, Southwestern Ethiopia
creator: Gobena Adeba, Tekalign Kejela, Tesfalem Atnafu
description: Sweet orange (Citrus sinensis L.) is a major fruit crop globally, but fungal pathogens have severely impacted its yield. Bilo Nopha, known for high-quality sweet oranges, has recently faced significant preharvest spoilage. This study aimed to isolate fungal pathogens associated with preharvest spoilage of sweet orange (Citrus sinensis L.) fruit in Bilo Nopha, southwestern Ethiopia.

title: A cost-effective data assimilation system for improving ROMS simulations in the Southwest Atlantic
creator: Geoff S. Dorfschäfer, Clemente A. S. Tanajura, Thiago P. De Paula, Filipe B. Costa, Janini Pereira
description: This study presents for the first time the integration of the low-cost REMO Ocean Data Assimilation System (RODAS) into the Regional Ocean Modeling System (ROMS) for assimilating Sea Surface Temperature (SST) observations. RODAS is an Ensemble Optimal Interpolation (EnOI)-based data assimilation system originally developed for use with the HYCOM model.

title: Integrating remote sensing and multi-criteria decision analysis for groundwater zoning in the Eastern Desert of Egypt
creator: H. Ezz
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The Eastern Desert of Egypt is a hyper-arid region where groundwater serves as the primary alternative to surface water for sustainable development. However, comprehensive assessments of groundwater potential across this vast and geologically complex region remain limited. This study addresses this gap by developing a spatial model for delineating groundwater potential zones (GWPZ) using an integrated approach that combines remote sensing, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), and the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP).

title: Research on deformation and seepage properties of Larssen pile reinforcing cofferdam based on numerical analysis, Tianjin, China
creator: Shejie Lin, Xinjian Wang, Xingsheng Zhang, Shipeng Liu
description: The construction of cofferdams poses significant challenges in hydraulic engineering, where optimized design is essential for risk mitigation and construction safety. This study investigates the performance of a Larssen pile-reinforced cofferdam in a field ridge remediation project through integrated numerical modeling and limit equilibrium analysis.

title: Characterization of therapeutic antibodies targeting lymphatic and vascular resistance factor for the treatment of hypervascularized and highly metastatic cancers
creator: Marion David, Arthur Karaulic, Audrey Bennetot, Clémence Fournier, Quentin Odet, Arthur Gouraud, Isabelle Bourget, Cédric Gaggioli, Sandy Giuliano, Frédéric Luciano, Olivier Léger, Zaki Sellam, Gilles Pagès
description: Angiogenesis is a major driver of tumor progression and a validated therapeutic target in highly vascularized cancers such as clear cell renal cell carcinoma. However, the clinical benefit of antivascular endothelial growth factor therapies is limited by the emergence of resistance.

title: Prevalence of gastrointestinal parasites in horses in the district of Abidjan, Ivory Coast
creator: Noumouké Kante, Lanceï Kaba, Kouadio-Ba Idrissa N’Gotta, Almamy Ousmane Deen Camara, Albert Sourou Salako, Kouramoudou Berete, Karim Tuo, Assi Fiacre-Tanguy N’Docho, Éric Gondo, Marie Marlène Cyriaque Teohou, Adjoua Aicha N’Gotta, Abdoulaye Kuan Traore, Nicolas Barro
description: Gastrointestinal parasitic infections constitute a major constraint to equine health and productivity, particularly in tropical regions where climatic and environmental conditions favor parasite survival and transmission. In Côte d’Ivoire, epidemiological data regarding gastrointestinal parasites in horses remain limited, especially in urban and peri-urban settings such as the district of Abidjan.

title: Dysregulated AKT signaling reprograms osteosarcoma to drive selective reliance on EP300
creator: Ian M. Delahunty, Stephanie Nance, Yang Zhang, Francois Lamoureux, Qi Liu, William C. Wright, K. Elaine Ritter, Noha A.M. Shendy, Bénédicte Brounais-Le Roye, Sandra J. Kietlinska, Mohammad A. Mohammad Nezhady, Yuan Feng, Barbara De Kegel, Matthew G. Rees, Mustafa Kocak, Ashish B. George, Meifen Lu,
description: Here, Delahunty et al. identify that EP300 controls the growth of AKT-dysregulated osteosarcoma cells by regulating expression of state-specific genetic dependencies. AKT inhibitors synergize with EP300 degraders to suppress osteosarcoma growth in vitro and in vivo. These agents positively combine across cancer cells in a manner dependent on control of protein synthesis.

title: Bi-temporal processing in music notation reading: a theory linking prediction, memory, and automaticity
creator: Karen L. Heath
description: Reading music notation requires musicians to extract and interpret visual information in real time while simultaneously anticipating future performance actions. This dual engagement, in which one acts in the present while processing material to be performed in the future, suggests that music reading relies on a bi-temporal cognitive architecture.

title: Clinical and genomic characterization of Influenza A co-infection with SARS-CoV-2 and Influenza B: a respiratory surveillance study in Assam, India
creator: Neelanjana Sarmah, Aktarul Islam Siddique, Mousumi Dutta, Aniruddha Jakharia, Nargis Bali, Neetu Vijay, Nivedita Gupta, Suman Kanungo, Biswajyoti Borkakoty
description: Influenza and SARS-CoV-2 are the primary contributors to seasonal respiratory infections and frequently co-circulate, creating significant health challenges. The present respiratory surveillance study was conducted in Dibrugarh, Assam, India from January 2025 to August 2025 to investigate the genomic characteristics of circulating viruses and identify potential co-infections.

title: Undertreatment of Wernicke encephalopathy in alcohol-related clinical contexts: a scoping review of diagnosis, thiamine regimens, and clinical management
creator: André Akira Sueno Goldani, Gabriel Feitosa, Eduarda Vasconcelos Colchete, Cristhian Ferreira Falleiro, Cristine Weihrauch Pedro, Félix Henrique Paim Kessler, Thiago M. Fidalgo, Lisia von Diemen
description: BackgroundWernicke encephalopathy (WE) is a potentially reversible neurological emergency that remains frequently missed and undertreated in patients with alcohol use disorder (AUD). Although thiamine is widely accepted as the cornerstone of prevention and treatment, diagnostic uncertainty, limited comparative evidence, and heterogeneous clinical recommendations contribute to substantial variability in real-world management.

title: Appendix300: Surgical video and patient metadata of 330 laparoscopic appendectomy cases from five institutions
creator: Fiona R. Kolbinger, Max Kirchner, Kevin Pfeiffer, Sebastian Bodenstedt, Alexander C. Jenke, Julia Barthel, Matthias Carstens, Karolin Dehlke, Sophia Dietz, Sotirios Emmanouilidis, Guido Fitze, Martin Freitag, Fabian Holderried, Thorsten Jacobi, Weam Kanjo, Linda Leitermann, Sören Torge Mees, Steffen
description: The limited availability of diverse and representative training data poses a critical barrier to the development of clinically relevant computational tools for intraoperative surgical decision support. Surgical procedures are not routinely recorded, and data annotation requires domain expertise, resulting in a scarcity of open-access surgical video datasets with high-quality annotations.

title: FAM50A promotes esophageal squamous cell carcinoma progression via splicing-dependent oncogenic circSDK1- and DUSP22-mediated MAPK/FAK activation
creator: Yan Bian, Ye Gao, Xin Chang, Bo Tian, Qianqian Meng, Lei Xin, Han Lin, Wei Wang, Zhaoshen Li, Luowei Wang
description: Dysregulated splicing factors play critical roles in tumor progression. Here, we identify family with sequence similarity 50 member A (FAM50A) as a pivotal oncogenic splicing factor involved in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). Multi-omics and multi-cohort analyses revealed that FAM50A is upregulated in ESCC and correlates with a poor prognosis.

title: Closed-loop iron chelate recycling via molecularly imprinted hydrogels suppresses ferroptosis
creator: Yubin Yao, Ting Ying, Chenyu Zong, Tao Ding, Qi Li, Zeyu Han, Fei Wang, Wenguo Cui, Mingzhu Zhang
description: Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of oxidative cell death, has emerged as a key driver of osteoarthritis, yet therapeutic strategies remain limited by the inability to safely eliminate iron–chelate complexes after treatment. Their local accumulation can lead to secondary iron release, oxidative stress, and sustained tissue damage.

title: Cytokine context shapes antigen-presenting and matrix-producing states of cancer-associated fibroblasts
creator: Feifei Song, Qi Chen, Dengfeng Huang, Youhua Zhang, Dongyan Han, Wei Rao, Man Li, Yaohui Gao, Renfeng Zhang, Huiyuan Zhu, Shufei Wang, Xiao Jiang, Shengli Lin, Dexi Bi, Haixian Zhang, Qing Wei, Huanlong Qin
description: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) exhibit remarkable functional heterogeneity, with conserved subtypes observed across diverse malignancies. However, their shared roles in shaping the tumor microenvironment (TME) and their dynamic plasticity remain incompletely understood. In this study, through integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomic profiling across four cancer types, we identified two distinct immunomodulatory CAF states, termed antigen-presenting CAFs (apCAFs) and matrix-producing CAFs (mCAFs).

title: Efficacy of blood copeptin level for the prediction of mortality of adult patients with sepsis: a meta-analysis
creator: Jiayang Huang, Tingting Niu, Huijie Shi
description: BackgroundCopeptin, the C-terminal fragment of provasopressin, has emerged as a potential prognostic biomarker in sepsis. However, its predictive accuracy for mortality in adult patients with sepsis remains uncertain. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the diagnostic performance of elevated blood copeptin levels for mortality prediction in this population.

title: Temporal dynamics of ammonia and nitrous oxide emissions following green crop residue recycling in soils
creator: Varunesh Chandra, Gwenaëlle Lashermes, Patricia Laville, Alain Fortineau, Benjamin Loubet, Raia Silvia Massad
description: The recycling of green crop residues is promoted for enhancing soil organic carbon sequestration and health, but can also stimulate emissions of nitrous oxide (N₂O) and ammonia (NH₃). Soil tillage can lead to different residue distributions which affect contact with decomposers and local gas and solute diffusion.

title: A novel strategy for reconstruction of AORI type III proximal tibial defects
creator: Xingzhen Li, Qing Han, Xue Zhao, Jinbo Zhang, Qian Wan, Zhennan Gan, Xiaonan Wang, Xin Zhao, Hao Chen, Aobo Zhang, Jincheng Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). AimsFor cases of Anderson Orthopaedic Research Institute (AORI) type III proximal tibial defects with intact medial collateral ligaments (MCLs), knee reconstruction is conventionally performed using semi-constrained prostheses with stemmed tibial components in conjunction with cones or sleeves. This study aimed to reconstruct AORI type III tibial defects using a 3D-printed extension-stem augment, followed by surface-type knee reconstruction to achieve long-term stability and promising clinical outcomes.MethodsA patient-specific porous extension-stem augment was designed based on the defect morphology.

title: Decoding phage communication: molecular networks, evolutionary dynamics, and therapeutic applications
creator: Sahar Abed, Mohammad Sholeh, Sara Sadeghi, Ameneh Khatami, Peter Speck, Morvarid Shafiei
description: Communication between bacteriophages, particularly in biofilms, has long been studied. The recent discovery of the arbitrium lysis-lysogeny switch in Bacillus phages, similar to bacterial quorum sensing, has renewed interest in phage communication. This review examines the arbitrium system alongside other switching mechanisms, explores its role in pathogen-phage-host immune interactions, and proposes design principles for “smart” phage therapies.

title: MIGC: Pseudotime differentially expressed genes detection with mutual information
creator: Jiachen Li, Ye Yuan
description: Trajectory analysis of single‐cell RNA sequencing (scRNA‐seq) data provides insights into cell differentiation and the underlying mechanisms at the gene level. Although various pseudotime inference methods have been proposed, the detection of pseudotime differentially expressed genes (DEGs) mainly relies on generalized additive model fitting followed by statistical hypothesis testing.

title: Unraveling the metabolic pathways between atherosclerosis and sarcopenia
creator: Mei Yu, Lichao Ge, Chen Fu, Rujia Zhao
description: Sarcopenia and atherosclerosis are age-related conditions pathologically intertwined through a self-reinforcing, bidirectional cycle. This review dissects the core mechanistic pillars of this synergy such as insulin resistance, chronic low-grade inflammation, ectopic lipid deposition, and hormonal dysregulation. We detail how skeletal muscle dysfunction exacerbates systemic insulin resistance and inflammatory cascades that accelerate endothelial damage and atherogenesis.

title: Dual-phase eutectic ceramics with improved hardness and toughness via nano-coherent high-entropy oxides
creator: Xu Wang, Yujie Zhong, Huadong Li, Ye Yuan, Xiangyu Huang, Cui Zhou, Detian Wan, Yuan Tian, Xingyue Zhai, Jihong Zhu, Zied Moumni, Jian Lu, Weihong Zhang
description: Alumina-based eutectic ceramics exhibited high high-temperature strength but their intrinsic brittleness constrained broad structural applications. Here, we broke this limitation by introducing high-entropy rare-earth aluminate (REAlO3, RE = Gd0.25Eu0.25Nd0.25Sm0.25) into the Al2O3 matrix via directional solidification. The resulting dual-phase eutectics exhibited a unique architecture where single-crystalline Al2O3 was interlocked with bicrystalline high-entropy REAlO3, forming nanoscale coherent grain boundaries (~57.

title: Discrepancy Between Clinical Suspicion and Legal Outcomes in Suspected Child Abuse: A 10-Year Single-Center Study
creator: Hye-Ri Jang, Chloe Jooan Lee, Ju Hyun Back, Eun Young Kim, Jaeso Cho, Hunmin Kim
description: Despite mandatory reporting, many suspected child abuse cases never proceed to formal investigation in Korea. We retrospectively reviewed 83 pediatric patients evaluated for suspected child abuse at a tertiary hospital between 2015 and 2025, screened using the Finding Instrument for Non-accidental Deeds score, and analyzed clinical characteristics, injury severity, and investigative outcomes. The mean age was 4.

title: Caring relationships in times of crisis: the role of families during the Covid-19 pandemic
creator: Isabella Crespi, Marta Scocco
description: IntroductionCaregiving is shaped by social system factors that influence the availability of formal and informal support and represents a key life-course experience linked to ageing and family roles. Intra-family relationships and the exchange of emotional and practical support are crucial for older adults’ well-being, yet remain underexplored in relation to the Covid-19 pandemic.

title: UAV multispectral sensing and data-driven modeling for precision onion yield prediction
creator: Sagar M. Wayal, Shardul Parab, Anusha Raj, Kiran Khandagale, Sanket Bhegde, Mukund Dawale, Indira Bhangare, Mahesh Khaire, Yogesh Kadam, Zafar Shaikh, V. Karuppaiah, Pranjali Gedam, Bhushan Bibwe, Sanket J. More, Lakesh K. Sharma, Vijay Mahajan, Suresh J. Gawande
description: The integration of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted remote sensing with the Internet of Things (IoT) and Internet of Everything (IoE) offers a robust platform for optimizing precision agriculture by capturing spatiotemporal variability in crop growth. In this context, the present study aimed to predict the bulb yield of rainy-season onion crops across four staggered planting dates using UAV-based multispectral imagery.

title: Intensivists’ Perspectives and Practices on Palliative Care in the ICU: A Nationwide Survey in Korea
creator: Tae Jung Kim, Yoon Sun Jung, Ye Sul Jeung, Woo Hyun Cho, Shin Hye Yoo, Jae Young Moon
description: BackgroundWhile many countries have made progress in integrating palliative care into intensive care units (ICUs), implementation remains highly context-dependent. In Korea, palliative care integration within ICUs remains limited, and intensivists’ perspectives on its role and applicability have not been well studied.

title: The impact of 1-hour plasma glucose on the metabolic characteristics and pregnancy outcomes in polycystic ovary syndrome
creator: Xiu Huang, Nan Lu, Hui Yu, Fan Yang, Lihua Wang, Meili Cai, Diliqingna Dilimulati, Yuqin Zhang, Jiayi Lu, Changbin Li, Shen Qu, Lan Fang, Hongwei Ji, Manna Zhang
description: BackgroundTo investigate the impact of 1-hour plasma glucose (1 h-PG) on the metabolic characteristics and pregnancy outcomes in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS).MethodsThis multicenter study analyzed 970 PCOS patients (2019–2025), including 289 undergoing assisted reproductive technology (198 successful deliveries). Participants were stratified by glucose tolerance: Group 1 (normal: fasting PG [FPG] ≤ 6.1, 1 h-PG < 8.

title: Five critical blind spots limiting translational progress in primary sclerosing cholangitis
creator: Martin Cornillet
description: t this translational gap reflects critical deficiencies in human translational infrastructure: many of the most informative patients, tissues, and disease stages remain understudied. In this Editorial, I discuss 5 blind spots that continue to limit progress and propose strategies to overcome them through human-centered translational research.

title: P-WIN deployment: real-time personalized machine learning to predict critical deterioration in a pediatric intensive care unit
creator: Eamonn Tweedy, Sanjiv Mehta, Sachin Grover, Hannah R Stinson, Victor M Ruiz, Erika Pleskunas, James Sannino, Akira Nishisaki, Fuchiang (Rich) Tsui
description: ObjectivesEarly recognition of critical deterioration events (CDEs) in pediatric intensive care units (PICUs) is crucial to improving outcomes, but the real-time performance of machine-learning (ML)-based alert systems is rarely assessed. We prospectively evaluated the performance, operational utility, and deployment feasibility of the PICU Warning Index (P-WIN), a personalized ML alert system predicting CDE in the PICU.

title: Preoperative gut microbial network alterations and BCAA-Related metabolic disturbance in postoperative delirium after cardiac surgery: a prospective matched multi-omic study
creator: Congmin Lyu, Ziying Wang, Ruojin Zhao, Haiping Zhao, Sheng Liu, Hong Lian, Xin Wang
description: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a frequent neuropsychiatric complication after cardiac surgery, yet the biological basis of individual susceptibility remains unclear. In this prospective cohort study, 317 adults undergoing elective on-pump cardiac surgery were enrolled and followed for POD during the first 7 postoperative days.

title: A rare case of gallbladder torsion with incidental stage IIIB gallbladder adenocarcinoma
creator: Makenna Marty, Jonathan Zuo, Linan Wang, Marc A Attiyeh
description: Gallbladder torsion is rare and can mimic acute cholecystitis. We report an 83-year-old female who presented with abdominal pain, leukocytosis, and hyperbilirubinemia. Work-up showed a distended, thick-walled gallbladder with stones and suspected choledocholithiasis. Because of worsening pain and concern for impending perforation, she underwent urgent cholecystectomy, which revealed a freely mobile gallbladder consistent with torsion. Final pathology showed a 0.

title: Efficacy of Pam3CSK4 as a cross-species adjuvant for polysaccharide vaccines in humanized mouse and non-human primate models
creator: Jamie E. Jennings-Gee, Alexis E. Adams-Sims, Karen M. Haas
description: Polysaccharide-based vaccines are essential for preventing bacterial infections, but their effectiveness is limited by weak antibody responses and lack of suitable adjuvants. TLR4 agonists enhance polysaccharide-specific antibody responses through B cell–intrinsic TLR4-MyD88 signaling in mice, but this mechanism is not conserved in primates, prompting the search for alternative MyD88-activating agonists.

title: Diffuse stimulant-associated vasculopathy presenting with acute limb ischemia, compartment syndrome, and multifocal visceral infarction
creator: Syed Azaan Adnan, Julianne Wanner, Syed Moaiz Adnan, Christopher Thompson
description: Stimulant-induced vasculopathy typically presents as localized ischemia secondary to vasospasm and thrombosis. Diffuse involvement of multiple vascular territories is uncommon and may result in severe, multisystem complications and increased morbidity. We report a 40-year-old female with polysubstance exposure, including cocaine and amphetamines, who presented with acute right lower extremity ischemia and compartment syndrome.

title: Relief of GbDEAH12G repression on the GbNAC072C-GbHOX3 axis improves lint percentage in Gossypium barbadense
creator: Bin Li, Nan Zhao, Kaiyun Jiang, Jie Kong, Meng Wang, Baoliang Wang, Weiran Wang, Suen Liu, Huijing Li, Zhuanxia Pan, Jiahui Zhu, Junyi Geng, Beibei Lv, Zhanghao Xia, Alifu Aierxi, Jingrou Zhang, Baosheng Guo, Pengbo Li, Daojun Yuan, Anhui Guo, Jinping Hua
description: Improving lint percentage (LP) is a key breeding target for Sea Island cotton (Gossypium barbadense), yet its genetic basis remains poorly understood. Here, we identify GbNAC072C as a positive regulator of LP that promotes fiber cell protrusions by directly activating the transcription of GbHOX3.

title: Neointimal Hyperplasia and Restenosis: Epidemiology, Pathophysiology, Animal Models, Clinical Features, Diagnosis, and Management
creator: Kaixu Wang, Daiyu Zhang, Yu Hu, Yixin Zhao, Xinling Wang, Long Jiang, Meixiu Jiang
description: In‐stent restenosis (ISR) remains a major complication following vascular interventions, with neointimal hyperplasia representing a central pathological process that can adversely affect postoperative outcomes. Accumulating evidence indicates that neointimal hyperplasia is driven by vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) phenotypic transition, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and multiple forms of programmed cell death. Despite substantial advances, the underlying pathogenic mechanisms remain incompletely understood.

title: Late-stage generation of 14C/3H-radiolabeled lysine residues via hydroformylation of peptides
creator: Anika Schick, Marc San Jose Gracia, Hans Christian D. Hammershøj, Johan Broddefalk, Pablo Martínez-Pardo, Vitus J. Enemærke, Lena von Sydow, Anna Holub, Ranganath Gopalakrishnan, Kim S. Mühlfenzl, Troels Skrydstrup, Charles S. Elmore
description: Peptides constitute a well-established and rapidly expanding field in the contemporary pharmaceutical drug landscape. Studies with 14C- or 3H-radiolabeled analogs are the gold standard for drug development, yet access to 14C-peptides is costly and limited to derivatization of the native structure with tags or lengthy multi-step syntheses.

title: Emphysematous gastritis with extensive portal venous gas and endoscopic mucosal necrosis: gastric preservation despite an alarming presentation
creator: Ettore Caruso, Carmine Gabriele, Denise Gambardella, Roccantonio Pellegrino, Maria Bonaddio, Luigi Strangis, Francesca Ibba, Martina De Luca, Martina Saragò, Martina Nicoletti, Laura Rizzo, Francesca Vescio, Vittorio Tedesco, Aurora Somma, Giuseppe Bonadio, Gianlorenzo Schicchi, Angelo Aldo Schicchi
description: Emphysematous gastritis (EG) is a rare, potentially life-threatening condition. Extensive gastric pneumatosis and portal venous gas may suggest irreversible ischemia, although radiological severity and mucosal injury do not necessarily indicate transmural necrosis. A 70-year-old man presented with acute epigastric pain and vomiting. Computed tomography (CT) demonstrated extensive gastric and duodenal pneumatosis with portomesenteric venous gas but patent visceral arteries.

title: Multiscale structural engineering enables superior energy storage in tetragonal tungsten bronze relaxor ferroelectrics
creator: Saifei Wang, Juntao Huang, Guangyao Li, Tao Yang, Haihua Huang, Yajie Han, Wei Li, Zhenxiang Cheng, He Qi, Mahesh Kumar Joshi, Peng Fu
description: Lead-free relaxor ferroelectric ceramics are promising for pulsed-power systems due to their ultrafast discharge and high-power density, yet their practical use remains limited by low breakdown strength and insufficient energy-storage density. Here, we report Ba2La1−xBixTi2Nb3O15 ceramics with a tetragonal tungsten bronze structure, which achieve a recoverable energy density of 14.39 J/cm3 and an efficiency of 87.

title: Correction to: Menstrual fluid-derived small extracellular vesicles: a novel reservoir with distinct molecular signatures and implications for endometriosis etiopathology
creator: Unknown
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ual fluid-derived small extracellular vesicles: a novel reservoir with distinct molecular signatures and implications for endometriosis etiopathology, Human Reproduction Open, Volume 2026, Issue 2, hoag020, https://doi.org/10.1093/hropen/hoag020. The RNA sequencing data deposited in the NCBI GEO repository under accession number GSE310627 and presented in the originally published version of Supplementary Table S1 were derived from menstrual fluid-derived mesenchymal stem cells instead of menstrual fluid-derived small extracellular vesicles.

title: A novel truncating FBN1 variant in a family with Marfan syndrome
creator: Yuka Ito, Hiroshi Suzumura, Yuko Tanaka, George Imataka, Shujiro Hayashi, Yoshimasa Kawarai, Hiroko Susaka, Miyuki Muramatsu, Hiromi Yuasa, Wakana Soeda, Sakae Ito, Takahiko Kogai, Takahiro Yamada, Katsuhiko Naruse
description: Marfan syndrome is caused by pathogenic variants in FBN1. We identified a novel heterozygous frameshift variant in FBN1 (NM_000138.5: c.6784_6787del, NP_000129.3:p.(Gln2262TrpfsTer28)) in an adult male with severe cardiovascular manifestations. The variant was absent from population databases and fulfilled PVS1 and PM2 criteria.

title: A multifunctional bishydroxycoumarin conjugate exhibiting AIE characteristics and tandem Co2+/ATP detection with logic gate operations, on-site sensing and bioimaging applications
creator: Rajendran Kishore Kumar, Suryaa Manoharan, Ekambaram Perumal, Balasubramanian Murugesapandian
description: An efficient coumarin-based fluorescent probe, HCPD, was synthesized via condensation of 7-diethylamino-4-hydroxycoumarin aldehyde with o-phenylenediamine. The structure of the probe was confirmed by FT-IR, NMR and HRMS studies. The probe, HCPD exhibited aggregation-induced emission (AIE) characteristics in a THF-water mixture, showing enhanced emission at 80% water fraction.

title: Anlotinib combined with neoadjuvant chemotherapy for HR+/HER2− breast cancer (ACNTBC): a prospective, single-arm, single-center phase II clinical study with real-world validation
creator: Jiajun Ding, Huimin Meng, Yidi Wang, Haoyi Zi, Mengxuan Li, He Chen, Cong Fan, Shuai Wang, Liying Zhang, Lei Shang, Jing Kong, Jing Fan, Ting Wang
description: Despite being an option for high-risk or inoperable cases, existing neoadjuvant therapies for hormone receptor-positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HR+/HER2−) breast cancer yield suboptimal pathological responses, necessitating novel strategies. This prospective, phase II ACNTBC trial (NCT05558722) investigated the efficacy and safety of combining anlotinib with chemotherapy as a neoadjuvant treatment for HR+/HER2− breast cancer.

title: Adsorption-assisted removal of chlorinated pollutants using a magnetically recoverable Fe3O4/CeO2 nanocomposite: kinetics, machine learning and first-principle insights
creator: Monika Dubey, Sunita Saharan, Monika Joshi, Piyush Kuchhal, Ranjit Kumar
description: The development of efficient and recyclable catalysts for persistent organic pollutant removal remains a major challenge in environmental nanotechnology. Herein, a mesoporous Fe3O4/CeO2 nanocomposite was synthesized and systematically characterized, confirming a particle size of (20 ± 10 nm) with a high surface area (44.6 m2 g−1), magnetic recoverability, and abundant oxygen vacancies.

title: Prospective Trial on Tolerability and Efficacy of Adjuvant Nedaplatin Plus Docetaxel for Non‐Small Cell Lung Cancer
creator: Koji Teramoto, Ryosuke Kaku, Tomoyuki Igarashi, Masayuki Hashimoto, Shoji Kitamura, Makoto Motoishi, Yuji Suzumura, Satoru Sawai, Yataro Daigo, Jun Hanaoka
description: Nedaplatin is a second‐generation platinum compound with reduced nephrotoxicity compared with cisplatin. Given its favorable tolerability in advanced non‐small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), we prospectively evaluated the tolerability and efficacy of an adjuvant nedaplatin plus docetaxel chemotherapy regimen in patients with completely resected NSCLC.

title: Factors Associated With In‐Hospital Mortality and Length of Stay Among Hospitalised Patients Receiving Carbapenem Therapy: A Retrospective Cohort Study
creator: Abdullah Faiz Zaihan, Dhivyaa K. Ganesan, Chia Siang Kow
description: BackgroundPatients receiving carbapenems are clinically heterogeneous and have severe infections and multiple comorbidities. Evidence on factors associated with mortality and length of stay (LOS) in this treatment‐defined population remains limited.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included adult hospital episodes involving at least one carbapenem dose at Hospital Shah Alam during 2025.

title: Small Extracellular Vesicle‐Associated Polymeric Immunoglobulin Receptor in Primary Liver Cancer: From Immunological Mediator to Oncogenic Driver and Biomarker
creator: Jeremy Ting Ruei Hsu, Samuel Wan Ki Wong, Judy Yam Wai Ping
description: types of primary liver cancers, HCC remains the predominant subtype, accounting for more than 80% of all cases [2]. In Hong Kong, HCC has an incidence rate of approximately 16.5 per 100,000 males, ranking as the fourth most common cancer affecting men in the region [3].

title: Periodontitis and Stroke Onset, Medical Costs and Length of Hospital Stay: A 5‐Year Cohort Study
creator: Mizuki Saito, Yoshihiro Shimazaki, Toshiya Nonoyama, Yoshinori Inamoto
description: AimsTo evaluate the longitudinal association between periodontitis and stroke onset using medical claims data and also to assess the relationship between periodontitis and stroke‐related medical costs and length of hospital stay.Materials and MethodsIn total, 1997 individuals aged 75 or 80 years were included.

title: Reconfigurable Light Field Generation With Hologram‐Enhanced Multicore Fibers
creator: Mohammadhossein Khosravi, Leonidas Zbinden, Bennet Fischer, Adrian Lorenz, Jian Kim, Robert Leitel, Zhirong Tao, Carsten Rockstuhl, Thomas Sturges, Markus Nyman, Markus A Schmidt
description: Tailoring light fields at remote or confined locations is a key requirement for many emerging photonic technologies. Here, a multicore fiber functionalized with a 3D‐printed hologram for the reconfigurable generation of structured light distributions is demonstrated. A computationally optimized 3D‐printed phase‐only hologram maps the fields emitted by the individual fiber cores onto prescribed output field distributions.

title: Accuracy of ophthalmic referral diagnoses by non-ophthalmologists in acute eye care: protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Luis Cunha Gil, Anaya Powis, Helen Wilson, Reshma Thampy, Obaid Kousha, Felipe Dhawahir-Scala
description: AbstractIntroductionOphthalmic complaints account for a substantial proportion of presentations to emergency and acute eye care services, yet initial assessment or referral is frequently performed by non-ophthalmologist healthcare professionals. Previous single-centre studies suggest that one-third of referrals are incorrectly diagnosed, potentially delaying appropriate management of vision-threatening conditions.

title: CAMELLIA: an alignment-free pipeline integrating k-mer feature selection and supervised classification for genomic sequence subtyping
creator: Tatiana Mari Saita, Matheus Henrique Pimenta-Zanon, Artur Trancoso Lopo de Queiroz, Glaucia Maria Bressan, Fabricio Martins Lopes
description: Scalable analysis of biological sequences is essential for functional characterization, biomarker discovery, and therapeutic and vaccine development. Alignment-based pipelines often fail to capture intraspecific variation and become computationally limited on large datasets, while alignment-free methods treat each class as homogeneous, ignoring sample heterogeneity.

title: Barriers and facilitators to digital health tool adoption for hypertension management: systematic review of qualitative studies
creator: Emily Motta-Yanac, Victoria Riley, Naomi J Ellis, Aman Mankoo, Christopher J Gidlow
description: AbstractObjectivesDigital health interventions (DHIs) show considerable promise in supporting hypertension self-management by promoting preventative care and self-monitoring. While their efficacy is increasingly evident, the long-term uptake, acceptance and sustained engagement with these tools are frequently challenged by issues such as usability, trust and varying user experiences.

title: Ultrasound-mediated structural and chemical modifications in wheat proteins and their impact on functional and storage properties: a review
creator: Kanu Garg, Shubhra Sinha, Kamaljit Kaur, Ovais Shafiq Qadri
description: Wheat is one of the most widely consumed cereal grains across the world because of its versatile adaptability and applications. Nearly 25% of the global cereal production is contributed by wheat. It is a rich source of carbohydrates, proteins, dietary fibres, and vitamins.

title: Randomised, double-blind clinical trial protocol to evaluate whether early and perioperative tranexamic acid administration reduces transfusion rates and blood loss of patients undergoing hip fracture surgery in Spain
creator: Josu Arrieta, Gaspar De La Herran, Luis Angel Mínguez Cabeza, María Isabel Fernández González, María Teresa Revilla Guarinos
description: IntroductionIn patients with a hip fracture, anaemia has been associated with increased transfusion requirements, poor functional outcomes, prolonged hospital stays and increased mortality. While anaemia in elderly patients with hip fractures has traditionally been attributed to bleeding during or after surgery, many of these patients are anaemic on hospital admission.

title: Updated International Patient Decision Aid Standards (IPDAS version 5.0): modified Delphi, evidence informed consensus process
creator: Robert J Volk, Krystina B Lewis, Maureen Smith, Meg Carley, Michael J Barry, Hilary L Bekker, Martin Härter, Tammy Hoffmann, Kirsten McCaffery, Michael Pignone, Karina Dahl Steffensen, Karen Sepucha, Rachel Thompson, Lyndal Trevena, Trudy van der Weijden, Holly O Witteman, Dawn Stacey
description: Patient decision aids (PDAs) are evidence informed tools designed to support patients in the process of making decisions about their health. The International Patient Decision Aid Standards (IPDAS) Collaboration last updated the standards in 2013 and the evidence about patient decision aids has expanded substantially.

title: Microalgal Synthetic Biotechnology: From Genetic Models to Deployable Photosynthetic Chassis
creator: Jin Liu
description: Microalgae have long been considered promising platforms for producing biochemicals and supporting environmental applications. Realizing this potential will require turning microalgal species into predictable and reusable engineering platforms. However, it remains challenging to engineer such evolutionarily diverse, compartmentalized photosynthetic eukaryotes in a predictable way, because their behavior depends strongly on organelle organization, gene-expression context, and cultivation conditions.

title: Exploring the organismal role of UFMylation in development, stress resilience, and neurological function in Caenorhabditis elegans
creator: Charlotte Sophia Kaiser, Janina Kahl, Emily Jeanne Kouekem, Emma Schröder, Luka Ressmann, Antonio Miranda-Vizuete, Eva Liebau
description: UFMylation is a posttranslational modification that conjugates ubiquitin-fold modifier 1 to substrate proteins, regulating fundamental processes including ribosomal homeostasis, the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress response and DNA damage repair. While loss-of-function mutations in the UFMylation cascade cause lethality in mammals, they are viable in Caenorhabditis elegans, offering a unique opportunity to investigate its physiological role at the organismal level.

title: The translational asymmetry of corpus callosotomy: Two literatures that answered different questions
creator: Vitória Bernal Cavalcanti, Paulo Henrique Pires de Aguiar
description: Corpus callosotomy is an established palliative operation for drug‐resistant epilepsy dominated by drop attacks, and it is performed in three extents: anterior, usually of the anterior two‐thirds; total, in one or two stages; and selective posterior, which preserves the genu and rostral body.

title: Both L-Lactyl and D-Lactyl Enantiomers Modify Histones in Mouse Testis
creator: Julie Manessier, Hassan Hijazi, Lisa Vizzini, Sabine Brugière, Marie Courçon, Christophe Masselon, Alberto de la Iglesia, Julie Cocquet, Delphine Pflieger
description: Dynamic histone posttranslational modifications are crucial to precisely orchestrate gene expression programs. The recently discovered histone lysine lactylation has already been explored in various pathological contexts, but less in normal tissues. This modification exists as two enantiomers, L- and D-lactylation; the former may more likely modify histones due to abundant L-lactate produced by glycolysis.

title: Mapping mental health complexity in esports: an exploratory psychosocial network approach
creator: Lucas Van Ruysevelt, Martijn Van Heel, Michael G Trotter, Matthew Watson, Ismael Pedraza-Ramirez, Iván Bonilla, Paul Davis, Jóhann Ragnarsson, Olivier Mairesse, Jolan Kegelaers
description: BackgroundThe rapid rise in popularity of esports has brought increased attention to the unique mental health challenges faced by esports players, yet research in this area remains in its infancy. Early research suggests a substantial mental health burden and has examined associations between esports-specific stressors, mental health, and sleep disturbances.

title: Systematic identification of characteristic chemical constituents in Cistanches Herba from saline-alkali land based on hierarchical filtering of mass spectrometry data and spatial metabolomics technology
creator: Mengjiao Li, Yaqi Wang, Chenghao Bi, Ruifen Wang, Fengdan Guo, Guiqing Shen, Zihan Hu, Kairui Liu, Xinrui Li, Renwei Guan, Songsong Wang, Hao Zhong, Xingjun Wang, Liwen Han
description: BackgroundThe traditional habitat of the Chinese medicinal plant Cistanches Herba (CH) is the deserts of northwestern China. Recently, CH cultivation has been introduced to saline-alkali land (SAL) in the Yellow River delta region. However, the effects of this SAL environment on the accumulation of secondary metabolites in CH remain unclear.

title: Ceramide kinase/ceramide 1-phosphate signaling regulates LC3B expression and autophagosome formation
creator: Hideki Funou, Natsuka Arai, Shimon Nakajima, Ryo Kadowaki, Kenta Nakamaura, Miaki Uzu, Takuya Honda, Hiroyuki Nakamura
description: Ceramide kinase (CerK) generates ceramide 1-phosphate (C1P), a bioactive sphingolipid involved in diverse cellular responses, but its role in autophagy is not fully understood. Here, we examined whether the CerK/C1P pathway regulates LC3B expression and autophagosome formation in HeLa cells. Proteomics analysis of cerebellum from Cerk-KO mice identified reduced levels of multiple autophagy-related proteins.

title: A pragmatic workflow for handling missing PROM data in registry studies: a methodological scoping review and simulated worked example
creator: Johan Eriksson
description: BackgroundPatient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) are increasingly integrated into clinical quality registries. Registry-based PROM data frequently exhibit structural non-response, including patients who never return PROMs (“never-responders”), and longitudinal attrition, making missing-not-at-random (MNAR) mechanisms plausible. Although MNAR sensitivity methods such as delta adjustment and tipping-point analysis are methodologically well-described, their uptake in registry-PROM practice is unknown.

title: Delayed and selective bone health assessment following cancer diagnosis: a real-world gap in survivorship care
creator: Vanessa Rouach, Ziv Versano, Meital Sasson, Yona Greenman, Arnon Makori
description: BackgroundCancer treatment–induced bone loss (CTIBL) is well-recognized in hormone-sensitive malignancies such as breast and prostate cancer but is less consistently implemented in patients with other solid tumors and hematologic malignancies. Furthermore, the long-term skeletal effects of newer systemic therapies, including immune checkpoint inhibitors and targeted agents, remain incompletely characterized.

title: Φ-Space ST: A platform-agnostic method to identify cell states in spatial transcriptomics studies
creator: Jiadong Mao, Jarny Choi, Kim-Anh Lê Cao
description: SummaryWe introduce Φ-Space ST, a platform-agnostic method to identify continuous cell states in spatial transcriptomics (ST) data using multiple scRNA-seq references. For ST with supercellular resolution, Φ-Space ST achieves interpretable cell-type deconvolution with significantly faster computation. For subcellular resolution, Φ-Space ST annotates cell states without cell segmentation, leading to highly insightful spatial niche identification.

title: Association Between Electronic Health Record–Based Nursing Workload and Turnover: Retrospective Cohort Study
creator: Linlin Xia, Daphne Lew, Lindsay Tessmer, Elise Eiden, Sunny Lou, Thomas Kannampallil, Elizabeth Borycki
description: BackgroundNurse turnover remains a major challenge for health systems, yet objective, scalable measures of workload that predict turnover are limited. Electronic health record (EHR) audit logs offer a potential data source to quantify nursing work patterns.ObjectiveThis study aimed to evaluate the association between EHR-derived measures of nursing workload and turnover among inpatient nurses.

title: Artificial intelligent computing of hybrid nano suspension for enhanced thermal mechanism in Jeffery Hamel configuration
creator: Adnan, Ali Khwaldeh, Mohamed Arbi Khlifi, Ahmed Najat Ahmed, Ayele Tulu, Taoufik Saidani, Muhammad Nasir Bashir, Sana Ullah Saqib
description: Nanofluids have potential role in the heat transfer enhancement for engineering applications. These fluids together with physical controls change the dynamics of flow inside oblique channel. Thus, this work focuses on the organization of hybrid model using dissipation function and enhanced properties nanoparticles (NiZnFe2O4, and MnZnFe2O4).

title: Cambio de paradigma en las curas paliativas modernas: necesidad de un enfoque multidimensional
creator: Maria Prats Orvay, Ana Lozano
description: a a la Pregunta Sorpresa negativa (PS-) y que, aun así, presentaron necesidades paliativas. Con este resultado no se cuestiona el valor de la pregunta como herramienta clínica, sino que se evidencian sus limitaciones y la necesidad de interpretarla dentro de una valoración más amplia, siempre por parte de un equipo de profesionales entrenados.

title: Multi-Omics Dataset of Heat Stress-Induced Memory in Arabidopsis
creator: Venkatesh P Thirumalaikumar, Liang Yu, Devender Arora, Umrah Mubeen, Andrew Wiszniewski, Dirk Walther, Patrick Giavalisco, Saleh Alseekh, Andrew D L Nelson, Aleksandra Skirycz, Salma Balazadeh
description: In their natural environment, plants experience temperature fluctuations, including intensified heat waves driven by climate change, which pose significant threats to their productivity. To adapt, plants have evolved diverse mechanisms to withstand heat stress (HS), minimizing potential damage and ensuring survival.

title: Seasonal vaccine-induced immunity shows preserved cross-reactivity to H3N2 subclade K in adults
creator: Adria Wilson, Brian Lerman, Reima Ramsamooj, Jacob Mischka, Jordan Ehrenhaus, Ashley Aracena, Yusuf Figueroa, Keith Farrugia, Ana S. Gonzalez-Reiche, Jessica Nardulli, Zain Khalil, Charles Gleason, Eniko Hermann, Komal Srivastava, Emilia Mia Sordillo, Harm van Bakel, Anass Abbad, Florian Krammer, Vi
description: SummaryBackgroundInfluenza A subclade K viruses caused high infection rates in the 2025/2026 Northern Hemisphere season, raising concerns about antigenic drift and reduced vaccine effectiveness.MethodsWe measured antibody responses in matched human pre- and post-vaccination sera, selected from two observational cohort studies of adults, against both a vaccine-like as well as subclade K isolates.

title: Author Correction: SESAME-catalyzed H3T11 phosphorylation inhibits Dot1-catalyzed H3K79me3 to regulate autophagy and telomere silencing
creator: Fei He, Qi Yu, Min Wang, Rongsha Wang, Xuanyunjing Gong, Feng Ge, Xilan Yu, Shanshan Li
description: t; in Fig. 6l and associated Source Data, data for the 16K-Replicate 3 were inadvertent duplicates of 25K-Replicate 3 data; in Supplementary Fig. 8c and associated Source Data, data for UBA2 and FAR3 from Replicate 3 were inadvertently duplicated into Replicate 2. For comparison, the original figures are available as Supplementary Information accompanying this amendment.

title: Emerging Role of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitors in Aortic Stenosis
creator: Piotr Mazur, Magdalena Kopytek, Joanna Natorska
description: Central Illustration Aortic stenosis (AS) is the most prevalent valvular heart disease in the Western world, and its incidence continues to rise with population aging. The disease is characterized by progressive fibrocalcific remodeling of the aortic valve (AV) and chronic pressure overload of the left ventricle (LV), resulting from outflow obstruction.

title: Dopamine amplifies subthalamic long-latency responses to cortical stimulation in patients with Parkinson’s disease
creator: Jean-Christin Beyer, Alessia Cavallo, Jojo Vanhoecke, Richard M. Köhler, Bassam Al-Fatly, Gerd-Helge Schneider, Katharina Faust, Gregor A. Brandt, Andrea A. Kühn, Wolf-Julian Neumann
description: The cortico-subthalamic hyperdirect pathway provides a rapid route for cortical influence over basal ganglia processing and is a key target of deep brain stimulation (DBS) in Parkinson’s disease (PD). However, to what degree dopamine modulates signal transmission along this pathway in humans remains unclear.

title: Long-term outcomes and treatment response in early-stage invasive lobular carcinoma: insights from a nationwide population-based study☆
creator: G Nader-Marta, L Ameye, D Martins-Branco, R Salgado, N Van Damme, J Verbeeck, P Aftimos, L Buisseret, M Paesmans, C Molinelli, EL Mayer, M Lambertini, K Van Baelen, C Desmedt, M Piccart, E de Azambuja
description: BackgroundInvasive lobular carcinoma (ILC), the second most common breast cancer subtype, differs from invasive breast carcinoma of no special type (BC-NST) in biology, presentation, and treatment response. Evidence on its prognostic impact remains inconsistent.Patients and methodsOur nationwide, population-based study of stage I-III breast cancer diagnosed in Belgium (2008-2014) compared characteristics, treatment patterns, and overall survival (OS) between ILC and BC-NST.

title: Lateral transpetrosal approaches for brainstem cavernous malformations: tailoring the operative trajectory according to lesion location. Illustrative cases
creator: Kazumi Ohmori, Taku Takeuchi, Shiduka Kamiyoshi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The authors propose a surgical strategy for the resection of lateral brainstem cavernous malformations (BSCMs) and demonstrate how the surgical corridor should be tailored according to lesion location.OBSERVATIONSThree consecutive patients with lateral BSCMs underwent microsurgical resection through transpetrosal approaches.

title: Spontaneous pneumorrhachis in adolescents: illustrative case
creator: Umika Paul, Constance Mietus, Brooke Honzel, Stephen Gutting
description: BACKGROUNDSpontaneous pneumorrhachis, defined as the presence of air in the spinal canal without trauma or iatrogenic intervention, is rare in adolescents. The clinical course remains anecdotal, and no standardized management guidelines exist. The authors performed the first systematic review focused on adolescent spontaneous pneumorrhachis and describe an illustrative case.

title: Prevalence and Predictors of Self-Reported Adverse Experiences in Digital Meditation Training: 2 Randomized Controlled Trials
creator: Polina Beloborodova, Lillian M Smith, Kevin M Riordan, Otto Simonsson, Lilah T Dottori, Helen Q Song, Nicholas S Shashko, Raquel Tatar, Scott A Baldwin, Amit Bernstein, John D Dunne, Richard J Davidson, Matthew J Hirshberg, Simon B Goldberg, John Torous
description: BackgroundDigital meditation-based interventions (MBIs) reach vast global audiences with millions of active users, yet concerns persist about the frequency and nature of adverse experiences (ie, AExs) occurring during meditation training. Some researchers have argued that AExs are substantially underdetected and reflect iatrogenic harm caused by meditation (ie, adverse effects [AEfs]).

title: Suprasellar hemangioblastoma during pregnancy: illustrative case
creator: Patrick Toyota, Michael McKenzie, Jason R. Shewchuk, Ryojo Akagami, Peter Gooderham, Stephen Yip, Peter W. Schutz
description: BACKGROUNDHemangioblastoma is a benign tumor that typically occurs in the posterior fossa but may be found anywhere along the neuroaxis. Its growth behavior may be difficult to predict, and pregnancy has been discussed as a possible growth-promoting factor.OBSERVATIONSThe authors report the case of a rare suprasellar apparently sporadic hemangioblastoma diagnosed during pregnancy.

title: Main Recommendations for Developing Education and Awareness Strategies for Rare Diseases: Scoping Review
creator: Diego Bettiol Yamada, Tatiana Takahasi Komoto, Vinícius Costa Lima, Julio Souza, Michele de Souza Seixas, Victor Cassão, Victor Evangelista de Faria Ferraz, Bibiana Mello de Oliveira, Têmis Maria Félix, Domingos Alves
description: BackgroundAccording to the World Health Organization, education and awareness are essential components of public health promotion strategies. In the context of rare diseases (RDs), these actions are particularly critical because of persistent stigma, fragmented knowledge, and the frequent absence of consolidated clinical and organizational protocols.

title: Skull infarction and chronic subdural exudates in a pediatric patient with sickle cell anemia: illustrative case
creator: Thach-Vu Nguyen, Sarah Silva, Kevin T Kim, Maureen Rakovec, Jordan R Saadon, Steven K Yarmoska, Regina Macatangay, Noushin Yahyavi-Firouz- Abadi, Whitney E Parker
description: BACKGROUNDSkull infarction is a rare sickle cell disease (SCD) complication. While epidural hematomas from calvarial infarction have been sporadically reported, subdural collections and sterile exudates mimicking intracranial empyema remain poorly characterized.OBSERVATIONSA 6-year-old boy with nonverbal autism and SCD presented with progressive periorbital swelling, fever, and extremity pain. CT raised concern for orbital cellulitis, subperiosteal abscess, and subdural empyema.

title: Generative AI for Personalized Learning Platforms in Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery Education: Scoping Review
creator: Jiang-Tao Zhong, Zai-Zai Cao, Shui-Hong Zhou, Stefano Brini
description: BackgroundGenerative AI, including large language models (LLMs), may enable personalized learning in medical education. In otolaryngology–head and neck surgery (ear, nose, and throat [ENT]) education, AI may support knowledge retrieval, adaptive assessment, feedback, and scalable learning, but evidence remains fragmented.

title: Uncovering the Experiences of Basti-Dwelling Adolescent Girls Who Menstruate in Hyderabad, India: Protocol for a Multimethod Critical Qualitative Study
creator: Snigdha Velugu, Erica Di Ruggiero, Nanda Kishore Kannuri, Anushka Ataullahjan, Amy Schwartz
description: BackgroundRapid urbanization in India is straining the government’s capacity to provide basic amenities such as housing, sanitation, electricity, and water. One group of people who are deeply affected are adolescent girls who menstruate. In urban slums, referred to as bastis in Telugu and Hindi, this reality is worsened by spatial congestion and limited water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) resources.

title: A High‐Current‐Tolerant Multimetallic Phosphide Electrode for Alkaline Water Electrolysis Toward Industrial Conditions
creator: Yang Li, Chunling Lu, Biao Wang, Dongchao Qiu, Bingbing Niu, Tao Feng
description: The development of electrocatalysts that maintain high efficiency and durability at industrial current densities remains a pivotal challenge for alkaline water electrolysis. Here, we present a high‐performance phosphide‐modified multimetallic hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) catalyst, NiFe0.33RuOx@P, with high‐current‐tolerant and low noble‐metal content.

title: Detection of Pathological Voice Samples Using a Text-to-Speech–Inspired Approach With Multiple Model Architectures: Method Development and Comparative Evaluation Study
creator: Marie Sophie Walter, Muhittin Demir, Mattias Heinrich, Felix Nensa, Stephan Lang, Nadia Sadok, René Hosch, Andrew Coristine
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundVoice disorders are common, yet access to timely specialist assessment is often limited. Automated analysis of short voice recordings may support early screening, but achieving robust performance on heterogeneous clinical datasets remains challenging.ObjectiveThis study aims to investigate the impact of synthetic speech augmentation on voice disorder recognition and classification using the Saarbrücken Voice Database (SVD) and to develop an adaptive ensemble with learnable weighting and optional sex embedding.MethodsSentence recordings from the SVD were used for binary voice disorder recognition (VDR, n=1988) and

title: Mechanical Activation of Piezo1 Drives Osteoarthritis Through Kdm5c‐Mediated Epigenetic Silencing
creator: Tianyou Kan, Xuran Li, Han Wang, Lin Sun, Yao Wang, Jiangdong Wu, Junqi Cui, Yiqi Yang, Kai Yuan, Linyang Chu, Liao Wang, Hanjun Li, Mengning Yan, Zhifeng Yu
description: Mechanical stress is the most important factor affecting the progression of osteoarthritis (OA), but the mechanism linking mechanical stress to transcriptional repression remains elusive. Here, the study finds that mechanical stress induced epigenetic changes that can serve as therapeutic targets for osteoarthritis.

title: Integrating Large Language Models and Metaverse-Related Technologies in Urology Education: Viewpoint
creator: Peizhe Li, Huijie Gong, Heyang Liu, Siyu Han, Yiqin Lu, Yongji Yan, Taiane de Azevedo Cardoso
description: Urology education must prepare learners to integrate anatomical visualization, diagnostic reasoning, technical performance, communication, and ethical judgment, often under restricted working hours and limited access to high-fidelity cases. This viewpoint argues that large language models (LLMs) and metaverse-related technologies should be integrated as complementary, supervised educational tools rather than treated as autonomous replacements for educators or clinical experience.

title: Hemoglobin's α‐Helix‐to‐β‐Sheet Transition Enables Targeted mRNA Delivery to the Lung
creator: Xihua Liu, Saiya Li, Guodong Wu, Shuangjian Li, Long Shuang Huang, Xiaoyang Li, Yiguo Zhao, Wei Lu, Cuixia Sun, Qin Cao, Yapeng Fang, Yiping Cao
description: Effective treatment of pulmonary diseases remains constrained by the scarcity of delivery systems capable of selective tissue targeting. Herein, we report a lung‐targeting platform created through the structural repurposing of hemoglobin (Hb). Acidic heating enables a conformational shift of Hb from α‐helix to β‐sheet, leading to its self‐assembly into fibrils (HbFs).

title: The New Gravity: How Generative AI Remapped Innovation and What Academia Must Do Next
creator: Hossein Akbarialiabad, Ayman Grada, Sancy A Leachman, David Rhew, Alireza Haghighi
description: Artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping clinical research, diagnostics, health system operations, and medical education. Frontier generative AI development is increasingly concentrated in private industry, whose computational infrastructure, proprietary datasets, and capital exceed those of most academic institutions. Although not designed exclusively for medicine, these systems increasingly influence clinical applications.

title: Bridged h‐BN Nanosheets Coatings: Simultaneous Shielding Atomic‐Oxygen Irradiation and Achieving Superior Friction Performance
creator: Zhuoyi Li, Changning Bai, Xingkai Zhang, Yusheng Liang, Wei Wu, Dingrui Zhou, Tao Du, Chunjin Wang
description: To confront extreme space environments, a combination of inorganic and organic coatings can provide a pathway for offering highly durable radiation resistance and anti‐friction simultaneously. Herein, a strong interfacial 3D hydrogen‐bonding network is designed to create robust hexagonal boron nitride (h‐BN) based polymer coatings with excellent mechanical and friction performance after atomic oxygen (AO) irradiation.

title: Embodied Intelligence Applications in Health Care Populations: Scoping Review
creator: Wan Shu, Ying Zhou, Erhong Sun, Lei Deng, Xuchun Ye
description: BackgroundEmbodied intelligence—artificial intelligence instantiated in physical or virtual bodies that can perceive, communicate, and interact with users and their environments—has been increasingly applied in health care. However, the evidence base remains fragmented because of inconsistent terminology, diverse embodiment forms, and limited synthesis of application domains, target populations, care settings, acceptability, and effectiveness.

title: Increase in 6-pentyl-alpha-pyrone production by Trichoderma spp. in liquid medium using in situ removal by adsorbent resin
creator: Alex Maan, Eirian Jones, John Hampton, Travis Glare, Artemio Mendoza-Mendoza
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The Trichoderma-produced secondary metabolite 6-pentyl-alpha-pyrone (6-PP) has demonstrated promise for agricultural applications, but cost-effective bioproduction remains limited by product inhibition during fermentation. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of media type on 6-PP production in T. atroviride IMI206040, screen production by nine New Zealand Trichoderma strains, and assess Amberlite XAD-4 in situ product removal in five strains to overcome self-inhibition.

title: Resistance mapping in mesoscopic films of low dimensional materials
creator: Nicolò Galizia, Rafael Luque Merino, Yigit Sozen, J. J. Riquelme, Riccardo Frisenda, Andres Castellanos-Gomez
description: We present a low-cost, scalable technique for mapping local electrical properties across large areas with micrometer-scale lateral resolution. The method utilizes a flexible polymer cantilever coated by microfabricated graphite electrodes to probe local surface resistance. Samples can be scanned on a motorized translation stage, enabling automated, spatially resolved electrical measurements over centimeter-scale regions.

title: An injectable, leadless bioelectronic interface for battery-free wireless peripheral neuromodulation
creator: Mohamed Elsherif, Salma Mansour, Zhansaya Makhambetova, Fotoon Aldhanhani, Batoul Khlaifat, Mahmoud Elbeh, Vega Pradana Rachim, Sohmyung Ha, Hicham Abada, Juan S. Barajas-Gamboa, Carlos M. Abril Vega, Khalil B. Ramadi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Injectable bioelectronics offer a minimally invasive approach to peripheral nerve stimulation but remain limited by onboard energy storage and fragile leads. Here, we present SEED, a leadless, battery-free bioelectronic interface engineered for percutaneous delivery through a standard 14-gauge needle.
