creator: Percina Chirinda, Llorenç Quintó, Corssino Tchavana, Augusto Messa, Arsénio Nhacolo, Sozinho Acacio, Tacilta Nhampossa, Quique Bassat, Goitom G Weldegebriel, Jacqueline E Tate, Umesh Parashar, Jason M Mwenda, Filomena Manjate, Inacio Mandomando
description: BackgroundDiarrhoea remains a major cause of death in children under five, despite the global decline in hospitalisations following the widespread introduction of rotavirus vaccines . As rotavirus-associated disease declines, it is important to identify other diarrhoea associated pathogens, although post-vaccine data remain limited in Mozambique.

title: Meeting clinicians where they are through signal-guided AI innovation
creator: Benjamin Rader, Ryan D Nagy, Heather L Nelson, Peter C Laussen, John S Brownstein
description: stitutional channels.1 2 This is not a governance issue alone; the tools clinicians independently adopt can reveal where existing systems are failing to deliver adequate clinical workflow support. We argue for signal-guided innovation: treating organic clinician behaviour as a leading indicator of where artificial intelligence (AI) can have impact.

title: When pupillometry indices disagree: does QPi add prognostic information beyond NPi?
creator: Li-Xia Xu
description: exposure. These findings support the authors’ conclusion that the two indices should not be considered interchangeable. However, an important clinical question remains: when NPi and QPi disagree, does QPi provide additional prognostic information, or does the disagreement primarily reflect differences in measurement susceptibility? The distinction matters because association with outcome and incremental clinical information are not equivalent.

title: Circannual pattern of milk crude protein and urea nitrogen and their relationship in Holstein cows in Swiss grassland-based dairy systems over a 30-year period
creator: Jedidiah Yi Lin Ong, Usman Arshad, Mutian Niu
description: Graphical AbstractSummary: The objectives of this study were to characterize circannual variations in milk crude protein (CP) and milk urea nitrogen (MUN) and to evaluate their relationship in Holstein cows managed under grassland-based dairy systems using a large national dataset. Historical milk recording data of 2.

title: Outdoor cycling competence and balance control in older adults – cross-sectional analysis of the BiPerAge trial
creator: Jana Rogler, Sebastian Krumpoch, Ellen Freiberger, Noam Margalit, Roee Zehavi, Itshak Melzer, Sharon Barak, Amir Shapiro, Dikla Judchak Amir, Shira Levi, Omri Lubovsky, Robert Kob
description: BackgroundAlthough cycling offers numerous health benefits, age-related functional decline can increase the risk of accidents. Identifying balance components linked to outdoor cycling competence could inform targeted assessment and training. We aimed to exploratorily investigate the association between outdoor cycling competence and static, dynamic, and reactive balance control in older adults.

title: The Morphological and Mechanistic Impact of an Investment Procedure on Coronary Chronic Total Occlusions
creator: Anja Øksnes, Akiko Maehara, Britt Engan, Vibeke Juliebø, Kalaivani Mahadevan, Kais Hyasat, Damien Collison, James Spratt, Ajay J Kirtane, Milada C Hagen, Svein Rotevatn, Tone Norekvål, Øyvind Bleie, Margaret B McEntegart
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundDuring chronic total occlusion (CTO) percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), a modification procedure is often performed after failure. Although this has been reported to improve subsequent procedural success, the anatomical impact and mechanism of benefit have never been systematically studied. The Invest-CTO study investigated whether a strategy of a planned 2-stage CTO PCI with upfront “investment” and staged “completion” procedure could improve procedural success and safety in high-risk CTO anatomy.

title: Scaling of dimensions and concentrations of plastics in two Dutch rivers
creator: Jasmijn Polinder, Frank P. L. Collas, Félix P. Leiva, Stephanie B. Oswald, Margriet M. Schoor, Wilco C. E. P. Verberk, A. Jan Hendriks
description: Plastic pollution raised great environmental concerns due to its persistence and widespread presence. To model ecological impacts, such as ingestion by wildlife, information on the abundance and dimensions of plastic particles is fundamental. Our study examined the relationships between size dimensions (length, area, circumference) of individual particles and the length of particles, their concentration, and cumulative surface area.

title: Fat matters: paraspinal muscle quality is associated with electromyographic fatigability and endurance in lumbar spinal stenosis
creator: David Koch, Corina Nüesch, Gerold Müller, Peter Stauffert, Annegret Mündermann, Alice Caimi, Dominika Ignasiak, Stefan Schären, Stephen J Ferguson, Hans-Joachim Wilke, Cordula Netzer
description: HIGHLIGHTS•Paraspinal muscle fat fraction predicted electromyographic fatigability.•Fat fraction predicted fatigability independent of age, sex, BMI and endurance.•Greater fat fraction was associated with lower trunk extension endurance.•Quantitative imaging and bilateral EMG enabled level- and side-specific assessment.•Muscle quality mattered more than quantity for electromyographic fatigability.

title: Comparable efficacy of extraoral and intraoral photobiomodulation in preventing oral mucositis during high-dose methotrexate therapy in pediatric oncology: A single-blind randomized controlled trial
creator: Isabela de Oliveira Plugge Freitas, Isabela Schuartz, Giovanna Leal Klein Renz, Rafael Zancan Mobile, Mariana Lena Sassi França, Mara Albonei Dudeque Pianovski, Laurindo Moacir Sassi, Melissa Rodrigues de Araujo
description: PurposeThis prospective randomized controlled clinical study compared intraoral (IO) and extraoral (EO) photobiomodulation (PBM) for the prevention of chemotherapy-induced oral mucositis (OM) in pediatric oncology patients.MethodsA total of 155 patients (1–18 years), receiving high-dose methotrexate (HDMTX) for leukemia, lymphoma, or osteosarcoma, were randomized to PBM-IO (n = 73) or PBM-EO (n = 82).

title: Diagnostic and operative challenge of a giant non-pancreatic intra-abdominal pseudocyst: a rare case report
creator: Om Jhaveri, Katie Scott, Joseph Galloway
description: BackgroundLarge, non-pancreatic pseudocysts are rare pathologies that present as lesions in the intra-abdominal wall or peritoneal cavity. These cases can be diagnostically difficult, particularly in situations where fine-needle aspiration yields nonspecific cytology and imaging is also often nonspecific and nondiagnostic.

title: Perivascular spaces are associated with T cell trafficking and may have prognostic relevance in brain metastases
creator: Claudia Maletzki, Eva Michaelis, Sae-Yeon Won, Artem Refaelian, Thomas Freitag, Thomas M Freiman, Julia Onken, David Wasilewski, Peter Vajkoczy, Jawed Nawabi, Nico Noah Martin, Annette Zimpfer, Daniel Cantré, Florian Gessler, Daniel Dubinski
description: BackgroundPerivascular structures, in particular, perivascular spaces (PVS) are emerging key immune modulators in the tumor microenvironment. However, their relationship with immune infiltration, vascular remodeling, and clinical outcomes in brain metastases is unclear.MethodsIn this retrospective two-center study, we analyzed 56 brain metastases. Perivascular spaces were graded on preoperatively T2-weighted MRI in the basal ganglia and centrum semiovale.

title: Comprehensive chemical and bioactive investigation of Chinese peony flower: a case of valorization of by-products as a new food ingredient from Chinese herb
creator: Meng-ling Peng, Ming-Jiong Gong, Jing Zhang, Anastassiya V. Gadetskaya, Qian-Wen Liang, Pei-Wen He, Xiao-Hui Qiu, Zhi-Hai Huang, Wen Xu
description: IntroductionIn the present study, the flower of Chinese peony (CPF), major waste by-product of Chinese Herb Radix paeoniae, was comprehensively investigated for the first time.MethodsA validated UHPLC Orbitrap Mass spectrometry combined a three-levels characterization strategy were used to analyze CPF samples from four representative cultivars. The anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities were analyzed using RAW264.

title: Molecular mechanisms of NLR proteins in inflammasome activation
creator: Yichao Liu, Kexin Ji, Liman Zhang
description: Nucleotide-binding domain and leucine-rich repeat-containing proteins (NLRs) are central mediators of inflammasome signaling, activating caspase-1 to drive pyroptotic cell death and pro-inflammatory responses. Although NLR activation is generally thought to involve conformational rearrangements that oligomerize their N- or C-terminal death domains to nucleate ASC or pro-caspase-1 oligomerization, the molecular mechanisms that enable these transitions vary substantially among family members.

title: Calculation of a conversion factor for estimating the glycolytic contribution in exercise from post-exercise blood lactate concentration
creator: David W. Hill, John Michael Mihalek
description: Purpose: Often, the glycolytic contribution in a bout of heavy or severe intensity exercise is estimated by multiplying the increase in blood lactate concentration above resting levels that is engendered by the exercise (in mM) by 3.3 (or 3) mL·kg−1 per mM.

title: Author Correction: Climate heterogeneity enhances macroclimate data-driven vegetation modeling on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
creator: Yanlong Guan, Wenqing Wu, Mengxi He, Huaikai Weng, Delong Li, Xiaoxun Huang, Deliang Chen, Shungui Zhou, Eduardo Eiji Maeda

The equations are now amended in the HTML and PDF versions of the article.

title: RET inhibition overcomes resistance to combined CDK4/6 inhibitor and endocrine therapy in ER+ breast cancer
creator: Charlotte K. Kindt, Sidse Ehmsen, Sofie Traynor, Benedetta Policastro, Nikoline Nissen, Mie K. Jakobsen, Monique F. Hundebøl, Lene E. Johansen, Martin Bak, Elsa Arbajian, Johan Staaf, Henrik J. Ditzel, Carla L. Alves
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundCombined CDK4/6 inhibitor (CDK4/6i) and endocrine therapy significantly improve the outcome of patients with advanced estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer. However, resistance to this treatment and disease progression remains a major clinical challenge.

title: The digital bioeconomy: microbiomes as a stress test for global digital sequence information governance
creator: Pierre-Mathieu Pélissier, Indré Karciauskaité, Tanja Kostic, Emmanuelle Maguin, Angela Sessitsch, Kosuke Shiraishi
description: Digital sequence information governance has entered a high-stakes implementation era. The Convention on Biological Diversity’s ‘Cali Fund’ is operationalised as the financial engine of its multilateral mechanism (MLM), with similar frameworks under negotiation across other international ocean and agricultural treaties. However, because microorganisms and their functional clusters transcend national borders, traditional bilateral mechanisms are difficult to implement.

title: Writing direction and language activation affect how Arabic-English bilingual speakers map time onto space
creator: Juana Park, Christina L. Gagné, Thomas L. Spalding
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). We investigated whether writing direction and language activation influence how bilingual speakers map time onto space. More specifically, we investigated how Arabic-English bilingual speakers conceived where (e.g., on the left or on the right) different time periods (e.g., past, present, future) were located, depending on whether they were tested in Arabic (a language that is written from right to left) or in English (a language that is written from left to right).

title: Implementing a professional youth mentoring program during times of crisis: lessons from the global pandemic
creator: Koren G. Hanson, A. Karryn Satchell, Martie L. Skinner, J. Mark Eddy
description: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted traditional youth mentoring practices as social distancing limited in-person interactions. This study analyzes how Friends of the Children (FOTC), a professional mentoring program, was able to maintain engagement with mentees during the pandemic. Using a sample of 112 youth (58% Black/African American) with an average age of 12.

title: Randomized controlled trials of mind–body interventions for posttraumatic stress disorder: a systematic review
creator: Josh Kaplan, Vanessa C. Somohano, Belle Zaccari, Maya E. O’Neil
description: Mind–body interventions (MBIs) include mindfulness-based interventions (MiBIs), meditation- and mantra-based interventions (MMIs), and movement-based interventions (MoBIs). These approaches have demonstrated preliminary efficacy in improving posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms. However, previous systematic reviews and meta-analyses have noted that this area of research is limited by inadequate comparator conditions, heterogeneity of measurement, and absence of objective outcome measures.

title: Multiple eccrine hidrocystomas on the bilateral forearms
creator: Kassidy Leibowitz, Candice E. Brem, Margaret S. Lee
description: Involvement of extra-facial sites, including the chest, axilla, and neck, have been reported but remain uncommon.3 We report a case of multiple eccrine hidrocystomas presenting as dermal nodules on the bilateral volar forearms in a young patient, an unusual clinical distribution for this entity.

title: Human targeting of morphologically unique fishes amplifies the risk of functional erosion
creator: Pierre Bouchet, Sébastien Brosse, Aurèle Toussaint
description: Human societies are drawing on wild species for food, fuel, medicines, and recreation. Yet, it remains unclear whether different types of human use target species with common or unique ecological roles. Here we show that humans use a fourth (26%) of the freshwater fish species and these species occupy almost half (45.2%) of the global spectrum of fish morphological diversity.

title: Author Correction: BRAHMA represses STOP1-NRT1.1 module to control plant rhizosphere alkalization and acid stress adaptation
creator: Jia Yuan Ye, Wen Hao Tian, De Rui Zhang, Qian Yi Yu, Ji Ming Xu, Wo Na Ding, Gui Xin Li, Jing Ying Yan, Chong Wei Jin, Moussa Benhamed, Shao Jian Zheng, Zhong Jie Ding

For Figs. 4c and 4d and Supplementary Fig. 14, in several cases, average values were inadvertently duplicated and pasted into cells that should have been empty due to data exclusions.

title: Predicting trail-making test performance using 7-Tesla structural cerebral MRI
creator: Gereon J Schnellbächer, Ravichandran Rajkumar, Tanja Veselinović, Shukti Ramkiran, Jana Hagen, Maria Collee, N Jon Shah, Irene Neuner, Jürgen Dammers
description: Psychopharmaceutical therapy has seen a lack of improvement in efficacy, highlighting the need for a more individualized treatment approach that optimally leverages pharmaceutical effects. To achieve this, it is necessary to identify factors that can predict psychological attributes and treatment outcomes. We hypothesize that brain morphology may serve as a predictor of performance in psychological tests.

title: Utilizing the Nursing Professional Development Model to create and sustain nursing education aimed at improving the care of patients with Parkinson’s Disease in the hospital
creator: Mary Bobek, Pamela Pascarelli, Lisa Cocoziello, Hooman Azmi
description: The Nurse Professional Development Model (NPD) has been utilized to improve quality of care for several conditions. Patients with Parkinson’s Disease (PD) are susceptible to higher risks while in the hospital. Educational efforts for this patient population are challenged by the small, disbursed number of patients as well as increased turn-over and reliance on temporary nursing staff.

title: Engineered Muscle Tissue Analysis of Irisin Protection Against Glucocorticoid- and Cancer Cachexia-Induced Muscle Wasting and Cardiotoxicity
creator: Young Hoon Son, Christina Y Sheng, Ji-Eun Jeong, Yuri Choi, Hyocheol Jung, Jihee Won, Audrey Atinsky, Junbeom Park, Jin Chul Kim, Keel Yong Lee, Young Il Park, Sung-Jin Park
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Muscle atrophy, a condition characterized by an imbalance between protein synthesis and degradation, leads to skeletal muscle wasting, exacerbating disease progression and increasing mortality rates. Exercise has been shown to counteract muscle wasting, with myokines—exercise-induced secretome proteins, and among them, irisin is known to mediate systemic benefits such as improved metabolism, reduction of oxidative stress, and promotion of tissue repair in skeletal muscle, thereby mediating beneficial effects of exercise against atrophy.

title: Abdominal functional electrical stimulation and binder to reduce orthostatic hypotension in individuals with a subacute spinal cord injury
creator: Chiettha Prajnadewie, Lynn Blecher, Keith MD McNaughton, Claire L Boswell-Ruys, Billy L Luu, Harrison T Finn, Elizabeth A Bye, Bonsan B Lee, Jane E Butler, Anne E Palermo, Euan J McCaughey
description: Study designRepeated measures comparative study.ObjectivesCompare acute effects of 4 treatment conditions: (i) abdominal binder (Binder), (ii) abdominal functional electrical stimulation (AFES), (iii) AFES and binder (AFES-Binder), and (iv) no intervention (Control), on signs of orthostatic hypotension (OH) and blood pressure (BP) maintenance in individuals with acute and subacute spinal cord injury (SCI).SettingSpinal injury inpatient ward.

title: Reply to “Methodological Concerns in ‘Prognostic Usefulness of Clinical Complete Response after PD-1 Inhibitor-Based Combination Therapy for Unresectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma’”
creator: Da-Long Yang, Jian-Li Huang, Hong-Gui Qin, Liang Ma, Jian-Hong Zhong, on behalf of the GUIDANCE Investigators
description: we believe will strengthen the interpretation of our findings. First, in our study, all patients with chronic hepatitis B/C infection received routine oral antiviral therapy [3, 4]. As this was a retrospective analysis, we did not adjust for antiviral therapy in the multivariable models because it was uniformly administered to all eligible patients.

title: Multiply recurrent pituitary apoplexy treated nonsurgically: illustrative case
creator: Alexander P. Landry, Maíra Cristina Velho, Luma Ghalib, Daniel M. Prevedello
description: BACKGROUNDPituitary apoplexy is rare clinical entity resulting from hemorrhage or infarction of a pituitary tumor, typically presenting with headaches, endocrinopathy, and variable neurological manifestations. Recurrent apoplexy, particularly multiply recurrent cases, is exceedingly rare and associated with clinical equipoise in many cases.

title: Treating depression in Muslim communities: Meta-analysis of three trials of culturally adapted behavioural activation for Muslims (BA-M)
creator: Ghazala Mir, Robert West, Evrim Anik, Shaista Meer, Saima Dawood, Nazish Habib, Jamal Magantor, Paulette Henry, Jamal Magantor
description: Faith-sensitive depression therapies address a core aspect of cultural values but are not specifically promoted within global mental health policy. This study evaluated a culturally adapted Behavioural Activation intervention for Muslim patients (BA-M) compared with standard treatments across diverse settings.

title: Basic Bronchoscopy Competence Achieved During a One-Day Workshop for a Multidisciplinary Critical Care Team: A simulation-based study
creator: B Jayakrishnan, Saif Musabah Al-Mubaihsi, Hasan Al-Sayegh, Ahmed Zaher Al-Abri, Issa Saif AlQarshoubi, Jehan Al-Abri, Sami M Bennji
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryObjectives:Fibreoptic bronchoscopy has become a key procedure in critical care, transitioning from pulmonologists to intensivists. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a one-day simulation-based training programme in acquiring basic bronchoscopy skills.Methods:A one-day workshop was conducted at Sultan Qaboos Comprehensive Cancer Care and Research Centre, University Medical City, Muscat, Oman, in October 2024 with didactic lectures, small group skill stations, virtual bronchoscopy simulations and hands-on training using manikins and a novel, cost-effective, 3D-printed airway model.

title: AI-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems in Primary Care: Systematic Review of Clinical Implementation
creator: Florian Naye, Steven Ouellet, Farzaneh Yousefi, Chloé Cachinho, Frédéric Bergeron, Onil Bhattacharyya, Vess Stamenova, Maxime Sasseville
description: BackgroundAI-based clinical decision support systems (AI-CDSSs) can help primary care clinicians provide higher quality care amid rising case complexity and resource constraints. However, evidence regarding their effectiveness and safety in primary care practice is lacking.ObjectiveWe synthesized evidence on the effectiveness and safety of AI-CDSSs compared with usual care or non–AI-based systems in primary care settings.

title: Physiological Responses, Exercise Intensity, and Enjoyment During Ring Fit Adventure in Adults With Chronic Diseases: Single-Arm, Pre-Post Experimental Study
creator: Muhammad Jazimin Haron, Shiek Abdullah Ismail, Gilbert Tian Seng Yeo, Ivan Steenstra
description: BackgroundPhysical inactivity and insufficient muscle-strengthening exercise remain important public health concerns among adults with chronic diseases. Active video games may offer an accessible way to support exercise participation, but many may not provide sufficient exercise intensity to produce meaningful physiological responses. Ring Fit Adventure (RFA) is an active video game that combines aerobic and resistance-based exercise.

title: A preliminary study of the immunogenic response of plant-derived multi-epitopic peptide vaccine candidate of Mycoplasma gallisepticum in chickens
creator: Susithra Priyadarhni Mugunthan, Divyadharshini Venkatesan, Chandramohan Govindasamy, Dhivya Selvaraj, Harish Mani Chandra
description: Mycoplasma gallisepticum (MG) is responsible for chronic respiratory disease in avian species, characterized by symptoms like respiratory rales and coughing. Existing vaccines for MG have limited efficacy and require multiple doses. Certain MG cytoadherence proteins (GapA, CrmA, PlpA, and Hlp3) play a crucial role in the pathogen’s respiratory tract colonization and infection.

title: Effect of Alloying and Phase Segregation on the Stability of High-Entropy Alloys: A Case Study on the Dissolution of Os–Ru–Rh–Ir–Pt Nanoparticles
creator: Tatiana Priamushko, Rebecca K. Pittkowski, Maria Minichova, Attila Kormányos, Valentin Briega-Martos, Luis A. Cipriano, Nicolas Schlegel, Rasmus Rohde, Espen D. Bøjesen, Kirsten M. Ø. Jensen, Jan Rossmeisl, Matthias Arenz, Serhiy Cherevko
description: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) have emerged as a class of promising electrocatalysts for energy-conversion reactions. In addition to catalytic activity, stability under the reaction conditions is paramount for practical applications. Understanding the dissolution behavior of these multimetallic, complex nanomaterials is therefore essential.

title: Screening and surveillance of esophageal cancer by magnifying endoscopy with narrow band imaging improves the survival of hypopharyngeal cancer patients
creator: Chen-Shuan Chung, Chia-Yun Wu, Yu-Hsuan Lin, Wu-Chia Lo, Ping-Chia Cheng, Wan-Lun Hsu, Li-Jen Liao
description: IntroductionPatients with head and neck cancer may develop a second primary neoplasm (SPN) of the esophagus due to field cancerization. This study investigated the impacts of esophageal cancer screening using magnifying endoscopy with narrow-band imaging (ME-NBI) on the outcomes of hypopharyngeal cancer patients.MethodsPatients with hypopharyngeal cancer diagnosed from 2008 to 2021 in a tertiary hospital were reviewed retrospectively.

title: Clinical, Economic, and System-Level Outcomes of Bariatric Surgery in Adults: Protocol for a Systematic Review
creator: Michał Bystram, Marlena Robakowska, Monika Proczko-Stepaniak, Javad Sarvestan
description: BackgroundObesity affects approximately 880 million adults worldwide and carries substantial health, economic, and social consequences. Although bariatric surgery achieves sustained weight loss and metabolic improvement, existing systematic reviews largely predate 2020 and rarely integrate clinical, economic, and system-level perspectives within a single synthesis.

title: From signal to bedside: the missing link between ECG-AI explainability and clinical trust
creator: Akinchan Bhardwaj, Ishita Vasudev, Pushkala Jayaraman
description: t attribution techniques exhibit limited reliability and should be used with caution in high-stakes clinical settings. While these conclusions are well-supported, an additional critical dimension warrants further discussion because it was not fully addressed in the study. The gap identified by Arends et al.

title: Metal Hypersensitivity Reactions Following Spinal Implants
creator: Joseph Abbo, Jacob Thomas, Christian Stipho, Erik Nakken, Rakesh Patel, Joshua D. Piche, IIyas Aleem
description: Background:Metal hypersensitivity reactions are infrequently reported but clinically significant after spinal implant surgery. Clinical presentation can mimic infection or mechanical failure, making diagnosis difficult. Evidence to guide diagnosis and management is largely limited to short case series and case reports.

title: Initiation phase cellular reprogramming ameliorates DNA damage in the ERCC1 mouse model of premature aging
creator: Patrick Treat Paine, Cheyenne Rechsteiner, Francesco Morandini, Gabriela Desdín-Micó, Calida Mrabti, Alberto Parras, Amin Haghani, Robert Brooke, Steve Horvath, Andrei Seluanov, Vera Gorbunova, Alejandro Ocampo
description: Unlike aged somatic cells, which exhibit a decline in molecular fidelity and eventually reach a state of replicative senescence, pluripotent stem cells can indefinitely replenish themselves while retaining full homeostatic capacity. The conferment of beneficial-pluripotency related traits via in vivo partial cellular reprogramming in vivo partial reprogramming significantly extends lifespan and restores aging phenotypes in mouse models.

title: Integrative Network Pharmacology Analysis of Gut Microbial Metabolite–Mediated Gut–Eye Axis Regulation in Major Blinding Retinal Diseases
creator: Bin Wei, Jingfen Zhang, Yichong Duan, Na Cheng, Xiaorong Wu
description: ObjectiveTo systematically investigate the shared and disease-specific mechanisms by which gut microbial metabolites may regulate age-related macular degeneration (AMD), diabetic retinopathy (DR), and retinal vein occlusion (RVO) through a network pharmacology framework.DesignBioinformatics-based network pharmacology study.SubjectsPublicly available gut microbial metabolite, metabolite-target, and disease-associated gene data sets related to AMD, DR, and RVO were analyzed.

title: Clinical Effectiveness of AI-Based Cardiac Arrest Prediction System for General Ward Patients (VITAL-MD): Protocol for a Multicenter Pragmatic Stepped Wedge Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial
creator: Mincheol Kim, Kyung Hoon Kim, Minsoo Kim, Sun Jung Kwon, Myung Soo Park, Ah Jin Kim, Man-Jong Lee, Mi Hwa Park, Hyung Keun Cha, Minhyeok Lee, In Beom Jeong, Soon Joo Wang, Sung Bak An, Jeen Hwa Lee, Kyung-Jae Cho, Jinhui Jang, HyoJin Jeong, Yoon Young Lee, Woori Han, VITAL-MD Study Group, Jung Soo K
description: BackgroundIn-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) remains a frequent and devastating event, and conventional early warning scores (EWSs) coupled with rapid response systems (RRSs) have shown inconsistent effects on patient-centered outcomes, largely owing to limited predictive accuracy and high false-alarm burden. AI-based EWSs (AI-EWSs) have demonstrated superior discrimination retrospectively, but high-quality prospective evidence in true external validation environments remains scarce.

title: Retrospective CBCT-based anatomical assessment of mandibular first and second molars: a cross-sectional study with potential implications for immediate implant planning
creator: Badr Othman
description: Immediate implant placement in mandibular molar sockets can shorten treatment and reduce the number of surgical interventions, but the anatomy of the posterior mandible may limit implant positioning and increase surgical risk. This study evaluated six cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)-derived anatomical parameters in mandibular first and second molars.

title: Large language model derived regular expressions for sleep phenotyping from electronic health record: a feasibility study
creator: Nathanael Hwang, M Brandon Westover, Diego R Mazzotti, Robert J Thomas, Lynn Marie Trotti, Dennis Hwang, Matt Gratton, Jiaxiao Shi, Rui Yan, Emmanuel Mignot, Gari D Clifford, Umakanth A Katwa, Kendra A Becker, Matthew T Klimper, Jessica K Jara, Haoqi Sun
description: Study ObjectivesLarge language models may efficiently develop Regular Expression (regex)-based natural language processing for electronic health record phenotyping. We present PromptNLP to assess feasibility by evaluating performance and generalizability to clinical notes across multiple institutions.MethodsSleep-related clinical notes from Kaiser Permanente Southern California, Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, and Emory University were used to extract apnea-hypopnea index and Epworth Sleepiness Scale.

title: Curcumin-coated anodized titanium surfaces for enhanced in vitro cytocompatibility and early osteogenic activity
creator: Nandita Suresh, Nebu G. Thomas, Matti Mauramo, Tuomas Waltimo, Timo Sorsa, Sukumaran Anil
description: ObjectiveTo characterize a carrier-free curcumin coating applied by dip-coating to acid-etched and anodized Ti-6Al-4 V (Cur-Ti) and to compare its in vitro cytocompatibility and early osteogenic activity, measured as total alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity, with those of a sol-gel hydroxyapatite coating (HA-Ti) prepared on the same substrate and of uncoated anodized titanium.

title: Correction to: Comprehensive Genomic Analysis in Hereditary Adrenal and Extra- Adrenal Paragangliomas
creator: Helia Purnaghshband, Elif Tuzlali, Kamalika Bhandari Deka, Jeffrey P Bruce, Kirsten M Farncombe, Brittany Gillies, Stephenie D Prokopec, Trevor Pugh, Sarah Redmond, Laura Redondo, Hong Wang, Shereen Ezzat, Ozgur Mete, Raymond H Kim
