title: Emergency surgery for blunt abdominal trauma in polytrauma – the impact of time to laparotomy on outcomes
creator: Gianmaria Rausch, Yannik Kalbas, Sascha Halvachizadeh, Jonin Zumsteg, Alba Shehu, Ester Mikova, Kuno Lehmann, Ladislav Mica, Roman Pfeifer, Hans-Christoph Pape, Valentin Neuhaus, Felix Karl-Ludwig Klingebiel, Michel Paul Johan Teuben
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeBlunt abdominal trauma (BAT) is common in polytrauma patients. Emergency surgery is required for haemodynamically significant solid organ injury and intra-abdominal hollow organ injury. The effect of time to surgery on outcomes in patients requiring emergency laparotomy remains uncertain.Materials & methodsAdult polytrauma patients (ISS > 16) who underwent emergency laparotomy for blunt abdominal trauma between 1996 and 2020 from a trauma registry of a single level one trauma centre were included.

title: Patterns and Drivers of Sustainable Agricultural Practice Adoption Among Mennonite Farmers in a Closed Endorheic Basin of Northern Mexico
creator: Emmanuel Yeboah Okyere, Jesus Manuel Ochoa-Rivero, Mercedes Borja-Bravo, John Amoah-Nuamah, Omar Castor Ponce-Garcia, Sergio Arellano-Arciniega, Hugo A. Gutiérrez-Jurado
description: Agricultural sustainability in closed endorheic basins is constrained by periodic water scarcity, hydrological isolation, and the cumulative effects of intensive land use. The Cuauhtémoc region of northern Mexico hosts long-established Mennonite farming communities whose mechanized and irrigation-dependent agriculture constitutes an important component of the regional economy and resource-use system.

title: Fabrication of a Maxillary Prosthesis for a Flap-Reconstructed Maxillary Defect Using a 3D-Printed Occlusal Record Base
creator: Mariko Hattori, Manjin Zhang, Yuka Sumita, Noriyuki Wakabayashi
description: The fabrication of maxillary prostheses in patients with flap-reconstructed maxillary defects continues to present both clinical and technical challenges. Conventional impression techniques can be hazardous and often require multiple adjustments. This report presents a simplified digital approach using 3D scan data of an existing, well-adjusted prosthesis.

title: Prevalence and determinants of probable dementia in rural India: a cross-sectional study in the APCAPS cohort
creator: Jagannadha Rao Basa, Kanokporn Pinyopornpanish, Poppy AC Mallinson, Papangkorn Inkeaw, Kanokwan Kulprachakarn, Judith Lieber, Santosh Kumar Banjara, Hemant Mahajan, Teena Dasi, Santhi Bhogadi, Srivalli Addanki, Gowri Iyer, Anoop SV Shah, Om Kurmi, Sureshkumar Kamalakannan, Sanjay Kinra, Chaisiri Ang
description: BackgroundDementia poses a growing public health challenge in India. Despite this, epidemiological data on the condition remain largely restricted to adults >60 years of age, despite the convergence of urbanisation-driven cardiometabolic risks and socioeconomic disadvantage in rural India potentially accelerating dementia onset.

title: Morphological Profile of Facial Acne Scars and Their Correlation With Body Image Concern and Scar-Specific Quality of Life: A Cross-Sectional Study From Rural India
creator: Jayaprakash M H, Mukunda R Swaroop, Vinay H R, Yogesh Devaraj, Rahul H V, Jithin Jayaraj, Harshavardhan M, Nisarga Yoganand, Esha Nobbay, Divyasree R
description: IntroductionAcne scarring represents a permanent structural sequela of acne vulgaris and is predominantly characterized by atrophic morphological patterns. Beyond cosmetic disfigurement, facial acne scars may contribute to significant psychosocial distress, including body image disturbance and quality-of-life impairment. Limited data are available correlating scar morphology with body image concerns and scar-specific quality-of-life impairment in the Indian population.

title: Evaluating COPD care assistance: a comparative study of ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4.0, and ERNIE bot performance
creator: Zhongshang Dai, Zihang Zeng, Zijie Zhan, Yan Chen
description: BackgroundLarge language model (LLM) chatbots are increasingly used to provide health information, yet their reliability in addressing chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) care questions in the Chinese context remains unclear. To evaluate and compare the performance of three publicly available LLM chatbots – ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4.

title: Cytotoxic Lesions of the Corpus Callosum: A Single-Center Case Series of Eight Patients With an Emphasis on Infectious Etiologies
creator: Takeshi Yamashita, Kai Saito, Fukuko Matsumoto, Katsuyuki Yoshida, Michiko Adachi Matsuzawa, Hidenori Sanayama, Tamami Watanabe, Takahiko Fukuchi
description: Background and aimCytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum (CLOCCs) are transient lesions characterized by restricted diffusion on MRI and are associated with various infectious and noninfectious conditions. However, the clinical spectrum of infection-related CLOCCs, particularly those associated with bacterial infections, remains incompletely defined.

title: Cost-effectiveness of monotherapy and combination therapy for myopia control in Chinese children
creator: Jinghui Wang, Xuan Li, Meinan He, Desheng Song, Bo Zhang, Bei Du, Ruihua Wei
description: BackgroundMyopia poses a major public health and economic burden in China, necessitating cost-effectiveness evaluations of control strategies. We aimed to assess cost-effectiveness of single/combined myopia control in children and adolescents to optimise strategies.MethodsWe conducted a network meta-analysis to evaluate the efficacy of myopia control interventions in Chinese children (aged 6–18 years).

title: Migration Intent Among Early-Career Doctors in Pakistan: A Cross-Sectional Study of Influencing Factors at a Tertiary Care Hospital
creator: Sadia Rehman, Shaikh Muhammad Owais Saeed, Muhammad Irfan Khattak, Hammad Ali, Gohar Awais, Sakina Shah Perver, Sania Nisar, Sana Younas
description: Objective: The objective of this study is to assess the prevalence of migration intent among interns and residents at a tertiary care institution in Pakistan and to identify perception-based factors associated with this intent.Methodology: A cross-sectional study was conducted at PNS Shifa Hospital using a structured, self-administered Google Form questionnaire (Google Inc., Mountain View, CA, USA).

title: Syntaxin11 deficiency inhibits CRAC channel priming to suppress cytotoxicity and gene expression in T lymphocytes independent of membrane trafficking
creator: Sritama Datta, Abhikarsh Gupta, Kunal M Jagetiya, Resmi Bera, Vikas R Tiwari, Megumi Yamashita, Atharva R Yande, Abdul Rishad, Vishal Malik, Sreejith Raran-Kurussi, Sandra Ammann, Mohammad Shahrooei, Kalyaneswar Mandal, Ramanathan Sowdhamini, Murali Prakriya, Adish Dani, Monika Vig, Kenton J Swartz,
description: Mutations in Syntaxin11 (STX11), a Q-SNARE, result in a fatal immune disorder known as familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis 4 (FHLH4) in human patients. A key diagnostic feature of FHLH4 is defective T and natural killer cell cytotoxicity. Here, we show that STX11 directly binds and regulates Orai1, the pore-forming subunit of calcium release-activated calcium (CRAC) channels.

title: Rasch Analysis of the Composite Autonomic Symptom Score-31 (COMPASS-31) Using Data From Chronic Pain Patients
creator: Wim Tuinebreijer, Henk Koning
description: Background: Patients with pain experience autonomic symptoms that are assessed using the patient-reported outcome measure known as the Composite Autonomic Symptom Score-31 (COMPASS-31).Objectives: This study aimed to analyze the Dutch version of the COMPASS-31 using Rasch analysis.Methods: Sixty-two patients completed the Dutch version of the COMPASS-31.

title: Plasma calprotectin as infection biomarker in hip fracture patients: a prospective cohort study
creator: Helmi-Sisko PYRHÖNEN, Johan THAM, Anna STEFÁNSDÓTTIR, Alicia PERSSON, Linnea MALMGREN, Cecilia ROGMARK
description: Background and purposeWe aimed to compare the diagnostic performance of plasma calprotectin in detecting infections following hip fracture surgery with 3 other biomarkers: procalcitonin (PCT), C-reactive protein (CRP), and white blood cell (WBC) count.MethodsThis prospective cohort study included surgically treated hip fracture patients aged ≥ 65 years, admitted to our department from April 2023 to August 2024.

title: Higher tissue concentrations of cefuroxime achieved with preoperative stand-alone intraosseous regional prophylaxis in robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty: a randomized controlled trial
creator: Te Liu, Heng Zhang, Ming Guo, Runkai Zhao, Ye Tao, Zhuo Zhang, Guoqiang Zhang, Jun Fu, Ming Ni
description: BackgroundIntraosseous regional administration (IORA) of antibiotics can achieve higher local tissue concentrations than intravenous administration in conventional total knee arthroplasty (TKA). This study aimed to evaluate the tissue concentration and systemic concentration of preoperative stand-alone intraosseous cefuroxime in robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (RA-TKA) and identify a candidate dose for further evaluation.

title: Case report: Pemigatinib-induced retinopathy: a serial examination of subretinal fluid secondary to an FGFR inhibitor
creator: Daniel Barmas-Alamdari, George Jiao, Ronni Lieberman
description: BackgroundModern chemotherapeutic agents continue to evolve as modern monoclonal antibody treatments are designed to directly target proteins, enzymes, and focal loci. A particular class of these medications, fibroblast growth factor (FGFR) inhibitors, specifically pemigatinib (Pemazyre®; Incyte), has been approved by the US Food and Drug Administration since April 2020 for the treatment of advanced or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma.

title: Prognostic Value of Plasma N-terminal Pro-B-Type Natriuretic Peptide (Nt-proBNP) Levels in Patients Presenting With Cardiac Arrhythmias to the Emergency Department: A Prospective Observational Study From India
creator: Shiwangini Jaiswal, Amit Rohila, Ankur Sharma, Mahaveer Singh Rodha, Rahul Choudhary, Bharat Choudhary, Siddhi Chawla
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Introduction and rationale: N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), a key marker of cardiac stress, is widely used in heart failure care. However, its role in patients presenting to the Emergency Department (ED) with cardiac arrhythmias remains underexplored.Aims and objectives: To evaluate the prognostic significance of plasma NT-proBNP levels in patients presenting to the ED with cardiac arrhythmias and to assess their clinical profile.Methodology: A prospective observational study was conducted over 18 months, from September 2023 to December 2024, with data analysis performed

title: Determinants of outcome in atrial functional tricuspid regurgitation
creator: Jawza Aldakhil, Kush Patel, Sveeta Badiani, Steffen E Petersen, Guy Lloyd, Sanjeev Bhattacharyya
description: BackgroundAtrial functional tricuspid regurgitation (AFTR) is increasingly recognized as a result of atrial remodelling in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). However, prognostic predictors in this population remain incompletely defined.ObjectivesTo evaluate echocardiographic characteristics and identify predictors of all-cause mortality in patients with AFTR.MethodsWe retrospectively studied consecutive patients with AF who underwent transthoracic echocardiography between 2017 and 2025.

title: Recurrent epithelioid trophoblastic tumor with complete response after surgery, chemotherapy, and immunotherapy: A case report and literature review
creator: Lingting Meng, Bin Yang, Jiaqi Ma, Juan Zhang, Lei Lei, Ye Hong, Xiaojun Hu
description: Background:Epithelioid trophoblastic tumor (ETT) is the rarest form of gestational trophoblastic neoplasm, accounting for 1.39–2% of gestational trophoblastic diseases. Its clinical behavior and pathogenesis remain poorly understood, and no standardized treatment guidelines currently exist, with surgery considered the most important therapeutic option. Emerging modalities, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, are under investigation.

title: Canine diabetes mellitus demonstrates multiple markers of chronic inflammation including Th40 cell increases and elevated systemic-immune inflammation index, consistent with autoimmune dysregulation
creator: Gisela Vaitaitis, Tracy Webb, Craig Webb, Christina Sharkey, Steve Sharkey, Dan Waid, David H. Wagner
description: IntroductionCanine diabetes mellitus (CDM) is a relatively common endocrine disease in dogs. Many CDM clinical features resemble human type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM), but lack of autoimmune biomarkers makes calling the disease autoimmune controversial. Autoimmune biomarkers linking CDM and T1DM would create an alternative model for drug development impacting both human and canine disease.

title: Agentic artificial intelligence in medicine and biomedical research: A primer and framework for clinicians and researchers
creator: Jonathan Kantor
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). oals through multistep processes rather than simply generating an isolated output in response to a single prompt—suggests that this next phase of AI implementation represents an escalation from revolution to true regime change. Agentic systems can plan tasks, use tools, retrieve information, monitor intermediate results, revise their approaches, loop, and execute complex iterative workflows with minimal (or no) human oversight (Table I).

title: Coping during socio-political uncertainty
creator: Myriam El Khoury-Malhame, Sandrella Bou Malhab, Roni Chaaya, Michel Sfeir, Samar El Khoury
description: IntroductionWell-being of young adults is known to be compromised in times of significant changes, such as economic and political turmoil. This study focuses on university students in Lebanon during one of the most prominent social unrests of its modern history to determine potential understudied protective factors that would predict the youth capacity to strive.

title: Endothelial exosomes remodel chromatin accessibility and superenhancer in cancer cells to promote liver metastatic colonization
creator: Bei Jin, Shenglan Liu, Hongke Huang, Luo Yang, Dong Wei, Wei Dai, Jingfeng Zhou, Yun Wang, Ping Zhang, Qianyun Ye, Jingxuan Pan
description: Liver-organotropic metastasis occurs in cancers such as uveal melanoma (UM) and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and is a leading cause of mortality at the terminal stage. Colonization is a rate-limiting and converging step in the metastatic cascade. The drivers underlying liver colonization have largely remained elusive.

title: Multi-level evidence of titanium dioxide nanoparticle toxicity in blueberry plantlets
creator: Viktor Husak, Ulyana Kilchytska, Ivan Myroniuk, Ihor Mykytyn, Volodymyr Lushchak, Alois Bilavcik, Olena Bobrova
description: Titanium dioxide nanoparticles (TiO2NPs) are increasingly proposed for agricultural applications; however, their crop-specific safety profiles remain insufficiently understood. Here, we provide, to our knowledge, the first integrative evidence that TiO2NPs exert predominantly negative effects on blueberry (Vaccinium corymbosum L.), a high-value woody perennial.

title: Multi-UAV simultaneous target assignment and path planning based on deep reinforcement learning in dynamic multiple obstacles environments
creator: Xiaoran Kong, Yatong Zhou, Zhe Li, Shaohai Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Target assignment and path planning are crucial for the cooperativity of multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) systems. However, it is a challenge considering the dynamics of environments and the partial observability of UAVs. In this article, the problem of multi-UAV target assignment and path planning is formulated as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP), and a novel deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based algorithm is proposed to address it.

title: The CYP4/20-HETE/GPR75 axis in the progression of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatosis liver disease (MASLD) to chronic liver disease
creator: James P. Hardwick, Byoung-Joon Song, Paul Rote, Charles Leahy, Yoon Kwang Lee, Alexandra Rudi Wolf, Danielle Diegisser, Victor Garcia
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionMetabolic-dysfunction-associated steatosis liver disease (MASLD) is a progressive liver disease from simple steatosis, steatohepatitis, fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. Chronic liver diseases (CLDs) can lead to portal hypertension, which is a major cause of complications of cirrhosis. CLDs cause structural alterations across the liver through increased contents of extracellular matrix (ECM), driving dysfunction of liver sinusoidal endothelial cells (LSECs) alongside hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) and activated resident or infiltrating immune cells. Bioactive arachidonic metabolites have diverse roles in the progression of MASLD.

title: Impact of p53 mutations on the synergistic effects of metformin and radiation on colorectal cancer cells
creator: Kyoko Sakamoto, Koji Okabayashi, Yujin Kato, Kaoru Hattori, Satoru Morita, Kohei Shigeta, Yuko Kitagawa
description: BackgroundMetformin has been reported to be effective as an adjunctive therapy in cancer treatment. In this study, the synergistic effects of metformin and radiotherapy were investigated in colorectal cancer cell lines and colorectal cancer organoids, as were the underlying mechanisms.MethodsThis was an experimental study conducted in vitro.

title: Nationwide Survey of Antimicrobial Stewardship in Korean Hospitals: Insights From the Early Stage of the 2024 National Pilot Implementation
creator: Sung Min Lim, Raeseok Lee, Se Yoon Park, Jinnam Kim, Ji Young Park, Choseok Yoon, Song Mi Moon, Yong Chan Kim, Hong Bin Kim, Myung Jin Lee, Bongyoung Kim
description: BackgroundAntimicrobial stewardship programmes (ASPs) are essential for optimising antibiotic use and mitigating antimicrobial resistance. In Korea, antimicrobial consumption exceeds the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development average, and ASP activities remain fragmented, particularly in smaller hospitals. In November 2024, the National Health Insurance Service introduced a pilot reimbursement scheme to support ASPs in hospitals with ≥ 300 beds.

title: Contrast-enhanced mammography in low- and middle-income countries: opportunities and challenges
creator: Hafiza Qurat Ul Ain, Muhammad Junaid Tahir, Khabab Abbasher Hussien Mohamed Ahmed, Waleed Tariq, Aamer Iftikhar
description: ]. Contrast-enhanced mammography (CEM) has emerged as a promising imaging technique that combines anatomical and functional assessment, offering a significant advantage, especially in resource-limited settings. Its role in LMICs should be interpreted with caution, as these settings are highly heterogeneous[1,3]. In this context, Pakistan is presented as a representative case study, but the feasibility and scalability of CEM are context-dependent.

title: Comparative the efficacy and safety of Gosuranemab, Semorinemab, Tilavonemab, and Zagotenemab in patients with Alzheimer’s disease: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
creator: Wenting Cai, Hui Zhang, Yan Wu, Yao Yao, Jinping Zhang
description: ObjectiveThe aim of this study was to compare the efficacy and safety of anti-tau protein monoclonal antibodies for Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Tau protein aggregation, a key pathological feature of AD, is closely associated with neurodegeneration and cognitive decline. Targeting tau protein has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy.

title: Itaconate as the endogenous brake of proinflammatory macrophage activation alleviates inflammation in liver fibrogenesis
creator: Kai Zhang, Tong Li, Wenhui Liu, Weiyang Li, Lin Yang, Na Chang, Liying Li
description: Background:Liver inflammation and fibrosis are reparative responses to chronic liver injury. Bone marrow–derived monocyte/macrophages (BMDMs) are key participants. Our previous study demonstrated that BMDM can be activated as a proinflammatory phenotype by sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P). Aconitate decarboxylase 1 (ACOD1)/itaconate is an anti-inflammatory molecule. However, it remains unclear whether ACOD1/itaconate is involved in S1P-induced BMDM activation.

title: Incorporating exosomes in tissue engineering scaffolds: pave the way toward clinical application
creator: Jiahui Zheng, Anqi Wang, Jingzhi Wang, Hui Ma, Caining Wen, Yuanmin Zhang
description: In recent years, the use of endosome-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) in regenerative therapies and tissue repair has attracted much attention. However, local or systemic injection of the free state of extracellular vesicles at the site of action is rapidly cleared and lacks a controlled release mechanism.

title: Effects of the GnRH agonist leuprorelin on liver volume in premenopausal women with severe polycystic liver disease
creator: Inge G Wijbenga, Renee Duijzer, Paul Geertsema, Sophie E Aapkes, Thomas Bais, Lianne A Messchendorp, Priya Vart, Robbert J de Haas, Marjan van den Berg, Hans Blokzijl, Astrid EP Cantineau, Maatje DA van Gastel, Joost PH Drenth, DrenthRon T Gansevoort
description: Background:Polycystic liver disease (PLD) is characterized by multiple liver cysts, sometimes leading to severe liver enlargement, with associated physical and psychosocial complaints. Treatment options are limited. Female gender is a risk factor for PLD; estrogen supplementation increases liver size in women with PLD, whereas the polycystic liver decreases after menopause. Estrogens may therefore be a target for therapy.

title: In silico characterisation of the avocado WAK/WAKL gene family with a focus on genes involved in defence against Phytophthora cinnamomi
creator: Aaron Harvey, Noëlani van den Berg, Velushka Swart
description: The avocado industry faces a significant threat from the hemibiotrophic oomycete pathogen Phytophthora cinnamomi. A variably expressed defence gene during an avocado infection trial was a Wall-associated kinase (WAK). WAK and WAK-Like (WAKL) proteins are known to bind to fragmented pectin (oligogalacturonides) produced during pathogen penetration, thereby activating downstream defence-related pathways. To better understand the P.

title: Multimodal quantitative ultrasound assessment of perioperative neck muscle alterations in patients with cervical spondylosis
creator: Rongchen Wang, Xinyi Tang, Yuanjiao Tang, Li Qiu
description: BackgroundCervical spondylosis (CS) involves degenerative changes that increase muscle fatigue and stiffness. Postoperative cervical collars are commonly used to maintain stability. This study used multimodal ultrasound to compare neck muscle thickness and stiffness between patients with CS and healthy controls (HC), and to longitudinally evaluate muscle parameter changes associated with different postoperative cervical collar wearing durations.

title: Salvage gastrectomy for perforated gastric intramural metastasis after definitive chemoradiotherapy for distal esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: a case report
creator: Jirat Leelapatanadit, Sawanya Sangthong, Rawat Waratchanont, Wichitra Asanprakit, Viriya Kaewkangsadan, Sukchai Satthaporn
description: Gastric intramural metastasis from esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is rare, and chemotherapy-associated perforation is exceptionally uncommon. We report a case of a 67-year-old man with distal ESCC and a separate cardia squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). He declined esophagectomy and received definitive chemoradiotherapy (dCRT) with paclitaxel, carboplatin, and 50.4 Gy radiotherapy.

title: Unveiling genetic basis of seedling emergence from deep soil depth under dry direct- seeded conditions in rice (Oryza sativa L.)
creator: Vagish Mishra, Shilpi Dixit, Swati Tyagi, Challa Venkateswarlu, Pronob J. Paul, Anoop Kishor Singh Gurjar, Shalabh Dixit, Nitika Sandhu, Smita Kurup, Arvind Kumar, Pallavi Sinha, Vikas Kumar Singh, Uma Maheshwar Singh
description: Water scarcity and labor shortage pose significant challenges in rice farming. Direct-seeded rice (DSR) is an efficient method that conserves water, reduces labor costs, and allows for full mechanization of cultivation. However, variable planting depth in undulated field leading to deep/shallow sowing of rice seeds during mechanical sowing presents a major hurdle, as existing varieties lack tolerance to deep sowing.

title: Factors Affecting Recollapse of the Augmented Vertebrae After Percutaneous Vertebral Augmentation: A Prospective Study
creator: Yawen Zhang, Junchuan Liu, Maoyu Zhao, Yudian Qiu, Quan Ji, Nan Min, Qiang Wang
description: ObjectiveTo investigate the relevant factors of augmented vertebrae recollapse after percutaneous vertebral augmentation (PVA) for the treatment of osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures (OVCFs).MethodA prospective study was performed on 116 patients who were diagnosed with osteoporotic compression fractures in which the anterior height loss of the vertebral body was greater than 1/3. All patients underwent percutaneous vertebral augmentation (PKP or PVP).

title: Response of bacterial community metabolites to bacterial wilt caused by Ralstonia solanacearum: a multi-omics analysis
creator: Chengjian Wei, Jinchang Liang, Rui Wang, Luping Chi, Wenjing Wang, Jun Tan, Heli Shi, Xueru Song, Zhenzhen Cui, Qiang Xie, Dejie Cheng, Xiaoqiang Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The soil microbial community plays a critical role in promoting robust plant growth and serves as an effective defence mechanism against root pathogens. Current research has focused on unravelling the compositions and functions of diverse microbial taxa in plant rhizospheres invaded by Ralstonia solanacearum, however, the specific mechanisms by which key microbial groups with distinct functions exert their effects remain unclear.

title: The Effect of Massage Therapy on Anxiety Levels Experienced by Traditional-Aged Undergraduate Business Students
creator: Jorge A. Pazmiño, Portia B. Resnick
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background:Anxiety is a prevalent concern among college students, impairing academic performance and increasing attrition risk for universities. Effective interventions are needed to reduce overall and test anxiety during high-stakes assessments.Purpose:This study explored the effect of massage therapy (MT) in reducing overall and test anxiety in traditional-aged undergraduate business students compared to a comparison group engaged in a relaxation activity (adult coloring).Setting:A private liberal arts university in the southeastern United States.Participants:Undergraduate business students (aged 18–23 years) enrolled in accounting, business administration, finance, economics,

title: Active Exsanguination Behind a Urinary Tract Infection (UTI) Diagnostic Label: A Quadruple-Hit Cardiorenal Collapse Following Ambulatory Urological Care
creator: Wutt Oo
description: We report the case of a 95-year-old man with a previous history of myocardial infarction, pulmonary oedema, and hypertension who developed recurrent collapse while undergoing ambulatory urological follow-up for a six-week history of macroscopic haematuria. Following a recent outpatient review, he had received oral antibiotics for a presumed urinary tract infection (UTI).

title: Red recombination enables a wide variety of markerless manipulation of porcine epidemic diarrhea virus genome to generate recombinant virus
creator: Shuonan Pan, Chunxiao Mou, Zhenhai Chen
description: Porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV) is a member of the genera Alphacoronavirus that has been associated with acute watery diarrhea and vomiting in swine. Unfortunately, no effective vaccines and antiviral drugs for PEDV are currently available. Reverse genetics systems are crucial tools for these researches. Here, a PEDV full-length cDNA clone was constructed.

title: Evaluation of The Spurgeon Method® as a Manual Therapy Protocol to Improve Shoulder Range of Motion and Function for Postmastectomy Patients
creator: Cynthia Veazey, Rebecca L. Wolf, Angela Zhu, Curt Bay, Sally Spurgeon, Jennifer Radziak
description: Study design:A single-group pretest–posttest interventional mixed-methods study with longitudinal follow-up.Introduction:After breast cancer surgery, women often experience reduced range of motion in the shoulder and chronic pain that negatively affect mental and physical quality of life and ability to complete daily activities.

title: Clinical Response to Upadacitinib in Treatment-Experienced Patients With Atopic Dermatitis: A Case Series From Latin America
creator: Ana B Crocker Sandoval, Yocelin N Lozano Figueroa, Ana G Perez-Romero, Alan O Muro-Davalos
description: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease that may require systemic therapy in patients with persistent disease activity or an inadequate response to previous treatments. Upadacitinib, a selective Janus kinase 1 inhibitor, has demonstrated rapid clinical efficacy in patients with moderate-to-severe AD; however, real-world data from Latin American populations remain limited.

title: Recombinant zoster vaccine immunization rate in patients on Janus kinase inhibitors for rheumatologic and dermatologic conditions
creator: Jessica B Michaud, Ruta Brazauskas, Sarah Wigfield, Shelby Shepard, Teresa Mysliwiec, Kylie Perez, Shikha Singla
description: ObjectivesPatients who receive Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors are at an increased risk of varicella zoster virus reactivation. The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the vaccination rates of recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV) for patients taking a JAK inhibitor for dermatologic or rheumatologic conditions.

title: Indigoidine and deoxyviolacein co-pigmentation in a single bacterial cell enables visual discrimination of Pb(ii) and Hg(ii) in environmental water matrices
creator: Zongjie Ma, Yan Guo, Wenjun Luo, Keyan Wei, Zhaobo Hu, Jiajun Huang, Yuting Chen, Chang-ye Hui
description: Heavy metal co-contamination of lead and mercury in aquatic environments poses escalating risks to public health and ecosystems. Conventional instrumental methods, while accurate, are ill-suited for routine on-site screening due to high costs and operational complexity. Here, we describe a dual-pigment whole-cell biosensor engineered in Escherichia coli TOP10 for simultaneous visual detection of Pb(ii) and Hg(ii).

title: Life satisfaction of Palestinian and Polish students after pandemic COVID-19
creator: Krzysztof Zdziarski, Anna Knyszyńska, Katarzyna Karakiewicz-Krawczyk, Mariam Awad, Salam Awad, Narmeen Qumsieh, Marek Landowski, Beata Karakiewicz
description: The COVID-19 pandemic has had a huge impact on the lives of all social groups around the world, including students who have had to face remote learning and isolation. Regardless of cultural, linguistic and religious differences, every young person is looking for the meaning of life and their place in the world.

title: Laser and Energy-Based Devices in Aesthetic Practice: A 10-Year Single-Surgeon Review of Treatments, Complications, and Same-Practice Surgical Crossover
creator: Carolyn Kim, Bhavana Thota, Vidhya Nadarajan, Anca Dogaroiu, Lauren Kim, Amor Niksic, Victoria Peters, Jennifer Barillas, John E Hoopman, Jeffrey M Kenkel
description: BackgroundThe use of lasers and energy-based devices in aesthetic plastic surgery has increased substantially; yet, long-term treatment patterns and their relationship to subsequent surgery remain unclear.ObjectivesTo evaluate patient demographics, device utilization patterns, complications, and same-practice surgical crossover over a 10-year single plastic surgeon's experience.

title: A comprehensive review on the role of zeolitic imidazolate frameworks (ZIFs) in facilitating catalytic transformations
creator: Kevin George, Abin Philip, Gautham Krishna K.
description: Catalysis plays an important role in modern chemistry by enabling efficient and sustainable chemical processes. Zeolitic Imidazolate Frameworks (ZIFs), a type of metal–organic framework, have gained attention because of their good stability, adjustable pore structure, and well-defined metal sites. This review focuses on ZIFs and their derived materials in three main areas: heterogeneous catalysis, electrocatalysis, and photocatalysis.

title: Effectiveness of mDiabetes intervention in enhancing diabetes awareness and promoting healthy lifestyle changes among the general population in rural India
creator: Padmaja Kumari Rani, Jachin David Williams, Nidhi Jaswal, Venkateswaralu Yandluri, Payal Sangani, Kavya Sanagavarapu, Ramya Natarajan, Sandhya Ramalingam, Nalini Saligram, Rohit C. Khanna
description: AimThis study aimed to assess the impact of a mHealth and community health education intervention on diabetes awareness and promoting healthy dietary and lifestyle habits within a rural population in Andhra Pradesh, India.MethodsUsing a quasi-experimental design, the mDiabetes program was implemented for 1 year, among 1,03,538 rural individuals.

title: Differences in category information processing between areas TEO and TE of the macaque
creator: Masaumi Shimizu, Shun Katakami, Masato Okada, Yasuko Sugase-Miyamoto, Kazuko Hayashi, Keiji Matsuda, Kenichiro Miura, Mark A. G. Eldridge, Richard C. Saunders, Barry J. Richmond, Narihisa Matsumoto
description: Object categorization is a fundamental visual function, via which primates group items based on perceptual similarity. Neurons that respond to a class of complex objects, such as faces, can be found in inferior temporal cortex of macaque monkeys, comprising areas TEO and TE.

title: Highly efficient MOF-808/polyethersulfone mixed matrix membranes for methyl orange filtration
creator: Xiao-Jing Hu, Qi-Qiang Li, Li-Jie Lin, Xiao-Hui Huang, Shao-Ming Ying
description: The development of free-standing membranes with high efficiency and robust environmental tolerance remains a key challenge in dye wastewater treatment. Herein, MOF-808-incorporated polyethersulfone (PES) mixed matrix membranes (MMMs) were fabricated for the adsorptive removal of methyl orange (MO). The optimized composite membrane (MOF@PES-2) achieved a maximum MO removal efficiency of 98%.

title: Organ preservation in rectal cancer following clinical complete response after short-course radiotherapy-based total neoadjuvant therapy
creator: Carlos G. Morales, Erik Manriquez-Alegria, Valentina Duran, Maite Gonzalez, Gonzalo Carvajal, Pamela Briones, Felipe Mena, Martin Quintana, Richard Castillo, Angelo Fulle, Manuel Cabreras, Rodrigo Kusanovich, Nicole Caire, Javier Retamales, Patricia García, Diego Muñoz-Salazar, Felipe F. Quezada-Día
description: Background and purposeOrgan preservation after total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) is feasible in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) who achieve a clinical complete response (cCR). However, most watch-and-wait (WW) evidence derives from long-course chemoradiotherapy (LCCRT), with limited data regarding short-course radiotherapy (SCRT)-based TNT. We evaluated response-adapted organ preservation following SCRT-based TNT in a public, resource-limited healthcare setting.

title: Deep learning-based echocardiography for cardiac assessment: a systematic literature review and meta-analysis
creator: Aida Romano-Martinez, Silav Zeid, Mykhailo Krolevets, Konstantin Kontohow-Beckers, Vincent ten Cate, Philipp Lurz, Sandy Engelhardt, Stefan Kramer, Sven-Oliver Troebs, Philipp S Wild
description: AimsArtificial intelligence, particularly deep learning (DL), has shown significant potential for enhancing the assessment of echocardiograms in clinical practice. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the performance of DL models and to identify factors affecting their performance.Methods and resultsA systematic review of the PubMed, CENTRAL, and Web of Science databases was conducted, yielding 16 248 potential publications.

title: 4,6-α-Glucanotransferase: An enzymatic biocatalyst for the modification of starch and starch-food systems
creator: Rana Roshanineshat, Salwa Karboune
description: The increased demand for healthier, low-calorie foods and ingredients with improved physicochemical properties has increased interest in starch modification strategies aimed at enhancing nutritional and techno-functional properties. Among these strategies, the use of a starch-converting enzyme known as 4,6-α-glucanotransferase (4,6-α-GTase) has attracted considerable attention.

title: Multilayer membranes of graphene oxide nanosheets on cellulose filter papers for high-flux water filtration and high proton conductivity
creator: Hon Nhien Le, Ngoc Quang Tran, Nang An Vu, Thi Bich Duyen Luu, Lam Nhu Pham, Thi Bang Tam Dao, Trung Do Nguyen, Chi Nhan Ha Thuc, Hieu Le Van
description: Two-dimensional graphene oxide (GO) nanosheets have emerged as multifunctional units for synthesizing nanostructured membranes for water filtration and proton transport technologies. In this research, advanced GO synthesis were conducted to produce GO dispersions at appropriate concentrations for building primary and secondary layers on cellulose filter papers (Cel).

title: The impact of SLCO1B1 polymorphisms on homocysteine concentrations: evidence for a stronger association in men
creator: Xinyuan Hu, Yanfang Jiang
description: BackgroundHomocysteine (Hcy) is a risk factor for stroke. In this study, we investigated the relationship between gene polymorphisms, particularly SLCO1B1 and homocysteine (Hcy) concentrations in ischemic stroke patients, with a focus on identifying potential risk factors for elevated Hcy levels.

title: NCAPD3-mediated ferroptosis of 2,3,5,4’-Tetrahydroxystilbene-2-O-β-D-glucoside inhibits proliferation in T47D cells
creator: Jianfen Shen, Shuo Zhang, Yan Song, Leiming Yang, Qi Huang, Pengyu Wang, Youzhi Zhang
description: ObjectiveNon-SMC condensin II complex subunit D3 (NCAPD3) has recently been demonstrated as a crucial oncogenic factor, nevertheless, the biological role of NCAPD3 in the pathogenesis of breast cancer has not been elucidated. Evidence suggests that targeting ferroptosis can inhibit the progression of breast cancer. Moreover, 2,3,5,4’-Tetrahydroxystilbene-2-O-β-D-glucoside (THSG) could modulate MCF-7 cell proliferation in our previous study.

title: Incidence and impact of intracranial complications in patients undergoing extracorporeal membrane oxygenation treatment
creator: Jan Wiefhoff, Friedrich Thomas Irmer, Felix Maximilian Gerach, Jan Rodemerk, Ramazan Jabbarli, Marvin Darkwah Oppong, Cornelius Deuschl, Börge Schmidt, Frank Herbstreit, Thorsten Brenner, Ulrich Sure, Laurèl Rauschenbach
description: IntroductionExtracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is a life-saving intervention for respiratory and/or cardiac failure but is associated with high morbidity and mortality, particularly due to intracranial complications.Research questionWhat is the incidence, type, and impact of intracranial complications in patients undergoing ECMO treatment?Material and methodsThis retrospective single-center study included ECMO patients treated at a tertiary care center between 2013 and 2023.

title: Identifying health risk determinants and molecular targets in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis via combined differential and weighted gene co-expression analysis
creator: Abu Tayab Moin, Md. Asad Ullah, Jannatul Ferdous Nipa, Mohammad Sheikh Farider Rahman, Afsana Emran, Md. Minhazul Islam, Swapnil Das, Tawsif Al Arian, Mohammad Mahfuz Enam Elahi, Mukta Akter, Umme Sadea Rahman, Arnab Halder, Shoaib Saikat, Mohammad Jakir Hosen
description: IntroductionIdiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a rare but debilitating lung disease characterized by excessive fibrotic tissue accumulation, primarily affecting individuals over 50 years of age. Early diagnosis is challenging, and without intervention, the prognosis remains poor. Understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying IPF pathogenesis is crucial for identifying diagnostic markers and therapeutic targets.

title: Andes Virus on a Cruise Ship, what it Tells us About the Global Pandemic Preparedness Agenda
creator: Marion Koopmans, Christian Brechot, Roberto Bruzzone, Moussa Moïse Diagne, Christian Drosten, Isabella Eckerle, Robert Gallo, David T.S. Hayman, Peter Horby, Peter Hotez, Menno de Jong, Florian Krammer, Jean Claude Manuguerra, Gustavo Palacios, Massimo Palmarini, Anja Schreijer, Nicole D. Tischler,
description: SummaryThe outbreak of hantavirus disease caused by Andes virus aboard a cruise ship is a reminder of the challenges posed by emerging diseases in the modern era. While Andes virus-associated disease can be particularly severe, it is unlikely to spread extensively beyond the current number of cases or emerge as a large epidemic, especially if public health measures are followed.

title: Formulation-dependent colloidal properties of redispersible lycopene nanoparticles: storage stability and enhanced in vitro bioactivity
creator: Ho Thi Oanh, Hong Tham Nguyen, Nguyen Phu Duc, Nhung Hac Thi, Dinh Dung Luong, Mai Ha Hoang
description: Lycopene is a bioactive carotenoid whose application is limited by poor aqueous dispersibility and susceptibility to degradation. Redispersible lycopene nanoparticles were prepared by solvent displacement–evaporation followed by freeze-drying, and interfacial composition and nominal lycopene fraction were evaluated sequentially. Among the tested interfacial compositions, a 2 : 1 Tween 80/phosphatidylcholine mass ratio produced the smallest particles and lowest dispersity.

title: Simulated accelerated aging controlled by temperature and humidity for regulating the quality of Citri grandis fructus immaturus
creator: Miao Su, Naiyu Xiao, Zheng Cheng, Lilan Huang, Xinye Ma, Qianbin Mo, Guojian Chen
description: Citri grandis fructus immaturus (CGFI) is well-known for its dual usage in medicine and food. After aging, it wound bring about the transformation and enrichment of its medicinal components in CGFI. The content of active ingredients including flavonoids (such as naringin and rhoifolin) would increase, making its medicinal properties milder and its taste more mellow.

title: Wearable-derived measures of stress physiology in patients with opioid use disorder treated with methadone: A stress-task study in a real-world clinic with healthy controls
creator: Tyler S. Oesterle, Yi Xiao, Nicholas L. Bormann, Dessa K. Bergen-Cico, Benjamin Lai, Harshit Sharma, Asif Salekin
description: BackgroundWearable biosensors enable real-time monitoring of physiological stress. While methadone maintenance treatment (MMT) is effective in opioid use disorder (OUD), inter-dose withdrawal and stress dysregulation remain challenges. We sought to identify wearable-derived digital biomarkers of stress in individuals with OUD receiving MMT.

title: Synthesis of halide perovskite thin films from an eutectic mixture of Pb(NO3)2, acetamide, and urea for fabricating resistive random-access memory (RRAM)
creator: Chuong Thanh Huynh, Vy Thao Ha Cao, Tai Duy Nguyen, Tung Thanh Ngo, Em Hoang Danh, Quan Phu Pham, Ngoc Kim Pham, Phuong Tuyet Nguyen
description: Methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI3) perovskite is conventionally synthesized in toxic solvents such as dimethylformamide and dimethyl sulfoxide, whose associated health and environmental risks limit large-scale and sustainable production. Building on our previous work, we further developed a synthesis route for MAPbI3 perovskite using a deep eutectic mixture composed of lead nitrate, acetamide, and urea.

title: Effect of modified atmosphere packaging on preservation property and microbial communities of golden pompano (Trachinotus ovatus) fillets during 0 °C storage
creator: Yisheng Huang, Zewei Zhang, Bin Zhang, Chang Liu, Yuzhong Zheng, Hui Zhu, Laihao Li, Wanling Lin
description: The effects of air packaging (AP) and modified atmosphere packaging 1 (MAP1) (50% CO₂/50% N₂), MAP2 (70% CO₂/30% N₂), and MAP3 (90% CO₂/10% N₂) on the preservation property of Golden Pompano Trachinotus ovatus stored at 0 °C were studied. Results demonstrated that MAP exhibited better preservation effects than AP.

title: Editorial: Industry and individuals: branding, labelling, and marketing of food products, volume II
creator: Daniel Adrian Gârdan, Paweł Bryła, Ionel Dumitru, Iuliana Petronela Gârdan
description: ronment looks rather different. Rates of obesity and diet-related noncommunicable disease continue to climb across both high- and low-income settings (2); online food retail has scaled rapidly; and the front-of-pack labeling (FOPL) debate, once largely European, is now playing out in Latin America, Africa, and Asia under quite different regulatory conditions (3, 4).

title: Precision nutrition in MASLD should incorporate metabolic and inflammatory phenotyping
creator: Anastasia Ntikoudi
description: n, as the cornerstone of management (1, 2). Evidence consistently demonstrates that the magnitude of weight loss correlates with improvement in steatohepatitis features and fibrosis regression in a subset of patients (3). Comprehensive reviews further reinforce that structured dietary modification and physical activity can improve hepatic steatosis and cardiometabolic risk parameters (4, 5).

title: Fermented garlic as a functional food strategy for malnutrition: microbial ecology, bioactive compounds, and clinical perspectives
creator: Miracle Amarachukwu Emmanuel-Fashagba, Yemisi Dorcas Obafemi, Solomon Uche Oranusi
description: Fermented garlic (Allium sativum) represents a promising functional food with potential applications as a complementary nutritional intervention for malnourished populations. Through microbial fermentation and thermal processing two mechanistically distinct pathways, garlic undergoes significant biochemical transformations that enhance the availability of bioactive compounds, including S-allyl-L-cysteine (SAC), polyphenols, and γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA), which collectively contribute to improved antioxidant capacity and gut health.

title: Universal CD7-targeted CAR T-cell therapy in T-ALL: a promising bridge to transplant, but not without caveats—a critical reappraisal
creator: Qinghua Ke, Shiqiong Zhou
description: oceed to allogeneic HSCT is not trivial for a disease with such a dismal post-relapse prognosis. However, as a clinician, I read these results with cautious skepticism rather than uncritical optimism. Based on only 11 patients and limited follow-up, the study answers some questions but raises several more pressing ones.

title: Comparative Seroprevalence of Brucella Antibodies in Apparently Healthy Sheep and Goats in a Rural District of Central Nigeria
creator: Martin Zang Pam, Alex Odoom, Charles Matthew Kakka, Fidelis Leo Latkal, Kete Clinton Waziri, Solomon Jere Dule, Suzanna Zakka Nyango, Pedung Raphael Emmanuel, Lipi Buch
description: BackgroundBrucellosis, caused by bacterial pathogens of the genus Brucella, is a chronic zoonotic disease affecting small ruminants such as sheep and goats. This study evaluated and compared the seroprevalence of Brucella antibodies among apparently healthy sheep and goats in Vwang District, Jos South Local Government Area, Plateau State, Nigeria.MethodologyA cross‐sectional study design was employed from May to June 2024.

title: Case Report: A rare case of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma with metastases to the pancreas and stomach
creator: Yuhang Lv, Yanting Jiang, Kaiyuan Hui, Xiaodong Jiang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Esophageal cancer is a highly aggressive malignancy associated with a generally poor clinical prognosis. While distant metastases are common, the metastasis of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) to the pancreas and stomach is extremely rare. We report the case of a 62-year-old male with a history of ESCC who presented with an incidentally discovered pancreatic mass on imaging 37 months after the completion of radiotherapy. The patient subsequently underwent radical surgical resection.

title: Molecular assessment of splicing variants in a cohort of patients with inborn errors of immunity: methodological approach and interpretation remarks
creator: Laura Miguel Berenguel, Carla Gianelli, Elisabet Matas Pérez, Teresa del Rosal, Ana Méndez Echevarría, Ángel Robles Marhuenda, Marta Feito Rodríguez, Maria Teresa Caballero Molina, Lorena Magallares García, Brenda Sánchez Garrido, Samantha Hita Díaz, Luis Allende Martínez, Pilar Nozal Aranda, Carmen
description: BackgroundSplicing is the molecular mechanism to produce mature messenger RNA (mRNA) before its translation into protein. It is estimated that 50% of disease-causing mutations disrupt splicing, mostly of them affecting canonical positions. However, variants occurring in coding regions or deep-intronic variants can also affect splicing. In these cases, interpretation of the results may be challenging and molecular validation is required.

title: Spatiotemporal Analysis of Molecular Continuity in Pathogenesis of Squamous Cell Carcinoma: From Normal Epithelium to Precancerous Lesions and Carcinoma
creator: Lan Lan, Xinyu Wang, Xiaoqi Jiang, Xiangyi Lin, Yancheng Lai, Wen Tan, Shaosen Zhang, Dongxin Lin, Chen Wu
description: Squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs) develop from the stratified epithelia of the esophagus, head and neck, lung, and skin, providing a tractable model to investigate how altered epithelial fields progress toward invasive cancer. Across SCC subtypes, evolution often begins before overt malignancy, with age- and exposure-associated mutant clones expanding within histologically normal epithelia.

title: Overall survival and prognostic factors of oral cavity and oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinomas in Saudi Arabia: a population-based cohort study (2000–2019)
creator: Waad R. Al-Amri, Abdullah S. Al-Swuailem
description: Oral cavity and oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinomas (OC-SCC and OP-SCC) are major contributors to head and neck cancer mortality worldwide. However, long-term population-based survival patterns that separately evaluate these subsites remain limited in Saudi Arabia. This study assessed overall survival (OS) and independent prognostic factors in a nationwide cohort diagnosed between 2000 and 2019.

title: What we know, don’t know, and need to know about patient authorship: a scoping review, evidence gap analysis, and research roadmap
creator: Karen L Woolley
description: BackgroundPatient authorship is an innovation, challenging a centuries-old medical publishing model. To guide best practices for patient authorship, a strong evidence base is required. The objectives of this research were to: (1) Identify ‘what we know’ about patient authorship via a scoping review. (2) Describe ‘what we don’t know’ about patient authorship via an evidence gap analysis.

title: Bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing data identified HMGB3 of chromatin regulators as a breast cancer biomarker associated with the cell cycle
creator: Huan Wang, Luhui Li, Dingyuan Tu, Ping Shen, Zheyao Song, Mengjiao An, Xudong Li, Qi Ji, Peng Chen, Rongjun Cui
description: BackgroundChromatin regulators (CRs) have been reported to modulate tumorigenesis and progression in multiple pathophysiological processes, but little is known about theirs role and association with the immune microenvironment in breast cancer (BRCA).MethodsThis study identified differential CRs gene expression in BRCA using transcriptome sequencing data and single-cell RNA sequencing data.

title: A tutorial on selecting, translating, and reporting variance priors in Bayesian multilevel models
creator: Liu Liu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Bayesian multilevel models are increasingly used in psychological, educational, and behavioral research, yet applied guidance on specifying priors for scalar variance components remains limited. This tutorial provides a practical workflow for identifying target variance components, selecting benchmark values, calibrating priors on variance and standard-deviation scales, translating them into software-compatible prior specifications, evaluating their implications through prior predictive checks, posterior comparison, sensitivity analysis, and transparent reporting.

title: Timing of a laparoscopic cholecystectomy in acute moderately severe to severe biliary pancreatitis
creator: Sjaak Pouwels, Omar Thaher, Dirk Bausch, Gauri Chillarge, Marcello Di Martino, Stijn van Laarhoven, Miljana Vladimirov, Suhaib JS Ahmad, Jens Hoeppner, Chetan Parmar
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). have a mild to moderate form of disease [3]. To reduce the risk of recurrent gallstone related complications, like (recurrent) pancreatitis, cholecystitis, cholangitis or gallstone colics, a timely cholecystectomy is indicated in these patients [4], [5], [6]. In the last few years, several aspects of the definitive treatment of the biliary pancreatitis (BP) have changed, based on some pivotal trials [7], [8].

title: LoCS-Net: Localizing convolutional spiking neural network for fast visual place recognition
creator: Ugur Akcal, Ivan Georgiev Raikov, Ekaterina Dmitrievna Gribkova, Anwesa Choudhuri, Seung Hyun Kim, Mattia Gazzola, Rhanor Gillette, Ivan Soltesz, Girish Chowdhary
description: Visual place recognition (VPR) is the ability to recognize locations in a physical environment based only on visual inputs. It is a challenging task due to perceptual aliasing, viewpoint and appearance variations and complexity of dynamic scenes. Despite promising demonstrations, many state-of-the-art (SOTA) VPR approaches based on artificial neural networks (ANNs) suffer from computational inefficiency.

title: A framework for multi-scale intervention modeling: virtual cohorts, virtual clinical trials, and model-to-model comparisons
creator: Christian T. Michael, Sayed Ahmad Almohri, Jennifer J. Linderman, Denise E. Kirschner
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Computational models of disease progression have been constructed for a myriad of pathologies. Typically, the conceptual implementation for pathology-related in silico intervention studies has been ad hoc and similar in design to experimental studies. We introduce a multi-scale interventional design (MID) framework toward two key goals: tracking of disease dynamics from within-body to patient to population scale; and tracking impact(s) of interventions across these same spatial scales.

title: Bibliometric analysis of ferroptosis: a comprehensive evaluation of its contribution to lung cancer
creator: Feifei Yao, Feng Guo, Chuanzhong Sun, Erdong Wang, Hang Wang, Na Li
description: ObjectivesThis study employs bibliometric analysis to track evolution and identify trends of key topics in ferroptosis within the context of lung cancer. By identifying emerging research areas, our aim is to provide valuable insights and directions for researchers in this field.

title: CMA-DTI: a cross-modal fusion and attentive interaction network for interpretable drug-target interaction prediction
creator: Chi Qin, Denggao Zheng, Ziyang Wang, Yu Li, Jingrui Cao, Houchun Qiu, Hongxing Kan, Liping Sun, Yu Liu, Jili Hu
description: BackgroundDrug–target interaction (DTI) prediction is an important task in early-stage drug discovery. Although deep learning methods have improved predictive performance, effectively integrating heterogeneous drug representations and providing interpretable evidence for local interaction patterns remain challenging.MethodsWe propose CMA-DTI, a cross-modal fusion and attentive interaction framework for DTI prediction.

title: MHD Natural convection and entropy generation of Fe3O4–MgO/water hybrid nanofluid in an inclined enclosure with flower-shaped heated fins
creator: Basma Souayeh, Najib Hdhiri
description: Controlling both the heat removal and the associated irreversibility is a central requirement in compact energy-storage and electronic-cooling systems containing multiple localized heat sources. This study presents a comprehensive numerical investigation of magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) natural convection and entropy generation in an inclined enclosure filled with a binary hybrid nanofluid composed of magnetite (Fe3O4)) and magnesium oxide (MgO) dispersed in water.

title: Discovery of direct-acting small-molecule RIG-I agonists through creation of a selective CARD activation platform
creator: Rong Guo, Kenneisha Norford, Ling Xu, Manyi Wei, Wenshuai Wang, Stephanie Halene, Anna Marie Pyle
description: Retinoic acid-inducible gene-I (RIG-I) plays a pivotal role in recognizing and combating RNA viruses in humans, and it has become a drug target of significant interest. RIG-I agonists composed of dsRNA represent antiviral and antitumor therapies, however the development of small-molecule RIG-I agonists, with their potential for improved pharmacokinetics, remains an unmet need.

title: Arabidopsis nanopore direct RNA sequencing data for mutants in splicing, polyadenylation, and m6A methylation
creator: Natalia Gumińska, Łukasz Szewc, Agnieszka Czarnocka-Cieciura, Wiktoria Orzeł, Sebastian Jeleń, Mateusz Bajczyk, Seweryn Mroczek, Andrzej Dziembowski, Artur Jarmołowski
description: Co-transcriptional RNA processing, including alternative splicing and polyadenylation, generates diverse mRNA isoforms essential for development, differentiation, and stress responses. We present Oxford Nanopore Direct RNA Sequencing (DRS) data from Arabidopsis thaliana wild-type (Col-0) plants and mutants defective in RNA processing pathways, including polyadenylation, RNA methylation, and pre-mRNA splicing. We obtained full-length reads together with native poly(A) tail information.

title: The spatial buildup of nonlinear compression in the cochlea
creator: Kostas Kondylidis, Anna Vavakou, Marcel van der Heijden
description: In the mammalian cochlea, the transduction from vibrations to inner hair cell receptor currents is preceded by a stage of mechanical pre-processing that involves a rapid, strongly nonlinear compression. The mechanisms by which the cochlea realizes this dynamic compression are still poorly understood.

title: Enhanced electrochemical performance of eco-friendly Cr-doped ZnO/RGO nanocomposites for pioneering supercapacitor applications
creator: Faiqa Arshad, Sammia Shahid, Sana Mansoor, Momna Qayyum, Mohsin Javed, Ayesha Khadim, Syed Kashif Ali, Ali Bahadur, Shahid Iqbal, Sajid Mahmood, Meznah M. Alanazi, Shaimaa A. M. Abdelmohsen
description: Herein, a straightforward, and mild synthetic co-precipitation method is used to prepare Cr-ZnO/RGO nanocomposite to be used in supercapacitor applications. First, the chromium (Cr) doping concentration in zinc oxide (ZnO) nanoparticles was systematically varied (2, 4, 6, 8, and 10%) to evaluate its influence on the electrochemical performance.

title: Focusing and weighing microanalytes in liquid enabled by higher-order piezoelectric resonant membranes
creator: Jingui Qian, Wenqi Fan, Sheng Tang, Cheng Guo, Xiangyang Wang, Mengyu Huang, Guoqiang Wu, Joshua E.-Y. Lee
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Micro-electromechanical-system (MEMS) resonators have been recognized as powerful tools for precision mass detection. However, achieving both flexible on-chip capture of microanalytes and high-sensitivity liquid-phase sensing remains a technical challenge. We present a fully anchored multi-modal piezoelectric resonant membrane (PRM) that utilizes self-excited bulk acoustic waves to rapidly enrich sparsely dispersed microparticles within milliliter droplets and precisely locate them at the region of highest vibrational amplitude — the most sensitive area for resonance detection.

title: Individualized treatment for pediatric intracranial aneurysms in China: case series and literature review
creator: Guohong Song, Haihui Jia, He Tong, Hua Xu, Changyi Hu, Bo Li, Hao Chen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivePediatric intracranial aneurysms are rare, accounting for a small proportion of all aneurysms, yet they often present with acute onset, rapid deterioration, and a high risk of rupture. Diagnostic and therapeutic standards remain inconsistent due to limited evidence.MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed four pediatric patients (≤14 years) with ruptured intracranial aneurysms treated at our center from January 1, 2021 to December 31, 2025. Clinical presentation, imaging findings, treatment selection, and postoperative outcomes were analyzed.

title: Psychosocial Distress and Radiation Treatment Interruptions in Patients With Cancer Using Machine Learning and Regression: Retrospective Cohort Study
creator: Soheil Hashtarkhani, Christopher L Brett, Fekede Asefa Kumsa, Rezaur Rashid, Parnian Kheirkhah Rahimabad, Saba Kheirinejad, Robert L Davis, David L Schwartz, Arash Shaban-Nejad
description: BackgroundUninterrupted delivery of radiation therapy is critical to cancer treatment quality. Unplanned radiation treatment interruptions compromise tumor control and survival. Although previous studies have explored clinical and sociodemographic factors influencing treatment adherence, the role of psychosocial distress and related symptoms remains unclear.

title: The infiltration risk prediction models by logistic regression for ground-glass pulmonary nodules: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Mengqian Li, Xiaomei Zhang, Yuxin Lai, Yunlong Sun, Tianshu Yang, Xinlei Tan
description: MethodsCNKI, Wanfang, VIP, Sinomed, Pubmed, Web of Science, Embase, and other databases were searched. The retrieval time was from the establishment of the database to January 31, 2024. We included all predictive models for the invasion of ground-glass pulmonary nodules established. The modeling group was patients with a pathological diagnosis of ground-glass pulmonary nodules.

title: Timely Initiation of Breastfeeding and Associated Factors in 20 Sub-Saharan African Countries: Cross-Sectional Multilevel Analysis of Recent Demographic and Health Surveys
creator: Tadele Derbew Kassie, Getnet Gedif, Mequanent Dessie Bitewa, Atsede Alle Ewunetie, Tewodros Shibabaw, Menberu Gete, Melkamu Siferih, Mikias Getahun Molla, Tirusew Wondie Wodie, Daniel Mulat Eshetu, Abebaw Abeje Muluneh, Aysheshim Asnake Abneh
description: BackgroundAn important strategy to decrease infant morbidity and mortality is timely initiation of breastfeeding (TIBF), which is defined as putting the newborn to the breast within 1 hour of delivery. Delayed initiation of breastfeeding may contribute to high neonatal and infant mortality in sub-Saharan Africa.

title: Use of Generative AI for Substance-Related Information Among Young Adults (Aged 18-29 Years) in the United States: Cross-Sectional Survey
creator: Mireia Triguero Roura, Pia M Mauro
description: One in three young adults reported substance-related generative AI use, mainly for seeking information on substances, with higher prevalence among Black and male respondents; findings highlight that generative AI might be shaping the substance-use ecosystem among young adults and further research is needed to understand its public health implications.

title: Effect of potato glycoside alkaloids on mitochondria energy metabolism of Fusarium solani, the root rot pathogen of Lycium barbarum
creator: Ruiyun Li, Bin Wang, Wei Chen, Chongqing Zhang, Nan Li, Yupeng Wang, Yuke Yan, Yuyan Sun, Jing He
description: Fusarium solani is a widely distributed pathogenic fungus that can cause soil borne diseases in various plants and is also one of the main pathogenic bacteria of Lycium barbarum root rot. This study employed tandem mass labeling (TMT) quantitative proteomics technology to investigate the antifungal mechanism of potato glycoside alkaloids (PGA) against Fusarium solani.

title: Retraction: Pyrroloquinoline Quinine Inhibits RANKL-Mediated Expression of NFATc1 in Part via Suppression of c-Fos in Mouse Bone Marrow Cells and Inhibits Wear Particle-Induced Osteolysis in Mice
creator: The
description: d/or between all Fig 1A panels. The Fig 2D NFATc1 panel of [1] appears similar to the Fig 3B NFATc1 panel of [2] despite being used to represent different experimental conditions. The Fig 2D NFATc1 panel of [1] appears similar to the Fig 3B NFATc1 panel of [2] despite being used to represent different experimental conditions.

title: The effect of dual-task on postural control and gait in individuals with Down syndrome: a systematic review
creator: Gülsüm Kargı, Kimia Karimi, Parisa Sedaghati, Mohammad Alghosi, Mohammad Alimoradi, Andreas Konrad, Ramila Abedi Azar
description: Background and aimsIndividuals with Down syndrome (DS) exhibit deficits in postural control (PC) and gait. Dual-task (DT) paradigms, which involve performing concurrent cognitive or motor tasks, may exacerbate these deficits or, conversely, serve as effective interventions.ObjectiveThis systematic review synthesizes evidence on how DT conditions affect PC and gait in individuals with DS, examining both acute effects and long-term training outcomes.

title: Expression of Concern: Electromyographic activity of pelvic floor muscles in different positions during the use an innovative vaginal educator: Cross-sectional study
creator: The
description:
