creator: Gülce Kiren, Gizem Yılmaz Çalık, Merve Güngören, Hikmet Can Çubukçu
description: Background/Objectives: Reference intervals (RIs) for thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), free thyroxine (FT4), and free triiodothyronine (FT3) are essential for accurate interpretation of thyroid function tests. Given the pronounced age- and sex-related biological variability of these analytes, locally derived and population-specific RIs are required.

title: Family screening for genetic cardiomyopathies in ECG-positive phenotype-negative adolescents: a joint clinical and genetic approach
creator: Mark Abela, Jessica Debattista, Jeanesse Scerri, Tiziana Felice, Victor Grech, Christian Scerri
description: Adolescents may present with abnormal ECG findings despite having no structural or electrical evidence of cardiomyopathy. The value of extending family screening to this subgroup remains uncertain. To evaluate the impact of family screening in ECG-positive phenotype-negative adolescents, and determine whether a joint clinical-genetic approach improves the diagnostic yield.

title: Retrieval augmented generation in dentistry: potentials, applications, and future directions
creator: Tahereh Firoozi, Rojin Adabdokht, Hollis Lai
description: Retrieval Augmented Generation offers a robust framework for developing reliable and evidence- aligned artificial intelligence in dentistry. By integrating external knowledge sources with the generative capabilities of large language models, RAG addresses key limitations of standalone LLMs, including outdated parametric knowledge, limited domain specificity, and hallucinations.

title: Pharmacist gatekeeper interventions for suicide prevention: how evidence from developed countries support their role in low- and middle-income countries
creator: Zixiao Zhou, Fahim Mohamed
description: BackgroundApproximately 70% of self-poisoning suicides occur in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs).The implementation of pesticide bans has significantly reduced the rate of pesticide self-poisoning in these regions; however, this has been accompanied by a shift toward an increased incidence of pharmaceutical poisoning, highlighting the importance of intervention strategies to prevent pharmaceutical self-poisoning in the future.

title: Artificial Intelligence Is a Useful Tool in Exercise Science and Sports Medicine
creator: BRADLEY C. NINDL, KARL E. FRIEDL
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). icine, rather than a replacement for expert judgment. AI has become sufficiently influential that Professor Karim Lakhani at Harvard Business School has asserted that “AI won’t replace humans—but humans with AI will replace humans without AI” (1). Not replacing human thinking but enhancing human performance, AI can rapidly perform a large number of computations in the analyses of massive amounts of information, with important applications such as the identification of complex patterns that exceed unaided human capabilities (2).

title: From innovation to implementation: a global scoping review of artificial intelligence applications, governance, and challenges in humanitarian contexts
creator: Mahima Jose, Fouzia Mueen, Junaid Qadir, Alaa Abd-alrazaq, Kwalombota Kwalombota, Diana Maddah
description: BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored as a tool for supporting humanitarian action through hazards and crisis prediction, real time monitoring of evolving crisis conditions and humanitarian needs, resource allocation, and decision-making. However, evidence on how AI is implemented, evaluated, and governed across humanitarian contexts remains fragmented.

title: Sexual Function and Libido Loss in Female Climbers—A Cross-Sectional Study
creator: Sabrina Vollrath, Anne-Sophie Koller, Norman Bitterlich, Ana Buadze, Alexandra S. Kohl Schwartz, Petra Stute, Anthony C. Hackney, Nathalie Werth
description: Aim: Increasing female participation in elite sports has highlighted the need to better understand how intensive training affects reproductive health and sexual function. The aim of this cross-sectional study was to assess the prevalence of libido loss and sexual dysfunction in female climbers and to explore potential associations with low energy availability within the “relative energy deficiency in sports” framework.

title: Mechanical thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke after cardiac surgery or intervention: a retrospective cohort analysis
creator: Rosa M. Eckert, Sarah Zweynert, Constanze Czimmeck, Maximilian Schoels, Georg Bohner, Eberhard Siebert, Yuriy Hrytsyna, Evgenij Potapov, Volkmar Falk, Christoph J. Ploner, Jörg Brandes, Christoph Leithner
description: BackgroundAcute stroke due to large vessel occlusion (LVO) is a serious complication of cardiac surgery or other cardiac interventions. Little is known about the epidemiological characteristics of affected patients, the temporal relationship between stroke detection and surgery/intervention, the efficacy of mechanical thrombectomy, or the associated clinical outcomes.

title: Comparative study of the direct and photocatalytic light activation of platinum(iv) prodrugs†
creator: Kinjal Mileche, Susana M. Meza Huaman, Ke Wu, Jake A. Vickery, Hannah Coxhead, Alexander N. Smith-Xu, Patricia Juhl Allworthy, Jovana Katrinka-Mavrak, Aminesena Baser, Safacan Kolemen, Manuel M. Müller, Mahvash Tavassoli, Ismael Diez-Perez, Eleanor Stride, John F. Callan, Adam C. Sedgwick
description: Here, we present a comparative study of direct and photocatalyst-mediated photoactivation of reporter-functionalised Pt(iv) prodrugs, Carbo-4NP and CarboNap. Direct blue-light irradiation and green-light activation using the photocatalyst Rose Bengal both achieved rapid and complete Pt(iv) reduction in solution, monitored by UV-Vis and fluorescence spectroscopy. Translation to live cells revealed a marked divergence between the two approaches.

title: A study on the impact of sports participation support on the level of sports participation of urban junior high school girls in China
creator: Mingyuan Dong, Mingtian Niu, Zhengxin Jiang, Yongchul Choi, Ning Li
description: BackgroundSocial support has been identified as a key factor influencing adolescents’ engagement in physical activities. However, the relationship between middle school girls’ physical activity levels and the actual social support they receive remains unclear.AimThis study aims to explore the support mechanisms that promote increased physical activity participation among middle school girls.

title: Triboelectric E-Skin Patch Decoding Silent Speech for Advanced Human–Machine Interaction and Augmented Virtual Communication
creator: Ziwei Huo, Nuo Xu, Yixuan Fu, Rui Gu, Chao Liu, Zhong Lin Wang, Qijun Sun
description: Highlights A triboelectric E-skin patch is developed to capture lip/facial muscle movements for silent speech decoding.The proposed four-layer convolutional neural network architecture assists to achieve a record high recognition accuracy of 98.75%.Featured human–machine interaction/virtual reality applications have been demonstrated, including silent speech display system, interactive game, and virtual communication.Supplementary InformationThe online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40820-026-02346-x.

title: Why is it so difficult to understand why we don’t understand human systemic lupus erythematosus? Contemplating facts, conflicts, and impact of “the causality cascade paradigm”
creator: Ole Petter Rekvig
description: In attempts to understand systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), we find ourselves in the intellectual cross-point between nosology, pathogenicity-oriented science, philosophy, empiricism, and qualified conjectures. A vital consequence in science theory is that scientific hypotheses that are not critically investigated are in danger of being transformed into scientific dogmas 1 . This statement has consequences for this study.

title: A systematic workflow for utilizing and evaluating large language models in public health policy framing analysis
creator: Johanna Wenderoth, Peter von Philipsborn, Anna Leibinger, Philipp Cimiano
description: BackgroundFor public health policy research, it is crucial to monitor policy debates to inform evidence-based policymaking. One popular method is to analyze the news for salient frames used to argue for or against a controversial topic. However, this method is time and resource-intensive since domain experts need to manually analyze relevant articles to identify frames.

title: Voice EHR: introducing multimodal audio data for health
creator: James Anibal, Hannah Huth, Ming Li, Lindsey Hazen, Veronica Daoud, Dominique Ebedes, Yen Minh Lam, Hang Nguyen, Phuc Vo Hong, Michael Kleinman, Shelley Ost, Christopher Jackson, Laura Sprabery, Cheran Elangovan, Balaji Krishnaiah, Lee Akst, Ioan Lina, Iqbal Elyazar, Lenny Ekawati, Stefan Jansen, Ric
description: IntroductionArtificial intelligence (AI) models trained on audio data may have the potential to rapidly perform clinical tasks, enhancing medical decision-making and potentially improving outcomes through early detection. Existing technologies depend on limited datasets collected with expensive recording equipment in high-income countries, which challenges deployment in resource-constrained, high-volume settings where audio data may have a profound impact on health equity.

title: Decoding radiation-induced transcriptomic signatures of human leukocytes using long-read RNA-seq: clinical and biodosimetric implications
creator: Ahmed Salah, Heinz Schmidberger, Federico Marini, Sebastian Zahnreich
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundGene expression profiling in radiation-exposed blood is a valuable tool for biodosimetry and clinical research. Evaluating the blood’s transcriptomic radiation response provides insight into absorbed dose, hematotoxicities, and immune reactions. However, detailed analysis using long-read RNA sequencing is currently limited in its diffusion, despite the potential additional insights that could be extracted, including novel isoform discovery and on-the-field gene expression studies, owing to its portability.ResultsIn this study, we utilized Oxford Nanopore Technologies’ long-read RNA sequencing on human peripheral blood leukocytes from three

title: Emotional Intelligence, Self-Regulation, and Children’s Well-Being in Fourth-Grade Students: Cross-Sectional Associations from Türkiye
creator: Ümit İzgi Onbaşılı, Aliye Tekir, Feride Ercan Yalman
description: This study examined the associations of self-reported emotional intelligence and self-regulation with children’s well-being among fourth-grade elementary school students in Mersin, Türkiye. The sample comprised 627 students, predominantly aged 9 to 10 years, from seven public elementary schools selected to reflect different district and school contexts.

title: Pembrolizumab-Associated Adrenal Insufficiency Presenting as Adrenal Crisis: A Case Report
creator: Laura Samet, Zainab Ali, Habib Haider
description: Immunotherapy regimens containing the programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) inhibitor pembrolizumab are widely utilised in the management of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the administration of pembrolizumab is associated with unique immune-related adverse events. Adrenal insufficiency is a rare, potentially life-threatening endocrinopathy that can manifest even after the cessation of planned treatment.

title: Synchronous malignant rhabdoid tumor of the kidney and adrenal neuroblastoma in an infant treated with proton beam therapy: a case report and literature review
creator: Wei Han, Huaida Teng, Junlei Shi, Nan Zhang, Jargal Tumendemberel, Ping Lu, Jie Wang, Jie Zheng, Xinan Liu, Deguang Meng, Shosei Shimizu
description: This case report and literature review presents a 4-month-old infant with a synchronous malignant rhabdoid tumor of the kidney and adrenal neuroblastoma, an exceptionally rare combination without established treatment guidelines. Following surgical resection, proton beam therapy (14 Gy in 10 fractions) was administered to the abdominal–pelvic tumor bed with stringent organ-sparing objectives.

title: Do non-mammary conditions influence patients’ cosmetic perception after breast conserving surgery?
creator: Idam de Oliveira-Junior, Fabíola Cristina Brandini da Silva, Almir José Sarri, René Aloísio da Costa Vieira
description: IntroductionCompared to mastectomy, breast-conserving surgery (BCS) guarantees equivalent local control and survival, with lower morbidity and better quality of life (QOL), even in the long term. However, some BCS patients consider the cosmetic result to be unsatisfactory, which may affect QOL.Material and methodsThis prospective, cross-sectional study included patients who underwent BCS.

title: Local Adaptation With Gene Flow Has a Polygenic Basis in a Threatened Coastal Songbird
creator: Jonathan D. Clark, Haw Chuan Lim, Brian J. Olsen, Adrienne I. Kovach
description: Species that span heterogenous environments often exhibit local adaptation despite gene flow among populations. In such cases, the maintenance of local adaptation is controlled by several factors, including the strength of selection, migration, assortative mating, and genomic architecture. The song sparrow ( Melospiza melodia ) is a widespread songbird with diverse subspecies, including the coastally adapted Atlantic song sparrow (M.

title: Ten-Year Trends in Candidemia at a Tertiary-Care Hospital in Spain (2015–2024): Epidemiological Shifts, Diagnostic Acceleration, and Impact of Antifungal Stewardship in the COVID-19 and Post-Pandemic Era
creator: Cristian Castelló-Abietar, Miguel Alaguero, Enrique García-Carús, Emilio García-Prieto, Silvia Bolaños, Jonathan Fernández-Suárez, Teresa Peláez García de la Rasilla
description: Candidemia is a major healthcare-associated bloodstream infection with high mortality, requiring ongoing surveillance to guide management. This retrospective study analyzed 306 candidemia episodes diagnosed between 2015 and 2024 at a Spanish tertiary-care hospital, comparing two periods (2015–2019 vs. 2020–2024). The overall incidence was 0.79 episodes per 1.000 admissions, with peaks in 2021 and 2024.

title: Rosemary Essential Oil as a Natural Preservative in Fermented Thick Cream: Effects on Microbial Stability, Physicochemical Properties, and Sensory Quality
creator: Karima Maaroufi, Baya Mhamdi, Chedia Aouadhi, Karim Hosni, Hichem Sebai
description: The present study evaluated the yield, phytochemical composition, antioxidant potential, and antimicrobial properties of Salvia rosmarinus essential oil (REO), as well as its potential application as a natural preservative in fermented thick cream. The essential oil obtained by hydrodistillation (yield: 0.9%) was analyzed by gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS), which identified 15 compounds representing 100% of the total composition.

title: Read at home to do well at school: informal reading predicts achievement and motivation in English as a foreign language
creator: Jennifer Meyer, Johanna Fleckenstein, Maleika Krüger, Stefan Daniel Keller, Nicolas Hübner
description: IntroductionLearning English as a foreign language is necessary for many students to actively participate in an increasingly globalized world. This study explores the role of informal English language engagement for students’ reading and listening skills, as well as motivation to learn English. In an era of global interconnectedness, informal learning gains importance as a supplement to formal education.

title: Elabela in Lipid-Related Cardiometabolic Dysfunction: A Critical Narrative Review
creator: Zuzanna Chęcińska-Maciejewska, Ewa Pruszyńska-Oszmałek, Paweł Kołodziejski, Andrzej Ciborek, Hanna Krauss
description: Elabela (ELA/APELA/Toddler) is an endogenous peptide ligand of the apelin receptor APLNR (also known as APJ) and, together with apelin, forms the apelinergic signalling system. Its role in embryonic development, the cardiovascular system, the kidneys and the endothelium is becoming increasingly well characterised, whilst its function in metabolic regulation remains unresolved.

title: Impacts of stem cells from different sources on wound healing rate in diabetic foot ulcers: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Le Tong, Lin Tang, Bangli Tang, Jianna Zhang
description: BackgroundDiabetic foot ulcers (DFU) are a significant complication of diabetes, with huge implications on patient morbidity and healthcare costs. The objective of this meta-analysis was to evaluate the impacts of stem cells from different sources on wound healing rate in DFU patients.

title: Icotrokinra, a Targeted Oral Peptide, in Participants With Moderate-to-Severe Plaque Psoriasis and Self-Reported Psoriatic Arthritis: Results From a Pooled Analysis of the Phase 3 ICONIC-LEAD, ICONIC-ADVANCE 1, and ICONIC-ADVANCE 2 Trials
creator: Iain B McInnes, Linda Stein Gold, Robert Bissonnette, Mark G Lebwohl, Ofelia Reyes-Servin, Joseph Cafone, Ya-Wen Yang, Soumya D Chakravarty, Charles Iaconangelo, Shu Li, Tasneam Shagroni, Karissa Lozenski, April W Armstrong, Joseph F Merola
description: BackgroundIcotrokinra, a targeted oral peptide that precisely blocks the interleukin-23 receptor, is approved to treat adult and pediatric (≥12 years, ≥40 kg) patients with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis (PsO).ObjectiveAssess psoriatic arthritis (PsA)–specific outcomes through Week (W) 16 in a subgroup of phase-3 study participants with moderate-to-severe plaque PsO and self-reported medical history of PsA (PsO+PsA).

title: Efficacy analysis of quadruple nerve decompression surgery for lower limb diabetic peripheral neuropathy
creator: Yong Zhang, Zonghan Li, Tianyi Ma, Xiaodong Xu, Jicheng Li, Rufei Dai, Jiawei Shen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveTo explore the efficacy of quadruple nerve decompression in treating painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy (PDPN) of lower extremity, and to evaluate its clinical value in pain relief and sensory recovery.MethodA retrospective analysis was performed on 26 PDPN patients (45 sides), all of whom underwent quadruple nerve decompression, including release of the common peroneal nerve (CPN), superficial peroneal nerve (SPN), deep peroneal nerve (DPN), and tibial nerve (TN).

title: Emulating a randomized clinical trial with real-world data to evaluate the effect of antidepressant use in PTSD patients with high suicide risk
creator: Oshin Miranda, Xiguang Qi, M. Daniel Brannock, Ryan Whitworth, Thomas Kosten, Neal David Ryan, Gretchen L. Haas, Levent Kirisci, LiRong Wang
description: IntroductionPost-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) entails behavioral changes with increased risk of suicide, and there is no consensus on the preferred antidepressants for treatment of those PTSD patients who are at elevated risk for suicide.MethodsWe conducted a clinical trial emulation study comparing suicide-related events (SREs) among those patients’ initiating antidepressants within 60 days after a qualifying SRE.

title: Disseminated Tuberculosis With Ocular Involvement After 12 Years of Anti–TNF‐α Therapy
creator: Muhammad Ali Muslimani, Alberto Ardizzone, Silvia Rossi, Francesco Siviero, Armanda Leka, Marco Vecchia, Alessandra Ricciardi, Pietro Valsecchi, Raffaele Bruno, Angela Maria Di Matteo, Cristiano Giusti
description: BackgroundOcular tuberculosis (TB) is an uncommon yet potentially vision‐threatening manifestation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, particularly difficult to diagnose in immunocompromised individuals. The increasing use of anti–tumor necrosis factor‐α (anti–TNF‐α) agents has markedly heightened the risk of TB reactivation, often with disseminated or extrapulmonary involvement despite negative baseline screening.

title: Structure of native photosystem II assembly intermediate from Chlamydomonas reinhardtii
creator: Mariia Fadeeva, Daniel Klaiman, Eaazhisai Kandiah, Nathan Nelson
description: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii Photosystem II (PSII) is a dimer consisting of at least 13 nuclear-encoded and four chloroplast-encoded protein subunits that collectively function as a sunlight-driven oxidoreductase. In this study, we present the inaugural structure of a green alga PSII assembly intermediate (pre-PSII-int).

title: Cell Line-Dependent Effects of Spheroid Formation Method on Drug Response in Melanoma Models
creator: Akvilė Žilytė, Vilma Petrikaitė
description: Highlights What are the main findings? A375 and IGR39 spheroids showed similar growth regardless of the formation method, while smaller spheroids grew faster.A375 spheroids formed on non-adhesive surfaces were more sensitive to doxorubicin, whereas IGR39 spheroids showed only minor method-dependent differences. What are the implications of the main findings? Spheroid formation method can influence drug response in melanoma models.

title: A network approach to investigating the inter-relationship between health-related quality of life dimensions and depression in 1735 Chinese patients with heterogeneous cancers
creator: Sulaiman Muhetaer, Peierdun Mijiti, Kaibinuer Aierken, Huang Ziyin, Wulan Talapuhan, Kaibinuer Tuoheti, Ye Lixia, Qi Shuang, Wei Jingjing
description: BackgroundWe aimed to explore the inter-connection between depression and HRQOL dimensions in cancer patients using a network approach, which might provide new insights for precise interventions to improve cancer patients’ overall HRQOL.MethodsBetween June 1, 2016, and August 31, 2017, a total of 1735 eligible patients with heterogeneous types of cancer were recruited.

title: Plant–Soil Feedbacks May Underlie Competitive Dynamics Between Co‐Occurring Invasive Annual Grasses Bromus tectorum and Ventenata dubia
creator: Lilly Sencenbaugh, Jane M. Mangold, Bruce D. Maxwell, Danielle E. M. Ulrich, Lisa J. Rew
description: Plant communities are shaped by interactions among plants and soil legacies. Plant–soil feedbacks (PSF) may alter invasion dynamics and change plant community species composition. There have been field observations of the invasive annual grass, Ventenata dubia , replacing another invasive annual grass, Bromus tectorum , though previous work has not found evidence of competition that would support these shifts.

title: Transcriptional profiles analysis of effects of Toxoplasma gondii rhoptry protein 16 on THP-1 macrophages
creator: Ningai Yang, Mingyang Li, Hong Yang, Jiaming Li, Tiantian Dang, Guangqi Li, Zhijun Zhao
description: Introduction Toxoplasma gondii, an intracellular parasitic protozoan, is globally recognized for its ability to cause parasitic diseases and has developed diverse strategies to evade immune-mediated elimination. The protein ROP16 of T.gondii plays a crucial role in this evasion process by specifically targeting macrophages and mononuclear phagocytes in vivo.

title: Multimodal Ayurveda Intervention in the Management of Recurrent Pilonidal Sinus: A Case Report
creator: Wicramanayake WAAP, Peshala KKVS, Semonti Nandi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Pilonidal sinus (PNS) is a chronic inflammatory condition that primarily originates from hair follicles in the natal cleft at the base of the spine and may also occur in other areas such as the axilla and umbilicus. A 25‐year‐old male patient presented to the outpatient department (OPD) of the surgery unit at the National Ayurveda Teaching Hospital, Borella, in November 2022 with complaints of pain and purulent discharge from the sacral region near the anus, accompanied by intermittent fever for 5 days.

title: Quantitative analysis of contrast-enhanced ultrasound in neoadjuvant treatment of locally advanced rectal cancer: a retrospective study
creator: Gouyang Bai, Congying Wang, Yi Sun, Jinghua Li, Xiangzhou Shi, Wei Zhang, Yilin Yang, Ruijing Yang
description: PurposeTo explore the clinical value of contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) quantitative analysis in the evaluation and prognosis of neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy for locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC).MethodsEighty-three consecutive patients undergoing neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy and total mesorectal excision for LARC were retrospectively included. According to pathological results, patients were categorized into complete or incomplete response groups.

title: Diagnosis-to-surgery lead time and future-health worry in women with primary breast cancer: a longitudinal Swedish registry-based cohort study
creator: Johan Eriksson, Irma Fredriksson, Lena Lindholm, Micael Appelblad, Malin Sund
description: PurposeThe interval between breast cancer diagnosis and surgery is psychologically demanding, and meeting the Swedish standardised care pathway target has remained challenging. We examined whether diagnosis-to-surgery lead time is associated with patient-reported psychological outcomes.MethodsWe conducted a longitudinal cohort study using Swedish National Quality Register for Breast Cancer data (2020–2024).

title: Targeting NANOS1 in triple-negative breast cancer: synergistic effects of digoxin and PD-1 inhibitors in modulating the tumor immune microenvironment
creator: Tangyi Wang, Yadian Lei, Jingwei Sun, Li Wang, Yuxin Lin, Zhijing Wu, Shoude Zhang, Chengzhu Cao, Haiyan Wang
description: IntroductionTriple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive subtype of breast cancer resistant to endocrine and targeted therapies. Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have shown significant efficacy in various cancers. Taraxacum officinale, commonly known as dandelion, has traditionally been used to treat breast-related diseases and is recognized for its beneficial composition and low side effects.

title: High-energy diets with reduced digestible lysine for Japanese laying quails under thermoneutral conditions: effects on laying performance, egg quality, and profitability
creator: Ana Paula S. Ton, Lidiane Staub, Aldemar M. de Jesus, Anderson Corassa, Adedoyin T. Amos, Adriana G. do Amaral, Ednaldo A. de Andrade, Leonardo W. de Freitas, Maicon Sbardella
description: Japanese quails (Coturnix coturnix japonica) are widely used for commercial egg production, requiring an adequate dietary energy-to-amino acid ratio to support egg production and economic returns. However, current recommendations for laying Japanese quails remain inconsistent due to variations among strains, production phases, and environmental conditions.

title: Dataset on criteria for evaluating teaching quality in blended learning environments: Evidence from a Vietnamese university
creator: An T Thuy Nguyen, Quang X Tran, Trung Tran, Lam Le
description: This article presents a dataset for evaluating teaching quality in a blended learning environment at the University of Education, Vietnam National University, Hanoi. The dataset includes 472 valid survey responses collected from undergraduate students and lecturers who participated in blended learning courses. Data were gathered using a newly developed 62-item instrument measured on a five-point Likert scale.

title: Clinical assessment and transcriptome analysis of host immune responses in a vaccination-challenge study using a glycoprotein G deletion mutant vaccine strain of infectious laryngotracheitis virus
creator: Gayathri Gopakumar, Mauricio J. C. Coppo, Andrés Diaz-Méndez, Carol A. Hartley, Joanne M. Devlin
description: A glycoprotein-G-deleted live-attenuated vaccine strain of the infectious laryngotracheitis virus (ILTV), ΔgG-ILTV, is safe and efficacious against ILTV challenge. In the current study, the transcriptome of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) of the ΔgG-ILTV-vaccinated group of specific-pathogen-free chickens were compared to those of the nonvaccinated group at 7 days post-vaccination.

title: CDK4/6 Inhibitors and Curcumin Synergistically Suppress HER2− Breast Cancer via Lethal ROS and Inhibition of Metastasis
creator: Chenyu Wang, Yiqin Zou, Chunyu Chang, Siyue Liu, Xiankun Ke, Liang Hu, Di Wang, Yukang Lu, Shiwen Luo, Sijian Huang, Yilan Hu, Wenqi Yu, Aiping Deng, Ming Yue, Jue Jiang
description: CDK4/6 inhibitors represent a key therapy for HR+/HER2− breast cancer, yet resistance and limited efficacy in triple‐negative breast cancer (TNBC) remain significant challenges. Using a self‐established drug combination prediction platform, we identified a strong synergy between the CDK4/6 inhibitor palbociclib and the natural compound curcumin across both HR+/HER2− and TNBC models, an effect that was also observed with ribociclib.

title: Painting psychosis: an empirical investigation of the self-portraits of Edvard Munch
creator: Eric C. Bettelheim, Jingyi Liu, Paola Dazzan, Federico Turkheimer
description: Substantial evidence demonstrates that the brain is more interested in faces than in other subjects and that self-related material, particularly self-images, have higher saliency than non-self-referential material. Studies of self-portraits have revealed correlations between stylistic elements and artists’ states of mind.

title: AQQD: Annotated Quranic Qira’at Dataset
creator: Linda Smail, Mohammed Lataifeh, Md Sohazur Islam Sozib, Arthur Diniz De Souza
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). AQQD (Annotated Quranic Qira'at Dataset) is an open audio dataset of Quranic recitations annotated across canonical Qira'at styles. The dataset is designed to support research in machine learning, speech and audio processing, computational linguistics, and Quranic studies. The current release contains 24,183 WAV audio files from 309 reciters and covers 70 selected Quranic Surahs segmented into representative verses and phonetic variation points.

title: Sex differences in intracranial plaque burden in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus with acute ischemic cerebrovascular disease: a pilot study based on high-resolution MRI
creator: Xuejiao Yan, Ling Li, Jie Gao, Lihui Wang, Kai Ai, Xiaoyan Lei, Min Tang, Xiaoling Zhang, Dongsheng Zhang
description: BackgroundAtherosclerosis (AS) is the main cause of macrovascular disease. Previous studies have found sex differences in the prevalence of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and its associated macrovascular disease outcomes. However, the relationship between sex differences, T2DM, and AS is not fully understood.

title: Benign Proliferative Nodules in a Giant Congenital Melanocytic Nevus: Diagnostic Challenge and Management
creator: Fenohasina Rakotonandrasana, Holy Tiana Andrianjafitrimo, Onivola Raharolahy, Andrianandrianina Mbolatiana Kiady Armando Rakotomanana, Georges Cheny Fenohasina, Voahanginirina Nathalie Ralimalala, Malalaniaina Andrianarison, Fandresena Arilala Sendrasoa, Irina Mamisoa Ranaivo, Fahafahantsoa Rapelano
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Congenital melanocytic nevi are cutaneous malformations present at birth, resulting from a benign proliferation of melanocytes. Although generally benign, they can have significant psychological impacts and carry a non‐negligible risk of progression to malignant melanoma. We report a case of a giant congenital melanocytic nevus associated with a perianal mass in an infant, two and half‐month‐old infant, with no notable medical history, born at term.

title: Molecular circuit for exponentiation based on the domain coding strategy
creator: Chun Huang, Xiaoqiang Duan, Yifei Guo, Panlong Li, Junwei Sun, Jiaying Shao, Yanfeng Wang
description: DNA strand displacement (DSD) is an efficient technology for constructing molecular circuits. However, system computing speed and the scale of logical gate circuits remain a huge challenge. In this paper, a new method of coding DNA domains is proposed to carry out logic computation. The structure of DNA strands is designed regularly, and the rules of domain coding are described.

title: AI-based prediction of heart failure progression in persistent atrial fibrillation using wearable electrocardiography: a brief research report
creator: Chae-Bin Song, Yun Kwan Kim, YouMi Hwang
description: BackgroundPersistent atrial fibrillation (AF) frequently coexists with heart failure (HF), yet HF monitoring remains limited by the need for repeated blood-based biomarkers such as N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP). Advances in wearable electrocardiography (ECG) and artificial intelligence (AI) now allow continuous extraction of digital physiologic signatures that may reflect hemodynamic stress.

title: Primary intraosseous cavernous hemangioma of the zygomatic bone☆
creator: Katerina Tori, Nicholas Levergood, Fernando Pellerano, Richard A Burgett, Ronald Martin
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeWe present an uncommon case of primary intraosseous cavernous hemangioma involving the zygoma which displayed CD31 positivity on pathologic analysis.ObservationsMacroscopic examination showed a bulging purple-red mass intrinsic to bone measuring 2.1 × 1.8 × 1.6 cm (Fig 2A). Histopathology demonstrated the lesion was comprised of thin-walled vascular channels lined by a monolayer of endothelial cells interspersed among bony trabeculae (Fig 2B) consistent with intraosseous cavernous hemangioma.7,8 Vascular walls lacked both venous and arterial features.

title: Influenza vaccine compatibility among hospitalized patients during and after the COVID-19 pandemic
creator: Ilana S. Fratty, Menucha Jurkowicz, Neta Zuckerman, Ital Nemet, Nofar Atari, Limor Kliker, Lea Gur-Arie, Alina Rosenberg, Aharona Glatman-Freedman, Yaniv Lustig, Michal Mandelboim
description: IntroductionFollowing the significant decrease in SARS-CoV-2 cases worldwide, Israel, as well as other countries, have again been faced with a rise in seasonal influenza. This study compared circulating influenza A and B in hospitalized patients in Israel with the influenza strains in the vaccine following the 2021–2022 winter season which was dominated by the omicron variant.

title: Advances in Smart Hydrogels for Myocardial Infarction Therapy: A Scoping Review of Applications, Challenges, and Future Perspectives
creator: Eyram Ahadzi, Otema Darfour Manu, Ruth Antwi-Baah, Henry Agbe, Prince Ebenezer Adjei
description: Smart hydrogels are stimuli‐responsive biomaterials that enable targeted, sustained, and controlled therapeutic delivery. Their unique ability to respond to physiological cues such as pH, temperature, reactive oxygen species (ROS), and enzymatic activity makes them highly attractive for myocardial infarction (MI) therapy. This scoping review explores advances, applications, challenges, and future perspectives related to the use of smart hydrogels in MI.

title: Feasibility and long-term outcomes of recanalization for De novo small vessel chronic total occlusions
creator: Jen-Fang Cheng, Cheng-Ting Tsai, Chien-Lin Lee, Jiun-Yang Chiang, Shih-Chi Liu, Chi-Jen Chang, Chia-Pin Lin, Chi-Hung Huang, Jun-Ting Liou, Chia-Ti Tsai, Yi-Chih Wang, Juey-Jen Hwang
description: BackgroundThe impact of small vessel size on chronic total occlusions (CTO) interventions remains underexplored. We compared revascularization feasibility and follow-up outcomes between patients with small- and non-small vessel de novo CTOs.MethodsIn total, 493 consecutive patients (64.0 ± 11.4 years, 432 men) undergoing wiring-based de novo CTO interventions were divided into two groups: small vessels (reference vessel diameter < 2.

title: Mechanistic evaluation of antiarthritic and anti-inflammatory effect of campesterol ester derivatives in complete Freund’s adjuvant-induced arthritic rats
creator: Sarwat Nazir, Ishtiaq Ahmad, Aisha Mobashar, Ali Sharif, Arham Shabbir, Waqas Ashraf Chaudhary
description: Background: Current therapies for RA have limitations and side effects, leading to a growing need for safer treatment options. Natural compounds from plants are gaining attention for their therapeutic benefits and fewer side effects. One such compound is the campesterol derivative, a steroid derivative occurring in plants.

title: A Research Project for Secondary Schools on Urban Plant Ecological Genetics
creator: Bruno Andreas Walther, Leonard Jakob Klamann, Sarah Victoria Weirauch, Ghinwa Mashhady, Hans‐Jörg Mai, Petra Bauer
description: Participation in authentic research projects benefits both teachers and students by linking hands‐on field work with experimental biology and quantitative analysis. Plant ecological genetics is especially well suited for classroom integration, but accessible, classroom‐ready outlines are scarce. Arabidopsis thaliana —a wild species in urban environments with a well‐characterized genome and extensive educational resources—provides an ideal model.

title: Mixed emotions: binary paths of humble leadership influencing employee behavior
creator: Yanping Shen, Wenbing Wu, Shufei Xu, Yi Wang, Fangyuan Cai
description: The importance of humble leadership has garnered increasing attention among researchers. Most existing research focuses on its positive effects, but its negative effects are rarely discussed. From a more dialectical perspective, this study found that humble leadership has a dual impact, as it can foster employee innovative behavior and also trigger instances of time theft.

title: Meta-EEGs: A structured approach for processing high-volume EEG data
creator: Palak Handa, Manya Joshi, Esha Gupta, Ramona Woitek
description: Electroencephalography (EEG) is widely used clinically and in research, including AI-driven applications for cognitive state analysis and neurological disorder detection, such as epilepsy. However, automated seizure detection faces challenges, including inconsistent windowing, timestamp misalignment, label-based signal segmentation, and unstructured large-scale EEG data—especially critical in event-driven settings.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Otolaryngology—From Demonstrating Capability to Delivering Trustworthy Clinical Impact
creator: Da‐Qing Li
description: analysis, medical imaging, computational and spatial pathology, predictive modeling, surgical video analysis, ambient documentation, and patient‐centered applications. Collectively, these studies illustrate how AI is moving beyond proof‐of‐concept demonstrations toward increasingly sophisticated clinical applications. At the same time, they remind us that technical performance alone is not sufficient to establish clinical value.

title: Odor-induced sweetness enhancement: EEG evidence for olfactory and gustatory cross-modal interactions
creator: Yuchao Yang, Yuchen Guo, Zhijie Hua, Qun Wang, Yan Shi, Hong Men
description: Reducing sugar content while maintaining perceived sweetness is a major challenge in beverage formulation. This study combined sensory evaluation and electroencephalography (EEG) to investigate how varying odor intensities influence sweetness perception in sucrose solutions. Sixteen participants evaluated solutions with matched sugar content but different odor levels while EEG signals were recorded.

title: Kindergarten teachers’ compassion fatigue: decreasing with empathic ability or empathic motivation or both?
creator: Fangyan Chen, Wenjun Xu, Yabo Ge, Weijian Li
description: Compassion fatigue, often referred to as the “cost of caring,” reflects a form of empathy deficit. However, it remains unclear whether it stems from a diminishment in empathic ability, empathic motivation, or both. To address this gap, we developed a hierarchical regression and structural equation model using survey data from 1,161 kindergarten teachers.

title: Sun Safety Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Among Farmers in Ede‐Oballa, Nigeria
creator: Ukah Cynthia Chinonso, Majani Edward
description: BackgroundExcessive exposure to ultraviolet (UV) radiation of the sun poses significant health risks to outdoor workers. Farmers are particularly vulnerable, yet their knowledge and practices regarding sun protection are underreported in low‐resource settings.AimTo assess the knowledge, attitudes, and practices of sun safety among farmers in Ede‐Oballa, Nsukka LGA, Enugu State, Nigeria.

title: Primary hepatic angiosarcoma misdiagnosed as hemangioma despite repeated negative biopsies and sclerotherapy: A diagnostic pitfall
creator: Faeze Salahshour, Masoomeh Safaei, Ahmad Rahimian, Mahdi Hazratgholi
description: Primary hepatic angiosarcoma is a very rare vascular malignancy with highly variable imaging and pathologic appearances, occasionally resembling a benign hemangioma. We describe a 62-year-old woman who presented with profound anemia and severe thrombocytopenia and multifocal hepatic lesions repeatedly interpreted as hemangioma on core needle biopsies. She underwent 1 sessions of sclerotherapy.

title: Palmar Cooling as a Thermoregulatory Intervention: Mechanistic Basis and Implications for Exercise and Clinical Applications
creator: Robert J Heins, William E Reisinger, Brett Norris, Robert Rogers, Shashank Kaushik
description: During exercise, rising metabolic heat production creates competition for blood flow between skeletal muscle and the cutaneous vasculature. The resulting redistribution elevates cardiovascular (CV) strain and accelerates fatigue, particularly during environmental heat stress or in individuals with impaired thermoregulatory capacity. Strategies that enhance heat dissipation without further burdening CV function may therefore improve exercise tolerance.

title: Anxiety and depression prevalence and associated factors in patients with knee osteoarthritis
creator: Qizhen Feng, Mingjie Weng, Xi Yang, Min Zhang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveWith the evolving spectrum of diseases, psychological conditions such as anxiety and depression have emerged as significant global public health concerns. Notably, these psychological disorders are prevalent among patients suffering from knee osteoarthritis (KOA).

title: Use of corneal allogenic intrastromal ring segments (CAIRS) in high astigmatism, a case report
creator: Bader Khayat, Omar M Alabbasi, Ghadi Aljohani
description: BackgroundCorneal allogenic intrastromal ring segments (CAIRS) were developed as a biologic alternative to synthetic intracorneal ring segments and are primarily reported in the management of keratoconus and corneal ectasia. Its role in high corneal astigmatism still limited.Case reportA 54-year-old male presented with decreased visual acuity in the left eye due to high regular corneal astigmatism.

title: Case report: Targeted sequencing facilitates the diagnosis and management of rare multifocal pure ground-glass opacities with intrapulmonary metastasis
creator: Yingshun Yang, Guotian Pei, Mingwei Li, Xiaoxue Ma, Shuai Wang, Xianjun Min, Shushi Meng, Jiayue Qin, Huina Wang, Jun Liu, Yuqing Huang
description: IntroductionTreatments for multiple ground-glass opacities (GGOs) for which the detection rate is increasing are still controversial. Next-generation sequencing (NGS) may provide additional key evidence for differential diagnosis or optimal therapeutic schedules.Case presentationWe first reported a rare case in which more than 100 bilateral pulmonary GGOs (91.

title: Immunological response of live-captured wild elk (Cervus canadensis) to Treponeme-Associated Hoof Disease antigens
creator: Jennifer Wilson-Welder, Kristin Mansfield, Sushan Han, Brock Hoenes, David Alt, Sam Humphrey, Steven C. Olsen
description: A severe hoof disease is affecting wild elk (Cervus canadensis) in the Pacific Northwest. Causing lameness, tissue ulceration and necrosis, hoof overgrowth, and often loss of the hoof itself, bacteria from the genus Treponema are found at the forefront of the lesions.

title: Severity and Determinants of Anemia Among Adolescent Girls in Africa: A Multicountry and Multilevel Analysis of 25 Countries
creator: Bedilu Alamirie Ejigu, Getnet Bogale Begashaw, Fentanesh Nibret Tiruneh
description: BackgroundAnemia remains a major public health concern in Africa, with substantial health and developmental consequences. Adolescents, particularly girls, are at increased risk due to rapid growth, menstruation, and inadequate dietary intake. Identifying the severity and determinants of anemia among adolescent girls in Africa is crucial for developing appropriate interventions, yet evidence remains scarce.

title: Comprehensive review of mapping climate change impacts on tea cultivation: bibliometric and content analysis of trends, influences, adaptation strategies, and future directions
creator: Altyeb Ali Abaker Omer, Chun-Hua Zhang, Jie Liu, Zhi-guo Shan
description: Climate change has a profound impact on tea cultivation, posing significant challenges to yield, quality, and sustainability due to stressors such as drought, temperature fluctuations, and elevated CO₂ levels. This study aims to address these challenges by identifying and synthesizing key themes, influential contributions, and effective adaptation strategies for mitigating the impacts of climate change on tea production.

title: Prognostic value of the Duke Activity Status Index for preoperative cardiac risk stratification: an international pooled cohort study
creator: Duminda N Wijeysundera, Brian H Cuthbertson, Emmanuelle Duceppe, Tom EF Abbott, Rupert M Pearse, Paul S Myles, Keying Xu, Julian F Daza, Calvin Diep, Leandra A Amado, Angela Jerath, Bernhard Riedel, Daniel I McIsaac, FIT After Surgery Investigators and METS Investigators
description: SummaryBackgroundGuidelines recommend structured self-reported functional capacity assessment for preoperative cardiac risk stratification, including the Duke Activity Status Index (DASI). However, evidence supporting its incremental prognostic value beyond established risk factors remains limited. We evaluated the prognostic performance of the DASI using pooled data from two prospective cohorts.

title: Does orchidopexy for testicular torsion affect long‐term fertility parameters in males: A systematic review
creator: Avula Aishwarya Rao, Muhammad Shariq Rahemtoola, Hassaan Aziz, Peter Grice, Mohamed Mubarak, Ian Pearce, Theodora Stasinou, Vaibhav Modgil
description: ObjectivesThe aim of this study is to investigate long‐term fertility outcomes following orchidopexy performed for testicular torsion.Patients and MethodsThis systematic review adhered to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta‐Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines and was registered with the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO: CRD420251152057).

title: Diffuse peritoneal mesothelioma presenting with the appearance of mesenteric panniculitis: A case report
creator: Yunfeng Chen, Qiong Fu, Jialing Xu, Rong Wang, Yongxiang Mo, Yuan Liu
description: Diffuse peritoneal mesothelioma (DPM) is a rare and aggressive malignancy of the peritoneum. Early symptoms are non-specific and the condition is liable to misdiagnosis. In the present case, a 54-year-old man was misdiagnosed between April 2020 and October 2021 with mesenteric panniculitis.

title: Patient Satisfaction With a One‐Stop Service Center in a Tertiary Hospital: A Cross‐Sectional Study
creator: Gong Xue, Chen Xia, Wei Li Li, Ding Xiao Rong, Peng Wei Qun
description: ObjectiveTo investigate the current status of outpatient satisfaction and its key influencing factors under the “One‐Stop” service model, providing an empirical basis for optimizing outpatient service processes and enhancing operational efficiency.MethodsA cross‐sectional survey was conducted from March to April 2025, selecting 1016 outpatients (or their family members) from 15 departments in our hospital.

title: Sexual harassment in sport: a systematic review of risk factors, theoretical frameworks, and prevention strategies (2020–2025)
creator: Behnam Oboudi, Robert Book, Ekaterina Glebova
description: Sexual harassment (SH) remains a persistent safeguarding problem in sport, yet recent research highlights that its drivers operate simultaneously across structural, cultural, interpersonal, and situational levels. To clarify current knowledge in this rapidly developing field, this review synthesizes studies published between 2020 and 2025 examining risk factors, theoretical interpretations, and emerging prevention strategies in sport settings. Four frameworks (e.g.

title: Shoulder-wearable soft robot for assisting older adults in scapular stretching
creator: Kosuke Isobe, Masakazu Hirokawa, Yasuhiro Suzuki, Hideki Kadone, Yukiyo Shimizu, Kenji Suzuki
description: We propose a wearable soft robot that assists with individualized scapula adduction and abduction for thoracic stretching in respiratory rehabilitation. Although thoracic stretching is known to be effective for respiratory rehabilitation, the range of motion of older adult patients narrows with age, and long-term external aid by physical therapists is required.

title: Towards greater sensitivity: advancing social life cycle assessment for the coffee sector in Brazil and the Democratic Republic of the Congo
creator: Braida Thom, Lea Fabritius, Marie Sigrist, Didace Banyanga, Stephan Pfister, Réussite Bugale Malembaka, Gabriela Schneider, Kokou Kintche, Johanna Jacobi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeLiterature on coffee sustainability focuses on environmental and economic challenges and often falls short on social factors that strongly influence overall sustainability. For coffee producers, social aspects are existentially important, while environmental concerns take lower priority.

title: KIR AA individuals possess strong inhibitory KIR alleles alongside HLA ligands that are protective against leukemia in the Chinese population
creator: Zhihui Deng, Jianxin Zhen, Yunan Li, Shuang Liang, Manru Zhang, Siqi Cai, Renhui Jiang, Zhichao Yang, Qiong Yu, Jinyong Wang, Jie Liu
description: IntroductionThe killer-cell immunoglobulin-like receptor (KIR) gene cluster exhibits complicated diversity in haplotype content, copy-number variation (CNV), and allelic polymorphism. To date, 2,286 distinct KIR alleles have been released in the IPD-KIR Database. However, little is known about the impact of high-resolution-level KIR allelic polymorphisms on leukemia.

title: Cuticular Barcoding—A Novel Method for Host Identification From Adult Parasitoid Wasps
creator: Maura Haas‐Renninger, Michael Haas, Manuel Stothut, Henrik Krehenwinkel, Johannes L M Steidle, Lars Krogmann
description: Parasitoid wasps are important regulators of their hosts and highly relevant for the resilience of terrestrial ecosystems. However, data on parasitoid‐host interactions are scarce and missing for many parasitoid species as parasitoids are mostly collected as adults without host association and rearing of parasitoids from their hosts can be difficult. Molecular methods can thus help to circumvent this bottleneck.

title: Immunothrombosis in hospitalized COVID-19 patients identified by multiomics profiling and linked to postacute complications
creator: Laura Ansone, Līva Pelcmane, Monta Brīvība, Rihards Saksis, Ivars Silamiķelis, Kristaps Korņejevs, Daniella Borisova, Kaspars Megnis, Līga Eliņa, Vita Rovite, Annija Vaska, Kristaps Klavins, Helgi B Schiöth, Janis Klovins
description: SummaryPost-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) disproportionately affect hospitalized patients and require improved molecular characterization to inform patient management. Here, we performed a prospective longitudinal multi-omics study of hospitalized COVID-19 patients, analyzing whole blood transcriptomics, targeted urine metabolomics, kidney injury biomarkers, and electronic health record-based outcome stratification across acute illness, one-month, and three-month recovery time points.

title: Endothelin-1 in the failing Fontan: pathobiology, precision therapeutics, and future trial design
creator: Iman Maiza
description: The Fontan circulation, devised as definitive palliation for single-ventricle congenital heart disease, imposes systemic venous hypertension, loss of pulmonary arterial pulsatility, and restricted preload reserve. These hemodynamic trade-offs progressively injure the pulmonary vasculature, liver, and lymphatic system, producing late morbidities including elevated pulmonary vascular resistance, Fontan-associated liver disease (FALD), protein-losing enteropathy, and arrhythmias.

title: Evaluating HEART: Student Engagement and Health System Impact in a Person‐Centered Learning Health System Initiative
creator: Tracey Carr, Stefanie Foster, Phoebe Stobart, Carson Squair, Taylor Spock, Candace Skrapek, Margaret King, Brenda Andreas, Noelle Rohatinsky, Christine Stobart, Caitlin Ward, Tina Zheng, Gerald Farthing
description: BackgroundHealthcare Education and Research Training (HEART) is a cocurricular, engaged learning initiative that supported undergraduate students in acquiring and applying healthcare research skills. The project was guided by a learning health system (LHS)‐aligned model focused on the collection, synthesis, and rapid translation of patient‐reported experience data into actionable recommendations.

title: A key role for the exoribonuclease XRN1 in regulating the hepatitis B viral transcriptome
creator: Senko Tsukuda, Nadina Wand, James M Harris, Olivia Dobrica, Medhi Boutasbih, Xiaxuan Zhu, Peter AC Wing, Peter Balfe, Jane A McKeating
description: SummaryChronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) is a leading cause of liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma that persists as a DNA mini-chromosome and replicates via genomic RNA intermediates. While HBV replication has been extensively studied, mechanisms governing viral RNA degradation remain unclear. Here, we identify a key role for the 5′–3′ exoribonuclease XRN1 in regulating the HBV transcriptome.

title: Freedom of choice supports social complexity in chimpanzees
creator: Andrew Halloran, Jake A Funkhouser, Sarah Poirier, Darby Proctor, Caroline Griffis, Skye Conners, Ashley Cooley, David Morgan, Crickette Sanz
description: SummaryFission-fusion sociality offers almost infinite options for individuals to make self-determined choices about how to range across space, spend time in different activities, and associate with conspecifics. Yet, how such freedoms contribute to the construction of functional social groups has received little attention.

title: Modelling C-arm fluoroscopy and operating table kinematics via machine learning
creator: Faria Jaheen, Vinod Gutta, Pascal Fallavollita
description: This work presents a machine learning driven framework for data-efficient kinematic modeling and workspace optimization in modular C-arm fluoroscopy systems integrated with operating tables. A comprehensive dataset of joint configurations and end-effector poses annotated with voxelized collision status enables the training of predictive models across multiple system configurations ranging from 5 to 9 degrees of freedom.

title: Neurokinin-3 receptor antagonists for vasomotor symptoms in menopause and breast cancer survivorship
creator: Nadia Linxi Feng, Anna N Wilkinson, Emily Delpero, Amirrtha Srikanthan
description: s that reduce vasomotor symptoms by targeting hypothalamic thermoregulatory pathways without systemic estrogen exposure. Fezolinetant and elinzanetant significantly reduce the frequency and severity of hot flashes, with elinzanetant supported by phase III evidence in patients receiving endocrine therapy for breast cancer.

title: Legacy of culture heritage building revitalization: place attachment and culture identity
creator: Suk Ha Grace Chan, Wing Han Helen Lee, Binglin Martin Tang, Ziyi Chen
description: IntroductionCultural heritage buildings are revitalized to promote culture instead of being neglected or demolished. For locals, the revitalization of heritage buildings symbolizes a commitment to the community and a taste of collective memory. The study attempts to test the effectiveness of heritage cultural building on visitors’ post-experience behavior through cultural identity and place attachment.

title: Canada’s AI for All strategy has a privacy problem that must be addressed
creator: Sheryl Spithoff, Teresa Scassa
description: for All strategy, with the intention of increasing the development and adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) while promising to protect privacy, address algorithmic bias, and support Indigenous self-determination over how AI is built and used. These promises are particularly important because the government’s priority for AI development is in the health and life sciences sector.

title: Selenium nanoparticles from Dermacoccus abyssi MT1.1ᵀ improve water status, biomass, and antioxidant defense in tomato under salt stress
creator: Pharada Rangseekaew, Supawitch Hoijang, Sirasit Srinuanpan, Mathurin Meethangdee, Sitthisak Intarasit, Wasu Pathom-aree
description: SummarySalt stress severely limits plant growth and agricultural productivity. Nanoparticles have emerged as a promising strategy to alleviate salinity stress. This study investigated the biogenic synthesis of selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs) using the culture supernatant of Dermacoccus abyssi MT1.1T and evaluated their effects on tomato germination and seedling growth under salt stress.

title: Association between gastroesophageal reflux disease and stroke: a bidirectional Mendelian randomization study
creator: Decheng Meng, Xin Zhang, Wenfei Yu, Guoliang Yin, Suwen Chen, Hongshuai Liu, Linya Wang, Fengxia Zhang
description: ObjectiveSome previous studies have suggested a potential link between stroke and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). We used a two-sample bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR) method to explore the causal relationship between stroke and GERD.DesignSummary-level data derived from the published genome-wide association studies (GWAS) were employed for analyses.

title: A Pilot Randomized Study of NAT2 and YEATS4 Pharmacogenetic Return of Results in Adults with Hypertension and African Ancestry: The GUARDD‐US PGx Study
creator: Philip E. Empey, Nita A. Limdi, Dinushika Mohottige, Kady‐Ann Steen‐Burrell, Hrishikesh Chakraborty, Khoa A. Nguyen, Alexander S. Parker, Emily J. Cicali, Girish N. Nadkarni, Michelle A. Ramos, Sabrina Clermont, Erica N. Elwood, Mimsie Robinson, Nandini Shroff, Marc B. Rosenman, Ronald Huang, Larisa
description: Almost half of individuals with hypertension fail to achieve recommended blood pressure (BP) goals. Pharmacogenetic gene‐drug interactions may alter the efficacy of antihypertensive agents. We conducted a multicenter randomized controlled sub‐study of participants (N = 1874) with hypertension and self‐reported African ancestry to determine whether pharmacogenetic return of results (RoR) would improve systolic blood pressure (SBP) at 3 months.

title: Intracellular microbial shifts during COVID-19 infection and longitudinal recovery revealed by single-cell RNA sequencing
creator: Jyoti Soni, Raiyan Ali, Partha Chattopadhyay, Priti Devi, Priyanka Mehta, Aanchal Yadav, Akshat Jaiswal, Bansidhar Tarai, Sandeep Budhiraja, Rajesh Pandey
description: SummaryHost-microbe dynamics during SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant infection and recovery remain poorly understood, particularly regarding intracellular microbial communities in immune cells. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing of 191,417 peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from 57 individuals (9 healthy, 24 Omicron-infected, 16 recently recovered, 8 long-recovered) using the BD Rhapsody platform.

title: Genetic and genomic insights into morphological defects in nellore cattle: a comprehensive review
creator: Milena Aparecida Ferreira Campos, Hinayah Rojas de Oliveira, Louise Sarmento Martins de Oliveira, Henrique Alberto Mulim, Eduarda da Silva Oliveira, Gregorio M F de Camargo, Raphael Bermal Costa
description: Morphological defects in Nellore cattle, including abnormalities in conformation, feet and legs, navel structure, pigmentation, and craniofacial development, negatively impact productivity, welfare, and long-term herd sustainability. This comprehensive review aimed to synthesize existing genetic and genomic evidence on these defects in purebred Nellore cattle. Studies were identified through searches of Web of Science, PubMed, and SciELO up to September 2025.

title: Afferent innervation of the kidney: projections to and processing in the central nervous system
creator: Brianna Dailey-Krempel, Louise C. Evans, John W. Osborn, Lucy Vulchanova
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). FDA approval for catheter-based renal nerve ablation has sparked renewed interest in the role of renal nerves in hypertension and their potential contribution to other pathophysiologies. While the anti-hypertensive effects of catheter-based renal nerve ablation were thought to be due to the ablation of the sympathetic efferent nerves going to the kidney, preclinical hypertensive rodent studies and unexpected beneficial clinical outcomes have highlighted the renal afferent (sensory) nerves as a contributor to the pathogenesis of hypertension.

title: Strongyloidiasis as a Focal Household Cluster of Soil‐Transmitted Helminthiasis in Rural Tropical Rainforest Southern Thailand: An Observational Study
creator: Attarat Pattanawongsa, Prasit Na-ek, Patthanasak Khammaneechan, Blego Sedionoto, Witthaya Anamnart, Anjali Chauhan
description: BackgroundIn southern Thailand, characterized by high rainfall for 9 months each year (2340 mm annually), hookworm prevalence is consistently higher than that of Strongyloides stercoralis. Such wet climatic conditions may favor hookworm transmission while limiting S. stercoralis. Conversely, living in crowded, cluster settlements may enhance the transmission of S. stercoralis. We aimed to determine whether S.

title: DH2-dependent trans-acting siRNAs regulate leaf and lemma development in rice
creator: Jun Tang, Tianye Li, Yuanzhuo Gao, Xinghang Li, Ziheng Huang, Hui Zhuang, Guanghua He, Hongfa Luo, Yunfeng Li
description: In most crops, the development of lateral organs such as leaves and floral organs plays important roles in the architecture of plants and grains and then determines the yield. Establishment of polarity in these lateral organs is one of the most critical events for their morphogenesis. However, the molecular mechanisms regarding this in rice remain unclear.

title: Regulatory‐Driven Pharmacokinetic and Immunogenicity Study of Siltartoxatug, a Recombinant Native Human Monoclonal Antibody Against Tetanus Toxin, in Cynomolgus Monkeys
creator: Xia Zhou, Fei Zhou, Zhenpeng Fu, Weijun Ye, Guo Li, Jason Li, Weihong Zheng, Hua-Xin Liao, Shaojie Wang, Xiaoyi Liu
description: Siltartoxatug—developed by Trinomab Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., using its proprietary HitmAb® platform—is the first‐in‐class recombinant monoclonal antibody drug for urgent prophylaxis of tetanus approved by China National Medical Products Administration in February 2025, which addresses the critical unmet need to substitute blood‐derived passive immunization preparations for prevention of tetanus.

title: Spatiotemporal patterns and optimization of dominant and recessive morphology of cultivated land use in the Ili River Valley
creator: Chunmei Zhou, Lihua Fu, Hui Xiang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryIn recent years, the rapid expansion and functional degradation of cultivated land have intensified the pressure on this crucial resource, and the protection of cultivated land needs urgent attention. Based on an integrated view of dominant and recessive, combined with landscape index selection, spatial mapping method, kernel density estimation, and coupling coordination degree, this study examines the spatiotemporal changes in cultivated land in the Ili River Valley from 2005 to 2020 and proposes optimization strategies.

title: Correction to “Growth‐Associated Protein 43 Levels in the Cerebrospinal Fluid Correspond to the Cerebral Blood Flow Alterations in Alzheimer's Dementia Continuum: An Original Study”
creator: Unknown
description: 70534. https://doi.org/10.1002/hsr2.70534 The following corrections have been made: the author list has been updated to remove researchers who were incorrectly listed as authors. The Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Database has been added as an author, with further explanation provided in the Acknowledgements. The authors have provided new details on the units and values in Table 1.

title: Development of a method and an assessment construct for person-centered translation of dementia public stigma scales
creator: Junfeng Lu, Yi Shan, Meng Ji, Lee-Fay Low, Sarang Kim, Annica Barcenilla-Wong, Sam Shen, Weiwei Chu
description: BackgroundWith the number of people with dementia dramatically increasing over time and dementia becoming a major health concern worldwide, scales have been developed to assess the stigma socially attached to this neurodegenerative disorder. There are, however, almost no available methods and assessment constructs for person-centered translation of dementia public stigma scales.

title: 1-Deoxynojirimycin with theaflavins ameliorates high-fat diet-induced insulin resistance in mice by modulating the gut microbiota
creator: Qiannan Di, Ting Yang, Yiwen Zhao, Wenqing Li, Chunbo Qu, Jingyi Zhang, Yichun Zhu, Chenyang Song, Lixin Na
description: BackgroundThis study investigated the ameliorative effects of combined 1-DNJ and TFs on IR in mice through gut microbiota modulation.MethodsAn HFD-induced IR model was established in male mice, which were subsequently divided into Control, Model, 1-DNJ (200 mg/kg·bw/day), TFs (100 mg/kg·bw/day), and 1-DNJ + TFs (200 + 100 mg/kg·bw/day) groups for daily oral administration over 11 consecutive weeks.

title: Climate resilient rubber cultivation zoning via species distribution and spatial optimization
creator: Guangxi Yang, Bihan Zhao, Yan Zhang, Longyu Sui, Jiazhen Zhang, Li Tian, Weihao Yang, Huabo Du, Shichuan Yu
description: SummaryClimate change is reshaping the geographic envelope of rubber cultivation in China, creating risks of maladaptation from ill-informed expansion or abandonment of viable regions. We compared five species distribution models (GLM, RF, BRT, MaxNet, and MaxEnt) under identical samples and spatial cross-validation, then projected suitability to 2100 under CMIP6 scenarios. MaxEnt demonstrated the highest accuracy and transferability (AUC 0.

title: Refractory Anti‐HMGCR Necrotizing Myopathy With Progressive Hypercapnic Respiratory Failure Responsive to a JAK Inhibitor
creator: N Huang, T B George, L Christopher-Stine, A Nicolas, C Oddis, D P Ascherman, V M Liarski, Ankit Dhoundiyal
description: Immune‐mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) associated with 3‐hydroxy‐3‐methylglutaryl‐coenzyme A reductase (HMGCR) antibodies is a rare condition often associated with statin use. It typically presents with proximal weakness and markedly elevated creatine phosphokinase (CPK) levels and is often refractory, requiring long‐term immunotherapy. Respiratory involvement is uncommon but can be life‐threatening.

title: Lysozyme revisited: evaluating models of a reference protein in structural biology
creator: Alexander Wlodawer, Pawel Rubach, Zbigniew Dauter, Wojciech Dec, Dariusz Brzezinski, Mariusz Jaskolski, Wladek Minor
description: We have evaluated the quality of over 1200 crystal structures of hen egg-white lysozyme (HEWL) deposited in the Protein Data Bank (PDB). These structures, collected over nearly 50 years, vary in quality, despite all representing essentially the same small enzyme consisting of 129 amino acid residues.

title: Factors associated with early death from de novo metastatic breast cancer in Ontario, Canada
creator: Priya Thomas, Brooke Carter, Craig C Earle, Salimah Z Shariff, Jacques Raphael, Alyson Mahar, Sarah Knowles, Muriel Brackstone, Michael Lock, Andrea Eisen, Areej Hezam, Phillip S Blanchette
description: Background:Early death from female breast cancer is influenced by disease biology and factors such as age, marginalization, socioeconomic status, rurality, and access to primary care. Our objective was to investigate factors associated with early death in the subgroup of patients diagnosed with advanced de novo metastatic breast cancer, defined by the presence of distant metastatic disease at initial presentation.

title: De novo activating GUCY2C variant with prenatal bowel dilatation, neonatal functional obstruction, and reversible intestinal failure: A case report
creator: Michele Maria Cantagalli, Tommaso Amato, Sofia Chioccioli, Riccardo Coletta, Antonino Morabito
description: BackgroundActivating variants in GUCY2C increase cyclic GMP signaling in enterocytes, driving chloride rich luminal secretion and impaired sodium absorption. Affected neonates can present with prenatal bowel dilatation and severe postnatal fluid losses that mimic mechanical obstruction.Case reportWe describe a term male infant with fetal ultrasound and MRI evidence of markedly dilated bowel loops and severe polyhydramnios.

title: A national framework for transition to precision medicine
creator: Samaneh Karimi Esboei, Sepehr Ghazinoory, Fatemeh Saghafi
description: Precision medicine (PM) is transforming healthcare by offering tailored interventions that address individual variability, transforming patient care and outcomes. PM is based on providing health-oriented services according to genetic characteristics, individual and family medical history, lifestyle, place of residence, and other personalized characteristics. This study aims to establish an appropriate framework for implementing PM in Iran.

title: A Novel LAMA5 Variant in Adult‐Onset Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis: A Case Report
creator: Randah Abdullah Dahlan, Roaa Hani Fairoozy, Neetu Rawal
description: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) is a common histopathological diagnosis among adult patients presenting with nephrotic syndrome. This pattern is associated with diverse underlying pathophysiological mechanisms, which may influence disease management, therapeutic response, and prognosis. Genetic forms of FSGS are caused by variants in genes encoding proteins expressed in podocytes or the glomerular basement membrane.

title: Outcomes of lynch syndrome endometrial surveillance in the Netherlands
creator: Malcolm Scott, Adam N. Rosenthal
description: ing cancer development. The study lacks data on atypical versus non-atypical hyperplasia, and since a third of general population atypical hyperplasia can coexist with endometrial cancer,2 hysterectomy is usually advised. While non-atypical hyperplasia in Lynch syndrome is poorly understood, only around 5% of non-atypical hyperplasia in the general population progresses to endometrial cancer over 20 years.

title: Evaluation of the efficacy of a novel lumbar exoskeleton with multiple interventions for patients with lumbar disc herniation: a multicenter randomized controlled trial of non-inferiority
creator: Xiaonan Huang, Lele Huang, Lei Shi, Lifan Xu, Chengbing Cao, Heng Wu, Min Cao, Can Lv, Ping Shi, Guohui Zhang, Fanfu Fang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundLumbar disc herniation (LDH) occurs when the nucleus pulposus or annulus fibrosus protrudes into the intervertebral space, potentially compressing nerve roots and causing symptoms such as sciatica, restricted mobility, and lower extremity weakness.

title: Influence of Polishing Treatment on the Topography of 3D‐Printed Provisional Resins: An In Vitro Study
creator: Yousif A Al-Dulaijan, Abdulrahman Mohammad Aldossari, Abdulrahman Salem Bin-jabair, Hamed S Alghamdi, Hanan Al-Johani, Abdulrahman A Balhaddad, Murilo Baena Lopes
description: Although 3D‐printing has been increasingly integrated in the fabrication of provisional restorations, the evidence regarding the impact of different polishing regimens on their topographical features is unclear. This in vitro study assessed the outcomes of different polishing treatments on roughness measurements of 3D‐printed provisional resin materials compared to that of a conventional polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA).

title: Nanobodies: a promising approach to treatment of viral diseases
creator: Vitória Meneghetti Minatel, Carlos Roberto Prudencio, Benedito Barraviera, Rui Seabra Ferreira
description: Since their discovery in the 1990s, heavy chain antibodies have garnered significant interest in the scientific community. These antibodies, found in camelids such as llamas and alpacas, exhibit distinct characteristics from conventional antibodies due to the absence of a light chain in their structure. Furthermore, they possess a single antigen-binding domain known as VHH or Nanobody (Nb).

title: Primary care experiences at the intersection of sexual minority status and long-term mental health conditions in England: a cross-sectional analysis using the English General Practice Patient Survey
creator: Arthur Gomes-Mendes, Sally McManus, Els van der Ven, Danai Dima, Anne-Kathrin Fett
description: SummaryBackgroundSexual minorities and individuals with mental health conditions (MHC) often report poorer healthcare experiences, but evidence on inequalities at their intersection remains limited.MethodsWe analysed data from 1,277,383 respondents to the 2022–23 English General Practice Patient Survey using survey-weighted logistic regressions.

title: Transient ischemic attack in the twenty first century: is it still a useful construct?
creator: Louis R. Caplan
description: Some argue that the term transient ischemic attack (TIA) has become obsolete in the current age of advanced modern technology. Let us look back and analyze the term, its support and detraction, and its potential continued usefulness. The best way to begin is a review of the history of the term.

title: Multivariate phenotyping reveals thermoregulatory patterns in crossbred cattle
creator: Robson Mateus Freitas Silveira, Isadora Emanoela Pereira Costa Andrade, Luciano Barreto-Mendes, Larissa de Melo Coelho, Concepta McManus, Luiz Paulo Fávero, Débora Andrea Evangelista Façanha
description: Improving the adaptation of beef cattle production to climate change requires crossbreeding strategies that enhance the ability of animals to maintain thermal stability under hot conditions. The objective of this exploratory study was to assess how coat characteristics are associated with rectal-temperature variation and to identify thermoregulatory patterns in Red Angus × Nelore crossbred cattle raised under tropical conditions.

title: The secreted host-cell protein clusterin interacts with PmpD and promotes Chlamydia trachomatis infection
creator: Fabienne Kocher, Johannes H. Hegemann
description: Attachment and uptake into host cells are pivotal steps in the life cycle of the Chlamydiaceae, a family of obligate intracellular pathogens. Chlamydia trachomatis (Ctr) possesses a family of nine polymorphic membrane proteins (Pmps), which have been shown to be crucial for adhesion and internalization. However, the host-cell molecules involved have so far remained unknown.

title: Vitamin D and antimicrobial peptides in skin health and disease: Mechanisms and therapeutic potential
creator: Hanlin Gao, Jianwei Zhu, Zhi Chen, Gang Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). As the body's frontline barrier against the external environment, the skin maintains homeostasis through a complex network of innate defense factors, among which antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) play pivotal roles in pathogen defense, inflammation regulation, and tissue repair. Apart from its classical role in bone metabolism, Vitamin D has been shown, mainly in experimental and translational studies, to modulate the expression and processing of selected AMPs through VDR-dependent and non-classical pathways.

title: Breeder age outweighs egg grading method on hatchability and chick quality in broiler hatcheries
creator: Jumara Coelho Ticiano, Roberto Carlos de Freitas, Luzianna Macedo Fonseca, Dauisia Corsino de Souza, Robson Mateus Freitas Silveira, Lúcio Francelino de Araújo, Arele Arlindo Calderano
description: Incubation efficiency and chick health are fundamentally linked to fertile egg quality, which is influenced by both grading methods and breeder age. This study evaluated the effects of manual versus automated grading and Cobb breeder age (28–42, 43–56, and 57–70 weeks) on hatchability, chick quality, and embryonic mortality.

title: Experimental determination of effective X-ray attenuation coefficients of 3D-printed materials under clinical mammography spectra
creator: Adrián Belarra, Irene Hernández-Girón, Julia Garayoa, Luis Carlos Martínez, Julio Valverde, María José Rot, Alejandro Ferrando, Antonio Martín, Margarita Chevalier
description: Background3D printing enables the fabrication of customized breast phantoms for image quality assessment in digital mammography (DM) and digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT). A major challenge is the absence of standardized, accessible methods to characterize the attenuation properties of 3D-printed materials under clinical DM/DBT spectra.

title: Natural deep eutectic solvents-based green extraction of vanillin: optimization, purification, and bioactivity assessment
creator: Lingxia Xu, Fakhra Liaqat, Mahammed Ilyas Khazi, Jianzhong Sun, Daochen Zhu
description: The sustainable extraction of natural compounds has recently attracted significant attention. The extraction of high-quality natural vanillin in active form is crucial for its efficient use in various industries, but conventional solvents are not suitable for this purpose. The flammability, volatility, and toxicity of organic solvents can harm extraction personnel, and their waste liquid can cause environmental pollution.

title: Diagnostic performance and pathologic associations of the UroVysion assay in patients with upper tract lesions and negative urinary cytology: a large-scale real-world study of 1,256 patients
creator: Longtao Zheng, Bao Guan, Zheng Wu, Yi Ding, Bei Zhang, Xuesong Li, Yanqing Gong
description: Purpose The UroVysion assay is widely used for diagnosing upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC), but its value in patients with negative urinary cytology remains unclear. This study evaluated its diagnostic performance and pathological associations in this specific population.Methods This retrospective study included 1,256 patients with upper tract lesions on imaging, negative urinary cytology, and preoperative UroVysion testing.

title: Transcriptomic signatures of synaptic loss in Alzheimer’s disease
creator: Lipeng Sun, Xinyuan Yang, Xiaomeng Xu, Lin Kang, Yingting Zheng, Qi Huang, Wei Xu, Yihui Guan, Yiwen Shen, Jun Liu, Yulei Deng, Shu Liu, Junfang Zhang, Fang Xie, Binyin Li
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummarySynaptic loss is a major pathological cause of cognitive impairment in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). We integrated in vivo synaptic density imaging using synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2A positron emission tomography (PET) from a prospective AD cohort with brain transcriptomic data. Partial least squares analysis identified 1,233 genes associated with synaptic loss, enriched for synaptic organization, Tau phosphorylation, cytoskeletal integrity, and ubiquitin-mediated protein degradation. Cell-type enrichment showed downregulation in glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons and upregulation in oligodendrocytes and endothelial cells.

title: Macular: a multi-scale simulation platform for the retina and the primary visual system
creator: Bruno Cessac, Erwan Demairy, Jérôme Emonet, Evgenia Kartsaki, Thibaud Kloczko, Côme Le Breton, Nicolas Niclausse, Selma Souihel, Jean-Luc Szpyrka, Julien Wintz
