ObjectiveThe study aimed to establish the relationship between attitudes towards persons with disabilities and personality traits among Polish students, and whether sociodemographic factors moderate this.MethodsA cross-sectional self-report online survey was conducted on 595 Polish students, aged 18–29, from different fields of study: 1) natural science and engineering technology; 2) social science and humanities; 3) medical and health sciences; 4) law, economics, and management.

title: Clinical experience with remote programming of cardiac implantable electronic devices
creator: Karthik Venkatesh Prasad, Marko Tietz, Bobak Salehi, Crystal Miller, Peter Kabus, David Hayes
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAs remote monitoring has become the standard of care for follow-up of cardiac implantable cardiac devices, extensions of remote monitoring can provide greater efficiency for the patient, caregiver, and industry representatives. To accomplish greater efficiency and flexibility of remote monitoring, and as an interim step toward "true" remote monitoring, LiveSupport was introduced as an innovative programmer and software solution that allows for remote programming of all current and most legacy BIOTRONIK devices.ObjectiveTo determine the utilization and efficacy of LiveSupport as an extension

title: Prescribing Trends of Osteoporosis Medications, Adherence and Persistence with Denosumab versus Alendronate: A Real-World Retrospective Study in China
creator: Jun Chen, Yuliang Huang, Puqing Liu, Lei Fan
description: IntroductionOsteoporosis, a common metabolic bone disease with high fracture risk and heavy global burden, requires long-term medication adherence and persistence for fracture prevention, yet both remain suboptimal. Prescribing trends, adherence, and persistence data for denosumab and alendronate remain limited, especially in Chinese populations.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study used hospital data.

title: A Self-Regenerating Mixed-Valence FeOx-TiO2 Nanoplatform for Mitochondrion-Targeted Triple-Modal Cancer Therapy
creator: Yongzhi Xia, Mengqin Wang, Yanyan Zhou, Ruiqi Wei, Yijie Wang, Lijuan Hua, Qiang Fang, Yan Chen
description: PurposeReactive oxygen species (ROS) cancer therapy is limited by short ROS lifetime, restricted diffusion, and lack of subcellular targeting. Current approaches physically mix independent components, causing complexity and decoupled actions. To overcome these barriers, we developed a mitochondrion-targeted nanoplatform (FTDT) built on a FeOₓ-TiO2 composite core with intrinsic mixed-valence Fe2⁺/Fe3⁺ pairs.

title: Knowledge Graphs for Cervical Cancer Across the Care Continuum: From Vaccination and Screening to Personalized Therapy
creator: Jiyan Leng, Wenzhi Wei, Xiaohua Wen, Shan Lu, Yanru Liu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cervical cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related death among women worldwide, with a disproportionately high burden in low- and middle-income countries. Infection with human papillomavirus (HPV) is the central etiological factor. Although HPV vaccination and standardized screening can substantially reduce incidence and mortality, major bottlenecks persist in real-world settings, including inadequate coverage, loss to follow-up, data silos, and limited interpretability of algorithms.

title: Causal Effects of Inflammatory Proteins and Metabolites on Skin Soft Tissue Infections: Mendelian Randomization and Mediation Analysis
creator: Jie Tang, Yi Chen, Yueru Ji, Xiao Zhang, Weiwei Qin, Zhuo Wan
description: IntroductionThe pathogenesis of skin and soft tissue infections (SSTIs) remains incompletely understood, particularly regarding the causal relationships between circulating inflammatory proteins (CIPs), metabolites, and infection susceptibility. Mendelian randomization (MR) provides an approach to investigate potential causal associations while reducing confounding and reverse causation.MethodsWe conducted a bidirectional two-sample MR study integrating proteomic and metabolomic data.

title: Cytokine- and Airflow-Based Clustering Identifies COPD Phenotypes with Differing Quantitative CT Features
creator: Qing Wang, Yinan Yao, Mengling Xia, Jingyang Huang, Xinhong Huang, Yuan Ye, Jianya Zhou
description: IntroductionChronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a heterogeneous disease with distinct inflammatory profiles that may be associated with key pathological features, including emphysema and airway wall remodeling. This study aimed to identify COPD subgroups based on circulating pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokine activity and airflow limitation and to examine their clinical, physiological, and quantitative CT characteristics.

title: Optimization of Anticoagulation Strategy During Cardiopulmonary Bypass in Neonates with Congenital Heart Disease: A Randomized Controlled Trial
creator: He Wang, Qindong Liu, Peng Gao, Jia Liu, Yu Jin, Tianyu Gao, Wenting Wang, Dabuxilite Bayartaikishigtai, Yang Zhang, Jinping Liu
description: PurposeNeonatal hemostatic immaturity complicates anticoagulation during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). Current practice largely follows the strategy of 400 U/kg from adult protocols, as neonatal-specific guidelines and high-quality evidence remain lacking, which frequently fails to achieve adequate anticoagulation. This single-center randomized controlled trial evaluated the initial heparin dose of 600 U/kg to refine neonatal CPB anticoagulation.

title: Screening for Early Endometriosis Detection (SEED): Co-development of a Symptom-Based Screening Measure for Canadian Young Adults in Primary Care
creator: Rachael Bosma, Brittany N. Rosenbloom, Adriano Nella, Lindsay Wolfson, Mathew Leonardi, Magali Robert, M. Jonathon Solnik, Arun Radhakrishnan, Katelynn E. Boerner, Philippa Bridge-Cook, Katelyn Luciani, Tania Di Renna
description: BackgroundMany Canadians experience prolonged pain, uncertainty, and stigma before receiving an endometriosis diagnosis, with delays averaging 11 years from symptom onset. Endometriosis, defined by the presence of endometrial-like tissue outside the uterine cavity, impacts 10% of Canadian women and approximately 9% of transgender men.

title: A novel nanoparticle-based co-delivery system of Fritillaria persica L. extract and gemcitabine for inhibiting breast cancer progression
creator: Reyhaneh Arefimehr, Mehrad Zibaei Moghadam, Negar Jamshidi, Nazanin Jamshidi, Yohann Corvis
description: Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, highlighting the urgent need for more effective and less toxic therapeutic strategies. In the present study, a novel nanotherapeutic platform composed of aqueous Fritillaria persica L. (FP) extract and gemcitabine (Gem)-loaded chitosan (CS) nanoparticles (FP/Gem/CS-NPs) was successfully developed and evaluated against MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cell lines.

title: SURVEY BEHAVIOR AND COGNITION ACROSS THE LIFE COURSE: EVIDENCE FROM THE PANEL STUDY OF INCOME DYNAMICS
creator: MALAK B. KALASHO, ESTHER M. FRIEDMAN, THOMAS F. CROSSLEY
description: Cognitive abilities across adulthood are important pre-cursors to dementia. The primary way to capture cognitive abilities is via expensive and time-consuming standardized cognitive tests. We explore the extent to which cognition can be inferred from indicators of survey response behavior (SRB), such as the time to complete a questionnaire and the incidence of contradictory responses.

title: Response to the Correspondence Regarding “Cutaneous Metastasis From Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma Eight Years After Initial Surgery”
creator: Yi‐Qing Gao, Xin‐Lu Yin, Lu‐Ying Zheng, Jia‐Dong Wang
description: We sincerely thank Dr. Sengul and colleagues for their insightful comments on our case report of skin metastasis in papillary thyroid cancer (PTC). They questioned the adequacy of local excision and suggested completion thyroidectomy to enable radioactive iodine (RAI) therapy or systemic therapy.

title: The PIEZO1/CISD1/IP3R Mechanotransduction Axis Drives Macrophage Mitochondrial Dysfunction and Inflammatory Activation in Pulmonary Fibrosis
creator: Yungeng Wei, Chao Xie, Xiangsheng Yang, Xiao Xiao Tang
description: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive and fatal interstitial lung disease characterized by excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition and elevated tissue stiffness. While aberrant mechanotransduction is increasingly recognized as a key driver of fibrotic progression, the mechanisms by which mechanical cues orchestrate macrophage dysfunction remain poorly elucidated.

title: Middle Cerebral Artery Occlusion-induced Deficits in Fine Skilled Motor Movement and Its Recovery Following Combined Treatment with Sodium Valproate and CIMT
creator: Rini PG, Yoganarasimha Doreswamy, Laxmi TR
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPreclinical studies have shown that sodium valproic acid (VPA) has neuroprotective properties following ischaemic injury. However, its compatibility as an adjuvant therapy with physical rehabilitation in ischaemic stroke recovery, with underlying neurophysiological mechanisms, has not been explored yet.PurposeThe present study has investigated the advantage of combination therapy over monotherapy in ameliorating ischaemic stroke-induced deficits in skilled fine motor movements with associated changes in local and interhemispheric neural connectivity.MethodsCerebral ischaemic stroke was induced by 60 min of middle cerebral artery occlusion in adult

title: Perspectives and experiences of nurse academics teaching reflective practice to undergraduate Bachelor of Nursing students: a scoping review
creator: Lisa Speedie, Gulzar Malik, Jacqueline Johnston, Christine East
description: Background:Reflective practice is essential in nursing education, as it promotes critical thinking and fosters professional growth. Although it is acknowledged in higher education and included in university attributes, the perspectives and experiences of nurse academics who teach it remain underexplored.

title: Optimizing Clinical Temporal Relation Extraction With Large Language Models: Comparative Analysis
creator: Jianping He, Zenan Sun, Laila Rasmy, Haifang Li, Jianfu Li, Evan Yu, Degui Zhi, Cui Tao, Arriel Benis
description: BackgroundClinical temporal relation extraction (CTRE) is essential for reconstructing patient timelines from unstructured electronic health records (EHRs). However, the linguistic complexity of clinical notes and the high cost of expert annotation impede the development of large-scale training corpora. While large language models (LLMs) have transformed general natural language processing, their application to CTRE remains underexplored.

title: Overcoming the nuclear barrier in nonviral gene therapy: mechanisms, carrier design, and translational perspectives on NLS peptide and DNA targeting sequence strategies
creator: Taegeun Lee, Ye-Rin Kim, Euijin Lee, Sae-Ock Oh
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Efficient delivery of plasmid DNA (pDNA) into the nucleus remains a major bottleneck in nonviral gene therapy, particularly in post-mitotic and slowly dividing cells where the nuclear envelope constitutes a permanent barrier to passive entry. This review considers the two main strategies for active nuclear targeting: nuclear localisation signal (NLS) peptides, which recruit importin-α/β receptors directly to DNA cargo, and DNA nuclear targeting sequences (DTS), which exploit NLS-bearing transcription factors to mediate piggyback nuclear import.

title: Network pharmacology–driven identification of PTP1β and rational design of simufilam-based allosteric inhibitors for neuroprotection in Alzheimer’s disease
creator: Vishnu Malakar, Rajeshkumar Raman, Antony Justin, Dhanabal SP, Dhritiman Roy, Chandi C Malakar, Dipen Purohit, Pratap Chand Mali
description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that predominantly affects elderly people and is characterized by cognitive decline and dementia. Protein tyrosine phosphatase-1B (PTP1B) is known to modulate pro-inflammatory mediators, and its overexpression in the brain has been implicated in AD-associated neuroinflammation.

title: Colitis-associated colorectal carcinogenesis: molecular mechanisms and therapeutic potential
creator: Yi Lu, Xixi Wang, Cuike Yin, Jiaxuan Wang, Shaoqing Guo, Zihan Wang, Jing Zhou, Mengyuan Cui, Xiaoxia Cheng, Lei Zhang, Changjiang Qin
description: Chronic colitis is a major risk factor for colorectal cancer (CRC), particularly for colitis-associated colorectal cancer (CAC), where persistent inflammation drives the transition from mucosal injury to malignant transformation. Accumulating evidence indicates that gut microbiota dysbiosis, epithelial barrier disruption, microbial translocation, chronic immune activation, and aberrant inflammatory signaling collectively contribute to CAC initiation and progression.

title: Improved Skills for Predicting Sub‐Seasonal to Seasonal Global Sea Surface Temperature
creator: Longhao Wang, Xuanze Zhang, Ruby L. Leung, Francis H. S. Chiew, Amir AghaKouchak, Kairan Ying, Yongqiang Zhang
description: Accurate prediction of global sea surface temperature at sub‐seasonal to seasonal (S2S) timescales is critical for drought and flood forecasting, as well as for improving disaster preparedness in human society. Operational physics‐based numerical models are run to predict S2S sea surface temperature and corresponding climate indices, such as El Niño‐Southern Oscillation.

title: Effect of Dietary Papaya (Carica papaya) Leaf Meal on Growth Performance and Haematological Responses of Nile Tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) Fingerlings Reared in a Recirculating Aquaculture System
creator: Farhabun Binte Farhad, Farzana Yasmin Ritu, Moupia Mustafi, Md. Abdus Salam, Shaharior Hashem
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In the pursuit of sustainable aquaculture, the integration of unconventional plant‐based feed additives like papaya leaf meal (PLM) offers a promising approach for enhancing fish growth while reducing feed costs and environmental impact. To evaluate the efficacy of PLM as a growth promoter, four experimental diets were formulated by gradually incorporating PLM at inclusion levels of 0%, 3%, 6% and 9%.

title: Molecular Landscapes of Tumor Dormancy in Gynecologic Malignancies: From Survival Mechanisms to Precision Interception
creator: Shih‐Hsuan Cheng, Ren‐Wang Peng, Chang‐Cheng Wu, Chi‐Wen Luo, Emmanuel Naveen Raj, Zhi‐Hong Wen, Tzu‐Hung Hsiao, Chia‐Jung Li
description: Late recurrence in gynecologic malignancies is associated with tumor dormancy and persistent minimal residual disease (MRD). Although current treatments reduce proliferating tumor burden, residual cells may survive therapy and drive delayed relapse. This Review examines dormancy in ovarian, endometrial, and cervical cancers using entry, maintenance, and awakening as an organizing framework rather than a universally demonstrated sequence.

title: Ultrasonographic Features of Pleural Thickening in Cats With Pulmonary Carcinoma and Pleural Effusion: A Retrospective Descriptive Study
creator: Atsushi Toshima, Caroline V. Fulkerson, Masahiro Murakami
description: BackgroundPleural involvement is an important but poorly described manifestation of feline pulmonary carcinoma. Thoracic ultrasonography may identify pleural abnormalities and accessible targets for cytologic sampling in cats with pleural effusion.ObjectivesTo describe ultrasonographic features of pleural thickening in cats with pulmonary carcinoma and pleural effusion and summarise cytologic findings from pleural effusion and ultrasound‐guided lesion sampling.

title: Increasing mobility while in hospital after hip fracture: even the best evidence may not translate to all national health services
creator: Nicola Maffulli, Fabrizio Rivera, Giovanna Truda, Filippo Migliorini, Francesco Oliva
description: Hip fracture rehabilitation is strongly influenced by the healthcare system in which postoperative care is delivered. The WHiTE 15: INITIATE trial represents an important pragmatic attempt to determine whether increasing the frequency and duration of in-hospital physiotherapy after hip fracture improves days at home within 30 days of admission.

title: Neuron‐Derived Vesicular circMagi1 Restrains Vascular Repair After Ischemic Stroke by Promoting TRIM65‐Mediated ANXA2 Degradation
creator: Youkun Bi, Qun Liu, Baohua Zou, Wenyuan Wang, Xinlong Qiao, Lin Gao, Chaoxu Miao, Ningning Huang, Shuqing Tang, Rui Guo, Changqing Zeng, Ce Jia, Yuanchao Xue, Xuejun Guo, Jianjun Chen, Huiwen Wang, Guangju Ji
description: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) contribute to stroke pathogenesis, yet their intercellular functions within the ischemic neurovascular unit remain poorly defined. Profiling of plasma extracellular vesicles (EVs) revealed a higher abundance of circMagi1 in patients with acute ischemic stroke compared with healthy controls.

title: Reprogramming tumor cells with LCOR mRNA nanotherapy to enhance immunotherapy
creator: Gabriel Serra‐Mir, Elena Haro‐Martínez, Sandra Blasco‐Benito, Chiara Cannatà, José Ángel Palomeque, Anna López‐Plana, Maria Sanz‐Flores, Marc Sabartés, Cristina Fornaguera, Toni Celià‐Terrassa
description: Transcription factors (TFs) are often considered undruggable due to their structural complexity. mRNA technologies can overcome this therapeutic limitation by enabling dynamic protein replacement therapies. Here, we explore the TF activity of LCOR (Ligand‐dependent corepressor), which suppresses tumor growth, at least in part by inducing the antigen presentation machinery (APM) in tumor cells and constraining cellular plasticity.

title: Co-developing equity-oriented neighbourhood care for children and young people with multiple long-term conditions: a concept mapping study in South London
creator: Nandeeta Samad, Ingrid Wolfe
description: Children and young people (CYP) with multiple long-term conditions (MLTCs) rely on services spanning health, education, and social care, but fragmented pathways may widen inequalities and shift coordination work to families. We aimed to identify priorities for equity-oriented neighbourhood care. We conducted a participatory mixed-methods study informed by the Medical Research Council framework and group concept mapping.

title: Clinical examination findings were not associated with isometric strength or functional performance in adults with groin pain
creator: Matheus Oliveira Branco, Tamiris Beppler Martins, Guilherme Vinicius da Costa, Vitor Mateus Madruga de Sousa, Alan Immich, Kaue Bertoto Dutra, Filippo Migliorini, Nicola Maffulli, Rodrigo Okubo
description: ObjectivesThe aim of this study was to investigate whether positive clinical examination findings were associated with selected measures of lower-limb isometric strength or functional performance in physically active adults with groin pain.MethodsThis was a cross-sectional, observational and exploratory study with blinded outcome assessment.

title: Comparative characterization and anti Helicobacter pylori activity of green synthesized silver nanoparticles from red and yellow fruited Ficus carica L. leaf extracts
creator: Hamda Al Jabri, Shaik Nyamathulla, Najihah Mohd Hashim, Lip Yong Chung, Saima Farooq, Zakira Naureen, Issa Sulaiman Al Amri, Sobia Ahsan Halim, Ajmal Khan, Mohammad Kamal Hossain, Ahmed Al Harrasi, Lebea N Nthunya, Amal Al Hinai, Zaaima Al Jabri
description: BackgroundGreen synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) using plant extracts offers an eco-friendly and sustainable approach for developing novel antimicrobial agents. Ficus carica L. leaf extract (FcLE), rich in bioactive phytochemicals, has potential as a natural reducing and stabilizing agent. This study aimed to comparatively evaluate AgNPs synthesized from yellow- and red-fruited F. carica L.

title: Revisiting Identification Thresholds of Specific Learning Disorders (SLD) in Gifted Children (GC). A Comparison of Three Groups: Twice‐Exceptional (TE) Children, GC Without SLD and Non‐GC With SLD
creator: Laurent Lesecq, Laurent Querne, Julie Gornes, Laura Buffo, Louise Corbel, Loïse Perrais, Maëlys Kartner, Anne Gaelle Le Moing, Beatrice Bourdin, Patrick Berquin
description: This study investigates assessment of Specific Learning Disorders (SLD) in Twice‐Exceptional (TE) children, gifted children (GC) who also present SLD, in oral and written language domains. Applying the standard threshold for identification (< 7th percentile) to GC often results in the assessment and identification of SLD in the TE population, thereby limiting access to appropriate support.

title: The cognitive-behavioral missing link in myotonic dystrophy type 1: Rethinking social cognition assessment
creator: Emanuele Maria Costantini, Silvi Cadri, Alice Ciattaglia, Michela Coccia, Valeria A. Sansone
description: BackgroundMyotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1) is associated with central nervous system involvement and cognitive–behavioral alterations, including deficits in social cognition. However, standard neuropsychological assessments based on accuracy may underestimate clinically relevant dysfunction.ObjectivesTo determine whether task completion times provide a more sensitive index of social-cognitive performance than accuracy-based metrics in DM1.

title: Functionally declining microbiota in chronic disease: beyond taxonomic loss
creator: Heenam Stanley Kim
description: Microbiota deterioration in modern human populations has been linked to chronic disease, and taxonomic profiling is increasingly used to understand, diagnose, and guide treatment. Yet such profiles do not fully capture disease-relevant microbiota states. I propose functional decline within retained taxa as a distinct axis of microbiota deterioration, complementary to taxonomic loss.

title: Rabies and rabies prophylaxis in Egypt: a nationwide cross-sectional study that calls for action
creator: Mohamed Basyouni Helal, Mohamed Ahmed Saeda, Ahmed Gamal Elshaar, Mohamed Elsayed Zayed, Ali M. Abdelaziz, Omnia M. Mostafa, Enas Sherif Adwy, Ahmed Barakat, Ibrahim Mohammed Abdelkader, Basma Amir Eldawody, Noor Maged Badrawy Ahmed, Mohanned Noah, Ashraf Aboismail, Abdelrahman Mohamed Mahmoud, Abda
description: BackgroundRabies is a fatal but preventable viral disease that poses a global health threat, especially in developing countries. Despite the high incidence of animal bites reported annually in Egypt, limited data exist regarding the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of the general population toward rabies and rabies prophylaxis.

title: Impact of Dimethyl Sulfoxide on Early Cardiotoxicity After Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation
creator: V Lábska, B Mladosievičová, J Dúbrava, B Žiaková, K Nemergutová, L Sopko, J Lukáš, Ľ Harvanová
description: During the COVID-19 pandemic, the use of cryopreserved grafts in allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) increased substantially. Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), used as a cryoprotective agent, is well recognized for its infusion-related toxicity; however, its impact on cardiac function remains unclear. Methods: This prospective study included 96 consecutive patients (median age 46 years) undergoing allogeneic HSCT.

title: Isolation and Identification of Staphylococcus Species From Mastitic Dairy Cows and Associated Risk Factors in and Around Bahir Dar, Ethiopia
creator: Dessie Debeb Getahun, Habtamu Tassew Tarekegn, Bizuneh Tsehayneh Azene, Laikemariam Teshome Abebe, Mequanint Addisu Belete, Tesfaye Sisay Tessema
description: BackgroundBovine mastitis remains one of the most frequent and costly diseases affecting dairy cattle, with significant impacts on health, welfare, and productivity. Staphylococcus species are among the major pathogens responsible for bovine mastitis, leading to reduced milk yield and posing a potential risk to public health.

title: Re: GSJ-26-1985 - Interlaminar Contralateral Endoscopic Foraminotomy Reduces Postoperative Dysesthesia in Patients With Degenerative Lumbar Deformity: A Multicenter Comparative Cohort Study
creator: Facundo Van Isseldyk
description: (new-onset burning leg pain occurring 3 to 7 days after surgery) and the reported onset range (2 to 6 days) in the TELF group. We have reviewed the source data and confirm that one patient (Patient 11, TELF group) had a symptom onset documented on postoperative day 2, which falls outside the stated 3 to 7 day window.

title: Behavior of Crystalline Water During Cation Adsorption and Desorption in Layered Zirconium Phosphate
creator: Masakuni Yamaguchi, Takahiro Toyoshima, Akira Takahashi, Tohru Kawamoto, Hisashi Tanaka
description: This study explores the behavior of crystalline water during the adsorption of Na+, K+, and NH4 + ions onto layered zirconium phosphate (ZrP) using powder X‐ray diffraction (XRD) and thermogravimetric analysis (TG). Cation uptake proceeded via two discrete adsorption steps, each accompanied by distinct structural transformations and water‐related phenomena.

title: Polystyrene nanoplastics induced toxicity in human endothelial cells via atherogenic and autophagy pathways
creator: Banafsheh Yalameha, Cigir Biray Avci, Sara Aghakhani Chegeni, Farhad Rahmanifar, Asghar Khalilnezhad, Mahdi Mahdipour, Elham Shahriyari, Farhad Bani, Adel Feizi, Reza Rahbarghazi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPolystyrene nanoplastics (PS NPs) pollution poses an emerging threat to the ecosystem and human health owing to their physicochemical properties. Excessive exposure to PS NPs can disrupt the cardiovascular system, especially the function of endothelial cells (ECs). Given the potential pathological significance of particles, the present study aimed to investigate the cytotoxic effects of PS NPs on ECs in in vitro and ex ovo models, as well as their underlying mechanisms.MethodsPS NPs were characterized using DLS, SEM, and FTIR.

title: Pharmacokinetics of Rifapentine and Desacetyl Rifapentine in Maternal Plasma and Breast Milk & Infant Cord Blood and Plasma: A Model‐Based Analysis of Mother–Infant Pairs for Tuberculosis Prevention
creator: Priya Jayachandran, Jyoti S. Mathad, Nan Zhang, Paula Britto, Lubbe Wiesner, Grace Montepiedra, Jennifer Norman, Ellen Townley, Sarah Bradford, Sandesh Patil, Stephanie Popson, Tsungai Chipato, Vanessa Rouzier, Deborah Langat, Amphan Chalermchockcharoentkit, Amita Gupta, Kelly E. Dooley, Radojka Sav
description: IMPAACT 2001 (NCT02651259) evaluated the safety and pharmacokinetics (PK) of once‐weekly isoniazid and rifapentine in pregnant and postpartum women for tuberculosis prevention. Rifapentine (RPT) and desacetyl rifapentine (desRPT) PK data were collected in maternal plasma, breast milk, infant cord blood, and infant plasma.

title: Controlling Epitaxial Zn Growth via Guided Laser Patterning toward High‐Performance 6Ah Aqueous Zn||I2 Batteries
creator: Suyeon Kim, Dongjae Kim, Youngeun Kim, Chaejeong Kim, Myunghyun Ryu, Wooyoung Jin, Hyeokjin Kwon, Kyu‐Nam Jung, Ki Jae Kim, Jong‐Won Lee, Jinhong Lee
description: Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) are attractive for grid‐scale energy storage because of their safety, low cost, and environmental benignity. However, their practical use is limited by interfacial instability at the Zn anode, which induces nonuniform Zn2+ flux, dendritic growth, and parasitic H2 evolution. Herein, we present a laser‐induced surface patterning stategy that guides Zn epitaxial growth through a resistance‐gradient‐driven mechanism.

title: Molecular Rectification: Mechanisms, Modulation Strategies, and Device Realization
creator: Junnan Guo, Shufan Song, Wenhui Fang, Jifeng Tang, Wenhao Li, Weikang Wu, Shishen Yan, Hui Li, Lishu Zhang
description: Molecular rectifiers, as prototypical components of molecular electronics, present unique opportunities for pushing device miniaturization to its ultimate limits. Nevertheless, challenges including limited rectification ratios, insufficient robustness, and poor reproducibility impede their practical deployment. To make molecular rectifiers competitive with silicon‐based devices, it is important to understand the design principles and fabrication methods from both mechanistic and experimental perspectives.

title: A Journey in Time: Aesthetic Surgery Research Evolution and Aesthetic Surgery Journal
creator: Ivona Percec, Yucel Akgul, Sebastian Cotofana, Anand Deva, Afshin Mosahebi
description: linical and basic science research in aesthetic surgery. The Research section of the journal was founded in 2009, and in the past 16 years, it has undergone tremendous growth, evidenced by the section being ranked #3 for ASJ by way of manuscript submission volume in 2025.

title: Green Nanoparticles in Precision Agriculture: A Critical Review of Smart Crop Management, Nano-Enabled Delivery Systems, and Sustainable Farming
creator: Abisha Meji Marshal Williams, Milon Selvam Dennison, Sarad Pawar Naik Bukke, Bosco Christin Maria Arputham Ashwin
description: Sustainable agricultural production requires approaches that improve resource-use efficiency while limiting environmental burdens. This critical review examines green-synthesized Nanoparticles (NPs) in precision agriculture, covering sustainable synthesis, smart crop management, nano-enabled delivery systems, nano-biosensors, plant-nanoparticle interactions, environmental risks, circular agriculture, and digital technologies.

title: Burnout in Gastrointestinal Endoscopy
creator: Clara Benedetta Conti, Susanne M O’Reilly, Belen Martinez-Moreno, Irina Gabriela Diaconu, Didintle Mokgoko, Malina Wiesand, Preetha Thomas, Daniela Tabacelia, Jennifer Merten, Nada El-Domiaty, Morenike Osundina, Hadil Layka, Annalisa De Silvestri, Marianna Arvanitakis, Cesare Hassan, Amrita Sethi, A
description: Objectives Burnout is underinvestigated in endoscopy. Given the increasing complexity of endoscopic practice, understanding burnout is crucial to addressing the problem and finding possible risk and protective factors. Methods A survey with 38 questions was internationally distributed via professional networks and social media. The survey investigated demographic data, professional experience, mentorship, work–life balance, and burnout.

title: Latent Profiles of Fear of Complications and Associated Factors Among Older Inpatients with Type 2 Diabetes: A Cross-Sectional Study
creator: Jinxian Xu, Juan Gao, Qin Wu, Yuhan Duan, Shuqin Zeng, Jiaqi Liao
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). AimIn the context of diabetes, fear of complications (FoC) refers to a psychological response to the anticipated onset or progression of diabetes-related chronic complications. However, analyses based solely on total scores may conceal the heterogeneity among patients.

title: Phage Therapy as a Self—Replicating Strategy for Besieged Health Systems
creator: Emmanuel Olalere, Sidra Saif, Warda Imran, Faiza Khalid, Dadullah Faiz, Javeria Akhter, Laiba Manzoor, Ashesh Das
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundActive conflict zones and resource-limited health settings face compounding challenges from disrupted antibiotic supply chains concurrent with the proliferation of multidrug-resistant (MDR) and pan-drug-resistant (PDR) pathogens. In such settings, drug availability directly determines clinical outcomes.MethodsA narrative review of the literature was conducted in accordance with adapted SANRA (Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles) criteria, searching PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, and grey literature sources for articles published between 1st January 2001 and 1st April 2026.

title: Nanoparticle-Mediated Brain-Targeted Drug Delivery for Methamphetamine Use Disorder: Advances, Challenges and Translational Perspectives
creator: Xinjie Zhang, Ruike Xu, Min Wang, Yan Du, Miao Zhang, Lihua Li, Genmeng Yang, Shijun Hong
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Methamphetamine use disorder (MUD) poses a significant global health challenge, lacking FDA-approved pharmacotherapies. Despite extensive exploration of therapeutic targets and interventions, effective treatment remains scarce due to challenges in delivering therapeutic agents to relevant brain regions at effective concentrations. Nanoparticle-mediated delivery offers a promising approach for transporting various therapeutic cargos to the central nervous system, including small molecules, nucleic acids, peptides, proteins, and gene-editing systems.

title: Unraveling the Genotype-Phenotype Landscape of Kleefstra Syndrome Through EHMT1 Variant Analysis
creator: Jee Min Kim, Jong Ho Cha, Woojoong Kim, Soo Yeon Kim, Jung Min Ko, Byungchan Lim, Seungbok Lee, Jong-Hee Chae
description: Background and ObjectivesKleefstra syndrome type 1 (KLEFS1) is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder caused by pathogenic variants in EHMT1, which play a key role in epigenetic regulation. Core features include global developmental delay (GDD), intellectual disability (ID), facial dysmorphism, congenital heart defects (CHDs), and neuropsychiatric manifestations.

title: Giant Cystic Lymphangioma of the Transverse Mesocolon in a 7-Year-Old Child: A Case Report
creator: Mohamed Abdullahi Awale, Mariam Hassan Ali, Intisar Ahmed Abdi, Mikail Mohamed Mohamoud, Abdirahman Omar Ahmed, Abdirahman Dahir Hayle, Abdullahi Farah Asseyr
description: BackgroundCystic lymphangiomas are rare benign lymphatic malformations that are usually diagnosed in early childhood. Intra-abdominal lesions are uncommon, and involvement of the transverse mesocolon is particularly rare.Case PresentationA 7-year-old girl presented with a 3–4 week history of vomiting, abdominal pain, progressive abdominal distension, poor appetite, abdominal fullness, generalized weakness, and irregular bowel movements.

title: Improving the Management of Patients’ Own Medications in Hospitalized Older Adults: A Multidisciplinary Before-And-After Intervention Study
creator: Xiaoyan Chen, Lin Liu, Jie Zhang, Linghua Zheng, Xiaona Chen, Mingxia Zhang
description: PurposePatients’ own medications (POMs) may pose safety risks when their use is not integrated into hospital medication-management processes. This study evaluated a multidisciplinary intervention for POM management in hospitalized older adults.Patients and MethodsThis single-center before-and-after intervention study was conducted from March 2024 to February 2025.

title: Acupotomy Alleviates Pain and Attenuates Spinal Neuronal Hyperexcitability in Knee Osteoarthritis Rats: Implication of the CaMKII/GluA1 Axis
creator: Meng Wu, Jinyan Teng, Ziyi Huang, Ruizhe Xu, Xiaoming Gao, Xin Hao, Zhigang Li, Zhaoheng Liu
description: ObjectiveTo investigate the spinal mechanisms underlying the analgesic effects of acupotomy on chronic pain and central sensitization in rats with monosodium iodoacetate (MIA)-induced knee osteoarthritis (KOA).MethodsFollowing MIA-induced KOA and a three-week acupotomy intervention in rats, pain behaviors and joint pathology were assessed. Spinal RNA-sequencing was performed to identify differentially expressed genes.

title: Social and Structural Determinants of Chronic Pain Among Migrant Workers: A Scoping Review Using an Intersectionality Framework
creator: Lise Dassieu, Jacqueline Schneider, Manon Choinière, Nataly Espinoza-Suarez
description: BackgroundDue to structural inequities, many migrant workers face adverse health outcomes potentially exposing them to long-term pain issues. However, the extent of current knowledge on chronic pain (>3 months) in this population is unclear. As labor migration policies evolve toward less protective measures, it is essential to gain insights into the experiences and drivers of chronic pain among migrant workers.

title: A helminth–microbiota metabolic relay promotes disease tolerance
creator: Ruohang Sun, Yi Liu, Yang Wang, Nuo Xu, Xiaoxiao Ma, Qingbo Lv, Xiufeng Zhao, Pascal Boireau, Zeming Wu, Mingyuan Liu, Xiaolei Liu, Xuemin Jin
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Persistent infection by helminths requires limiting inflammatory damage despite incomplete pathogen clearance, yet how helminths mobilize resident microbiota to establish this state remains unclear. Here we identify a cross-kingdom metabolic relay through which Trichinella spiralis promotes systemic disease tolerance. Infection selectively expanded Ligilactobacillus murinus and redirected microbial tryptophan metabolism toward indole-3-lactic acid (ILA), a direct ligand of the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR). Antibiotic perturbation abrogated ILA production, AhR activation and Treg–Th17 remodeling, whereas transfer of helminth-conditioned fecal preparations or supplementation with L.

title: Safety and immunogenicity of a first-generation modified vaccinia virus Ankara-vectored SARS-CoV-2 vaccine candidate with mRNA-based booster vaccination: A phase 1 trial
creator: Anahita Fathi, Christine Dahlke, Leonie Mayer, Sibylle C Mellinghoff, Verena Krähling, Sandro Halwe, Helena Müller-Kräuter, Rolf Fendel, Peter Kremsner, Meral Esen, Martha Klug, Marc Lütgehetmann, Leonie M Weskamm, MVA-SARS-2-S Study Group, Gerd Sutter, Stephan Becker, Svenja Hardtke, Marylyn M Addo
description: The rapid development of effective COVID-19 vaccines was enabled by the parallel assessment of multiple candidates early in the pandemic, including candidates based on the Modified Vaccinia virus Ankara (MVA) vector platform. This Phase 1 trial (NCT04569383) evaluated the MVA-based vaccine candidate MVA-SARS-2-S, expressing the full-length native SARS-CoV-2 spike glycoprotein (Wuhan-HU-1).

title: Biomarkers of subclinical cholestasis predict cancer immunotherapy outcomes
creator: Anne-Laure Mallard de La Varende, Marine Fidelle, Guido Kroemer, Laurence Zitvogel
description: In a recent paper published in Cancer Cell, we identified subclinical cholestasis as an accessible imprint of gut dysbiosis predicting resistance to immune checkpoint blockade. Our work connects γ-glutamyl transferase, bile-acid remodeling, and MAdCAM-1 loss to compromised antitumor immunity, opening avenues for novel biomarker-guided microbiota interventions.

title: Recognising Mild Cognitive Impairment and Early Alzheimer's Disease in General and Psychiatric Practice: Clinical Clues and Appropriate Referral
creator: Kengo Shimoda
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Early cognitive decline may become evident through changes in daily activities or behaviour before it is apparent in a brief consultation. This selective narrative review supports case‐finding and appropriate referral in general and psychiatric practice. Four actions organise the review: identify decline in previously mastered instrumental activities of daily living; recognise new apathy or sustained behavioural change; use a cognitive screen sensitive to mild impairment, such as the Montreal Cognitive Assessment; and refer when clinically meaningful concern remains.

title: Distinct cadmium detoxicity response between rice cultivars carrying functional or loss-of-function OsHMA3 allele
creator: Fuqing Sui, Jing Tian, Ziyuan Yang, Yanzheng Yang, Chang Li, Hongen Liu, Jiali Yan, Peng Zhao
description: Background and aimsPlants encounter various abiotic stress during their growth, making it essential to understand their responses to such challenges. Though function of OsHMA3 in cadmium (Cd) sequestration into rice root vacuoles has been well characterized, little is known about how different OsHMA3 alleles influence plant responses to high Cd exposure.

title: SLC25A4high Hepatocytes Enhance Lifestyle Intervention Response in MASLD by Recruiting Eating Macrophages
creator: Yiting Qian, Linying Lai, Yu Zhang, Yan Meng, Ziping Song, Baoyuan Huang, Guisheng Song, Bo Sun, Wenzhuo Yang
description: While lifestyle interventions (LSI) are the cornerstone of metabolic dysfunction‐associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) management, the molecular mechanisms driving the histological and metabolic regression in LSI‐responsive patients remain unclear. C57BL/6N mice were hydrodynamically injected with Slc25a4 and Sleeping Beauty transposon. Single‐cell RNA sequencing (scRNA‐seq) profiled the hepatic immune landscape. Metabolomics and co‐culture assays analyzed intercellular crosstalk.

title: Who's in the Game? Cross‐Sectional Analysis of Sport Participation in Youth With and Without Disabilities
creator: Natalie H. Stagnone, Andrew Parks, Travis E. Dorsch, Jordan A. Blazo, Tom Farrey, Jon Solomon, Jennifer Brown Lerner
description: BackgroundAlthough participating in youth sports benefits both youth with and without disabilities, those with disabilities are less likely to participate in organized sports than peers without disabilities and little remains known about the specific types of sports or the amount of time youth with disabilities engage.

title: Animal models of anemia of inflammation: Methodological advances, limitations, and translational applications
creator: Jiayi Cheng, Xiaodi Zhou, Qian Liu, Zixian Liu, Hao Wu
description: Anemia of inflammation (AI) represents one of the most prevalent secondary anemias in clinical practice, frequently complicating a wide spectrum of chronic inflammatory diseases. Given its highly heterogeneous etiology and complex pathophysiological mechanisms, the establishment of rational and high‐fidelity animal models is vital for elucidating the core mechanisms of AI and optimizing clinical diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

title: Tobacco Retailer Perspectives on Potential Phase Out of Tobacco Sales in South Australia: An Exploratory Survey
creator: Joshua Trigg, Ella Vallelonga, Chelsea Falso, Ashleigh Guillaumier, Heewon Kang, Jennifer Baldock, Ryan Calabro, Janet Hoek, Coral Gartner
description: Issue AddressedTo examine tobacco retailers' perspectives on the potential phase out of tobacco sales in South Australia, a retail‐based tobacco endgame strategy that directly targets product availability.MethodsA cross‐sectional mixed‐methods survey of licensed tobacco retailers conducted in South Australia in April 2025.

title: Blood Transfusion Rates and Predictive Factors in Posterior-Based Minimally Invasive Scoliosis Surgery for Idiopathic Scoliosis: A LASSO-Based Prediction Model
creator: Hong Jin Kim, Dong Yun Kim, Subin Lim, Hyung-Rae Lee, Jae Hyuk Yang, Seung Woo Suh
description: Study DesignRetrospective cohort study.ObjectivesTo investigate blood transfusion rates in posterior-based minimally invasive scoliosis surgery (MISS) for idiopathic scoliosis (IS) and to develop a prediction model for perioperative blood transfusion.MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed data of 751 patients with IS who underwent posterior-based MISS between 2015 and 2026.

title: Sulfur-incorporated copper catalysts for enhanced ethylene production in membrane electrode assembly CO2 electrolysis
creator: Juho Ha, Hyunki Kim, Seohyeon Jang, Andi Haryanto, Jungmin Yoo, Yeonghye Yun, Sunbeom Ahn, Gyeong Ho Han, Myoung Hwan Oh, Soo Young Kim, Chan Woo Lee, Inho Nam, Sang Hyun Ahn
description: Copper sulfides typically favor formate production in CO2 electrolysis, yet their behavior under membrane electrode assembly (MEA) conditions remains largely uncharted. In this study, CuxS/Cu electrodes with tunable morphologies, including spheres, films, polygons, and cubes, were synthesized, and the surface sulfur content was systematically tuned through electrodeposition followed by controlled sulfidation.

title: Managing and Preventing Placement‐Based Fatigue in Radiography and Allied Health Students: A Narrative Review
creator: Yalindi Binduhewa, Vicki Braithwaite, Therese Gunn
description: Clinical placement plays a key role in the education of allied health students by providing real‐world experiences required to develop professional competence and confidence. For radiography students, extensive unpaid clinical placements form a substantial component of professional training. Despite their educational value, clinical placements expose students to physical, emotional, and financial stressors that may contribute to fatigue.

title: Chemically stabilized long antisense oligonucleotides perturb RNA exosome function
creator: Daniel Tobias Hofacker, Stefanie Gackstatter, Vanessa Deisling, Thorsten Stafforst
description: The interaction with intracellular proteins shapes the pharmacology and toxicity of RNA drugs like gapmers and siRNAs. Here, we identify the RNA exosome as a modification-sensitive interaction partner of long, chemically stabilized, single-stranded RNA drugs. Using proximity biotinylation proteomics, we observe preferential binding of the catalytic exosome subunits DIS3 and EXOSC10 to oligonucleotides stabilized by 2′-ribose modifications and phosphorothioate linkages.

title: PbSnRK1‐Mediated Phosphorylation of PbTCP13 Regulates Glucose‐Responsive Lignin Biosynthesis via PbMYB11 During Pear Stone Cell Formation
creator: Jianan He, Xuxu Wang, Abdul Basit, Wen Li, Jiahui Chao, Wenyu Zhao, Mingxu Niu, Xin Yan, Yuanhui Yu, Kaijie Qi, Zhihua Xie, Shaoling Zhang, Katsuhiro Shiratake, Khanizadeh Shahrokh, Shutian Tao
description: Stone cell lignification is a key determinant of pear fruit texture and commercial quality, and this process has been reported to be tightly coupled to cellular glucose availability. However, how glucose dose‐dependently targets transcription factor phosphorylation during lignin biosynthesis remains largely unknown.

title: RNA base-modification and A-to-I editing landscapes of oxidatively stressed human retinal pigment epithelium under Quantum Molecular Resonance electrotherapy and blood-derived secretome
creator: Domenico Mordà, Simona Alibrandi, Concetta Scimone, Angela D’ascola, Federica Aliquò, Giorgia Abate, Gianantonio Pozzato, Sergio Zaccaria Scalinci, Rosalia D’angelo, Antonina Sidoti, Luigi Donato
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Chemical modifications of RNA bases and adenosine-to-inosine (A-to-I) editing are regulatory layers essentially unexplored in the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), whose oxidative dysfunction underlies age-related macular degeneration. We mapped both layers in ARPE-19 cells exposed to tert-butyl hydroperoxide under two non-pharmacological interventions, Quantum Molecular Resonance (QMR) electrotherapy and a patient blood-derived secretome, across 56 libraries spanning four arms, three time points and matched stressed and stress-free conditions (GEO: GSE328981).

title: Predicting Hospital-associated complications in older adults: methodological considerations
creator: Shukhrat Valiev, Dilnavoz Yuldasheva, Malika Khojimatova, Dilorom Saidova, Shaxlo R Sodiqova, Nizom Ermatov, Zeynab Afzali
description: Machine learning is increasingly used to predict post-surgical complications, but predictive performance does not guarantee clinical readiness. Shimizu and colleagues developed a promising model for older adults undergoing tibial fracture surgery using a large Japanese database. However, four methodological pitfalls warrant attention.

title: Environmental impact of a radiology department: greenhouse gas emissions and primary energy accounting and strategies for sustainable practice
creator: Stefania Rizzo, Christoph Rüesch, Marco Budin, Rolf Wyttenbach, Ermidio Rezzonico, Filippo Del Grande
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivesTo assess the environmental impact of a radiology department’s operations (primary energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions (GHG); to identify the main levers for reduction.Materials and methodsData collection included measured and calculated energy consumption of imaging machines (2 MRI, 2 CT, 1 interventional radiology (IR) suite, 2 US, 3 radiography machines), workstations, lighting, ventilation; cooling and heating for imaging systems and rooms; materials/pharmaceuticals; external services (e.g. laundry and information technology (IT)).

title: The durability of different anchoring points and anchoring types in the left ventricle in an ex vivo porcine model
creator: Henrik Bjursten, Per Wierup, Sasha Koul, Matthias Götberg, Magnus Dencker
description: ObjectiveSurgical mitral valve repair, including anchoring in different parts of the mitral apparatus, is the standard of care for severe mitral regurgitation. Various percutaneous approaches have been developed and are currently under development, but are struggling with durable results. This study investigates the durability of different anatomic anchoring points and anchoring types in the left ventricle.

title: Recent advances in coarse-grained simulations of nucleic acid condensation
creator: Jessica Fong Ng, Shanlong Li, Jianhan Chen
description: Biomolecular condensates, formed through phase separation of multivalent biomolecules, play essential roles in cellular processes such as stress response, RNA processing, transcriptional control, and genome organization. Nucleic acids are increasingly recognized as important drivers and regulators of condensate formation and dynamics. This review examines recent advances in coarse-grained molecular simulations of dynamic nucleic acids and their phase transitions.

title: Disabling COMPASS Promoter Licensing Shifts HDAC‐Inhibited Gastric Cancer Toward Sustained Transcriptional Suppression During Recovery
creator: Jintian Song, Hui Yu, Jianping Jiang, Zhihui Jiang, Zhongshi Hong, Xu Zhang, Luchuan Chen, Shenghong Wei, Yi Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Histone deacetylase inhibitors (HDACi) broadly increase chromatin acetylation but have limited and variable activity in solid tumors. To define the epigenetic buffering axis that sustains promoter output during HDAC inhibition in gastric cancer. We integrated pharmacologic profiling across a molecularly diverse gastric cancer panel with an epigenetic‐focused pooled CRISPR‐Cas9 screening library, domain‐resolved genetic perturbation, structure‐guided WIN‐pocket targeting, CCK8 time‐course proliferation assays, and pulse‐washout clonogenic recovery assays.

title: Early disruptions in brain capillary blood flow control in a mouse model of Alzheimer’s disease
creator: Ashwini Hariharan, Abigail Vigderman, Dominic P. Isaacs, Nick Weir, Gyubyung Park, Serena Edwards, Thomas A. Longden
description: Hariharan et al. show that in a mouse model of Alzheimer’s disease, capillary blood flow control fails early: endothelial Kir2.1 currents decline at 2–4 mo, followed by pericyte KATP channel impairment by 6–8 mo. Notably, the early Kir2.1 deficit can be rescued by restoring PIP2 levels, which reinstates communication between deep capillary pericytes and upstream arterioles.

title: Sequential Exposure to Acute, Intermediate, and Late Synovial Fluid Fracture Hematoma after Ankle Fracture Promotes Cartilage Damage in Vitro Partially Attenuated by Anti Inflammatory Agents
creator: Evan Fedock, Nicholas B Allen, Alexandra Hunter Aitchison, Will Sharp, Olivia Blaber, Zachary Aman, Austin Cates, Lucas Domberg, Samuel B Adams
description: BackgroundPost-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA) following intra-articular fractures (IAFs) remains a common sequela after injury. Cartilage degeneration after injury is influenced by multiple factors, including elevated proinflammatory cytokines produced by synovial fluid fracture hematoma (SFFH). Targeting this inflammatory response may reduce cartilage damage.

title: Cardiovascular Health Among High School Students — Youth Risk Behavior Survey, United States, 2025
creator: Izraelle I. McKinnon, Ryan Saelee, Kathleen H. Krause, Domonique Hargrave, Caitlin Merlo, Shannon L. Michael, Philip E. Rosenbaum, Ahlia Sekkarie, Christopher J. Kissler, Jonetta J. Mpofu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Monitoring cardiovascular health (CVH) among adolescents can identify opportunities for school and community programs to promote healthy behaviors and reduce cardiovascular disease risk. In this report, data from the nationally representative 2025 Youth Risk Behavior Survey (YRBS) of U.S. high school students were used to calculate scores for five metrics of CVH aligned with the American Heart Association’s Life’s Essential 8 framework: diet, physical activity, nicotine exposure, sleep health, and body mass index (BMI).

title: Sperm-TLR2 activation enhances bovine embryo developmental competence via modulation of intracellular calcium and autophagic flux
creator: Taiyo HASHIMOTO, Ihshan AKTHAR, Yu MATSUZAWA, Alireza MANSOURI, Ren UCHIYAMA, Fumie MAGATA, Akio MIYAMOTO
description: The optimization of in vitro embryo production (IVP) is critical for bovine biotechnology, particularly for maximizing the yield of high-quality embryos suitable for transfer. This study investigated how Toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2) activation in sperm, using the agonist Pam3CSK4 (Pam), influences fertilization outcomes, metabolic activity, and cryotolerance.

title: Associations between professional values and self-actualization among South Korean and Chinese medical students
creator: Hyojeong Hwang, Jun-Ki Lee, Qiuyue Fang, Hyo Hyun Yoo
description: ObjectivesTo compare professional values endorsed at one South Korean and one Chinese medical school, examine which values were associated with endorsement of self-actualization, and identify latent value classes. MethodsCross-sectional convenience survey of 321 medical students: 211 second- and third-year students at a Korean national university, 110 at a Chinese medical college.

title: Cost-Effectiveness of Culmerciclib Plus Fulvestrant for Previously Treated HR-Positive/HER2-Negative Advanced Breast Cancer in China: An Integrated GBD 2023 Analysis
creator: Feng Xuan, Mengjuan Ding, Zhaoqi Qiu, Liejiong Wang, Haiyan Xu
description: BackgroundBreast cancer (BC) imposes a substantial and evolving health and economic burden in China. We integrated population-level disease burden with treatment-specific economic evaluation to assess the cost-effectiveness of culmerciclib plus fulvestrant for previously treated hormone receptor-positive (HR+), human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HER2−) advanced breast cancer (ABC).

title: Effects of Mind-Body Exercises on Pain Intensity in Individuals with Chronic Nonspecific Low Back Pain: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
creator: Yi Xiang, Zengao Lu, Liang Li, Tonggang Fan
description: ObjectiveTo synthesize the effects of mind–body exercises (MBEs) on pain in adults with chronic nonspecific low back pain (CNLBP) and assess whether comparative and study-level dose evidence can inform exercise selection.MethodsWe searched 10 databases from inception to 11 July 2026 for randomized controlled trials. Random-effects pairwise meta-analysis compared MBEs with control conditions.

title: Autologous Mastoid Cortex Bone Graft for Multilayer Repair of Lateral Skull Base Defects
creator: Christopher Z Wen, Daniel C Fong, Vera Bzhilyanskaya, Adam C Kaufman, Ronna Hertzano, David J Eisenman
description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Multilayer repair of lateral skull base cerebrospinal fluid leaks and encephaloceles can be reinforced with rigid autologous grafts. Harvesting a monocortical mastoid cortex bone graft is effective and easy to implement without conferring additional morbidity.Keywords: bone graft, CSF leak repair, CSF otorrhea

Introduction

Cerebrospinal fluid leaks are due to defects between the intracranial space, bony skull base, and overlying periosteum and soft tissue. They can be iatrogenic, post‐traumatic, or spontaneous in nature.

title: Trends, Risk Factors, and Future Burden of Female Breast Cancer in China and Other G20 Countries, 1990–2050: A Comparative Global Burden of Disease 2023 Analysis
creator: Xubin Dong, Xiyu Kang, Zeyu Wu, Guangyu Li, Jiaxian Yue, Jiaxiang Liu, Qingyao Shang, Tianxiao Wang, Dongmin Yang, Jiayi Ma, Huiming Wu, Chenxuan Yang, Xin Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveThis study analyzes the burden of female breast cancer in China and other G20 countries from 1990 to 2023, characterizes its trends and risk factors, and projects the burden to 2050.MethodsUsing Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 estimates, we evaluated age-standardized rates of incidence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), the mortality-to-incidence ratio (MIR), and trends (estimated annual percentage change, EAPC); applied Das Gupta decomposition, sociodemographic index (SDI) gradient, attributable-risk, and socioeconomic-inequality analyses, with stratification by premenopausal (20–54 years) and postmenopausal (≥55

title: Effect of Alveolar Ridge Inclination on Dynamic Navigation Accuracy of Implant Surgery: A Retrospective Clinical Study
creator: Xuechun Jiang, Ran Zhang, Huiyun Jiang, Ni Zeng, Huimin Nie, Wenjuan Zhou, Zhonghao Liu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveTo evaluate the accuracy of dynamic navigation-guided dental implantation system across different alveolar ridge inclinations.Materials and MethodsThis retrospective study included 34 patients (120 implants) who underwent dynamic navigation-assisted dental implantation between January 2021 and December 2025. Deviations at the entry point of the initial drill and pilot drill were recorded to analyze the influence of alveolar ridge inclination on surgical accuracy.

title: Genome-wide association and MaODR-based multi-locus interaction analyses reveal a susceptibility gene network for newly identified metabolic syndrome
creator: Yu-Da Lin, Kuei-Hau Luo, Li-Yeh Chuang, Hung-Yi Chuang, Cheng-Hong Yang
description: BackgroundMetabolic syndrome involves several lipid-related genes, including apolipoprotein A5 (APOA5), lipoprotein lipase (LPL), and cholesteryl ester transfer protein (CETP). Although individual SNP susceptibility has been reported, gene–gene interactions remain underexplored. To address this gap, we apply many-objective multifactor dimensionality reduction (MaODR)—previously developed by our group—to detect gene‒gene interactions in unbalanced newly identified MetS and non-MetS subjects.

title: OHVIRA Syndrome with Incomplete Vaginal Obstruction, Hematocolpos, and Pyocolpos Despite Regular Menstruation in an Adolescent: A Case Report
creator: Rico Henando Sembiring, Aria Prasetya Ma’soem, Amillia Siddiq
description: BackgroundObstructed hemivagina and ipsilateral renal anomaly (OHVIRA) syndrome is a rare congenital Müllerian anomaly characterized by uterus didelphys, obstructed hemivagina, and ipsilateral renal anomaly. Patients with complete vaginal obstruction typically present shortly after menarche with severe dysmenorrhea and cyclic pelvic pain. Incomplete obstruction may permit partial menstrual drainage, resulting in atypical manifestations and delayed diagnosis.

title: Correction: Obinutuzumab as salvage anti-CD20 therapy in poly-refractory difficult-to-treat seropositive rheumatoid arthritis
creator: Unknown
description:
Practice, Volume 10, Issue 3, 2026, rkag089, https://doi.org/10.1093/rap/rkag089

The following change has been made to the originally published paper.

Text in the first sentence of the second paragraph is corrected to read: “A woman was diagnosed with seropositive RA in May 2010, aged 36,[…]” instead of: “A woman was diagnosed with seropositive RA in May 2010, aged 46,[…]”.

title: High-fat diet-derived metabolite uridine diphosphate (UDP) impairs epithelial regeneration by P2Y 6 -receptor signaling
creator: Rebecca Springer, Philip Claus, Marius Hörner, Christoph Otto, Natalie Burkard, Jakob Lauerer, Hanna Deinlein, Agnes Fekete, Werner Schmitz, Florian Seyfried, Nicolas Schlegel
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Obesity is associated with a chronic low-grade inflammation affecting metabolic changes and organ dysfunction. Impairment of the intestinal epithelial barrier (IEB) and alterations in gut microbiota are considered to contribute to this phenotype by largely undefined mechanisms. Here, we used a diet-induced obesity model in rats to investigate the early interplay between a high-fat diet (HFD), gut microbiota composition, metabolic stool contents and IEB regeneration. Male Wistar rats received either a high-fat diet or a low-fat diet (LFD) ad libitum.

title: Longitudinal peripheral DNA methylation remodeling following ketamine-assisted psychotherapy in major depressive disorder
creator: Arghavan Nepton, Sonya C. Faber, Zachary Kaminsky, Mario Nucci, Hesam Farahani, Monnica T. Williams, Sergio R. Perez Rosal
description: Ketamine produces rapid antidepressant effects, but the molecular processes associated with their persistence remain poorly defined in humans. We examined longitudinal DNA methylation changes in 10 adults with major depressive disorder undergoing ketamine-assisted psychotherapy using two pre-treatment assessments (T1, T2) and one post-treatment assessment (T3). Participants received three sessions of intranasal racemic ketamine within a structured psychotherapy protocol.

title: Lactoferrin-Modified Ultra-Sustained Release Propofol Nanoparticles for Multi-Pathway Therapy of Depression via Intraperitoneal Injection
creator: Zhenyi Wu, Junze Deng, Shunlian Li, Lu Yu, Hang Zhang, Yufeng Xun, Jing Bian, Jing Liu, Jianbo Zhang, Pu Lei, Qingyan Ma, Yajuan Fan, Zai Yang, Feng Zhu, Xiancang Ma, Daocheng Wu, Shuo Zhang
description: BackgroundDepression imposes a significant burden on global public health, and traditional antidepressants are limited by slow onset, low efficacy, and high recurrence rates. Intraperitoneal injection of propofol can rapidly exert anti-anhedonic effects by regulating the VTA–NAc dopaminergic and GABAergic signaling pathways. However, its application in depression treatment is limited by rapid systemic clearance, poor brain permeability, and significant systemic toxicity.

title: Application of Machine Learning Models to Predict Tigecycline Exposure in Critically Ill Patients Using Different Limited Sampling Strategies
creator: Anran Dai, Hao Liu, Bo Yang, Feiyue Zheng, Yan Guan, Jieqiong Liu, Jianping Zhu, Gang Liang, Yi Yang, Lingyan Yu, Yuhua Zhao, Zhenwei Yu
description: BackgroundThe high variability in the pharmacokinetics of tigecycline may impact therapeutic efficacy, particularly in critically ill patients. This study introduces machine learning (ML) methods, aiming to clarify their effectiveness in individualized drug exposure prediction and determine the optimal modeling strategy.MethodsThe least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) method was used to screen the covariates.

title: Novel Target for Pathogenic Leptospira Detection via Colorimetric Loop‐Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP): Development, Validation, and Comparative Analysis
creator: Peyman Ghoraishizadeh, Benjie Clemente, Kween Saimuang, Sakaorat Lertjuthaporn, Sukhonta limsampan, Patcharapan Suwannin, Mongkol Techakasikornpanich, Galayanee Doungchawee, Edilberto Manahan, Kulachart Jangpatarapongsa
description: BackgroundLeptospirosis is a globally prevalent zoonotic disease that remains challenging to diagnose due to its nonspecific symptoms and the limitations of current diagnostic methods and targets. To address these challenges, we developed and validated a naked‐eye loop‐mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) assay targeting the newly identified orpH region for the rapid detection of pathogenic Leptospira species.

title: Targeting Cannabinoid 1 Receptor in Macrophages Alleviates Psoriatic Skin Inflammation Through the AUF1–NLRP3 Axis
creator: Hongseo Choi, Sukyoung Han, Jinho Kim, Ji Hye Han, Eunsu Kim, Yeonjeong Heo, Minju Lee, Jooyoung Lee, Heerim You, Soyoun Lee, Su‐Hee Han, Ilrok Yoon, Sung Anjeon, Hyerim Kang, Seungyeon Ryu, Hyun‐Ji Park, Eunha Kim, Chul Hwan Bang, Ji Hyun Lee, Josephine M. Egan, Jung‐Woong Kim, Eun Kyung Lee, Wook
description: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease associated with systemic metabolic dysregulation; however, the molecular pathways linking metabolic signaling to skin inflammation remain poorly understood. Here, we identify cannabinoid 1 receptor (CB1R) in macrophages as a key immunometabolic regulator of psoriatic inflammation and a potential therapeutic target.

title: Unlocking the Full Potential of Jumping Condensation on Microstructured Surfaces
creator: Mariia S. Kiseleva, Tytti Kärki, Mika Latikka, Parham Koochak, Sakari Lepikko, Maja Vuckovac, Tomi Koskinen, Ramesh Raju, Ville P. Jokinen, Jiazheng Liu, Nenad Miljkovic, Jaakko V. I. Timonen, Ilkka Tittonen, Robin H. A. Ras
description: Water condensation on superhydrophobic surfaces can generate spontaneous droplet jumping, enabling rapid condensate removal and improved thermal and mass transfer. Although this effect has been extensively demonstrated on densely packed nanostructures, the capability of microscale textures to support jumping condensation remains poorly understood.

title: Toward Rational Design of Aqueous Battery Membranes Beyond the Selectivity‐Conductivity Trade‐Off
creator: Jinkang Liu, Mingbo Xie, Zhenghao Wang, Huacun Li, Jun Xie, Pan Liu, Qingwei Wang, Xu Yan, Meiqing Shi, Liyuan Chai, Yue Luo, Zining Tang, Rui Tan, Liyuan Zhang
description: Electrochemical energy‐storage systems increasingly require membranes that can simultaneously deliver fast ion transport, suppressed active‐species crossover, chemical and dimensional stability, and scalable manufacturability. Yet conventional membrane platforms still struggle to reconcile conductivity with selectivity, while durability and processability remain important practical constraints. Sulfonic‐acid‐based membranes are particularly attractive because they combine strong acidity, fixed‐charge character, and tunable hydrated ionic domains.

title: Long‐Lifespan Polyorganosiloxane‐Based Silicone Evaporator for High‐Efficiency Seawater Desalination
creator: Jiaxian Zheng, Liqiang Zhang, Haoqi Ni, Shuozhen Chen, Xiangfeng Lin, Liwei Wang, Zhanhui Yuan
description: Conventional evaporators suffer from poor mechanical strength, salt crystallization, and degradation in sea water. We design a white polyorganosiloxane‐based solar evaporator (PDMSE) that exploits siliconeʼs unique attributes. These include chemical inertness, anti‑corrosion, high flexibility, and chemical resistance. Such characteristics ensure structural integrity and anti‑fouling performance under harsh brine conditions.

title: Extract from Eucommia ulmoides Oliv. Leaves alleviates APAP-induced acute liver injury via reshaping gut microbiota and attenuating microbial bile acids metabolism disorder
creator: Dan He, Hai-chao Zhang, Bing-bing Shen, Di Zhao, Xue-yang Tang, Jing Xie, Rong-rong Zhou, Hong-liang Zeng, Shui-han Zhang
description: BackgroundIncreasing studies suggest that supplementing flavonoids from Eucommia ulmoides Oliv. Leaves (EUL) exerts liver protective effects via reshaping gut microbiota and regulating bile acids (BAs) metabolism. However, the relationship between EUL, gut microbiota and BAs metabolism remains unclear and the potential mechanisms of action has not been expounded clearly.

title: Uniaxial Strain‐Driven Ferroelastic Domain Tuning in LaAlO3
creator: Matthias Roeper, Robin Buschbeck, Jakob Wetzel, Tobias Ritschel, Anna‐Lena Hofmann, Vladyslav Kovtunovych, Mike N Pionteck, Javier Taboada‐Gutiérrez, Alexey B Kuzmenko, Martina Basini, Vivek Unikandanunni, Iuliia Kiseleva, Jochen Geck, Susanne C Kehr, Maximilian Lederer, Simone Sanna, Lukas M Eng, S
description: Multiferroic domain walls in functional oxides exhibit properties distinct from the bulk and are increasingly exploited as active elements in nanoelectronic and photonic devices. Deterministic tuning of domain populations has typically remained limited to local solutions, or removal with temperature.

title: Success of femtosecond laser-assisted deep anterior lamellar keratoplasty (Femto-DALK): a clinical case series of 42 eyes using an intraoperative optical coherence tomography (iOCT)-guided laser-generated pre-descemet tunnel
creator: Nicola R. Otto, Friedrich A. Steindor, Gerd Geerling, Theo G. Seiler
description: PurposeTo evaluate the success of Femto-DALK with an iOCT-guided generated intrastromal pre-Descemet tunnel.MethodsThis monocentric, retrospective study evaluated all patients treated with Femto-DALK between January 2020 and December 2023 at the Department of Ophthalmology at the University of Düsseldorf (Germany). The iOCT-guided tunnel was generated 30 microns anterior of Descemet’s membrane.

title: Association of regulatory B, T cells and cytokine production with disease stage in non-small cell lung cancer patients: prospective case control study
creator: Helal F Hetta, Asmaa M Zahran, Emad Eldin Nabil, Azza A Elkady, Asmaa M Goda, Tamer M Soliman, Abeer Elkady, Hend M Esmaeel, Abdelazeem M Algammal, Nahed A Mohamed, Hala M ElBadre, Hani Alrefai, Ashraf Elyamany, Ola A Alkady
description: Background and aimThe role of regulatory B cells (Bregs) cells and regulatory T cells (Tregs) has been little investigated in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Therefore, we investigated the frequency of circulating Bregs, Tregs cells, and the serum cytokine profile in NSCLC and their association with disease progression.

title: Loss‐Engineered Terahertz Pixelated Metasensors for Enhanced Molecular Vibrational Fingerprint Sensing
creator: Chenglin Yang, Yuqing Cui, Donghai Han, Yushan Hou, Zhonglei Shen, Andreas Tittl, Liuyang Zhang, Ruqiang Yan, Xuefeng Chen
description: Molecular vibrational fingerprints in the terahertz (THz) regime offer unique opportunities for label‐free chemical and biological sensing. Metasensors can amplify these vibrational signals through local near‐field enhancement. However, current THz molecular fingerprint metasensors lack a systematic design and optimization methodology, which severely limits their potential.

title: MRI-based preoperative WHO grade prediction in meningioma: development and comparison of deep learning, radiomics, clinical, and combined models in multicenter data
creator: Cagin Huryol, Umid Sulaimanov, Murat Yuce, Nafiye Sanlier, Fikret Ozturk, Oyku Ozturk, Irem Altun, Gular Ismayilova, Huseyin Bozkurt, Taha Yasin Altunkaya, Ferdi Afsin, Abdullah Soydan Mahmutoglu, Amine Durmus, Burak Karaaslan, Ilhan Aydin, Mehmet Sabri Gurbuz, Ahmet Tan Cimilli, Okan Turk, Ufuk Erg
description: PurposeThe objective of this study was to develop and externally validate complementary magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based models and their stacked combinations for preoperative World Health Organization (WHO) grading of intracranial meningioma.MethodsThis retrospective multicenter study included 455 histopathologically confirmed meningiomas: a four-center development cohort (n = 346) with leave-one-center-out cross-validation and an external cohort (n = 109).

title: Global inequities and fragmentation in guidelines for endometriosis: a scoping review
creator: Dereje G. Gete, Devon Evans, Jason Abbott, Leticia W. Ribeiro, Krina T. Zondervan, Linda C. Giudice, Luk Rombauts, Mathew Leonardi, Hemantha Senanayake, G. David Adamson, Elsie Wandera, Femke Jansen, Sally Motlock, Angela G. Sison-Aguilar, Sawsan As-Sanie, Idhaliz Flores, Kaori Koga, Marina Kvaskoff
description: BackgroundDespite the availability of endometriosis care guidelines from multiple governmental and professional organisations, their global applicability and recommendations have been insufficiently examined. This scoping review examines endometriosis guidelines worldwide, evaluating their availability, target audiences and populations, methodologies, and clinical recommendations, building on a previous review of region-specific endometriosis care guidance.

title: Universal crystallization kinetics of solution-processed semiconductors
creator: Zhitian Ling, Mateusz Brzezinski, Shuanglong Wang, Konstantinos Bidinakis, Lei Gao, Chongyao Li, Xin Zhou, Hai I. Wang, Stefan A. L. Weber, Paul W. M. Blom, Wojciech Pisula, Tomasz Marszalek
description: Heterogeneous crystallization kinetics critically govern the morphology and performance of solution-processed semiconductors, yet morphology control is often achieved through trial-and-error optimization. Quantitative understanding of crystallization is essential for precise morphology control but is limited by the simultaneous occurrence of heterogeneous nucleation and crystal growth.

title: Rewilding the atoll engine
creator: Hillary Young
description: Seabirds and native forests reconnect ocean, reef, and island processes, strengthening the physical foundations of atoll resilience. Low-lying atoll islands are often portrayed as passive, helpless victims of sea-level rise. Yet, they are living landforms, built and maintained through interactions among coral reefs, sediment-producing organisms, waves, plants, and animals.

title: Current Evidence on the Use of Calcitonin Gene-Related Peptide-Targeting Therapies in Children and Adolescents
creator: Lauren Shin, Ryan Moon, Amy Gelfand
description: Purpose of ReviewThis is a narrative review to summarize current evidence on use of therapies targeting calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) for children and adolescents with headache disorders.Recent FindingsThe CGRP-targeting therapies have been used in adults for prevention of migraine since 2018.

title: Pasture area increases livestock rabies risk in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil: a geospatial analysis of neurological syndrome cases (2020–2024)
creator: Rafael Veríssimo Monteiro, Renata Falcão Rabello da Costa, Leda Maria Silva Kimura, Glenda Ribeiro de Oliveira, Natiane Rodrigues Viana, Alessandro de Sá Guimarães, Márcio Roberto Silva, Guilherme Nunes de Souza
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Animal rabies poses a risk to livestock in Brazil due to transmission by hematophagous bats. The Brazilian sanitary surveillance system mandates rabies testing for any livestock exhibiting signs of neurological syndrome. This geospatial, retrospective, longitudinal, observational study analyzed rabies test results for 204 cattle and 56 horses presenting with neurological syndrome in Rio de Janeiro State, Brazil, from 2020 to 2024. We calculated correlations and linear models between rabies results and municipal land-use types, as well the population of herbivores.

title: Temporal trends in the clinical presentation, management, and outcomes of children with congenital cytomegalovirus infection
creator: Jitka Bolchová, Despoina Gkentzi, Roberto Pedrero Tomé, Garyfallia Syridou, Antoni Noguera-Julián, María Ríos-Barnés, Serena Salomé, Francesco Raimondi, Serena Villaverde, Fernando Baquero-Artigao, Paula Rodriguez-Molino, Danilo Buonsenso, Laura Martino, Beatriz Álvarez-Vallejo, Jesús Saavedra, Yves
description: Congenital cytomegalovirus (cCMV) is the most common congenital infection and a leading cause of sensorineural hearing loss as well as neurodevelopmental impairment. In recent years, awareness, screening, and management strategies for cCMV have evolved. This study aimed to assess temporal changes in the clinical presentation, treatment, and outcomes of children diagnosed with cCMV infection.

title: Colourimetric LAMP detection of Escherichia coli in bovine milk using a simplified DNA preparation method
creator: Tewodros Fentahun Jember, Mark Edward Westman, Sameer Dinkar Pant, Seyed Ali Ghorashi
description: Escherichia coli (E. coli) is a common cause of bovine mastitis, and rapid detection from milk is important for timely disease management. However, molecular assays such as colourimetric loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) are often limited by laboratory-based DNA extraction. This study evaluated a simplified HotSHOT (HS) DNA preparation method for extracting E.

title: Reproductive system and agronomic performance of the wild husk tomatillo Physalis gracilis
creator: Omar Enríquez-Antonio, María del Pilar Zamora-Tavares, Lislie Solís-Montero, Fabián A. Rodríguez-Zaragoza, Carla Vanessa Sánchez-Hernández, Gabriela Alcalá-Gómez, José Alberto Sánchez-Nuño, Ofelia Vargas-Ponce
description: Physalis gracilis is a wild perennial herb with sweet, orange-colored fruits harvested for household consumption in Mexico. For species with potential for cultivation and nutritional value, a basic information is known their reproductive system. This study aimed to evaluate the reproductive system of P. gracilis and its agronomic performance.

title: Temporomandibular disorders in women with psoriatic arthritis by history of psoriasis: a cross-sectional study
creator: Negin Yekkalam, Anders Wänman, Göran Isacsson, Aylin Canbek, Milad Rizk
description: Temporomandibular joint involvement in psoriatic arthritis may result in impaired jaw function and reduced oral health-related quality of life. Patients with PsA have generally been analyzed as a single group regardless of psoriasis history, despite a reported association between psoriasis and TMJ involvement.

title: RSV vaccine uptake among Medicare Advantage enrollees: August 2023 to December 2024
creator: Vishal Saundankar, Reiko Sato, Robyn Moucka, Pamela Smith, Kimbal Ford, Edward W Casey, Chris Barger, Richard Sheer, Brandon Suehs
description: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is one of the most common causes of respiratory tract infections, disproportionately affecting young children, older adults, and those with chronic medical conditions. In the US, RSV vaccine recommendations by the US Centers for Disease Control (CDC) for adults were first issued in 2023 and have since evolved.

title: Effects of centrifugation-based therapeutic plasma exchange on coagulation parameters in dogs with canine visceral leishmaniasis
creator: Suellen Rodrigues Maia, Silvano Salgueiro Geraldes, Fábio dos Santos Nogueira, Maria Gabriela Picelli de Azevedo, Reiner Silveira de Moraes, Julia Franco Ferreira, Teresa Alessandra de Lima Núñez, Regina Kiomi Takahira, Alessandra Melchert, Adriano Sakai Okamoto, Priscylla Tatiana Chalfun Guimarães-
description: As in humans, therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) has been investigated in veterinary medicine for managing immune-mediated diseases such as canine visceral leishmaniasis (CVL). TPE may improve clinical outcomes by removing circulating immune complexes and excess antibodies; however, its physiological effects must be understood to ensure safety.

title: Quantitative analysis of intrarenal nerve‐associated profiles in the human foetal kidney between 14 and 30 gestational weeks: An S100 immunohistochemical study
creator: Ivan Petrović, Ana Balenović, Milana Bosanac, Srdjan Stanković, Isidora Milosavljević, Milena Šunjević, Sandra Trivunić Dajko, Bojana Andrejić‐Višnjić
description: Quantitative data on the spatial development of intrarenal S100‐positive nerve‐associated profiles in human foetal kidneys remain limited, despite the established importance of renal nerves. Building on the previously published semiquantitative observations, this study aimed to generate a quantitative, compartment‐resolved map of S100‐positive nerve‐associated profiles in human foetal kidneys.

title: The Current State of Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction: Graft Selection, Lateral Augmentation, Rehabilitation, and Return-to-Play
