Paired hematoxylin and eosin whole‐slide images are organized as T0, the earlier specimen, and T1, the later specimen.

title: Practical Application of the AO Spine Primary Infection Classification System: Clarifying Definitions, Borderline Cases and Common Misinterpretations
creator: Barry Ting Sheen Kweh, Alexander R Vaccaro, Gregory Schroeder, Mohamed Aly, Mohammad El-Sharkawi, Charlotte Dandurand, Jonathan Neuhoff, Brian Karamian, Grace Xiong, Harvinder Singh Chhabra, Richard Bransford, Andrei Fernandes Joaquim, Jin Wee Tee
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Study DesignNarrative review.ObjectiveTo clarify nuances when applying the AO Spine Primary Infection Classification.MethodsThe international validation of the AO Spine Primary Infection Classification System was successful but recurring themes caused confusion. This included the exact definition and reasons for infections to transition between categories, definition of canal involvement or neural compression and whether an epidural infection superimposed on degenerative disease escalates infection severity.

title: Safety signals of tocilizumab in pediatric patients: A real-world pharmacovigilance analysis based on the FAERS database with network pharmacology insights
creator: Gang Wu, Xueqing Ma, Bin Zhu, Ben Liu
description: Tocilizumab, a humanized monoclonal antibody targeting the interleukin-6 receptor, is widely used in immune-mediated diseases, yet its real-world safety in pediatric populations remains insufficiently characterized. This retrospective pharmacovigilance study analyzed adverse event (AE) reports from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database (2010–2025), focusing on pediatric cases where tocilizumab was the primary suspect drug.

title: Closing the loop: establishing an autonomous test-learn cycle to optimize induction of bacterial systems using a robotic platform
creator: Jan Benedict Spannenkrebs, Aron Eiermann, Thomas Zoll, Silke Hackenschmidt, Johannes Kabisch
description: One goal of synthetic biology is to provide well-characterised biological parts that behave predictably in genetic assemblies. To achieve this, each part must be characterised in a time-resolved manner under relevant conditions. Robotic platforms can be used to automate this task and provide sufficiently large and reproducible data sets including provenance.

title: Longitudinal Validity of the DUNDRUM-1 Triage Security Scale in a Canadian Not Criminally Responsible Cohort: A Retrospective Study of 85 Patients
creator: Alexandre Hudon, Fanie Chainey, Catherine Degré, Anne-Renée Courtemanche, Marc-André Meunier, Allyson Fortier, Camille Bourque, Loriane Boulé, Vincent Latreille, Sophie Mongeon, Jeanne-Marie Allard, Stéphanie Borduas Pagé
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveTo evaluate the longitudinal stability of DUNDRUM-1 Triage Security Scale recommendations among individuals found not criminally responsible on account of mental disorder (NCRMD) receiving care within a Canadian forensic psychiatric service.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults found NCRMD who received a DUNDRUM-1 assessment at a tertiary academic forensic psychiatric centre in Quebec between 1 January 2019 and 31 December 2024. Eligible participants were aged ≥18 years and had a minimum of 12 months of follow-up.

title: Factors affecting risk perception of COVID-19: differences by age and gender
creator: Sungwook Kang, Chang Hoon You, Young Dae Kwon
description: IntroductionAddressing emerging infectious diseases is a major task in public health. This study investigated the factors influencing the perception of risk related to COVID-19.MethodsThis study analyzed data from the 2020 Social Survey conducted nationwide in South Korea, targeting 34,909 individuals aged 13 years and older.

title: Alistipes-derived monomethyl branched-chain fatty acid iso-15:0 suppresses hepatocellular carcinoma progression by inhibiting Gβγ/PI3K/AKT signaling
creator: Juan He, Yu Chen, Liwen Kuang, Yang Xiao, Jiongming Chen, Xudong Liu, Jiangang Zhang, Ziyi Li, Dongqin Zhou, Miaoyu Song, Yi Yi, Danyang Li, Haili Shang, Nan Zhang, Ran Ren, Yu Zhou, Juan Lei, Huakan Zhao, Yongsheng Li
description: The role of gut microbiota and their metabolites in the progression of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has garnered increasing attention. Although Alistipes, a genus frequently reported as a beneficial bacterium, has been associated with antitumor effects and enhanced efficacy of cancer therapies, its specific functions and underlying mechanisms in HCC remain poorly defined.

title: Socioeconomic status and delayed surgery: impact on non-metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma outcomes
creator: Kun Zhang, Xinyi Wang, Jianyong Lei, Anping Su, Tao Wei, Zhihui Li, Ya-Wen Chen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionThe growing popularity of active surveillance for papillary thyroid cancer and the COVID-19 pandemic have increased surgery delay, further necessitating a reassessment of the link between surgery delay and survival outcomes for papillary thyroid cancer.

title: Maternal Readiness for Newborn Self-Care in the Early Postpartum Period: Associations with Maternal Psychophysical State and Declared Breastfeeding Readiness
creator: Anna Prokopowicz, Kinga Tułacz, Kamila Drobina, Łukasz Lewandowski, Izabella Uchmanowicz
description: Objectives: To assess maternal readiness for newborn self-care and its associations with breastfeeding readiness and psychophysical condition in early postpartum rooming-in care. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 200 women at 48–72 h postpartum. Maternal readiness was assessed with three 0–10 self-report scales: daytime newborn care, nighttime newborn care, and breastfeeding readiness.

title: Single-cell Transcriptomics in Autoimmune Diseases: Mechanistic Insights, Cross-disease Convergence, and Translational Challenges in Rheumatoid Arthritis, Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, Type 1 Diabetes, and Multiple Sclerosis
creator: Thanh-Hong Nguyen, Tuan-Dinh Nguyen, Oanh-Thi Hoang, Thuy-Thu T Can, Minh-Huyen T Nguyen, Mai-Hoang Tran, Hieu-Chi Chu, Dinh-Van Nguyen
description: Autoimmune diseases are characterized by loss of immune tolerance and substantial heterogeneity across patients, tissues, and disease stages. Although bulk transcriptomic studies have identified important inflammatory pathways, they cannot directly resolve rare, transitional, and tissue-contextualized cell states that may be relevant to disease mechanisms and therapeutic response.

title: Minoxidil and Prostaglandin Analogs for Chemotherapy-Induced Alopecia: A Scoping Review
creator: Yohei Iimura, Tomoya Yokota, Hironobu Hashimoto, Seiichiro Kuroda
description: BackgroundChemotherapy-induced alopecia (CIA) is common, distressing, and markedly impairs patients’ quality of life. Although scalp cooling is the only approved preventive strategy, its effectiveness and accessibility remain limited. Therefore, alternative pharmacologic approaches, such as minoxidil and prostaglandin analogs, have been explored.

title: Late transfer to seawater improves intestinal development of osmoregulatory capacity in Atlantic salmon smolts
creator: Raneesha de Fonseka, Marius Takvam, Kristina Sundell, Elisabeth Jönsson, Tom Ole Nilsen, Vibeke Vikeså, Henrik Sundh
description: The development and function of intestinal fluid transport capacity in Atlantic salmon, determine seawater (SW) readiness, but poorly understood in modern aquaculture practices. This study aimed to investigate the development of intestinal fluid transport capacity during smoltification and the effect of short-term fasting and a high-lipid diet.

title: Electrical stimulation of the sciatic nerve restores inspiratory diaphragm function in mice after spinal cord injury
creator: Ian Walling, Sarah Baumgartner, Mitesh Patel, Steven A. Crone
description: IntroductionSpinal cord injury in the high cervical cord can impair breathing due to disruption of pathways between brainstem respiratory centers and respiratory motor neurons in the spinal cord. Electrical stimulation of limb afferents can increase ventilation in healthy humans and animals, but it is not known if limb afferent stimulation can improve breathing following a cervical injury.

title: From proton microdomains to protein migration: hypothesis for ΔpH-controlled PSII relocation
creator: Matthias Ostermeier
description: Thylakoid membranes are highly organized yet dynamic systems in which Photosystem II (PSII) complexes undergo continual assembly, repair and lateral redistribution. Here a hypothesis is proposed that local lumenal pH, generated by the trans-thylakoidal proton gradient and potentially exhibiting transient spatial heterogeneity, may contribute to the regulation of protein movement and PSII maturation within the thylakoid membrane.

title: Does Workforce Participation After Retirement Age Affect the Use of Healthcare Services?
creator: Liqing Li, Jiashan Teng, Haifeng Ding
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Highlights What are the main findings? Using CHARLS 2018 data, this study finds that workforce participation after retirement age is significantly associated with lower healthcare utilization among older adults in China.This lower utilization is primarily driven by tighter time constraints for seeking care and differences in income levels, explicitly rather than reflecting an actual improvement in the underlying health status of the working population.This negative association exhibits heterogeneity, varying significantly across sub-populations based on gender, self-rated health status, and educational attainment.

title: Yinhua Gouteng decoction alleviates tic disorder symptoms by modulating neuro-inflammation in a rat model
creator: Mingge Hu, Yan Yang, Shuxia Wang, LiRong Huang, Lifei Chen, Xinguang Zhang, Wenbo Yao, Zheng Xue
description: BackgroundTic disorders (TDs) are childhood-onset neurodevelopmental disorders characterized by complex neurochemical dysregulation, and inflammation plays a critical role in TD pathogenesis. Yinhua Gouteng Decoction (YHGTD), a traditional Chinese medicinal formula, has demonstrated clinical efficacy in TD management. However, the specific pharmacological mechanisms underlying its effects remain unclear.

title: From smart sensing to adaptive remediation: artificial intelligence and Internet of Things for persistent organic pollutants
creator: Khaled Chawraba, Abrar Hussain, Obaid A Alharbi, Amal Abdelhaleem
description: Persistent organic pollutants (POPs) remain a major environmental challenge because of their persistence, long-range transport, bioaccumulation, and resistance to degradation. Conventional monitoring and remediation systems provide reliable analytical performance but are largely fragmented, laboratory dependent, and unable to deliver the continuous, predictive, and adaptive management required for complex, dynamic contamination scenarios.

title: AIDET communication combined with alternating prone ventilation for HIF-1α, sTREM-1 and hs-CRP in awake elderly patients with severe pneumonia
creator: YanHong Wang, Rong Zhang, XiaoYan Li, Xuejiao Deng
description: BackgroundSevere pneumonia in elderly patients carries high mortality, with inflammatory markers such as HIF-1α, sTREM-1, and hs-CRP associated with disease severity. Combining alternating prone ventilation with AIDET communication may improve outcomes.ObjectiveTo evaluate the effects of AIDET communication combined with alternating prone ventilation on comfort, oxygenation, inflammatory markers, and prognosis in awake elderly patients with severe pneumonia.

title: Human papillomavirus, vaginal microbiota and metagenomics: the interplay between development and progression of cervical cancer
creator: Paul Leon-Gomez, Vanessa I. Romero
description: Persistent infection with oncogenic human papillomavirus (HPV) types, such as HPV 16 or 18, is a major factor in cervical cancer development. However, only a small percentage of infected women develop cancer, indicating that other factors are involved. Emerging evidence links vaginal microbiota with HPV persistence and cancer progression.

title: Red Fluorescent Labeling of Myelin by Membrane‐Targeted tdTomato in Transgenic Mouse Lines
creator: Anja Reinert, Ulrike Winkler, Sandra Goebbels, Lina Komarek, Wiebke Möbius, Henri Seraf Zanker, Karl Schoknecht, Grit Bornschein, Hartmut Schmidt, Robert Fledrich, Ruth M. Stassart, Petra G. Hirrlinger, Klaus‐Armin Nave, Hauke B. Werner, Aiman S. Saab, Johannes Hirrlinger
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Myelin is a highly complex membranous structure wrapped around axons by oligodendrocytes or Schwann cells in the central and peripheral nervous system, respectively. Fluorescent labeling is widely used to study the structure and dynamics of myelin. Combining structural with functional imaging requires labeling of myelin with red fluorescence, as many functional sensors, including Ca2+ indicators and genetically encoded metabolite sensors, fluoresce in the green spectral range.

title: The magnitude of perinatal depression and associated factors among women in Kutaber woreda public health institution and Boru Meda general hospital, Ethiopia, 2022: a cross-sectional study
creator: Jemal Seid, Emam Mohammed, Nigusie Cherie, Husnia Yasin, Elsabeth Addisu
description: BackgroundPerinatal depression, characterized by the presence of depressive symptoms during pregnancy and/or within the first 12 months postpartum, poses a significant global public health concern. It contributes to a multitude of health risks for mothers, their infants, and their families. Understanding of perinatal depression and its associated factors is crucial for effective prevention and intervention strategies.

title: The Impact of Hip Osteoarthritis on Patient Reported Outcomes Following Lumbar Fusion
creator: Ali Farooqi, Joshua Mathew, Mitchell Ng, Roy Miloh, Emily Berthiaume, Yulia Lee, Gregorio Baek, William Green, Morgan Hitchner, Yasmine Eichbaum, Steven Banko, Manav Dasondi, Alan Mathew, Matthew Silva, Darshan Patel, Dipti Venkatesh, Andrew Vanichkachorn, Brandon Martinazzi, Alec Giakas, Bradley Ha
description: Study DesignRetrospective Cohort Study.ObjectivesWith an aging population, the burden of concomitant joint disease continues to rise. The effects of hip OA on lumbar fusion outcomes are underexplored. Therefore, this study aimed to: (1) describe demographic differences between Osteoarthritis (OA) patients and those without OA; (2) assess perioperative differences; and (3) compare patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs).

title: Epigenetically silencing gluconeogenic enzyme PCK1 by EZH2 promotes renal tubulointerstitial fibrosis
creator: Ming Wu, Pinglan Lin, Zhiqiang Yan, Yanzhe Wang, Anna Rinaldi, Pietro E Cippà, Di Huang, Jiayi Qiao, Aidong Yang, Bo Tan, Chaoyang Ye, Dongping Chen
description: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a leading cause of global morbidity. The kidney is a major gluconeogenic organ, and impaired renal gluconeogenesis contributes to CKD, yet the regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here we show that enhancer of zeste homolog 2 (EZH2), a histone H3K27 trimethyltransferase, epigenetically suppresses renal gluconeogenesis and drives tubulointerstitial fibrosis.

title: Novel pencil-beam scanning proton lattice radiation therapy for the treatment of bulky liver cancer: dosimetric comparison with VMAT-lattice radiotherapy
creator: Yuting Li, Rachael M. Martin-Paulpeter, Christine V. Chung, Miguel A. Aguilar, Carlos A. Matias, Adrian Delgado, Saurabh S. Nair, Laurence E. Court, Luis Perles, Narayan Sahoo, Ronald X. Zhu, Falk Poenisch, David B. Flint, Gabriel O. Sawakuchi, Sam Beddar, Eugene Koay, Jamie S. Baker, Ethan B. Ludmi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundSpatially fractionated radiotherapy (SFRT) delivered as lattice radiotherapy (LRT) creates high-dose ‘vertex’ subvolumes (VTVH) embedded within low-dose ‘valley’ regions (VTVL) to intensify intratumoral dose while minimizing radiation dose and toxicity to organs at risk (OARs).

title: A bibliometric analysis of exosomes in aging from 2007 to 2023
creator: Zenghui Niu, Meiyu Cui, Yingkun Fu, Lingfeng Zhou, Jiali Wang, Yan Lei, Xinrong Fan, Qiang Wang, Jing Yang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundAging is the primary factor contributing to the development of aging-related diseases. As research on exosomes continues to advance, its relationship with aging and aging-related diseases has become a hot topic This article analyzes the research hotspots of exosomes in aging and aging-related diseases, aiming to fill the gap in bibliometric research in this field and help researchers better understand the current status and future trends of both fundamental and clinical research in this field.MethodsThe articles were retrieved and exported from WoSCC

title: Genome-wide association studies for a comprehensive understanding of the genetic architecture of culm strength and yield traits in rice
creator: Jyothi Badri, Revadi Padmashree, Chandrappa Anilkumar, Akshay Mamidi, Subhakara Rao Isetty, AVSR Swamy, Raman Menakshi Sundaram
description: Lodging resistance in rice is a complex trait determined by culm morphological and culm physical strength traits, and these traits are a major determinant of yield. We made a detailed analysis of various component traits with the aim of deriving optimized parameters for measuring culm strength.

title: Early emergence of inter-lobar heterogeneity in mouse embryonic lung
creator: Yun Yang, Yonggao Fu, Shiting Li, Zhiwen Liu, Mingzhu Wen, Naihe Jing, Xianfa Yang
description: The mammalian lung is organized into anatomically distinct lobes, yet whether regional heterogeneity arises among different lobes remains poorly understood. Here, we performed comprehensive transcriptomic profiling of individual lung lobes at the pseudoglandular stage. Comparative analyses revealed that consistent inter-lobar divergence occurs primarily at the level of protein-coding genes.

title: Drug-loaded nanoparticles reduced platelet aggregation and blood coagulation
creator: Sarah Majin, Afrida Malik, Pratima Poudel, E. Vincent S. Faustino, Nubia Zuverza-Mena, John Hwa, Seyedtaghi Takyar, Susan Shea, Kagya A. Amoako
description: Surface-induced thrombosis remains a significant limitation of blood-contacting medical devices, driven primarily by platelet activation and rapid clot formation. Nitric oxide (NO), a potent endogenous antiplatelet agent, has therefore inspired the development of targeted NO-delivery strategies to mitigate device-associated thrombosis.

title: Improving the N-glycosylation occupancy of plant-produced IgG1 by engineering the amino acid environment at Asn297
creator: Kathrin Göritzer, Valentina Ruocco, Ulrike Vavra, Shiva Izadi, Omayra C. Bolaños-Martínez, Thareeya Phetphoung, Nuttapat Pisuttinusart, Waranyoo Phoolcharoen, Richard Strasser
description: Monoclonal antibodies are crucial recombinant biopharmaceuticals, with N-glycosylation at Asn297 essential for their functionality. Plants are increasingly used for antibody production, achieving high expression levels and enabling glycoengineering to produce homogenous human-like N-glycan structures. However, plant-produced human IgG1 often shows significant underglycosylation with potential adverse effects for immune functions and stability.

title: Assessment of community-based intervention approaches to improve the health and welfare of working donkeys in selected areas of Sidama region, Southern Ethiopia
creator: Aweke Yalew, Daniel Darge, Berhanu Mekibib Melake
description: BackgroundAlthough efforts have been made by certain non-governmental organizations, like the Donkey Sanctuary, SPANA (Society for the Protection of Animals Abroad), and Brooke Ethiopia, to change the attitudes and practices of donkey owners toward improving the health and welfare of working donkeys, their impact has not been assessed so far.

title: Prevalence and Associations of Abnormal Levels of Vitamin B6 in People with Parkinson's Disease
creator: Karlo J. Lizarraga, Lu Wang, Hannah Mesmer, Nami Shah, William Barbosa, Eric Logigian, Michael P. McDermott, Anthony E. Lang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundIn people with Parkinson's disease, abnormal levels of vitamin B6 may be associated with polyneuropathy and epileptic seizures, including medication‐refractory status epilepticus.ObjectivesTo estimate the prevalence and explore associations of abnormal levels of vitamin B6 in people with Parkinson's disease.MethodsIn this cross‐sectional study, fasting serum levels of vitamin B6 and related metabolites were measured in 144 people with Parkinson's disease randomly recruited from eligible clinic patients, compared with 144 historical controls matched for age, sex, diet, and vitamin supplementation.

title: First lactation performance of sows in Maternity Ring housing is comparable to that in farrowing crates
creator: Kate J. Plush, Kirsty L. Chidgey, Nigel Young, Darryl N. D’Souza, Robert J. van Barneveld
description: There is a trade-off between sow and piglet welfare in farrowing pens, whereby increased behavioural freedom of sows results in unacceptable levels of piglet mortality. Improvements in sow welfare have been demonstrated in such housing systems; however, the footprint is often at least 50% greater than a standard farrowing crate. This remains an impediment to the adoption of confinement-free farrowing.

title: Early prognosis prediction in acute myeloid and acute lymphoid leukemia patients using cell-free DNA concentration ratios
creator: Noreen Grace George, Bhavika Rishi, Amitabh Singh, Sree Vishmaya, Rakesh Kumar, Neetu Kushwaha, Manpreet Kaur, Reena Bhardwaj, Ankur Jain, Aditi Jain, Sumita Chaudhry, Aroonima Misra
description: Background: Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is a promising biomarker for disease prediction in many cancers, including acute leukemia (acute myeloid leukemia [AML] and acute lymphoblastic leukemia [ALL]). This study investigated the role of cfDNA in predicting relapse or unfavorable outcomes in acute leukemia patients upon initial diagnosis.

title: Bayesian Optimization of insect trap distribution for pest monitoring efficiency in agroecosystems
creator: Eric Yanchenko, Thomas M. Chappell, Anders S. Huseth
description: Insect trap networks targeting agricultural pests are commonplace but seldom optimized to improve precision or efficiency. Trap site selection is often driven by user convenience or predetermined trap densities relative to sensitive host crop abundance in the landscape. Monitoring for invasive pests often requires expedient decisions based on dispersal potential and ecology to inform trap placement.

title: Comment on “Cardiometabolic Multimorbidity Increases the Risk of Hip Fracture: A Longitudinal Cohort Study Based on CHARLS”
creator: Harun Sağlıcak
description: In the CHARLS cohort of Tian et al., the abstract's 13% versus 8% are column percentages from Table 1: the prevalence of cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) among participants with and without hip fracture. Read across rows, the same counts give a nine‐year hip fracture incidence of 6.6% (36/544) with CMM and 4.4% (251/5770) without, an absolute difference of 2.

title: Divergent roles of the regulatory subunits of class IA PI3K
creator: Cho-Won Kim, Junsik M. Lee, Sang Won Park
description: The regulatory subunit of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K), known as p85, is a critical component in the insulin signaling pathway. Extensive research has shed light on the diverse roles played by the two isoforms of p85, namely p85α and p85β. The gene pik3r1 encodes p85α and its variants, p55α and p50α, while pik3r2 encodes p85β.

title: Immune regulatory genes impact the hot/cold tumor microenvironment, affecting cancer treatment and patient outcomes
creator: Mengmeng Sang, Jia Ge, Juan Ge, Gu Tang, Qiwen Wang, Jiarun Wu, Liming Mao, Xiaoling Ding, Xiaorong Zhou
description: Background and aimsImmunologically hot tumors, characterized by an inflamed tumor microenvironment (TME), contrast significantly with immunologically cold tumors. The identification of these tumor immune subtypes holds clinical significance, as hot tumors may exhibit improved prognoses and heightened responsiveness to checkpoint blockade therapy.

title: Effect of death education interventions on death attitudes in medical students: systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Nan Wang, Zhizhong Wang
description: BackgroundThe quality of palliative care depends on medical practitioners’ death cognition and care ability, however, medical students worldwide generally face problems such as death anxiety and insufficient palliative communication skills. Existing studies have not yet formed systematic conclusions on the consistency of the effects of death education interventions and the optimal intervention model.

title: The basal ganglia and the epilepsies
creator: Willian Lazarini‐Lopes, Logan Perry, Patrick A Forcelli
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The basal ganglia are an evolutionarily conserved neural circuit best known for the selection and sequencing of voluntary movement. Increasing evidence, however, indicates that these structures also play an important role in regulating pathological brain states, including seizures. Early pharmacological and lesion studies demonstrated that manipulation of basal ganglia output nuclei, particularly the substantia nigra pars reticulata, profoundly alters seizure susceptibility across multiple experimental models.

title: Sequential transcriptome profiling: comparative analysis of normal and canine lymphoma preceding detailed T-cell and B-cell subtype comparison
creator: Yeji Kim, Jihyun Kim, Yunji Song, Keunhwan Jang, Se Eun Kim, Ha-Jung Kim
description: IntroductionAs the lifespan of companion animals extends, the incidence of tumor also increases. Among these tumors, lymphoma is reported as the most prevalent hematopoietic tumor with a 80-90% prevalence rate. Ongoing research spans multiple domains, aiming to uncover novel therapeutic targets, including small molecular weight inhibitors, antibody treatments, and subtype-specific selective agents.

title: Functional Imaging of Hippocampal Layers Using VASO and BOLD on the Next Generation (NexGen) 7T Scanner
creator: Suvi Häkkinen, Alexander Beckett, Erica Walker, Laurentius Huber, David A Feinberg
description: Spatial accuracy and venous biases are a central concern in mesoscale fMRI, with subcortical brain regions facing additional challenges due to lower sensitivity, high physiological noise, and complicated vasculature. Here, we optimized CBV VASO on the NexGen 7T scanner for layer‐specific investigations of the human hippocampus.

title: Hepatocyte senescence in metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD)
creator: Xinyue Pang, Nan Geng, Chenqi Lu, Qianwen Zhao, Junping Shi, Yali Xiong, Wenhao Li, Jie Li
description: Metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has emerged as a major global health challenge, with particularly high morbidity and disease burden. Cellular senescence has been identified as one of the core mechanisms driving the onset and progression of MASLD. Hepatocytes, the primary functional cells of the liver, can undergo a senescent state under metabolic stress.

title: Potential role for vitamin D vs. intermittent fasting in controlling aquaporin-1 and aquaporin-3 expression in HFD-induced urinary bladder alterations in rats
creator: Hend M. Hassan, Randa El-Gamal, Walaa. H. E. Hamed, Ola Ali Habotta, Mervat Samy, Rasha Elmowafy, Eman Mohamed ElNashar, Mansour Abdullah Alghamdi, Rashid A. Aldahhan, Khulood Mohammed Al-Khater, Mohammed A. Alshehri, Magda E. Ahmed
description: Background: High-fat diet-induced obesity is linked to suppression of aquaporins (AQPs) expression in different tissues. Both vitamin D and intermittent fasting were identified to enhance AQPs expression. In the urinary bladder, AQP-1 and AQP-3 mRNA transcripts were identified. Vitamin D has an impact on a variety of genes that encode proteins that control cell proliferation, differentiation, and death.

title: Machine learning models of noninvasive tests to predict metabolic dysfunction–associated steatohepatitis and fibrosis stage
creator: Rohit Loomba, Rebecca Taub, Dominic Labriola, Jan Priel, Krishna Padmanabhan, W Ray Kim
description: Background:Fibrosis stage in metabolic dysfunction–associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is currently diagnosed by liver biopsy in clinical trials. Using noninvasive tests, no consensus method exists for staging fibrosis or diagnosing MASH. We aimed to develop machine learning (ML) methods to predict fibrosis stage and MASH with F2/F3 fibrosis using noninvasive biomarkers.

title: Improved overall survival in patients with high-grade serous ovarian cancer is associated with CD16a+ immunologic neighborhoods containing NK cells, T cells and macrophages
creator: Sarah Nersesian, Riley J. Arseneau, Jorge P. Mejia, Stacey N. Lee, Lauren P. Westhaver, Nigel W. Griffiths, Stephanie R. Grantham, Liliane Meunier, Laudine Communal, Avik Mukherjee, Anne-Marie Mes-Masson, Thomas Arnason, Brad H. Nelson, Jeanette E. Boudreau
description: BackgroundFor patients with high grade serous carcinoma of the ovary (HGSC), survival rates have remained static for the last half century. Despite the presence of tumor mutations and infiltration of immune cells, existing immunotherapies have achieved little success against HGSC. These observations highlight a gap in the understanding of how the immune system functions and interacts within HGSC tumors.

title: Healthcare Waste Generation Rates in the Three Categories of Public Healthcare Facilities in Malawi
creator: Grace O. Ogbonna, Russel C. G. Chidya, Brighton A. Chunga, Rosemary C. Ogbonna, Fanuel Kapute, Thokozani Mzumara
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThe assessment of the waste generation rate is an initial and critical step in addressing poor healthcare waste management practices.AimThis study aimed to determine the healthcare waste generation rates in primary, secondary, and tertiary healthcare facilities in Malawi.MethodsThis cross‐sectional quantitative study was conducted in two tertiary (Kamuzu and Mzuzu Central Hospital [MCH]), secondary (Nkhata Bay and Rumphi), and primary (Bolero and Chintheche Rural) healthcare facilities.

title: Diagnosis and management of type 2 diabetes mellitus in patients with ischaemic heart disease and acute coronary syndromes - a review of evidence and recommendations
creator: Muhammad Usman Shah, Alun Roebuck, Bala Srinivasan, Joanna Kate Ward, Paul Edward Squires, Claire Elizabeth Hills, Kelvin Lee
description: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) represents a major healthcare condition of the 21st century. It is characterised by persistently elevated blood glucose occurring as a result of peripheral insulin resistance and reduced insulin production which may lead to multiple long-term health conditions such as retinopathy, neuropathy, and nephropathy.

title: Gaming disorder prevention among adolescents in Japan: Challenges and future directions
creator: Kai Kobayashi, Tsubasa Sasaki, Eiji Shimizu
description: valence among adolescents, prevention of GD is urgently needed. This article reviews domestic and international preventive policies and initiatives and discusses GD prevention tailored to Japanese adolescents. Given the limited research on GD prevention, this letter focuses on GD while considering prevention studies on related concepts, including problematic internet use, internet addiction, and internet use disorder.

title: The effect of the number of endometrial CD138+ cells on the pregnancy outcomes of infertile patients in the proliferative phase
creator: Yuye Li, Shuyi Yu, Wenjuan Liu, Yawen Chen, Xiaobing Yang, Juanhua Wu, Mingjuan Xu, Guanying You, Ruochun Lian, Chunyu Huang, Wanru Chen, Yong Zeng, Fenghua Liu, Lianghui Diao
description: ObjectiveThis study was conducted to determine the influence of the number of CD138+ cells in the proliferative endometrium on pregnancy outcomes.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study was conducted from January to August 2018. A total of 664 infertile women who were not diagnosed with chronic endometritis (CE) and who had not received the respective antibiotic treatment were studied.

title: Efficacy of SGLT2 inhibitors in IgA nephropathy associated with alcoholic liver cirrhosis accompanied by nephrotic syndrome: a case report
creator: Yusuke Yoshimura, Daisuke Ikuma, Hiroki Mizuno, Kei Kono, Keiichi Kinowaki, Hisashi Sugimoto, Hisashi Kamido, Yuichiro Sawada, Masato Mizuta, Shigekazu Kurihara, Yuki Oba, Masayuki Yamanouchi, Tatsuya Suwabe, Kenichi Ohashi, Yoshifumi Ubara, Naoki Sawa
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). We present a 51-year-old male patient with a history of Child-Pugh Grade B alcoholic liver cirrhosis (ALC) who developed renal impairment (serum creatinine of 2.00 mg/dL) and nephrotic syndrome (a urinary protein level of 4.35 g/gCr). The patient was diagnosed with immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) associated with ALC based on findings from comprehensive evaluations, including markedly elevated serum IgA levels (883.7 mg/dL), a kidney biopsy revealing significant IgA deposition in the para-mesangial area, and a liver diagnosis showing long-standing advanced ALC.

title: Substrate energetics in non-templated DNA synthesis by terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase
creator: Katrina Mogannam, Andrej Lupták
description: DNA polymerases typically use deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates (dNTPs) for DNA synthesis, yet the contribution of the γ-phosphate to catalysis remains unclear. Here, we examine the role of substrate energetics in enzyme-catalyzed polymerization using a fidelity-independent model polymerase, terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase (TdT).

title: Investigation of the effectiveness of parent-child interaction therapy on adjustment and behavioral problems in children with subthreshold autism
creator: İsmail Seçer, Sümeyye Ulaş, Eda Tatlı, Fatmanur Çimen, Burcu Bülbül, Beyzanur Tosunoğlu
description: BackgroundAutism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is an increasingly prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder. However, the number of children who exhibit subthreshold levels of ASD symptoms, significant enough to experience functional and adaptive difficulties, is also substantial. These children require early interventions, similar to those diagnosed with ASD, due to their exhibited adaptive and behavioral challenges.

title: HURDLER: a cloning method to overcome length limits in designed repeat proteins
creator: Wenzhao Dai, Matthias Schuster, Oliver Zerbe
description: The number of internal repeat modules remains a major limiting factor in the construction and functional exploration of long repeat proteins. As a solution, we present High-Utility Recursive Directional Ligation for Extended Repeat proteins (HURDLER)—a modular cloning strategy combining codon optimization, seamless insertion of restriction sites, and modified recursive directional ligation.

title: Freestanding PZT Films for Integrated Wearable Sensing and Intelligent Acoustic Recognition
creator: Hailong Pan, Zhichao Xu, Rongxiao Liu, Jianmei Pei, Changhong Yang, Shifeng Huang, Michael Wübbenhorst
description: Flexible, self‐powered sensors are pivotal for next‐generation human‐machine interfaces. However, substrate‐induced clamping fundamentally restricts their electromechanical performance by suppressing longitudinal deformation, thereby reducing signal sensitivity. Here, we report a high‐performance freestanding PbZr0.52Ti0.48O3 (PZT) thin film based on a layered Mica/Pt/LaNiO3 heterostructure. The complete release of substrate constraints unlocks markedly enhanced properties, including a 1.

title: Sex Does Not Impact Outcomes of Arthroscopic Treatment of Hip Labral Tears: A Systematic Review and Meta‐analysis
creator: Anne Gordon, Jacob Adams, Reed Coda, Grace Tideman, Damon Mar, Lisa Vopat, Bryan G Vopat, John Paul Schroeppel, Rachel Long, Sterre Van Den Anker
description: PurposeTo conduct a systematic review and meta‐analysis to evaluate sex‐specific outcomes after arthroscopic treatments for hip labral tears.MethodsA review of literature was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta‐Analyses guidelines. Risk of Bias in Non‐Randomized Studies‐Intervention tool was used for the risk‐of‐bias assessment.

title: Listening habits and subjective effects of background music in young adults with and without ADHD
creator: Kelly-Ann Lachance, Pénélope Pelland-Goulet, Nathalie Gosselin
description: Adults listen to an average of 20.7 hours of music per week, according to a study conducted across 26 countries. Numerous studies indicate that listening to music can have beneficial effects on cognitive performance and emotional well-being. Music listening habits may vary depending on individual needs and listening contexts.

title: Local application of silver nitrate as an adjuvant treatment before deep lamellar keratoplasty for fungal keratitis poorly responsive to medical treatment
creator: Gang Ding, Xin Gao, Yue Tan, Zhongkai Hao, Ximing Wang, Chenming Zhang, Aijun Deng
description: ObjectiveThe purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of the local application of silver nitrate (LASN) as an adjuvant treatment before deep lamellar keratoplasty (DLKP) for fungal keratitis responding poorly to medical treatment.MethodsA total of 12 patients (12 eyes) with fungal keratitis responding poorly to medical treatment (for at least 2 weeks) were included.

title: Ets2 Is an Activity‐Dependent Transcriptional Regulator of a Fast‐Twitch Muscle Program
creator: Zaheer A. Rana, Jo C. Bruusgaard, Jens R. Wendland, Ivan Winje, Ingrid M. Egner, Irina Karavanova, Einar Eftestøl, Detlef Vullhorst, Kristian Gundersen, Andres Buonanno
description: The functional properties of excitable cells, including skeletal muscle, are regulated by electrical activity. Distinct motoneuron firing patterns control contraction speed, strength, and endurance of fast‐ and slow‐twitch myofibers by activating transcriptional programs that specify contractile and metabolic protein isoforms.

title: Validation of a MALDI Intact Cell Mass Spectrometry Workflow for Routine Application in Monitoring Industrial E. coli Fermentations
creator: Cristian Zanetti, Christopher Stephan, Rudolf Bednar, Alexandra Foettinger‐Vacha, Martina Marchetti‐Deschmann
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Today, matrix‐assisted laser desorption/ionization‐intact cell mass spectrometry (MALDI‐ICMS) is used in clinical environments for rapid pathogen identification, referred to as MALDI biotyping. This method relies on the generation of characteristic mass spectrometric profiles of intact microorganisms. Single‐celled organisms are often used for pharmaceutical production, while this allows for the production of complex products, close monitoring and control of these processes is essential.

title: MR imaging-based risk stratification scoring system to predict clinical outcomes in carotid body tumors
creator: Abhishek Mahajan, Atif Shaikh, Shreya Shukla, Richa Vaish, Ujjwal Agarwal, Vasundhara Smriti, Shivam Rastogi, Shonal Deokar, Shubham Suryavanshi, Pankaj Chaturvedi, Sarbani Ghosh Laskar, Kumar Prabhash, Vijay Patil, Vanita Noronha, Nandini Menon, Prathamesh Pai, Gouri Pantvaidya, Swapnil Ulhas Rane,
description: ObjectivesThis study aims to evaluate the role of pretherapy MRI in predicting outcomes in carotid body tumors and propose a grading system for high- and low-risk characteristics.Materials and methodsA retrospective observational study of 44 patients with 51 lesions was carried out from year 2005 to 2020.

title: The impact of a nurse navigation program on health, economic and medical outcomes of cancer patients in Saxony – a multicenter, prospective, randomized controlled trial
creator: Ralf Porzig, Thomas Heckmann, Jens Schnabel, Detlef Quietzsch, Christine König, Daniela Adolf, Ursula G Froster
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundCancer patients frequently experience complex psychosocial and informational needs that are challenging to address within fragmented healthcare environments, resulting in care inefficiencies and patient distress. Nurse navigation programs aim to provide structured, continuous coordination.

title: Exploring 3D anatomy: A free online course supporting novice learner inquiry and spatial conceptualization
creator: Jiayi Zhang, Moksh Sachdeva, Calum McCaig, Eleanor Gordon, Leonard Shapiro, Iain D. Keenan
description: Application of three‐dimensional anatomical knowledge is essential for patient examination, diagnosis, and treatment and is crucial in the training of medical and healthcare students. Moreover, critical observation and spatial awareness are vital for learner understanding of three‐dimensional anatomical structures and relationships. However, there are logistical barriers to curricular integration of teaching that explicitly targets these skills.

title: Cardiorespiratory and metabolic consequences of detraining in endurance athletes
creator: Arianna Barbieri, Andrea Fuk, Gabriele Gallo, Daniel Gotti, Andrea Meloni, Antonio La Torre, Luca Filipas, Roberto Codella
description: Background: A training program can stimulate physiological, anatomical, and performance adaptations, but these improvements can be partially or entirely reversed due to the cessation of habitual physical activity resulting from illness, injury, or other influencing factors. Purpose: To investigate the effects of detraining on cardiorespiratory, metabolic, hormonal, muscular adaptations, as well as short-term and long-term performance changes in endurance athletes.

title: Why Anthropologists Should Study Dogs
creator: Kyle C. M. Smith
description: While primates have traditionally been a focus of evolutionary anthropologists, the domestic dog represents a valuable complementary model due to its long shared evolutionary history with humans. The advantages of studying dogs are particularly evident in four key areas: (1) analyzing evolutionary adaptations, (2) understanding humanity's past, (3) examining humanity's cultural diversity, and (4) assessing factors that influence human health.

title: Understanding cultural perceptions of sexuality in China and their influence on human papillomavirus vaccine hesitancy
creator: Jiayuan Jin, Yanchao Han
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionThe human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine prevents infections that may result in precancerous lesions, cervical cancers, genital warts, and many other diseases. However, its uptake rate in China is 2.24%, and HPV vaccine hesitancy is widespread.

title: Symbolic and non-symbolic geometric abilities across development and in individuals with dyscalculia and dyslexia
creator: Elisa Castaldi, Giovanni Anobile, Moreno Marazzi, Stefano Federici, Paola Angelelli, Marco Turi
description: SummaryGeometry is fundamental to mathematical thinking, yet its foundations and difficulties in learning disorders remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the development of geometric abilities and their relationship with developmental dyscalculia and dyslexia. Seventy-nine children and adults, including individuals with and without learning difficulties, completed behavioral measures of non-symbolic geometry and a paper-and-pencil assessment of symbolic geometry.

title: Persistent functionalized triarylmethyl radicals: when spin meets chirality
creator: Imma Ratera, Jaume Veciana, Paula Mayorga-Burrezo
description: For decades, persistent trityl radical derivatives have been the object of intense research in a wide variety of disciplines, ranging from fundamental to applied science, thanks to the versatility of their properties (magnetic, optical, redox, etc.) and their potential as multifunctional open-shell building blocks.

title: Chiral coronene diimide assemblies with strong chiroptical properties in solution and thin-films
creator: Denis Hartmann, Artemijs Krimovs, Oussama Errida, Tiberiu-M. Gianga, Giuliano Siligardi, Robert Pal, Timothy A. Barendt
description: The self-assembly of chiral organic dyes provides an effective route to strongly chiral optical materials. Herein, we report a novel coronene diimide derivative with point-chiral imide groups derived from l/d-valinol. This chiral chromophore shows solvent-dependent aggregation and readily self-assembles via π-stacking into strongly chiroptically active materials, effectively translating point chirality into supramolecular chirality in the assembly.

title: Psychometrics assessment of ethical decision-making around end-of-life care scale for adolescents in the final stage of life
creator: Fateme Mohammadi, Seyedeh Zahra Masoumi, Salman Khazaei, Seyyed Mohammad Mahdi Hosseiny
description: IntroductionHealthcare professionals have a critical role in ethical decision-making around end-of-life care. Properly evaluating the ethical decision-making of health care professionals in end-of-life care requires reliable, tailored, and comprehensive assessments. The current study aimed to translate and assess psychometrically a Persian version of the ethical decision making in end-of-life care scale for Iranian adolescents in the final stages of life.

title: Unraveling the impact of nitric oxide, almitrine, and their combination in COVID-19 (at the edge of sepsis) patients: a systematic review
creator: Ying Wang, Qian Yu, Yuan Tian, Shiying Ren, Liping Liu, Chaojie Wei, Renli Liu, Jing Wang, Dong Li, Kun Zhu
description: Introduction: During the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, a large number of critically ill and severe COVID-19 patients meet the diagnostic criteria for sepsis and even septic shock. The treatments for COVID-19 patients with sepsis are still very limited. For sepsis, improving ventilation is one of the main treatments.

title: A randomized, placebo-controlled, phase II study of docetaxel and platinum with or without erlotinib in recurrent/metastatic head and neck squamous-cell carcinomas
creator: W.N. William, L. Feng, M.S. Kies, S. Ahmed, G.R. Blumenschein, B.S. Glisson, E. Massarelli, F.M. Johnson, C. Lu, X. Le, L.P. Kowalski, E.S. Kim
description: PurposeWe conducted a randomized phase II trial to evaluate whether adding erlotinib to platinum/docetaxel improves clinical outcomes in the first-line treatment of recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous-cell carcinomas, building on our previous single-arm phase II trial.Patients and methodsThis was a placebo-controlled, double-blind, single-center phase II study.

title: Notes on psychiatrist liability around the world regarding suicide
creator: Anna Saya, Giuseppe Albanesi, Diego Cichetti, Matteo Di Molfetta, Yuri Guarino, Cinzia Niolu, Alberto Siracusano
description: BackgroundCurrently, there is a lively debate regarding involuntary treatment and the psychiatrist's liability for suicide of patients with serious mental illness. This article aims to highlight the worldwide differences, considering that in some countries suicide is still considered a crime, while elsewhere, access to euthanasia/medically assisted suicide is allowed even for psychiatric patients.

title: A Shared Chemokine Signature of Triglyceride-Rich Lipoproteins and lipoprotein(a)
creator: Mira Mousa, Jeffrey Kroon
description: Corresponding Author Low-density lipoprotein (LDL), triglyceride-rich lipoproteins/remnants (TRL), and lipoprotein(a) (Lp[a]) are causal drivers of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (CVD), yet they do not appear to act through identical biological pathways.1 TRL/remnants and Lp(a) may be several-fold more atherogenic per particle than LDL, raising an important biological question: what distinguishes one atherogenic apolipoprotein B (apoB)-containing particle from another?

title: 12-week yoga intervention effect on metabolome in Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS): An LC-MS-based study
creator: Deepika Kumari, Hanuman Prasad Sharma, Yashwant Kumar, Neena Malhotra, Reeta Mahey, Rima Dada
description: BackgroundPolyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is a complex, heterogeneous disorder affecting endocrine, reproductive, and metabolic health. It is fundamentally a systemic metabolic defect that, if not addressed in time, can compromise the function of multiple systems, resulting in conditions such as impaired glucose tolerance, insulin resistance, cardiovascular disease, dyslipidemia, fatty liver disease, and type 2 diabetes mellitus.

title: Integrating technology in leech therapy: Toward standardized evidence-based Ayurvedic practice
creator: Ramakrishna Allam, B. Kothainayagi, P.A. Sudhir, Vanitha R. Muralikumar, S. Sajitha, K. Sudharsan, S. Vasanth
description: Jalaukavacharana (leech therapy), an integral part of Ayurvedic medicine, is widely recognized for its benefits in managing chronic wounds, inflammatory conditions, and vascular disorders. However, its traditional application often lacks standardized procedures, real-time monitoring, and regulatory oversight, limiting its acceptance in modern clinical practice.

title: Case report: Rare observation of thyroid-like cholangiocarcinoma
creator: Ekaterina Bondarenko, Dmitriy Kalinin, Liliya Urusova, Dariya Pastukhova, Rustam Salimkhanov, Natalia Mokrysheva
description: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma is a highly malignant tumor with a poor prognosis. Radical surgical resection remains the “gold standard” for improving patient outcomes; however, only a minority of patients qualify for this approach. Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma is primarily classified into two major histologic types: small and large ductal cholangiocarcinomas. Nevertheless, rare subtypes with unique diagnostic and prognostic characteristics are increasingly reported.

title: Aggressive features and immune landscape of macrotrabecular hepatocellular carcinoma
creator: Lixia Wu, Meidan Li, Xuefang Wang, Qionglan Wu, Yi Chen, Bin Wang, Lihong Chen
description: Highlights•MT-HCC exhibits more aggressive clinical and pathological features than CV-HCC.•Higher AFP, larger tumor size and more vascular invasion are observed in MT-HCC.•Distinct immune cell distribution patterns are identified in different tumor regions.•CD20+ B cells in the tumor margin correlate with favorable prognosis.•FOXP3+ regulatory T cells and CTLA-4+ lymphocytes are linked to poorer outcomes.

title: Body donor reperfusion and re-ventilation in medical training: an Italian study testing SimLife®
creator: Irene Neri, Giulio Vara, Antonietta Fazio, Maria Vittoria Marvi, Foteini-Dionysia Koufi, Elisa Boschetti, Simone Lodi, Giulia Adalgisa Mariani, Marilisa Quaranta, Anna Maria Billi, Alessandra Ruggeri, Carlo Barausse, Cyril Brèque, Annalisa Plava, Veronica Moretti, Lucia Manzoli, Stefano Ratti
description: BackgroundMedical simulations have emerged as a valuable tool in anatomical-medical training, allowing healthcare professionals to gain hands-on experience in a controlled and safe environment. One such simulation platform is SimLife®, which uses the Pulse for Practice (P4P) system to enable realistic restoration of airflow (“re-ventilation”) and blood flow (“revascularization”) in bodies donated to science.

title: Role of Psychological Resilience on Emotional Health in Kidney and Liver Transplant Recipients
creator: Marta Katarzyna Hreńczuk, Tomasz Dawid Piątek, Joanna Gotlib-Małkowska, Mariusz Panczyk, Piotr Małkowski
description: BackgroundPsychological resilience is an increasingly recognized important protective factor for emotional health after solid organ transplantation; however, its role in the early post-transplant period is insufficiently explored. This study examined the role of psychological resilience in emotional health among kidney and liver transplant recipients, using a cross-sectional indirect-effect model.Material/MethodsA cross-sectional, multicenter study was conducted at 4 transplant centers in Poland.

title: Hair cortisol concentration in finishing pigs on commercial farms: variability between pigs, batches, and farms
creator: Pierre Levallois, Mily Leblanc-Maridor, Anne Lehébel, Solenn Gavaud, Blandine Lieubeau, Julie Hervé, Christine Fourichon, Catherine Belloc
description: Hair cortisol is a stress indicator and could be used to assess the pigs’ exposure to stressors in the weeks/months prior to non-invasive hair sampling. The main aim of this study was to describe the hair cortisol concentration (HCC) variability between individuals within a batch, between farms and between batches within a farm.

title: Aqueous humor metabolomic profiling identifies a distinct signature in pseudoexfoliation syndrome
creator: Arturs Zemitis, Juris Vanags, Theresa Schiemer, Kristaps Klavins, Guna Laganovska
description: PurposePEXS was first described in 1917, yet its etiology still needs clarification. An imbalance between oxidants and antioxidants plays a significant role. PEXS leads to various ocular complications, including increased risk during cataract surgery due to weak zonules, lens dislocation, and reduced visual outcomes. Our study investigates whether metabolomics can provide insights into this ocular pathology.

title: Reply to “Methodological caveats in interpreting slow-wave slope as a marker of synaptic homeostasis in OSA”
creator: Rama Maganti, Jun Wang, Scott Hetzel
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). synaptic dynamics and that physiological and structural factors can influence its measurement. Widespread structural brain abnormalities, including white matter injury and cortical changes, were shown in OSA that may alter neuronal synchronization and signal propagation [3]. Furthermore, any change caused by a structural brain abnormality would likely be persistent throughout the night and, in part, may contribute to changes in scalp-recorded slow-wave characteristics. We acknowledge the lack of imaging as a limitation of our study.

title: The relationship between deltamethrin-induced behavioral changes and acetylcholinesterase activity in zebrafish embryos or larvae based on transcriptome
creator: Chunyu Liu, Yantong Guo, Xue Zhang, Hongsong Chen, Maomao Han, Han Wang, Jieyao Niu, Jinfei He, Jingfeng Yang, Wu Dong, Jiangdong Xue
description: BackgroundDeltamethrin (DM) is a broad-spectrum insecticide that is widely used to control agricultural pests. Recently, DM has posed a potential threat to the health of infants and young children, and this is because of the environmental and food pollution that is caused by the extensive use of DM.

title: MRI for restaging pancreatic cancer
creator: Giulia A. Zamboni, Federica Omboni, Irene Panozzo
description: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma is a tumor with a dismal prognosis, as the majority of patients are diagnosed when the tumor is not resectable. Neoadjuvant treatment has significantly improved prognosis, but assessing treatment response can be challenging for radiologists. Given the fibrotic nature of the primary tumor, differentiating between residual viable tumor and fibrotic response can be difficult.

title: Single-cell RNA sequencing reveals the dysfunctional characteristics of PBMCs in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus
creator: Jindong Zhao, Zhaohui Fang
description: IntroductionType 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a disease that involves autoimmunity. However, how immune cells function in the peripheral blood remains unclear. Exploring T2DM biomarkers via single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) could provide new insights into the underlying molecular mechanisms.MethodsThe clinical trial registration number is ChiCTR2100049613. In this study, we included three healthy participants and three T2DM patients.

title: Erythropoietin supplementation induces dysbiosis of the gut microbiota and impacts mucosal immunity in a non-diseased mouse model
creator: Guillaume Sarrabayrouse, Corentin Joulain, Stéphanie Bessoles, Andrada S. Chiron, Amine M. Abina, Salima Hacein-Bey-Abina
description: A number of drug treatments are known to alter the dialogue between the gut microbiota and the immune system components in the digestive mucosa. Alterations in intestinal homeostasis are now well known to affect peripheral immune responses and favor the occurrence of a number of pathologies such as allergies and cancers.

title: Evaluation of early C‐reactive protein kinetics as an early response marker in biliary tract cancer treated with combined chemoimmunotherapy: A multicenter observational study
creator: Gabriel Allo, Joshua Leutiger, Catherine Leyh, Christian Möhring, Ann‐Kristin Zöller, Vera Himmelsbach, Gianluca Ciarlo, Maryam Barsch, Christoph Neumann‐Haefelin, Bertram Bengsch, Fabian Finkelmeier, Mohamad Murad, Cennet Sahin, Marie‐Luise Berres, Maria A. Gonzalez‐Carmona, Christoph Roderburg, Ar
description: BackgroundReliable prognostic biomarkers for treatment response in patients with biliary tract cancer (BTC) who receive chemoimmunotherapy are still lacking. The objective of this study was to evaluate the potential of early C‐reactive protein (CRP) kinetics as a tool for predicting survival in these patients.

title: Bioactive adrenomedullin dynamics and microcirculatory changes in a porcine model of hemorrhagic shock
creator: Carolin Vekla, Oliver Hartmann, Sebastian O Decker, Maik von der Forst, Florian Uhle, Alexander Studier-Fischer, Berkin Özdemir, Felix Nickel, Stephan Katzenschlager, Frank Weilbacher, Thorsten Brenner, Erik Popp, Markus A Weigand, Karsten Schmidt, Maximilian Dietrich, Daniel Gruneberg
description: BackgroundHemorrhagic shock is a leading cause of preventable trauma death, marked by impaired oxygen delivery and endothelial dysfunction. Bioactive adrenomedullin (bio-ADM) regulates endothelial barrier integrity, but its dynamics during hemorrhagic shock and resuscitation remain unclear. This secondary analysis of a porcine hemorrhagic shock model investigated bio-ADM and its association with macro- and microcirculatory parameters during resuscitation.

title: Population genetics of Plasmodium vivax with transmission decline and rebound in two endemic areas of Papua New Guinea
creator: Abebe A. Fola, Somya Mehra, Zahra Razook, Dulcie Lautu-Gumal, Elma Nate, Stuart Lee, Johanna Helena Kattenberg, Cristian Koepfli, James Kazura, Maria Ome-Kaius, Moses Laman, Leanne J. Robinson, Ivo Mueller, Alyssa E. Barry
description: BackgroundGlobal efforts to control and eventually eliminate malaria have been less effective for Plasmodium vivax relative to Plasmodium falciparum due to its unique biology, including dormant liver stages that cause later relapse, and earlier commitment to transmission stages. After the nationwide distribution of long-lasting insecticide treated nets (LLIN) in Papua New Guinea (PNG), P.

title: Psychological, psychiatric, and behavioral sciences measurement scales: best practice guidelines for their development and validation
creator: Alberto Stefana, Stefano Damiani, Umberto Granziol, Umberto Provenzani, Marco Solmi, Eric A. Youngstrom, Paolo Fusar-Poli
description: Psychiatric, psychological, and behavioral sciences scales provide quantitative representations of phenomena such as emotions, beliefs, functioning, and social role perceptions. Methodologists and researchers have criticized current scale development practices, emphasizing that inaccurate measurements can derail theory development and clinical decisions, thereby impeding progress in mental health research and practice.

title: Precise and interpretable neural networks reveal epigenetic signatures of aging across youth in health and disease
creator: David Martínez-Enguita, Thomas Hillerton, Julia Åkesson, Daniel Kling, Maria Lerm, Mika Gustafsson
description: IntroductionDNA methylation (DNAm) age clocks are powerful tools for measuring biological age, providing insights into aging risks and outcomes beyond chronological age. While traditional models are effective, their interpretability is limited by their dependence on small and potentially stochastic sets of CpG sites.

title: In vitro evaluation of bio-fortification effects on the nutritional quality, toxicological safety, and antioxidant of cassava (Manihot esculenta) flour, and environmental safety of processing water, using natural additives
creator: Tasahil S. Albishi, D. Adaigho, Nashi K. Alqahtani, Rokayya Sami, Hilary Uguru, Mahmoud Helal, Shatha H. Alaoufi, Mohammed Saeed Alkaltham, D. Osiga-Aibangbee, G. I. Okolotu, E. P. Emumejaye, Sameer H. Qari
description: The impact of bio-fortification on the nutritional quality, anti-nutritional factors, glycemic indices, and toxicological effects of cassava (Manihot esculenta) flour (CF), was investigated in vitro in this scientific research. The cassava roots were administered with, eleven distinct treatment strategies (F1 to F11), formulated from Moringa oleífera leaves, Syzygium aromaticum seeds, and Curcuma longa rhizomes derivatives.

title: Language-supervised electrocardiogram interpretation with vision transformer
creator: Xue Zhou, Tianhui Li, Keijiro Nakamura, Hiromasa Hayama, Shing-Hong Liu, Tetsuo Sasano, Wenxi Chen, Xin Zhu
description: PurposeMost artificial intelligence models for electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation rely on task-specific supervised learning, requiring dedicated labeled datasets for each diagnostic task and limiting scalability across diverse cardiac conditions. This study investigated whether vision-language learning from paired ECG recordings and summary reports could enable transferable ECG representations without task-specific supervised training.

title: Enhancing smart home environments: a novel pattern recognition approach to ambient acoustic event detection and localization
creator: Ahsan Shabbir, Abdul Haleem Butt, Taha Khan, Lorenzo Chiari, Ahmad Almadhor, Vincent Karovic
description: IntroductionAmbient acoustic detection and localization play a vital role in identifying events and their origins from acoustic data. This study aimed to establish a comprehensive framework for classifying activities in home environments to detect emergency events and transmit emergency signals.

title: Management of Merkel Cell Carcinoma of the Digits, Hand, and Wrist
creator: Karanvir S Raman, Rahul Thareja, Gabriel Bensimon, Charles Arcand, Abdulaziz AlAzzam, Caroline Esmonde-White, Gabriel N Kuper, Raisa Chowdhury, Maitha AlShamsi, Charlotte Jaloux
description: IntroductionMerkel cell carcinoma (MCC) is a rare and often lethal cancer, with few cases presenting on the hand and digits. Treatments such as ray amputation can drastically impact quality of life and the existing literature is inconclusive. This systematic review evaluates the comprehensive management of surgically treated patients with MCC involving the digits, hand, and wrist.

title: Differential eco-physiological performance to declining groundwater depth in Central Asian C3 and C4 shrubs in the Gurbantunggut Desert
creator: Bahejiayinaer Tiemuerbieke, Jian-Ying Ma, Wei Sun
description: Resources in water-limited ecosystems are highly variable and unpredictable, and the maintenance of functional diversity among coexisting species is a crucial ecological strategy through which plants mitigate environmental stress. The comparison of differential eco-physiological responses among co-occurring plants in harsh environments could help provide deep insights into the coexistence mechanisms of competing species.

title: Extracellular ATP/adenosine dynamics in the brain and its role in health and disease
creator: Eiji Shigetomi, Kent Sakai, Schuichi Koizumi
description: Extracellular ATP and adenosine are neuromodulators that regulate numerous neuronal functions in the brain. Neuronal activity and brain insults such as ischemic and traumatic injury upregulate these neuromodulators, which exert their effects by activating purinergic receptors. In addition, extracellular ATP/adenosine signaling plays a pivotal role in the pathogenesis of neurological diseases.

title: Circular bioeconomy-driven carotenoid production by Agrococcus sp. NP24 using cheese whey byproduct: process optimization and bioactivity assessment
creator: Nehad Noby, Fatma Elsayed, Mahmoud M. Agami, Nadia A. Soliman
description: Growing interest in the circular economy has promoted the use of agri-food wastes as fermentable and readily available substrates for microbial cultivation, offering a sustainable and cost-effective strategy for natural pigment production. In this study, cheese whey was utilized as a nutritional substrate for pigment synthesis by an isolated strain identified as Agrococcus sp. NP24 (PQ097720.1).

title: Cytochalasins are a fascinating class of natural compounds: advances in the chemistry, biological activities, mode of action, and structure-activity relationships of novel cytochalasins isolated in the last decade are described
creator: Antonio Evidente
description: Cytochalasins are a very intriguing group of natural compounds. Since the first isolation of the well-known cytochalasins A and B in 1966, over 300 analogues have been described as metabolites, primarily produced by various fungal genera. Their bioactivities, targets, total syntheses, and biosyntheses had been also extensively investigated. After the review of Scherlach et al.

title: Ischemic paralysis caused by internal iliac artery embolism after endovascular recanalization for lower extremity arteriosclerosis obliterans: a case report
creator: Jing Wang, Jing Li, Xuemin Zhang, Xiaoming Zhang, Tao Zhang
description: BackgroundLower extremity paralysis is a devastating complication after endovascular therapy for lower extremity arteriosclerosis obliterans (LEAOD). Common mechanisms include ischemia–reperfusion injury, acute arterial embolism, and thrombosis. Paralysis caused by internal iliac artery embolism is exceptionally rare and may be overlooked when postoperative neurologic deficits are initially attributed to spinal or cerebral causes.

title: Prevalence and characteristics of gastrointestinal disorders, medication use, and diagnostic interventions in pediatric patients with cystic fibrosis: a nested case–control analysis from the TriNetX EMR-derived global research network real-world dataset
creator: Carolena Trocchia, Maua Mosha, Bailey Hamner, Neil Goldenberg, Racha Khalaf
description: BackgroundGastrointestinal (GI) disease in pediatric patients with cystic fibrosis (CF) is a growing concern in the era of improved lung disease; however, the true prevalence of GI diagnoses, medical therapies, and frequency of diagnostic and therapeutic interventions in this population have yet to be explored on a multisystem scale.

title: Hearing Preservation Rates After Cochlear Implantation Using Soft Surgery Techniques
creator: Tina C Huang, Scott Lunos
description: ObjectivesTo determine if hearing preservation rates after cochlear implantation varied over time with soft surgery techniques.MethodsThe hearing preservation rate over time in adult cochlear implant patients over 10 years was analyzed. The association between hearing preservation rate and sex, age, perioperative steroid dose, and type of electrode was analyzed. Low frequency hearing preservation was analyzed separately.

title: Identification of wheat seedling varieties based on MssiapNet
creator: Yongqiang Feng, Chengzhong Liu, Junying Han, Qinglin Lu, Xue Xing
description: IntroductionIn the actual planting of wheat, there are often shortages of seedlings and broken seedlings on long ridges in the field, thus affecting grain yield and indirectly causing economic losses. Variety identification of wheat seedlings using physical methods timeliness and is unsuitable for universal dissemination.

title: Positive youth development and youth peacebuilding in Colombia
creator: Vivian Liu, Ellen Kneeskern, Valentina Duarte Valderrama, Claudia Pineda‐Marin, Laura K. Taylor
description: Positive Youth Development (PYD) is a strengths‐based framework related to young people's well‐being and agency in their environment, which has been recognized as a cornerstone of peaceful societies. Similarly, a growing body of research has documented youth peacebuilding as a way for youth to engage with and foster constructive change interpersonally, structurally, and culturally.

title: Infrared imaging and intravascular laser irradiation of blood therapy for glycemic control in type 2 diabetes mellitus: a technical note
creator: Philype Antonio Calazans Candido, Gabriel Carneiro Brioschi, Marcos Leal Brioschi, Kathleen Melchior Altruda
description: This technical note presents a standardized method that integrates intravascular laser irradiation of blood (ILIB) with infrared thermography to visualize real-time physiological responses during treatment. One adult male with long-standing type 2 diabetes underwent ten ILIB sessions using a 660 nm transcutaneous laser applied over the left radial artery.

title: Renal Neuroendocrine Tumor Mimicking Upper Tract Urothelial Carcinoma
creator: Jia‐Yuh Sheu, Yun‐Sheng Wu, Jeff S. Chueh
description: IntroductionRenal pelvic or peripelvic neuroendocrine tumors are rare and may radiologically mimic invasive upper tract urothelial carcinoma.Case PresentationA man in his 70s presented with two episodes of painless gross hematuria and lower urinary tract symptoms from benign prostatic hyperplasia. Computed tomography urography and magnetic resonance imaging showed a 3.

title: Differential expression of complement Properdin and Factor H in the placentae and umbilical cords of mothers with Preeclampsia, Gestational Diabetes Mellitus and Recurrent Pregnancy Loss
creator: Tamali Roy, Ananya Das, Nabanita Chatterjee, Shyama Prasad Saha, Rajib Prasad, Taruna Madan, Hadida Yasmin, Uday Kishore
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundProperdin and factor H (FH), the two regulatory proteins of the alternative complement pathway, oppose each other to maintain the complement system’s activation. While properdin upregulates, FH downregulates the complement alternative pathway.

title: Perspective on Electrochemical Lead Detection: Distributed Sensing to Address Unevenly Distributed Risk
creator: Elizabeth R. Jacobia, A. Andrew D. Jones III
description: Lead contamination is a global issue and requires detection for risk evaluation and remediation. Standardized testing is accurate and effective for water quality monitoring, however, does not provide real-time results and is not widely accessible. Electrochemical detection methods have been developed with comparable lead sensitivity and selectivity to standard methods.

title: Exploring the feasibility of real-time on-device ECG biometric classification using quantized neural networks
creator: Martin Berki, Anton Mateasik, Michal Micjan, Erik Vavrinsky, Krisztian Gasparek, Lubos Cernaj
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Biometric classification using electrocardiogram (ECG) signals offers a promising pathway for continuous, personalized healthcare monitoring. This work presents a proof-of-concept embedded deep learning system for real-time ECG biometric classification on wearable Holter devices, reducing reliance on continuous cloud connectivity. A quantized convolutional neural network (CNN) was deployed on an STM32H7 microcontroller to identify individuals based on unique ECG patterns, incorporating an initial signal quality assessment stage to ensure that only high-quality segments are processed.

title: Synergistic and antibiofilm activity of colistin combined with cinnamaldehyde and eugenol against colistin-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii clinical isolates
creator: Abdulhamit Çalı, Rukiye Aslan, Kübra Fırtına Topcu, Cem Çelik
description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of combinations of colistin (COL) with cinnamaldehyde (CIN) or eugenol (EUG) against planktonic and biofilm forms of colistin-resistant clinical Acinetobacter baumannii isolates.MethodsMinimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values of COL and essential oil components in 10 colistin-resistant clinical isolates were evaluated by the broth microdilution method.

title: Discontinuation of palopegteriparatide in chronic hypoparathyroidism without rebound hypocalcemia
creator: Lars Rejnmark, Line Underbjerg
description: A woman with chronic hypoparathyroidism following total thyroidectomy was treated with palopegteriparatide, a long-acting parathyroid hormone replacement therapy, for more than 4 years. Previous reports have suggested that stopping parathyroid hormone therapy may lead to severe rebound hypocalcemia and increased calcium requirements due to a “hungry bone syndrome.

title: High monocytic MDSC signature predicts multi-drug resistance and cancer relapse in non-Hodgkin lymphoma patients treated with R-CHOP
creator: Sukanya Dhar, Mohona Chakravarti, Nilanjan Ganguly, Akata Saha, Shayani Dasgupta, Saurav Bera, Anirban Sarkar, Kamalika Roy, Juhina Das, Avishek Bhuniya, Sarbari Ghosh, Madhurima Sarkar, Srabanti Hajra, Saptak Banerjee, Chiranjib Pal, Bhaskar Saha, Kalyan Kusum Mukherjee, Rathindranath Baral, Anamik
description: IntroductionNon-Hodgkin Lymphoma (NHL) is a heterogeneous lymphoproliferative malignancy with B cell origin. Combinatorial treatment of rituximab, cyclophsphamide, hydroxydaunorubicin, oncovin, prednisone (R-CHOP) is the standard treatment regimen for NHL, yielding a complete remission (CR) rate of 40-50%. Unfortunately, considerable patients undergo relapse after CR or initial treatment, resulting in poor clinical implications.

title: Detection of Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis in Bovine Faeces Using a Rhodamine B Hydrazone Immunosensor on Antibody‐Coated Nitrocellulose Membranes
creator: Mohammad Khosravi, Darioush Gharibi, Rozhin Ansari, Mahdi Pourmahdi Borujeni, Mohammad Nouri
description: Rapid, inexpensive and reliable detection of Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis (MAP) is essential for the control of Johne's disease. This study developed a rhodamine B hydrazone nanoparticle‐based immunosensor coupled with antibody‐coated nitrocellulose membranes (IMS‐CNM) for the detection of MAP in bovine faecal samples. Anti‐MAP antibodies were purified from hyperimmune donkey and rabbit sera.

title: Elucidating the susceptibility to breast cancer: an in-depth proteomic and transcriptomic investigation into novel potential plasma protein biomarkers
creator: Yang Wang, Kexin Yi, Baoyue Chen, Bailin Zhang, Gao Jidong
description: Objectives: This study aimed to identify plasma proteins that are associated with and causative of breast cancer through Proteome and Transcriptome-wide association studies combining Mendelian Randomization. Methods: Utilizing high-throughput datasets, we designed a two-phase analytical framework aimed at identifying novel plasma proteins that are both associated with and causative of breast cancer.

title: The mediating role of body surface area-adjusted basal metabolic rate: effects of low muscle mass and central obesity on cognitive impairment in Chinese patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus
creator: Ya-Jie Zhai, Fang Li, Chen-Ying Lin, Fan Wu, Hui-Na Qiu, Jing-Bo Li, Jing-Na Lin
description: BackgroundThis study investigates the relationship between basal metabolic rate (BMR), body composition, obesity indices, and cognitive impairment (CI) in middle-aged and older type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) patients, assessing their potential role in CI screening.MethodsA cross-sectional study included 1243 T2DM patients over 45 years old. CI was assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment.

title: Highly neutralizing anti–IFN-ω autoantibodies underlie severe pediatric adenovirus infection
creator: Chen-Xuan Kang, Jing-Ya Ding, Yu-Fang Lo, Tsai-Yi Wu, Han-Po Shih, Jhan-Jie Peng, Kung-Wei Lin, You-Ning Lin, Chia-Chi Lo, Shao-Hsuan Hsia, Jainn-Jim Lin, En-Pei Lee, Oi-Wa Chan, Yhu-Chering Huang, Chih-Jung Chen, Tzou-Yien Lin, Cheng-Lung Ku, Chen-Yen Kuo
description: A case of neutralizing anti–IFN-ω autoantibodies impairing antiviral defense and driving severe adenovirus pneumonia in a child. Introduction Human adenoviruses (HAdVs) are non-enveloped double-stranded DNA viruses that commonly infect children under 5 years of age, largely due to the immaturity of humoral immunity in young children (1, 2). HAdVs are classified into seven species (A–G) comprising 113 genotypes (http://hadvwg.gmu.edu).

title: Identification and functional analysis of sRNAs in Pseudomonas aeruginosa quorum sensing and virulence regulation
creator: Tianmin Li, Beifang Lu, Fang Chen, Letong Xu, Yizhou Zhang, Fangzhou Xie, Yue Sun, Chunyan Yao, Jiadai Huang, Tianlong He, Youyue Li, Yiqing Ding, Haiyan Hu, Shaojun Tang, Xin Deng
description: Small RNAs (sRNAs) act as critical regulators of post-transcriptional activity and diverse cellular processes in bacteria. However, the entire repertoire of sRNAs and their functions has not yet been extensively studied. This study employs a novel combined computational-experimental prediction approach to identify and characterize small RNAs (sRNAs) in Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1.

title: Moyamoya disease presenting as galactorrhea
creator: Sasan D Noveir, Nupur Agrawal
description: Moyamoya disease (MMD) is a progressive cerebrovascular condition marked by carotid narrowing and collateral vessel formation. Patients are often diagnosed after a stroke, but here we describe a case of galactorrhea as the presenting symptom of MMD. A 30-year-old gravida 1, para 0 woman noted milky, nonbloody discharge leaking from both breasts after manual compression during sexual intercourse.

title: Multiple sclerosis clinical forms classification with graph convolutional networks based on brain morphological connectivity
creator: Enyi Chen, Berardino Barile, Françoise Durand-Dubief, Thomas Grenier, Dominique Sappey-Marinier
description: Multiple Sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune disease that combines chronic inflammatory and neurodegenerative processes underlying different clinical forms of evolution, such as relapsing-remitting, secondary progressive, or primary progressive MS. This identification is usually performed by clinical evaluation at the diagnosis or during the course of the disease for the secondary progressive phase.

title: Generalisability of an adult-trained AI model to paediatric coeliac disease diagnosis: a multicentre external validation study
creator: Florian Jaeckle, Peter M Gillett, Kathryn J Kirkwood, Shonali Natu, James YH Chan, Adrian C Bateman, Mark J Arends, Elizabeth J Soilleux
description: SummaryBackgroundCoeliac disease diagnosis on duodenal biopsies is limited by interobserver variability. We have previously demonstrated pathologist-level performance with our artificial intelligence (AI) model for the histopathological diagnosis of adult coeliac disease, but not in paediatric practice. As paediatric coeliac disease screening programmes expand internationally, accurate and scalable diagnostic tools are needed.

title: Epigenome-wide DNA methylation profiling in septic and non-septic patients with similar infections: potential use as sepsis biomarkers
