In rapidly growing tumors, including gliomas, heterogeneous microenvironments with fluctuating oxygen and nutrient availability impose strong selective pressure for metabolic adaptation. For over a century, mitochondria have been recognized as central to the reprogramming of cancer metabolism. However, it remains unclear whether and how remodeling of oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), including organization of electron transport chain (ETC) complexes, contributes to the proliferation of cancer cells.

title: Effective microorganisms input efficiently improves the vegetation and microbial community of degraded alpine grassland
creator: Jinsheng Li, Juping Wei, Xinqing Shao, Xinhui Yan, Kesi Liu
description: Soil beneficial microorganism deficiency in the degraded grasslands have emerged as the major factors negatively impacting soil quality and vegetation productivity. EM (effective microorganisms) has been regarded as a good ameliorant in improving microbial communities and restoring degraded soil of agricultural systems. However, knowledge was inadequate regarding the effects of adding EM on the degraded alpine grassland.

title: Long-term outcome of patients with severe pulmonary hypertension undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation
creator: Oliver D. Bhadra, Jessica Weimann, Lara Waldschmidt, Till J. Demal, Ina von der Heide, Laura Hannen, David Grundmann, Sebastian Ludwig, Lisa Voigtlaender-Buschmann, Johannes Schirmer, Simon Pecha, Stefan Blankenberg, Hermann Reichenspurner, Moritz Seiffert, Lenard Conradi, Niklas Schofer, Andreas Sc
description: ObjectivesRecent reports suggest that pulmonary hypertension (PH) is associated with a significantly higher acute mortality after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). The aim of this study is to characterize patients undergoing TAVI with preoperative echocardiographically determined severe PH and to investigate acute clinical and long-term outcomes.

title: MaMPK3‐2 Phosphorylating and Stabilizing Transcriptional Repressor MaAS1 by Counteracting MaRNF4‐Mediated Ubiquitination During Banana Fruit Ripening
creator: Ting‐Ting Luo, Ying‐Ying Yang, Hai‐Ke Tan, Wen Song, Wei Wei, Wei Shan, Jian‐Fei Kuang, Jian‐Ye Chen, Wang‐Jin Lu
description: The ripening of fleshy fruits is strongly regulated by a complex interplay between transcriptional regulation and post‐translational modifications (PTMs). However, the specific PTM regulatory networks involved in fruit ripening remain poorly understood. In this study, we identify MaAS1, an R2R3‐type MYB transcription factor, as a key negative regulator of banana fruit ripening.

title: Resistance‐trained young men exhibit enhanced carotid vasoreactivity during the cold pressor test
creator: Ian Hornby‐Foster, Cory T Richards, Aimee L Drane, Freya M Lodge, Michael Stembridge, Rachel Lord, Zaheer Yousef, Keeron Stone, Barry J McDonnell, Christopher J A Pugh
description: The function of the common carotid artery (CCA) is integral to the regulation of cerebral perfusion. Although endurance training is associated with consistent vascular benefits, the effects of resistance training on CCA function are unclear. The cold pressor test (CPT) assesses CCA vasoreactivity via sympathetic stimulation, with peak CCA vasoreactivity (CAR%peak) reflecting integrated endothelial–autonomic vascular function.

title: Calcium-dependent protein kinases as central hubs in plant abiotic stress signaling: mechanisms and prospects for crop improvement
creator: Samuel Azupio, Yu Wang, Joshua Obeng, Abdul Kadir Issah, Jing Chu, Hongmei Zhang, Qing Xie, Xingyu Jiang
description: Calcium-dependent protein kinases (CDPKs) are key Ca²+ sensors that decode stress-induced calcium signatures through substrate phosphorylation, ROS regulation, kinase cross-talk, and precise spatiotemporal activity, playing a central role in orchestrating plant responses to abiotic stress. This review systematically examines the central role of CDPKs in mediating plant tolerance to drought, salinity, and extreme temperatures.

title: Hypoinsulinemic hypoglycemia with hemihypertrophy in a Filipino infant: management in a resource-limited setting
creator: Elizabeth Grace M Perez, Sylvia C Estrada
description: Persistent infantile hypoglycemia is a medical emergency associated with significant risk of neurological injury. Although most commonly attributed to congenital hyperinsulinism, disorders of impaired insulin signaling with hypoketotic hypoglycemia despite low or undetectable insulin occur in fewer than 1 in 1 000 000 infants worldwide, leading to misdiagnosis and ineffective therapy.

title: Obesity-related asthma and its relationship with microbiota
creator: Jinli Huang, Xuehua Zhou, Bo Dong, Hong Tan, Qiuhong Li, Juan Zhang, Hui Su, Xin Sun
description: Obesity and asthma are global public health problems. Obesity-related asthma is a special phenotype of asthma with a complex pathogenesis. Its occurrence and development are related to mechanical compression, inflammatory response, metabolic regulation, gene regulation, and vitamin D deficiency. Different treatment strategies used in the process of weight loss have a beneficial impact on asthma.

title: Global prevalence of Eimeria species in goats: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Endris A. Ali, Abdul Ghafar, Juan C. Angeles-Hernandez, Muhammad Yaseen, Charles G. Gauci, Ian Beveridge, Sandra Baxendell, Abdul Jabbar
description: BackgroundCoccidiosis is a protozoal disease caused by Eimeria species, the main symptom of which is diarrhea. Eimeria spp. infection can cause weight loss and ill-thrift in goats, and in severe cases, it can lead to mortality in kids, resulting in economic losses for the goat industry. This study aimed to determine the global prevalence of Eimeria spp.

title: Calcimimetic therapy modified the radiological, surgical, and histopathological features of a parathyroid adenoma
creator: Hiroyuki Yamashita, Hisakazu Shindo, Daisuke Tatsushima, Hirokazu Kurohama, Kenichiro Koga, Masahiro Nakashima
description: Calcimimetics are increasingly used to control hypercalcemia before parathyroidectomy. Although treatment-induced degenerative changes have been reported in parathyroid adenomas, their effects on preoperative imaging and surgical planning remain unclear. A 70-year-old woman with primary hyperparathyroidism was administered preoperative evocalcet (2 mg/day). After ∼2 months, serum calcium levels decreased to the hypocalcemic range, prompting drug discontinuation before surgery referral.

title: Evaluation of the healing potential of short-term ozone therapy for the treatment of diabetic foot ulcers
creator: Haojie Sun, Hao Heng, Xuekui Liu, Houfa Geng, Jun Liang
description: BackgroundThe availability of research on short-term ozone therapy for diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) is limited, and even when it is accessible, it mainly comprises of basic analysis conducted during long-term ozone therapy. This study was to evaluate the efficacy of short-term ozone therapy in promoting wound healing in DFUs.

title: The impact of metal amino acid complexes on cuticle quality and Salmonella Enteritidis contamination in laying hens’ eggs
creator: Saruanna M. S. Clemente, Mércia R. Barros, Carlos B. V. Rabello, Marcos Jose Batista dos Santos, Waleska R. L. Medeiros-Ventura, Rogério Ventura da Silva Junior, Felipe P. Melo, Priscila O. Silva, Fábio A. B. Santos, Raquel Burin, Alba Fireman
description: IntroducionEggshell quality and microbial safety are critical concerns in poultry production, with Salmonella Enteritidis contamination representing a significant public health risk. Traditional inorganic mineral supplementation may not optimize eggshell integrity against bacterial penetration. This study investigated the effects of different metal–amino acid complexes on eggshell cuticle quality and resistance to S. Enteritidis penetration in egg laying hens.

title: Case report: Toxic epidermal necrolysis as a unique presentation of acute graft versus host disease in a pediatric patient
creator: Elizabeth Marlowe, Rachel Palmer, April L. Rahrig, Devin Dinora, Jessica Harrison, Jodi Skiles, Mahvish Q. Rahim
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionAcute graft versus host disease (aGVHD) is a common complication of stem cell transplant (SCT), with skin involvement being most common. Severe presentations of skin aGVHD involving rapid progression of rash to bullae formation and mucosal involvement are rare. There are reports of patients with skin aGVHD that present with clinical characteristics mimicking toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN), suggesting a possible overlap between the two.

title: Aortic coarctation and McArdle disease in histiocytosis-lymphadenopathy plus syndrome: expanding the SLC29A3 spectrum
creator: Bushra Rehman, Syed Muhammad Dayyan Hassan, Muhammad Nasheet Sagri, Salman Kirmani, Muzna Arif
description: Histiocytosis-lymphadenopathy plus syndrome (HLPS) is a rare inherited disorder caused by SLC29A3 variants. We report 2 Pakistani brothers with HLPS and markedly different clinical features despite identical genotypes. The 15-year-old had severe growth failure, facial dysmorphism, insulin-dependent diabetes, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, and coarctation of the aorta (CoA) requiring balloon dilatation.

title: Lipoxin A4 levels correlate with severity in a Spanish COVID-19 cohort: potential use of endogenous pro-resolving mediators as biomarkers
creator: Sergio Sánchez-García, Rafael I. Jaén, Roberto Lozano-Rodríguez, José Avendaño-Ortiz, Alejandro Pascual‐Iglesias, Laura Hurtado-Navarro, Eduardo López-Collazo, Lisardo Boscá, Patricia Prieto
description: BackgroundSARS-CoV-2, the causative virus of the COVID-19 global pandemic, leads to a wide variety of responses among patients. Some of them present a very severe phenotype, while others only experience mild symptoms or are even asymptomatic. This differential prognosis is tightly related to the inflammatory status of the patient.

title: Diffusion Basis Spectrum Imaging of Tissue Microstructure and Early Treatment in Multiple Sclerosis
creator: Apisit Kaewsanit, Aime Luna, Bradley Judge, Nicole Shelley, Karl Friedrichsen, Jayashree Rajamanickam, Zhude Tu, Yong Wang, Tammie L S Benzinger, Qing Wang, Matthew R Brier
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveConventional MRI cannot resolve the coexisting pathological processes within multiple sclerosis tissue. Diffusion Basis Spectrum Imaging decomposes the diffusion signal into fiber, cell, and hindered ratios indexing axonal integrity, cellularity, and extracellular space, respectively. We asked how these ratios differ between early relapsing and established non‐relapsing disease, change with early treatment, and relate to disability, and secondarily, whether lesions form reproducible microstructural subtypes.MethodsThirty‐seven participants underwent multi‐shell diffusion MRI: 11 healthy controls, 15 treatment‐naïve relapsing, and 11 non‐relapsing patients.

title: From maturation to degeneration: Distinct biological trajectories in bicuspid and tricuspid aortopathy
creator: Riaz Akhtar, Daniel Olaf Riley, Jillian Madine, Mark Field
description: Ascending thoracic aortic aneurysm formation differs fundamentally between patients with bicuspid (BAV) and tricuspid (TAV) aortic valve phenotypes, yet current clinical management largely relies on shared diameter thresholds, although clinical and scientific data fail to correlate with diameter and risk of rupture.

title: Late age at first birth is a protective factor for oesophageal cancer and gastro-oesophageal reflux: the evidence from the genetic study
creator: Yani Su, Yiwei Xu, Yunfeng Hu, Yu Chang, Fangcai Wu, Mingyi Yang, Yuhui Peng
description: ObjectiveThe primary objective of this research endeavor was to examine the underlying genetic causality between the age at first birth (AFB) and four prevalent esophageal diseases, namely oesophageal obstruction (OO), oesophageal varices (OV), gastro-oesophageal reflux (GOR), and oesophageal cancer (OC).MethodsWe conducted a two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis to examine the causal association between AFB and four prevalent esophageal disorders.

title: Impact of pneumatic tube vs. bicycle courier transport on platelet aggregation: influence of sex and diabetes
creator: Anna Hohneck, Elisabeth Kliemank, Simon Bach, Sebastian Brings, Lukas Seebauer, Mani Roshan, Zoltan Kender, Stefan Kopf, Norbert Frey, Markus Zorn, Stefan M. Woerner, Thomas Fleming, Julia Szendroedi
description: AimPneumatic tube (PT) transport can impact platelet function, often altering platelet aggregation. Consequently, manual transport is frequently recommended to mitigate preanalytical effects on platelet function tests. However, comparative data between PT and bicycle courier (BC) transport remain limited, and it is unclear whether different agonist pathways or specific patient characteristics, such as sex and diabetes, modify transport-related effects.

title: Evaluating Perfusion Quantification for Phase‐Resolved Functional Lung MRI Using Gaussian Filtering
creator: Kirsten J. Schmidt, Andreas Voskrebenzev, Julian M. W. Glandorf, Marius M. Klein, Lea Behrendt, Frank Wacker, Jens Vogel‐Claussen, Filip Klimeš
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Phase‐resolved functional lung (PREFUL) MRI enables contrast‐free lung perfusion quantification (QQuant). Current quantification uses a single median value per slice of maximal blood exchange fraction (ΔS), which limits regional assessment, whereas regional ΔS causes artifacts.

title: Genomic sequence context differentially impacts stepwise oxidation by TET enzymes to shape DNA hydroxymethylation landscapes
creator: Noa Erlitzki, Christian E Loo, Johanna M Fowler, Wanding Zhou, Rahul M Kohli
description: Ten-eleven translocation (TET) enzymes reverse gene silencing imposed by 5-methylcytosine (5mC) in mammalian genomes by catalyzing the stepwise oxidation of 5mC to 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC), 5-formylcytosine (5fC), and 5-carboxycytosine (5caC). 5hmC both acts as an independent epigenetic mark and promotes replication-dependent DNA demethylation by antagonizing maintenance DNA methylation.

title: Protein undernutrition alters the colonic bacteriome, disrupts intestinal immune homeostasis, and impairs control of Leishmania infantum infection in a murine model of visceral leishmaniasis
creator: Renata Azevedo, Monica Losada-Barragán, Erika M. Costa, Heidi Pauer, Cristiane Cassiolato Pires Hardoim, Filipe Lima, Nathalia Pinho, Jonathan Durães, Felipe Gaitán-Albarracín, Sergio Cuervo-Escobar, Sebastián Arcila-Barrera, Adriana Umaña-Pérez, Luis Caetano M. Antunes, Patricia Cuervo
description: IntroductionUndernutrition is a significant global health issue that exacerbates susceptibility to infectious diseases, including visceral leishmaniasis (VL), caused by Leishmania infantum. Here, we investigated the interplay between undernutrition, immune responses, and the colonic microbiota composition in a murine model of VL.MethodsWe used BALB/c mice subjected to a low-protein diet and infected with L.

title: Impact of cardiovascular disease on health-related quality of life among older adults in eastern China: evidence from a national cross-sectional survey
creator: Leping Wan, Guangmei Yang, Haiying Dong, Xiaoxiao Liang, Yan He
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ObjectiveThis study explores the health-related quality of life (HRQoL) scores of Chinese older adults with Cardiovascular Disease(CVD) using the EQ-5D-3L, the aim of this study is to investigate the association between health and HRQoL in older adults with CVD.MethodsThe data for this study were obtained from a cross-sectional study involving older adults residing in Chinese communities The EQ-5D-3L is used to measure the HRQoL scores in the older adults with CVD.

title: Distinct ways by which Srs2 helicase and Rrp1 translocase shape Rad51–DNA interactions in fission yeast
creator: Dorota Misiorna, Dorota Dziadkowiec, Karol Kramarz
description: Precise regulation of homologous recombination is essential for genome stability. Multiple helicases and translocases prevent toxic, unscheduled association of the Rad51 recombinase with chromatin, and their levels are frequently dysregulated in cancer. It remains unclear how anti-recombinogenic enzymes act on distinct pools of Rad51.

title: The potential of the serum uric acid to high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio as a predictive biomarker of diabetes risk: a study based on NHANES 2005–2018
creator: Jianming Yin, Chuanjie Zheng, Xiaoqian Lin, Chaoqiang Huang, Zhanhui Hu, Shuyuan Lin, Yiqian Qu
description: Previous studies have indicated an association between UHR and diabetes risk, but evidence from large-scale and diverse populations remains limited. This study aims to verify UHR’s independent role in diabetes risk prediction in a large sample population and assess its applicability across different populations. We drew upon data from 30,813 participants collected during the 2005–2018 NHANES cycle.

title: Development of CRISPR/Cas13-based analytical tools to study RNA–protein interactions
creator: Keita Yamamoto, Shiori Shikata, Yangying Hao, Takuya Tomita, Rina Kanai, Els Verhoeyen, Yasushi Saeki, Susumu Goyama
description: RNA–protein interactions (RPIs) are as important as protein–protein interactions (PPIs) for the formation of membraneless organelles (MLOs) and play vital roles in diverse biological processes. Despite remarkable advances in PPI analysis technologies, the development of tools for RPI analysis has lagged behind. To address this challenge, we integrated three established PPI technologies—bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC), NanoBiT, and split-TurboID—with RNA-targeting CRISPR/dCas13.

title: Weight loss and blood pressure lowering with GLP-1 receptor agonists and multi-hormone receptor modulators in overweight and obesity: a systematic review and meta-regression of phase 3 clinical trials
creator: Massimo Nardone, Luxcia Kugathasan, Lauren Daunt, Ethan J. Parikh, Hao-Yuan River Zhang, Sachin V. Pasricha, Ani Orchanian-Cheff, David Z.I. Cherney, Ayodele Odutayo, Marcel H.A. Muskiet
description: SummaryBackgroundObesity and hypertension frequently coexist, and weight-reduction is recommended as a core strategy for blood pressure (BP) management in adults with overweight or obesity. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and emerging multi-hormone receptor modulators (MHRMs) induce substantial weight loss alongside modest BP reductions. However, the extent to which weight-loss is associated with BP lowering across these therapies remains unclear.

title: Causal relationship between immune cells and risk of heart failure: evidence from a Mendelian randomization study
creator: Wenjing Cao, Zefu Yang, Liumei Mo, Zhenhao Liu, Jiawei Wang, Zhenhong Zhang, Kui Wang, Wei Pan
description: BackgroundHeart failure (HF) is a clinical syndrome resulting from structural damage or dysfunction of the heart. Previous investigations have highlighted the critical involvement of immune cells in the progression of heart failure, with distinct roles attributed to different types of immune cells.

title: IκBζ target genes in chronic lymphocytic leukemia
creator: Ilenia Sana, Miriam Meloni, Francesca Genova, Maria Elena Mantione, Anna Sofia Tascini, Ettore Zapparoli, Greta Carbone Faccin, Dimitra Paschaloudi, Martina Del Nero, Chiara Lenzi, Pamela Ranghetti, Eleonora Perotta, Lydia Scarfò, Paolo Ghia, Marta Muzio
description: SummaryIκBζ, an atypical IκB protein induced downstream of Toll-like receptor (TLR) signaling, is pivotal in orchestrating inflammatory responses and modulating inflammation-associated B cell malignancies. However, the transcriptional and epigenetic programs regulated by IκBζ in both normal and malignant B cells remain poorly described.

title: Exploration of oxidized phosphocholine profile in non-small-cell lung cancer
creator: Joanna Godzien, Angeles Lopez-Lopez, Julia Sieminska, Kacper Jablonowski, Karolina Pietrowska, Joanna Kisluk, Malgorzata Mojsak, Zofia Dzieciol-Anikiej, Coral Barbas, Joanna Reszec, Miroslaw Kozlowski, Marcin Moniuszko, Adam Kretowski, Jacek Niklinski, Michal Ciborowski
description: Introduction: Lung cancer is one of the most frequently studied types of cancer and represents the most common and lethal neoplasm. Our previous research on non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has revealed deep lipid profile reprogramming and redox status disruption in cancer patients.

title: GmCYP86A37 is a bifunctional cytochrome P450 essential for soybean root aliphatic suberin biosynthesis
creator: Lorena S. Yeung, Andrea Ong, Sangeeta Dhaubhadel, Mark A. Bernards
description: 18-Hydroxyoleic acid and its dioic acid derivative, oleic-1,18-dioic acid, are the two most prominent aliphatic monomers in soybean root suberin. While hydroxylated fatty acids are known to be formed by cytochrome P450 monooxygenases (P450), mainly from the CYP86A and CYP86B subfamilies, the biosynthetic origin of their corresponding dioic acids in soybean remains unclear.

title: Drosophila Appl loss disrupts proteins in mitochondrial oxidative and glycosylation pathways conserved in Alzheimer's disease
creator: Zachary M Smith, Fernando J Vonhoff
description: SummaryThe physiological functions of the amyloid precursor protein (APP) remain unclear due to genetic redundancy and complex phenotypes. For decades, Drosophila amyloid precursor protein-like (Appl) research has relied on Appld, a presumed null allele generated by irradiation. Here, we show that Appld contains complex chromosomal rearrangements and background mutations confounding the interpretation of gene function.

title: Smoking status and survival by cancer type and treatment intent in a population-based cohort with adjustment for major prognostic factors
creator: E Heervä, A Ellonen, S Kukkurainen, T Mikkola, K Savolainen, T Laitinen, K Mattila, H Blomster, H Minn, H Irjala, A Karlsson, M Bärlund, P Österlund
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundTobacco smoking after cancer diagnosis is associated with impaired survival but large real-world evidence across cancers accounting for treatment intent and key prognostic factors remains scarce. We evaluated associations between smoking and survival in a population-based cohort.Materials and methodsWe identified all patients who were diagnosed with solid cancers (International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision codes C00-C43, C45-C68) and treated at two Finnish university hospitals (2009-2019).

title: Phenology analysis for trait prediction using UAVs in a MAGIC rice population with different transplanting protocols
creator: Shoji Taniguchi, Toshihiro Sakamoto, Haruki Nakamura, Yasunori Nonoue, Di Guan, Akari Fukuda, Hirofumi Fukuda, Kaede C. Wada, Takuro Ishii, Jun-Ichi Yonemaru, Daisuke Ogawa
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are one of the most effective tools for crop monitoring in the field. Time-series RGB and multispectral data obtained with UAVs can be used for revealing changes of three-dimensional growth. We previously showed using a rice population with our regular cultivation protocol that canopy height (CH) parameters extracted from time-series RGB data are useful for predicting manually measured traits such as days to heading (DTH), culm length (CL), and aboveground dried weight (ADW).

title: Environmental filters drive functional similarity in disjunct ferruginous outcrops of Eastern Amazonia
creator: Viviane Vasconcelos Chaves, Priscila Sarmento, Arianne Flexa de Castro, José Tasso Felix Guimarães, André Luiz de Rezende Cardoso, Lourival Tyski, Rayara do Socorro Souza da Silva, Thyago Gonçalves Miranda, Sílvio Ramos, Cecílio Caldeira, Markus Gastauer
description: Ferruginous outcrops are ecologically formations that host high biodiversity and edaphic endemism. While canga outcrops in Carajás have been the focus of more extensive research, ferruginous outcrops in the Araguaia remain poorly studied, especially with respect to their functional ecology and conservation value.

title: Case report: The evolving phenotype of ESCO2 spectrum disorder in a 15-year-old Malaysian child
creator: Sok-Kun Tae, Mazlan RA, Meow-Keong Thong
description: ESCO2 spectrum disorder is an autosomal recessive developmental disorder characterized by growth retardation, symmetrical mesomelic limb malformation, and distinctive facies with microcephaly, with a wide phenotypic continuum that ranges from Roberts syndrome (MIM #268300) at the severe end to SC phocomelia (MIM #269000) at the milder end.

title: Key genes and pathways of pulmonary hypertension identified by integrating bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing
creator: Peipei Wu, Jingru Huan, Chengliang Liu, Haiyang Jin, Ran Wang, Yong Wang, Cheng Cao, Binbin Zhang
description: SummaryPulmonary hypertension (PH) is a progressive vascular disease, yet the underlying cell-type-specific molecular networks and diagnostic biomarkers remain incompletely defined. Integrating single-cell and bulk transcriptomics, we identified 14 pulmonary cell types in PH, with smooth muscle cells (SMCs) as a central communication hub interacting with monocytes and macrophages.

title: The effect of age-related decline in physiological activity on the concealed information test
creator: Robin Orthey, Yoshiyuki Tsuyama, Izumi Ikeda, Takahiro Yoshioka, Masaki Ishihara, Izumi Matsuda
description: A demographic shift towards aging societies necessitates a reexamination of established psychological tests with age-related decline of physiological responsivity in mind. The Concealed Information Test (CIT), a physiological test to detect memory of crime details, is frequently and effectively used in criminal investigations in Japan, a severe case of an aging society.

title: Complication of hyperbaric oxygen therapy
creator: Ke Liu, Lei Wang, Lili Liang, Jinyuan Wei
description: d to 69%. The patient then developed cyanosis of the head and neck, generalized subcutaneous emphysema (Fig 1), absent bilateral breath sounds, and abdominal distension. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation was initiated, and a 12-gauge needle was inserted into the left thoracic cavity.

title: Spatial heterogeneity of soil phosphorus influencing bacterial functional adaptations in alkaline calcareous soils
creator: Saira Tabbasum, Mahreen Yahya, Munir Zia, Midrar ul Haq, Samina Anwar, Usama Azeem Khan, Naima Mahreen, Khansa Ejaz, Mika Tapio Tarkka, Sumera Yasmin
description: To enhance sustainable soil fertility and efficient phosphorus (P) management, phosphate-solubilizing bacteria (PSB) play a central role in solubilizing soil mineral phosphorus by releasing organic acids and acidifying micro-niches. Thus far, the influence of spatial P heterogeneity on bacterial eco-physiological adaptations to P-limited, alkaline soils remains poorly understood.

title: Lactate-Informed Exercise Prescription in Mild Cognitive Impairment and Alzheimer’s Disease: A Translational Framework for Preserving Cognition, Mobility, and Independence
creator: Xiaolin Li
description: BackgroundThis narrative review proposes a conceptual, lactate-informed framework for individualized exercise prescription in mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Exercise is recommended in these populations, but fixed external doses do not account for heterogeneity in disease stage, frailty, sarcopenia, cardiovascular risk, or recovery.

title: Virulence factors of bovine mastitis pathogens: distribution, pathogenesis, and emerging vaccines targeting virulence factors: a literature review
creator: Hao Li, Ziyan Wang, Herman W. Barkema, Xiaohan Li, Deyuan Song, Meiyi Ren, Jingdi Tong, Mingchao Liu, Jian Gao, Jia Cheng
description: Bovine mastitis, mainly caused by contagious pathogens like Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus agalactiae, and Mycoplasma bovis, environmental pathogens such as Escherichia coli, Streptococcus uberis, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and a more opportunistic pathogen like Streptococcus dysgalactiae, severely threatens dairy production. These mastitis pathogens rely on their respective virulence characteristics to exert different inflammation of the mammary gland.

title: Intensive smoking cessation intervention in a nature-based setting: a feasibility study of the Danish gold standard program
creator: Mie Sylow Liljendahl, Sanne Staal, Hanne Tønnesen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The implementation of nature-based interventions has demonstrated a positive impact on health outcomes and overall wellbeing. The knowledge of nature-based smoking cessation interventions is sparse but might offer potential benefits for smokers undertaking an intensive smoking cessation program. This study assessed the feasibility in real life of the 6-week Danish Intensive Gold Standard Program (GSP) for smoking cessation in nature compared to the standard setting in primary healthcare.

title: Set binding factor 1 (SBF1/MTMR5) as a potential novel target in colorectal cancer: an exploratory immunohistochemical and bioinformatics study
creator: A. Alatawi, I. Alhabib, M. Fagere, F.A. Al-Jindan, K. Alsamman, F.M. Alzahrani, A.Y. Owaidah, O.S. El-Masry
description: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a major cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide, and dysregulation of phosphoinositides signaling pathways plays a critical role in its pathogenesis. The involvement of Set Binding Factor 1 (SBF1; MTMR5), a pseudophosphatase of the myotubularin family in CRC, remains unexplored.

title: Late-onset first epileptic seizure and cerebral small vessel disease: role of juxtacortical white matter lesions
creator: Adrian Nasca, Leo Sokolovič, Oliver Koprda, Patrick Haage, Thorsten Schmidt, Juraj Kukolja
description: ObjectiveThe cause of late-onset first epileptic seizures (LOFES) in older age is often not readily evident. In absence of probable causes, it has been suggested that cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD), which is common with increasing age, may be crucial. We aimed to further investigate the impact of white matter lesion (WML) burden and distribution pattern on LOFES.

title: B-cell epitope mapping and characterization of antibody responses to recombinant PvRipr in malaria-exposed individuals
creator: Isabela Ferreira Soares, Cinthia Magalhães Rodolphi, Ana Luiza Carneiro Alencar, Ada da Silva Matos, Rodrigo Nunes Rodrigues-da-Silva, Barbara de Oliveira Baptista, Rodrigo Medeiros Martorano, Hugo Amorim dos Santos de Souza, Evelyn Kety Pratt Riccio, Jenifer Peixoto de Barros, Paulo Renato Rivas To
description: IntroductionMalaria caused by P. vivax continues to be a serious public health problem, especially in countries like Brazil where P. vivax accounts for more than 80% of diagnosed cases. Since this plasmodial species is characterized as one of the most difficult to eliminate, the development of a specific vaccine for P.

title: Gastrin-releasing peptide, neuromedin B, and symptom severity in adult attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder
creator: Elif Özcan Tozoğlu, Alev Lazoğlu Özkaya
description: SUMMARYOBJECTIVE:Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder is a neurodevelopmental disorder associated with metabolic and neuropeptidergic processes. Gastrin-releasing peptide and neuromedin B, which are bombesin-like peptides, have been studied only to a limited extent in adult attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, despite their role in energy homeostasis and central nervous system function.

title: Can social adversity and mental, physical and oral multimorbidity form a syndemic? A concept and protocol paper
creator: Easter Joury, Eliana Nakhleh, Ed Beveridge, Derek Tracy, Ellie Heidari, David Shiers, Silke Vereeken, Emily Peckham, Simon Gilbody, Jayati Das-Munshi, Farida Fortune, Vishal R. Aggarwal, Masuma Mishu, Joseph Firth, Kamaldeep Bhui
description: BackgroundClustering mental, physical and oral conditions reduce drastically the life expectancy. These conditions are precipitated and perpetuated by adverse social, economic, environmental, political and healthcare contextual factors, and sustained through bidirectional interactions forming potentially a ‘syndemic’. No previous study has investigated such potential syndemic.

title: Comparative evaluation of ChatGPT and Gemini feedback in scenario-based clinical reasoning among medical interns
creator: Hilal Hatice Ülkü, Fulya Torun, Selcen Öncü
description: SUMMARYOBJECTIVE:Artificial intelligence tools are increasingly used to provide individualized feedback in medical education. The aim of this study was to compare the quality of feedback generated by ChatGPT and Gemini during scenario-based clinical reasoning activities.METHODS:A convergent mixed-methods study was conducted with 32 medical interns randomly assigned to ChatGPT (n=16) or Gemini (n=16).

title: Successful inguinal interstitial brachytherapy in metastatic cervical carcinoma: a case report
creator: Yi Qin, Ping Guan, Dan Li, Huailin He, Wenfeng He, Longjing Tan, Xiangyu Deng, Bizhen Liao, Qinglian Wen, Zhenhua Zhang
description: BackgroundTreatment of metastatic cervical cancer is a tricky issue. Currently, the National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) guideline recommends chemotherapy combined with bevacizumab for recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer. Still, the recurrence rate is high and the survival rate is low after standard treatment. We urgently need to achieve a multimodal therapy approach for recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer.

title: A novel lossless encoding algorithm for data compression–genomics data as an exemplar
creator: Anas Al-okaily, Abdelghani Tbakhi
description: Data compression is a challenging and increasingly important problem. As the amount of data generated daily continues to increase, efficient transmission and storage have never been more critical. In this study, a novel encoding algorithm is proposed, motivated by the compression of DNA data and associated characteristics.

title: Preparation, immunological and pharmacological effects of flavonoids in Scutellariae radix: a review
creator: Haixia Chen, Yumin Wei, Jing Song, Yue Yang, Yanli Chen, Jiteng Sun, Daoming Bai, Zhiqiang Sun, Mingze Wu, Xiaomei Liu, Yanru Lin, Shaoping Wang, Long Dai, Yanan Li
description: In traditional Chinese medicine theory, Scutellaria baicalensis Georgi [Lamiaceae; Scutellariae radix] (SR) is bitter and cold in nature. It enters the lung, gallbladder, spleen, large intestine, and small intestine meridians. It clears heat and dries dampness, purges fire and detoxifies, stops bleeding, and stabilizes pregnancy. It excels at clearing lung fire and upper-body heat.

title: Sustained potassium control and recurrent hyperkalemia during individualized potassium-guided sodium zirconium cyclosilicate titration in maintenance hemodialysis: a post hoc analysis of a randomized trial
creator: Haiming Wang, Wei Zhou, Yan Jiang
description: BackgroundA mean predialysis potassium value at a single visit does not show whether the same patient remains controlled across consecutive months or repeatedly crosses hyperkalemic thresholds. We evaluated sustained patient-level potassium control and recurrent hyperkalemia during individualized potassium-guided sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (SZC) therapy on non-dialysis days.

title: Probiotic Lactobacillus plantarum GUANKE effectively alleviates allergic rhinitis symptoms by modulating functions of various cytokines and chemokines
creator: Haijun Han, Guoliang Chen, Bin Zhang, Xuewen Zhang, Jingmin He, Wenjuan Du, Ming D. Li
description: BackgroundCurrently, the prevalence of allergic rhinitis (AR) remains high and there is a great need to develop better and safer ways to alleviate AR symptoms. The Lactobacillus plantarum GUANKE probiotic was reported as an immunomodulator through maintaining Th1/Th2 balance. This study aimed to determine the efficacy of GUANKE in AR subjects.

title: Trazodone effectiveness in depression: impacts of trazodone extended release vs SSRIs on the health status and quality of life of patients with major depressive disorder
creator: Marcin Siwek, Adrian Andrzej Chrobak, Anna Julia Krupa, Aleksandra Gorostowicz, Andrzej Juryk, Dominika Dudek
description: IntroductionEarly research on the pharmacotherapy for major depressive disorder (MDD) has largely focused on symptomatic improvements, whereas this focus has shifted to functioning and quality of life in recent years. Studies have confirmed that antidepressants generally improve the functional outcomes in MDD, but very few works have compared the efficacies of specific drugs.

title: Striatal network dysfunction underlying speech impairment in early Parkinson’s disease
creator: Caitlin Paige Rogers, Sandy Mournet, Cécile Gallea, Emma Biondetti, Graziella Mangone, Sara Sambin, Lydia Chougar, Nicolas Villain, Rahul Gaurav, Isabelle Arnulf, Marie-Odile Habert, Dijana Petrovska-Delacrétaz, Jean-Christophe Corvol, Habib Benali, Marie Vidailhet, Stéphane Lehéricy, Laetitia Jeanc
description: The pathophysiology underlying Parkinson’s disease (PD) speech impairments and its potential sex differences remain unclear. We investigated sex-specific alterations in speech and striato-cortical networks in 104 patients with early PD (68M/36F), and 44 healthy controls (23M/21F), using quantitative speech markers and multimodal neuroimaging.

title: Taking stock of the 2017–2027 federal mental health transfer
creator: Mary Bartram
description: ilateral agreements with provinces and territories and shared indicators. Transparency and accountability improved through the publication of detailed bilateral agreements with provinces and territories and shared indicators. However, expenditure tracking and outcome measurement remain limited. However, expenditure tracking and outcome measurement remain limited.

title: The protective effect of neurointerventional recanalization on the neurovascular unit in acute ischemic stroke and its correlation with serum GFAP and NfL levels
creator: Ju Luo, Yang Yang, Jingmin Zhou
description: AimThis study aimed to investigate the neuroprotective mechanisms of mechanical thrombectomy (MT) by evaluating its effects on the neurovascular unit (NVU) and correlating these effects with dynamic changes in serum biomarkers in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS).MethodsA prospective cohort of 128 AIS patients with anterior circulation large vessel occlusion was enrolled.

title: Education as a predictor of mental illness familiarity and attitudes in a Muslim community
creator: Zaiboonnisha Mayet, Lebogang Phiri-Sithole
description: BackgroundMental illness is a leading cause of disability in South Africa, where stigma, educational disparities, and cultural beliefs are critical barriers to care. Research has largely overlooked the South African Muslim community, particularly regarding how education influences mental illness familiarity and attitudes within a context where spiritual interpretations may uniquely shape stigma.

title: The Safe Social Media Act: lessons from international online safety policies for protecting child health in Canada
creator: Christo Hall, Reshma Patel, Charlotte Moore Hepburn
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). eople, their content and design often contribute to serious harms for children and youth globally, given the vulnerabilities associated with child and youth cognitive development. Bill C-34, the Safe Social Media Act, contains many essential elements of an effective framework for child online safety, positioning Canada to join other jurisdictions in protecting young people while preserving their ability to access, learn from, and connect in online and digital spaces.

title: Acute effects of plyometric-based conditioning activity and warm-up music stimuli on physical performance and affective state in male taekwondo athletes
creator: Hamdi Messaoudi, Ibrahim Ouergui, Slaheddine Delleli, Christopher Garrett Ballmann, Luca Paolo Ardigò, Hamdi Chtourou
description: IntroductionThis study assesses the acute effects of combining a plyometric-based conditioning activity (CA) with different musical stimuli during warm-up on taekwondo (TKD) performance and related psychological aspects.MethodsIn a randomized cross-over study design, 16 male TKD athletes (age: 19.94 ± 1.

title: Sustained type I interferon activity and N-antigenemia form a vicious cycle during severe COVID-19
creator: William Mouton, Kahina Saker, Priscille Franc, Marine Mommert-Tripon, Guy Oriol, Laurence Generenaz, Valérie Cheynet, Antonin Bal, Léa Pons, Brice Wittmann, David Bussy, Paul Bastard, Jean-Laurent Casanova, Sarah Sebai, Amel Chebel, Fabrice Chatonnet, Dominique Costagliola, Jose Arribas, Hans-Kittil
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryBackgroundAlthough antigenemia is associated with poor outcomes in respiratory viral infections, the underlying mechanisms driving viral bloodstream dissemination remain not fully understood. Herein, we aimed to characterise SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid (N)-antigenemia kinetics in patients with severe COVID-19.

title: Immunotherapy of osteosarcoma based on immune microenvironment modulation
creator: Heping Lian, Jiakui Zhang, Shuna Hou, Shuang Ma, Jiachen Yu, Wei Zhao, Duoyi Zhao, Zhiyu Zhang
description: Osteosarcoma is a highly malignant tumor with unsatisfactory therapeutic outcomes achieved by chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and surgery. As an emerging oncological treatment, immunotherapy has shown potential in the clinical management of many tumors but has a poor response rate in osteosarcoma.

title: Differential effects on tumor progression by APOBEC3A, APOBEC3B, and APOBEC3H Haplotype I in a breast cancer mouse xenograft model
creator: Milaid Granadillo Rodríguez, Lai Wong, Arzhang Shayeganmehr, Diogo Pellegrina, Frederick S. Vizeacoumar, Franco J. Vizeacoumar, Mohamed Helmy, Linda Chelico
description: IntroductionThe APOBEC3 family of cytidine deaminases induces somatic mutations that are highly prevalent in cancers, but the functional consequences remain largely unknown.MethodsTo determine these consequences, we exposed MCF7 tumorigenic breast epithelial cells to APOBEC3A, APOBEC3B or APOBEC3H Haplotype I.ResultsComparative analysis between cells pre and post ‐APOBEC3 exposure revealed fewer deamination‐dependent γH2AX foci post‐APOBEC3 exposure, despite maintaining APOBEC3 protein expression.

title: Temporal interference stimulation for treating Wilson disease: A prospective clinical and functional MRI study
creator: Nan Cheng, Yanming Wang, Huiyu Du, Guofang Yu, Xiaojing Han, Yangfei Huang, Chunsheng Xu, Bensheng Qiu, Ting Dong
description: Wilson disease (WD) is an inherited disorder of copper metabolism caused by ATP7B mutations, and persistent neurological deficits, especially dystonia and motor disability, may remain despite standard anti-copper therapy. The putamen is a deep gray-matter nucleus frequently affected by copper deposition in WD and may therefore represent a plausible target for non-invasive neuromodulation.

title: Identification and validation of glycolysis-related diagnostic signatures in diabetic nephropathy: a study based on integrative machine learning and single-cell sequence
creator: Xiaoyin Wu, Buyu Guo, Xingyu Chang, Yuxuan Yang, Qianqian Liu, Jiahui Liu, Yichen Yang, Kang Zhang, Yumei Ma, Songbo Fu
description: BackgroundDiabetic nephropathy (DN) is a complication of systemic microvascular disease in diabetes mellitus. Abnormal glycolysis has emerged as a potential factor for chronic renal dysfunction in DN. The current lack of reliable predictive biomarkers hinders early diagnosis and personalized therapy.MethodsTranscriptomic profiles of DN samples and controls were extracted from GEO databases.

title: Efficacy and safety of intravenous mesenchymal stem cells for ischemic stroke patients, a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Maged Elsayed Hassanein, Jaber Fayad, Jilan Ali Shabana, Esraa M. AlEdani, Mahmoud Tarek Hefnawy, Hazem S. Ghaith, Ahmed Negida
description: BackgroundClinical trials have evaluated the efficacy of intravenous mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) for acute and subacute ischemic stroke. Therefore, we conducted this meta-analysis to investigate the efficacy and safety of intravenous MSC treatments compared to placebo for acute and subacute ischemic stroke patients.

title: Immunosenescence as a modifiable driver of neurodegenerative diseases: Pathways and multidimensional emerging strategies for Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases
creator: Jingyu Zhao, Linzhuo Qu, Hongjian Guan, Huiying Che, Fei Shi, Yang Yang
description: Immunosenescence represents a core upstream driver of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD), exerting its pathological effects through four mechanistically interconnected cascades: chronic inflammatory imbalance mediated by the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), oxidative stress arising from immune-metabolic reprogramming, protein homeostasis dysfunction caused by autophagy-lysosomal failure, and disrupted neuro-immune crosstalk secondary to breakdown of central nervous system (CNS) immune privilege.

title: Improvised cardiac function of siddha formulation Sikkanjar elixir® through CAMK2 and VEGF mechanism-in experimentally induced cardiac hypertrophy model in rats
creator: S Joseph Maria Adaikalam, J Tejasri, R Arunagiri, B Naveen Kumar, M Ramanathan
description: BackgroundSikkanjar elixir® (SE) contains 29 herbs, honey and fermented rice water. It is a modified and fortified form of Sikkanjar Manappagu (Manappagu means syrup), a Siddha traditional medicine. SE has its reference to treat vascular block, high cholesterol, varicose vein, hypertension; improved cardiac efficiency and blood circulation.

title: KASP-IEva: an intelligent typing evaluation model for KASP primers
creator: Xiaojing Chen, Longyu Huang, Jingchao Fan, Shen Yan, Guomin Zhou, Jianhua Zhang
description: KASP marker technology has been used in molecular marker-assisted breeding because of its high efficiency and flexibility, and an intelligent evaluation model of KASP marker primer typing results is essential to improve the efficiency of marker development on a large scale.

title: Energy intake insufficiency due to underestimated energy requirement by common predictive formulas can be identified by urinary amino acid levels in advanced heart failure
creator: Yoko Sakamoto, Tomohito Ohtani, Kei Nakamoto, Fusako Sera, Shungo Hikoso, Yasushi Sakata
description: BackgroundElevated resting energy expenditure (REE) promotes cachexia, worsening prognosis in patients with advanced heart failure (HF). However, adequate assessment of energy balance is challenging because of unvalidated common prediction methods and unestablished determinants of REE, resulting in a lack of biomarkers for predicting insufficient energy intake.

title: Comparative effectiveness of amlodipine versus nifedipine prescribed at discharge in patients with ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack: A nationwide 5-year follow-up registry study
creator: Xinya Li, Xue Xia, Meng Gao, Qin Xu, Yijun Zhang, Jing Jing, Yi Zhai, Xia Meng, Anxin Wang
description: BackgroundAmlodipine and nifedipine are the most commonly prescribed calcium channel blockers (CCB) for patients suffering from ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA). Nevertheless, there is a scarcity of direct comparative evidence on their effectiveness. This study aimed to compare the effectiveness of amlodipine and nifedipine in patients with ischemic stroke or TIA.

title: Advancing ecological validity and clinical utility in virtual reality-based continuous performance test: exploring the effects of task difficulty and environmental distractors
creator: Hyang-Kyeong Oh, Yoon Jae Cho, Jae-Jin Kim, Bokyoung Shin, Soo-Jeong Kim, Soobin Park, Jeong-Ho Seok, Soyeon Kim, Eunjoo Kim
description: IntroductionResearchers have highlighted concerns regarding the limited diagnostic utility and ecological validity of the Continuous Performance Test (CPT). Recent advancements in VR-based CPTs have attempted to address these concerns by simulating real-life scenarios and enhancing attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) diagnosis; however, certain areas require improvement for obtaining reliable data from both healthy individuals and those with ADHD.

title: PSYCHOMETRIC PROPERTIES OF THE TIMED BACKWARD WALK TEST IN PEOPLE WITH STROKE
creator: Yu QIN, Siyue LI, Peiming CHEN, Thomson W.L. WONG, Cynthia Y.Y. LAI, Shamay S.M. NG
description: ObjectiveTo examine the psychometric properties of the Timed Backward Walk test in people with stroke.DesignCross-sectional study.Subjects60 people with stroke and 30 healthy adults aged 55 years and older.MethodsParticipants performed the Timed Backward Walk test and standard clinical assessments. Discriminative validity was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve. Reliability (one-week test–retest, inter-rater, intra-rater) was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients.

title: Does the therapeutic alliance process explain the results of the Egokitzen post-divorce intervention program?
creator: Irati Alvarez, Marta Herrero, Ana Martínez-Pampliega
description: ObjectiveThe objective of this study was to explain the relationship between therapeutic alliance and the changes observed in the parents’ psychological symptomatology after participation in the Egokitzen program, analyzing the mediating role of emotion regulation.MethodsThe study involved 117 divorced parents and 40 therapists.

title: Legislating novel psychoactive substances: lessons from 15 years of UK mortality data (2007-2022)
creator: Kirsten L. Rock, Ric Treble, Caroline S. Copeland
description: BackgroundNovel Psychoactive Substances (NPS) emerged in the early 2000s as chemically designed alternatives to circumvent laws which internationally control drugs. There is limited evidence that NPS are produced in the UK, whereas China has long been recognised as a primary source of NPS.

title: Female Athletes Are Half as Likely to Return to High-Risk Sports Compared With Male Athletes After Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction: An Exploration of Return-to-Sport Outcomes Between Sexes
creator: Hana Marmura, Andrew Firth, Alan MJ Getgood, STABILITY Study Group, Dianne M Bryant
description: Background:Differences in female and male athletes’ return-to-sport (RTS) outcomes after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) are not well understood. The purpose of this study was to explore sex-based differences in RTS rates and predictors of RTS after ACLR for athletes participating in high-risk sports.Hypothesis:Female athletes will have significantly lower RTS rates than male athletes.

title: Beneficial effects of berberine in the treatment of diabetes and its complications
creator: Shanyao Liu, Jie Shen, Fanghui Xu, Lu Niu, Fengchan Wang, Guojing Zhao
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Coptis chinensis (Huanglian), a key component in numerous classical Chinese herbal formulas, is traditionally applied for treating metabolic diseases based on its activity including clear heat, dry dampness, purge fire, and detoxify. Berberine (BBR), one key active component from Coptis chinensis, was contained in numerous classical Chinese herbal formulas for improving insulin resistance and regulating blood glucose levels, making them applicable for diabetes mellitus (DM) treatment.

title: Role of plasma metabolome in mediating the effect of plasma lipidome on NAFLD: a Mendelian randomization study
creator: Zhuyuan Zheng, Shaojie Yang, Wanlin Dai, Yang Sun, Jingnan Wang, Xiaolin Zhang, Yiming Zheng, Jing Kong
description: BackgroundThis study explored the causal connection among the plasma lipidome, nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), and potential metabolome mediators through Mendelian randomization (MR).MethodsWe obtained summary statistics for 179 plasma lipidome traits (N = 7,174), 1,400 plasma metabolome traits (N = 8,299), and one NAFLD trait from publicly available genome-wide association studies. A two-sample MR analysis was conducted to infer causality.

title: Exploring SLEEPINESS through home monitoring with ultra-long-term subcutaneous EEG and ecological momentary assessment in sleepy treatment naïve obstructive sleep apnea patients starting CPAP treatment—A study protocol article
creator: Mathias Sarkez-Knudsen, Martin Ballegaard, Henning Piilgaard, Esben Ahrens, Martin Christian Hemmsen, Tobias Søren Andersen, Jakob Eyvind Bradram, Preben Homøe
description: IntroductionExcessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) is a key symptom for patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). Despite important limitations in the longitudinal monitoring of EDS, the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS), the Maintenance of Wakefulness Test, and the Multiple Sleep Latency Test (MSLT) are the best available objective tests to predict EDS.

title: Evaluating a Modified American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status‐Based Sedation Management System for Pancreatobiliary Endoscopy: A Prospective Feasibility Study
creator: Taro Hanaoka, Kosuke Okuwaki, Masafumi Watanabe, Hiromi Matsuda, Kai Adachi, Akihiro Tamaki, Daisuke Ogawa, Mayuko Sakai, Chika Kusano
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivesTo prospectively evaluate the feasibility of implementing a modified American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status (ASA‐PS)‐based sedation management system for endoscopist‐managed sedation in pancreatobiliary endoscopy.MethodsThis single‐center, single‐arm prospective feasibility study involved 2000 patients (2024–2025). Sedation risk was stratified using a modified ASA‐PS classification system combined with predefined high‐risk clinical factors (severe obesity, obstructive sleep apnea requiring continuous positive airway pressure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease requiring home oxygen therapy, reduced functional capacity, and difficult sedation history).

title: Transfer learning for improving generalizability in predicting soybean maturity date using UAV imagery
creator: Jing Zhou, Jianfeng Zhou, Andrew Scaboo, Eduardo Beche, Ziteng Xu, Zhou Zhang
description: IntroductionHigh-throughput and accurate phenotyping is critical for enhancing crop breeding efficiency by enabling rapid identification of superior cultivars within large populations. For soybean [Glycine max (L.) Merr.], maturity group is a key determinant of geographic adaptation and influences yield potential. Consequently, accurate assessment of physiological maturity dates is essential for selecting lines suited to specific environments.

title: Relationship between academic procrastination and internet addiction in Peruvian university students: the mediating role of academic self-efficacy
creator: Dana Rocio Chavez-Yacolca, Ruth Beatriz Castro-Champión, Nely Marlene Cisneros-Gonzales, Denis Frank Cunza-Aranzábal, Mardel Morales-García, Carlos D. Abanto-Ramírez
description: IntroductionThis study evaluated the mediating role of academic self-efficacy in the relationship between internet addiction and academic procrastination among Peruvian university students.MethodA cross-sectional explanatory design was employed with a convenience sample of 334 participants. Instruments used included the Specific Perceived Self-Efficacy Scale of Academic Situations (EAPESA), the Lima Internet Addiction Scale (EAIL), and the Academic Procrastination Scale (APS).

title: Arousal dysregulation and executive dysfunction in attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
creator: Valeria Isaac, Vladimir Lopez, Maria Josefina Escobar
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition, that continues to have an elusive etiological background. A number of extant models and theories have historically intended to explain the many factors contributing to ADHD behaviors. One of the most accepted hypotheses has been the executive dysfunction theory associating reduction in executive control to abnormalities in structure and operational dysfunction of dopaminergic signaling networks.

title: Markedly Delayed Onset ICANS in the Setting of CAR T-Cell-Mediated Aseptic Meningoencephalitis: Two Cases
creator: Andy Y Wang, Catherine Suen, Iyas Daghlas, Anupama Kumar, David Oh, Douglas Pet, Vanja Douglas
description: ObjectiveImmune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) typically manifests within the first week following chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy and has rarely been described to develop beyond 1 month after treatment. This report describes the occurrence of markedly delayed ICANS in the setting of non-infectious meningoencephalitis.

title: PointNeXt-DBSCAN: a hybrid point cloud deep learning framework for multi-stage cotton leaf instance segmentation
creator: Zeyu Lei, Debin Zeng, Liangfang Zheng
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study addresses the challenge of organ-level instance segmentation in cotton point clouds, which arises from significant morphological variations and leaf occlusion across growth stages. To achieve high-precision leaf extraction, a hybrid framework integrating PointNeXt and DBSCAN is proposed. A dataset containing 1,065 cotton plants from seedling to boll-opening stages was constructed via multi-view image reconstruction and augmented through random rotation and scaling.

title: Study protocol – elucidating the neural correlates of functional remediation for older adults with bipolar disorder
creator: Laura Montejo, Brisa Sole, Lydia Fortea, Esther Jimenez, Anabel Martinez-Aran, Eloy Martinez-Heras, Jose Sanchez-Moreno, Maria Ortuño, Jose Pariente, Aleix Solanes, Carla Torrent, Enric Vilajosana, Michele De Prisco, Eduard Vieta, Joaquim Radua
description: IntroductionBeyond mood abnormalities, bipolar disorder (BD) includes cognitive impairments that worsen psychosocial functioning and quality of life. These deficits are especially severe in older adults with BD (OABD), a condition expected to represent most individuals with BD in the upcoming years. Restoring the psychosocial functioning of this population will thus soon represent a public health priority.

title: A Dual‐Functional Nanoplatform Targeting the dsDNA–cGAS Axis to Mitigate Disc Degeneration and Aberrant Innervation
creator: Zhaojun He, Tianyu Chen, Zezheng Liu, Xinlin Huang, Ruitangbin Jiang, Yihao Liu, Baojing Xu, Yuxiang Li, Kangning Zhao, Huibo Yan, Lei Zhou, Can Liu, Qingchu Li
description: Pathological sensory nerve ingrowth into degenerated intervertebral discs contributes to discogenic pain, yet strategies that concurrently mitigate disc degeneration and pathological innervation remain limited. Here, we found that senescent nucleus pulposus (NP) cells accumulated and released double‐stranded DNA (dsDNA), which reinforced NP cell senescence and matrix catabolism.

title: Baseline Knee Extension Is Associated With Volumetric Femoral Cartilage Loss in the Central Region of the Mid-lateral and External Medial Femoral Condyles: Data From the Osteoarthritis Initiative
creator: Domenica Cirone, Darsan Sadacharam, T Mark Campbell
description: ObjectiveData evaluating knee flexion contracture (FC)-associated regional changes on femoral articular cartilage are lacking. We compared regional femoral articular cartilage outcomes of people with knee osteoarthritis (OA) with and without FC using quantitative MRI data.MethodsArticular cartilage of the medial and lateral femoral condyles were segmented into internal, central, and external subregions on MRI. Goniometry measured knee extension.

title: Epidemiological profile of acquired syphilis in children and adolescents in Brazil: a nationwide observational study
creator: Gabrielle Oliveira Silva, Amanda Souza Barbosa, Catarina David Rodamilans Ferreira, Igor Macedo Pinto, Bárbara Simone David Ferreira
description: Acquired syphilis, which is historically considered a condition with almost exclusive prevalence in adults, has shown, in recent evidence, an alarming increase amongst the pediatric population. The objective of this study is to analyze and compare the time trends and epidemiological profile of acquired syphilis in the Brazilian population from ages 0 to 19 from 2015 to 2023.

title: Salt tolerance evaluation and key salt-tolerant traits at germination stage of upland cotton
creator: Mengjie An, Xinhui Huang, Yilei Long, Yin Wang, Yanping Tan, Zhen Qin, Xiantao Ai, Yan Wang
description: Cotton is an important cash crop with a certain salt tolerance, but its germination stage is very susceptible to the damage of salt stress, causing significant yield loss. However, few studies have evaluated the cotton salt tolerance and selected salt tolerance traits at germination stage.

title: Thoracic and retroperitoneal lymphatic injuries following spine surgery: illustrative cases
creator: Thiago P Rodrigues, Mariana A S Rodrigues, Katherine Jensen, Clayton L Rosinski, Mani Ratnesh S Sandhu, Satoshi Yamaguchi, Mauricio Amoedo, Matthew A Howard III, Patrick Hitchon
description: BACKGROUNDPostoperative lymphatic leakage is a rare complication of spine surgery caused by injury to the thoracic duct, cisterna chyli, or retroperitoneal lymphatic channels. Because of its rarity, diagnosis is often delayed and optimal management remains poorly defined. The authors present 3 illustrative cases and review current diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

title: Feedforward Pre‐Activation of Lateral Ankle Muscles Is Insufficient Against Excessive Ankle Inversion During Perturbation in Individuals With Chronic Ankle Instability
creator: Wenqi Ran, Qipeng Song, Wei Yin
description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to compare ankle kinematics and muscle activation between individuals with and without chronic ankle instability (CAI), both prior to and following landing on an inversion trapdoor during walking, with a particular focus on the feedforward pre‐activation of lateral ankle muscles and the consequent ankle kinematics post‐perturbation.

title: The effect of preload on Doppler systolic time in a large emergency department cohort with suspected sepsis
creator: Sarah Atwi, Jared Nunnally, Kristen Ugale, So Mi Ko, Jaclyn Bond, Kimberly Boozer, Raymond J Bautista, Catalina Torres, Matthew Sedillo, Daniel Lachner-Piza, Tracy Savery, Melissa Hebscher, Joseph K Eibl, Jon-Emile S Kenny, Korbin Haycock
description: BackgroundChange in the corrected flow time of the common carotid artery (ccFTΔ) during a preload challenge (PC) is a surrogate for stroke volume change (SVΔ) to infer preload responsiveness (PR).MethodsThis is a retrospective cohort study comprising patients with suspected sepsis in a large, publicly funded, academic emergency department; no patient health information is linked to the Doppler assessments.

title: Analysis of organoid and immune cell co-cultures by machine learning-empowered image cytometry
creator: Philipp Stüve, Benedikt Nerb, Selina Harrer, Marina Wuttke, Markus Feuerer, Henrik Junger, Elke Eggenhofer, Bianca Lungu, Simina Laslau, Uwe Ritter
description: n vivo processes since 2D cell-monolayer models do not contain a tissue-specific microenvironment (1). During the last decades, stem cell- or adult tissue progenitor cell-derived organoids have emerged as suitable in vitro applications in translational research of human chronic diseases (2, 3). Organoids are self-organized, 3D multicellular tissue cultures, serving as artificial model systems of organs (2, 4–7).

title: A protocol for mobilising novel finance models for collaborative health promotion and disease prevention initiatives: taking a smart capacitating investment approach in the Invest4Health project
creator: Joanna Lane, Rhiannon T. Edwards, Balázs Babarczy, Holly Whiteley, Vidya Oruganti, Maureen Rutten-van Mölken, Caroline Costongs, Anant R. Jani, Sarah Wordsworth, Alison Maassen, Apostolos Tsiachristas, Jacob Davies, Bengt Stavenow, Jolanda van Vliet, Steve Wright, Lina Papartyte, Jennifer Catherine
description: BackgroundThe prevalence of preventable non-communicable disease (NCD) underpins the need for a life-course and cross-sectoral approach to population health that is grounded in health promotion and disease prevention. European Union (EU) countries typically spend 6 to 13% of gross domestic product (GDP) on health care, yet less than 3% of this is dedicated to prevention.

title: Tuberculous discitis following traumatic intravesical Bacillus Calmette-Guérin treatment: illustrative case
creator: Ishan R. Perera, Sydney E. Moriarty, Jaret S. Ly, Heather Heitkotter, Daniel Carr
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Tuberculous spondylitis/discitis is a rare presentation of mycobacterial infection, typically secondary to Mycobacterium tuberculosis; however, patients receiving intravesical Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) are at risk of developing tuberculous spondylitis secondary to Mycobacterium bovis.OBSERVATIONSThis article reports a rare case of tuberculous spondylitis/discitis with a recent history of traumatic intravesical BCG therapy for superficial bladder cancer, which required surgical decompression of an abscess in the setting of intractable back pain.LESSONSThis case highlights the importance of a focused, yet relevant understanding of a patient’s history in

title: Case presentation and management of Lyme disease patients: a 9-year retrospective analysis in France
creator: Emeline Perthame, Loïc Chartier, Jean-Claude George, Marie Varloud, Elisabeth Ferquel, Valérie Choumet
description: IntroductionLyme borreliosis (LB) is the most common vector disease in temperate countries of the northern hemisphere. It is caused by Borrelia burgdorferi sensu lato complex.MethodsTo study the case presentation of LB in France, we contacted about 700 physicians every year between 2003 and 2011. An anonymous questionnaire was established allowing the collection of 3,509 cases.

title: Impact of biologicals on revision ESS numbers in CRSwNP in a tertiary care rhinology center
creator: Judith E. Adriaenssens, An-Sofie Viskens, Elien Borgers, Peter W. Hellings
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundSince 2022, several biologics are indicated and reimbursed for Belgian patients with severe uncontrolled CRSwNP despite previous endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS). Data on the impact of biologics on the number of patients undergoing revision ESS are lacking.MethodsWe analyzed the trend in numbers and percentages of patients with severe uncontrolled CRSwNP being offered primary ESS, revision ESS or biologics according to both academic- and reimbursement criteria at a tertiary care Rhinology center (University Hospitals Leuven) in Belgium, from 2019 until 2023.ResultsA total of

title: Colour maps for representation of quantitative metrics in radiology: meaningful or misleading?
creator: Nico Sollmann, Maria T. Wetscherek, Barbara D. Wichtmann, Miha Fuderer, Clemens C. Cyran, Edwin H. G. Oei, Fabio Crameri, Nandita M. deSouza
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The increased utility of quantitative metrics in medical imaging has prompted the use of colour representation of the data. Colour schemes for image display can highlight pathology and distinguish normal anatomy, thus potentially aiding image interpretation. Adding colour schemes to images may serve the sole purpose of visualising an abnormality or may seek to represent and meaningfully convey a quantitative metric.

title: Structure-based virtual screening and molecular dynamics studies to explore potential natural inhibitors against 3C protease of foot-and-mouth disease virus
creator: Sthitaprajna Sahoo, Hak-Kyo Lee, Donghyun Shin
description: Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) is a highly infectious animal disease caused by foot-and-mouth disease virus (FMDV) and primarily infects cloven-hoofed animals such as cattle, sheep, goats, and pigs. It has become a significant health concern in global livestock industries because of diverse serotypes, high mutation rates, and contagious nature. There is no specific antiviral treatment available for FMD.

title: Comments on: Flow Cytometric Profiling Reveals Platelet Dysfunction and Impaired Immune Communication in Acute and Chronic Cerebrovascular Disease
creator: Rajesh Prasad Jayaswal, Azeem Rizvi, Javed Siddiqui, Maajid Mohi Ud Din Malik
description: ctions across acute and chronic cerebrovascular disease moves the discussion beyond platelet count and routine coagulation assays toward functional thromboimmune phenotyping. The strength of the article lies in its laboratory‐to‐clinic orientation: It invites clinical laboratories to consider whether platelet activation and platelet‐immune communication can become measurable, reproducible, and interpretable signals of neurovascular injury.

title: Shunt configuration’s role in shaping hemodynamics of reverse Potts shunt in pediatric pulmonary arterial hypertension
creator: Jinlong Liu, Xiafeng Yu, Jiwen Xiong, Yi Yan, Yanjun Sun, Yumin Zhong, Hao Zhang
description: ObjectivesReverse Potts shunt is a promising yet high-risk therapy for pediatric pulmonary arterial hypertension. Postoperative hemodynamics is critically influenced by shunt configuration but is difficult to predict. This study aimed to quantify the effects of shunt size and location on hemodynamics to guide surgical planning.

title: Sleep does not occur in isolation: contextualizing adolescent sleep disparities
creator: BreAnne Young, Azizi Seixas, Girardin Jean-Louis
description: easingly compete for finite sleep opportunity. Adolescence is also marked by a shift in circadian biology as the body enters puberty, leading to a shift in the release of melatonin that leaves most teens struggling to fall asleep before 11 pm [1].

title: Addressing the challenges of intellectual disability identification for health policy and research in Australia
creator: Helen Leonard, Kingsley Wong, Peiwen Liao, Manzoor Khan, Zoe Aitken, Jenny Bourke, Julian N. Trollor, Jenny Downs, Mary-Ann O’Donovan, Anne M. Kavanagh, Preeyaporn Srasuebkul
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This article discusses the important issue of the need for a stable definition of intellectual disability in order to allow comparisons by place and over time such as in the monitoring of this population’s health needs and utilization. The aim of the new Australian National Centre for Intellectual Disability Health, established in 2023, is to ensure that all Australian children and adults with intellectual disability receive high-quality healthcare that meets their needs.

title: Cross database bibliometric and knowledge mapping analysis of nanoplatform mediated tumor associated macrophage reprogramming
creator: Chang Su, Jiayue Gao, Boyang Li, Zehao Hong, Lucy Yue Lau, Richard J Aldridge, Elizabeth A Whitmore, Guian Xu, Yi Chen, Boxiang Zhang
description: BackgroundNanoplatforms are evolving from passive delivery vehicles into multifunctional engineered systems capable of remodeling the tumor microenvironment. Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are important biological interfaces because of their abundance, plasticity, and roles in immune suppression and therapeutic resistance. However, the knowledge structure and developmental trajectory of nanoplatform-mediated TAM reprogramming remain insufficiently characterized.

title: FI-CEUS: a solution to improve the diagnostic accuracy in MRI LI-RADS-indeterminate (LR-3/4) FLLs at risk for HCC
creator: Qingjing Zeng, Sidong Xie, Xuqi He, Yuefei Guo, Yuxuan Wu, Na He, Lanxia Zhang, Xuan Yu, Rongqin Zheng, Kai Li
description: ObjectiveTo evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of fusion imaging contrast-enhanced ultrasound (FI-CEUS) of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) LI-RADS-indeterminate (LR-3/4) and conventional ultrasound undetected focal liver lesions (FLLs) in patients at risk for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).MethodsBetween February 2020 and July 2021, 71 FLLs in 63 patients were registered for diagnostic performance evaluation respectively for ultrasound-guided thermal ablation evaluation in this retrospective study.

title: Working With AI and Robotic Systems While Preserving Clinical Judgement, Professional Accountability and Person‐Centred Care: Critical Care Nurses’ Perspectives
creator: Tuba Sengul, Dilek Yilmaz Akyaz, Buse Macit Kaplan, Yunus Emre Akyol, Tuğba Cevizci, Melek Demiral, Deema Mahasneh, Noordeen Shoqirat, Holly Kirkland‐Kyhn
description: BackgroundThe integration of AI and robotic systems into critical care necessitates examining how ICU nurses preserve clinical judgement, professional accountability and person‐centred care while using these technologies.AimsTo explore ICU nurses' perceptions of AI and robotic systems in critical care, focusing on clinical judgement, trust, responsibility, professional roles and person‐centred care.Study DesignA qualitative descriptive study using scenario‐based elicitation was conducted.

title: Prognostic role of prognostic nutritional index in patients with bladder cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Jing Sun, Zhenzhen Li, Xiaming Zhu
description: AimsAn increasing number of studies have explored the prognostic significance of the prognostic nutritional index (PNI) in bladder cancer patients, but the results are inconsistent. This study systematically investigates the prognostic value of baseline PNI in patients with bladder cancer through a meta-analytic approach.

title: Metagenomic and metatranscriptomic profiling of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid identifies microbial and host biomarkers of drug-resistant tuberculosis
creator: Haiqing Zhang, Limao Zhang, Bin Yang, Chunjing Gao, Huimei Liu, Yunshi Zhang, Xiaoyou Chen
description: BackgroundDrug-resistant tuberculosis (DR-TB) undermines global TB control, yet how resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains interact with the lung microbiome, phage communities, and local host immunity remains poorly defined.MethodsIn a prospective cohort of 130 pulmonary TB patients (49 DR-TB, 81 drug-susceptible TB [DS-TB] patients), bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) was subjected to paired metagenomic and transcriptomic profiling.

title: Novel insights on carbon source influence on azomycin production by Streptomyces eurocidicus
creator: Julia de Macedo Robert, Wagner Lopes, Alexandre Andrade de Souza Costa, Otavio Padula de Miranda, Tatiane Aparecida Nascimento, Maria da Conceição Avelino Dias, Filipe Soares Quirino da Silva, Fabius Vieira Leineweber, Graziela Jardim Pacheco
description: Azomycin (2-nitroimidazole), a compound synthesized by Streptomyces eurocidicus, is medically significant as a build block for the drug applied in treatment for drug-resistant tuberculosis and Chagas disease, as well as tumor hypoxia imaging. Despite its clinical value, the optimized bioprocess parameters for its production remain largely unexplored.

title: Online misinformation can distort witnesses’ memories. Analysis of co-witness discussions using an online version of the MORI-v technique
creator: Magdalena Kękuś, Malwina Szpitalak, Romuald Polczyk, Krystian Barzykowski
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionThe memory conformity effect occurs when people witness a given incident and then talk to each other about it, and the statement of one person affects the memory account of another person with respect to that incident.

title: A Living Multi‐Omics PDX Biobank of High‐Risk Sarcomas Reveals ecDNA‐Driven Oncogene Amplification in Osteosarcoma and Enables Preclinical Precision Oncology
creator: Weisong Zhao, Zhiwei Cheng, Kai Tian, Mengxiong Sun, Zhuoying Wang, Ming Jiao, Jens Luebeck, Kaiyuan Zhu, Xiao Zhang, Dongqing Zuo, Hongsheng Wang, Chongren Wang, Jiakang Shen, Xiaojun Ma, Gangyang Wang, Zongyi Wang, Jing Han, Kaiyuan Liu, Haoran Mu, Weiqi Ma, Yongyong Ren, Shibing Guo, Huangxin Tu,
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Sarcomas are rare, genomically heterogeneous malignancies for which prognosis has remained poor and largely unchanged over recent decades. Patient‐derived xenograft (PDX) models are an important tool for cancer research, but their availability and utility remain limited in sarcoma. Here, we establish the SGH sarcoma PDX biobank, a living multi‐omics resource comprising 155 xenografts from 132 patients across 11 sarcoma histotypes, with osteosarcoma as the predominant subtype. This cohort is enriched for high‐risk sarcomas characterized by poor prognosis and widespread copy‐number alterations.

title: Current knowledge of morbidities and direct costs related to diabetic foot disorders: a literature review
creator: Felix W. A. Waibel, Ilker Uçkay, Laura Soldevila-Boixader, Christina Sydler, Karim Gariani
description: Diabetes is a chronic disease associated with numerous complications including diabetic foot disorders, which are associated with significant morbidity and mortality as well as high costs. The costs associated with diabetic foot disorders comprise those linked to care (direct) and loss of productivity and poor quality of life (indirect).

title: Enhanced disease resistance in chickpea and canola via MAGPIE: Major‐Effect Allele and Genomic Polygenic Integration for Enhancement
creator: Zibei Lin, Irene van den Berg, Shahin Yazdifar, Shimna Sudheesh, Adnan Riaz, Denise Barbulescu, Yongjun Li, Kristy Hobson, Muhammad Ahsan Asif, Matthew Hayden, Sukhjiwan Kaur
description: The global agricultural industry suffers major economic losses due to fungal diseases. Though selective breeding and introgression of resistance genes with major effects have helped to reduce the impact of these diseases, resistance breakdown occurs within a few generations. Quantitative resistance that relies on multiple small effect genes has proven to be more durable than relying on major effect genes.

title: Identification and functional analysis of differential miRNAs in young and middle-aged adults with essential hypertension: exploring potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets
creator: Xiu-Long Niu, Xiao-Jing Wang, Xin Zhang, Wei Pang, Qiong Guo, Tao Wang, Yu-Tian Liang, Chao Liu, Fang Hao, Guo-Hong Yang, Wei Cai, Hui-Xin Li, Shao-Bo Chen, Rui Shi
description: BackgroundEssential hypertension (EH) in young and middle-aged adults is a major risk factor for cardiovascular morbidity, yet the detailed molecular mechanisms underlying this condition have not been fully understood. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) have emerged as critical regulators of gene expression and have been increasingly associated with hypertension pathogenesis.

title: Identification and preliminary validation of biomarkers associated with mitochondrial and programmed cell death in pre-eclampsia
creator: Rong Lin, XiaoYing Weng, Liang Lin, XuYang Hu, ZhiYan Liu, Jing Zheng, FenFang Shen, Rui Li
description: BackgroundThe involvement of mitochondrial and programmed cell death (mtPCD)–related genes in the pathogenesis of pre-eclampsia (PE) remains inadequately characterized.MethodsThis study explores the role of mtPCD genes in PE through bioinformatics and experimental approaches.
