Differentially expressed mtPCD genes were identified as potential biomarkers from the GSE10588 and GSE98224 datasets and subsequently validated.

title: Novel Carbazole–Acylthiourea Derivatives: Synthesis, Antimicrobial, Antioxidant, Hemocompatibility, Cytotoxicity, and ADME‐Tox Profiling
creator: Carmen Limban, Ioana Cristina Marinaş, Mariana Carmen Chifiriuc, Miron Teodor Căproiu, Florea Dumitraşcu, Erzsébet‐Eleonóra Kapronczai, Irina Zarafu, Diana Camelia Nuţă, Petre Ioniţă, Speranţa Avram, Cătălina Mareş, Andra Maria Păun, Bogdan Mihai Cristea, Carmellina Daniela Bădiceanu, Ilinca Margare
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). A focused series of four carprofen‐derived carbazole–acylthiourea N‐(arylcarbamothioyl)propanamides (1a–d) was synthesized by in situ generation of 2‐(6‐chloro‐9H‐carbazol‐2‐yl)propanoyl isothiocyanate followed by reaction with aniline, para‐toluidine, para‐bromoaniline, and para‐iodoaniline, respectively. The structures were supported by FT‐IR, NMR, and APCI‐HRMS analyses. The compounds were evaluated against clinically relevant bacterial and fungal strains, complemented by antioxidant assays, hemocompatibility/antihemolysis models, cancer cell viability assays, and in silico drug‐likeness, pharmacokinetic, pharmacogenomic, and toxicity prediction.

title: Investigating diet to control asparagine uptake as an adjunct to asparaginase treatment
creator: Zara Forbrigger, Tamara MacDonald, Ketan Kulkarni, Andrew W. Stadnyk
description: Ongoing refinements of multidrug regimens, and particularly the addition of L-asparaginase, resulted in an immediate gain in survival for pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia patients. Yet L-asparaginase has substantial side effects which may require dose reductions or delays in subsequent doses.

title: Teachers’ responses to racism and racist bullying in Dutch primary schools
creator: Karen M. A. Sieben-Aduful, Roy A. Willems, Trijntje Völlink, Nico van der Wiel, Maria Sapouna, Pieter de Bruijn, Gemma Blok, Arjan E. R. Bos, Giel van Lankveld
description: BackgroundEarly in life, children with a non-White skin color, or a non-Western cultural or religious background, are susceptible of experiencing acts of racism. Since they spend a significant time of their daily life in school, teachers have a crucial role in providing a safe and bias-free environment for these children.

title: Assessing the current landscape of North American pediatric nutrition support teams: A survey study
creator: Rachel E Herdes, Lily Xia, Atu Agawu, Arun Ajmera, Mary Abigail S Garcia, Rahiya Rehman, Kanika Puri, Michael Carver, Danielle Wendel, Vijay Mehta, Bridget Dowd Kiernan, Tanyaporn K Kaenkumchorn, Rachel Knight, Nicole Martin, Alexandra Carey, Jennifer Panganiban, Deb Duro
description: IntroductionNutrition support teams (NSTs) were developed to standardize nutrition evaluation practices and coordinate transdisciplinary expertise for appropriate administration of inpatient nutritional care. Minimal data are available regarding the current practices, structure, and perceived utility of pediatric NSTs in diverse hospital systems.

title: Beyond vascular recanalization: precision medicine in cervical artery dissection guided by multiple mechanisms and multimodal imaging for brain functional recovery
creator: Tao Li, Linna Li, Kexin Zhao, Jiaqi Dai, Xueliang Tian, Xuanxiao Zhang, Shuo Yin, Wenjing Lan, Hongwei Zhou
description: Cervical artery dissection (CAD), a critical etiological contributor of stroke in young adults, exerts direct influence on neurological prognosis through its vascular recanalization outcomes. However, pathological heterogeneity and ongoing controversies surrounding treatment strategies hinder the optimization of clinical decision-making; its prognosis is often not favorable. At present, there are a relative paucity of studies on recanalization of CAD.

title: A case report of Behcet's disease in a child with trisomy 8 and literature review
creator: Kaixi Zhang, Chenxi Wei, Lijun Jiang, Xue Zhao, Qingxiao Su, Xingjie Qi, Hui Zhao, Zanhua Rong
description: ObjectiveReport a case of Behcet's disease (BD) in a child with trisomy 8 mosaicism (T8M), providing insights for the diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis of this condition.MethodsThe clinical data of an 11-year-old girl with T8M mosaicism and BD who was admitted to our hospital in August 2022 were retrospectively analyzed, and the relevant literature was reviewed.

title: Broadly Accessible and Highly Active Hydrophosphination Catalysis With Simple Calcium Compounds in DMSO Solution
creator: Moniruzzaman Moniruzzaman, Rory Waterman
description: Highly earth‐abundant and simple calcium precatalysts are reported that address the long‐standing challenge of broad scope in hydrophosphination catalysis. With more than 120 examples of hydrophosphination reactions, calcium catalysts are the broadest in scope, including traditional styrene substrates and activated alkenes (Michael acceptors), conjugated dienes, heterocumulenes, alkynes, unactivated alkenes, and even naturally occurring alkenes.

title: Treatment outcomes and its associated factors among neonates admitted with sepsis in Hiwot Fana Comprehensive Specialized University Hospital, Harar, Ethiopia
creator: Betelhem Gezahegn, Ahmed Abdella, Fentahun Meseret, Ahmed Mohammed, Mulualem Keneni, Tesfaye Asfaw, Diribsa Tizazu, Assefa Desalew
description: BackgroundSepsis in the neonatal period is a major health challenge in neonatal medicine because of its potential for rapid progression to multi-organ dysfunction, leading to higher morbidity and mortality. Although efforts have been made to advance the outcomes of neonates admitted to hospitals, there is a paucity of data regarding neonatal sepsis treatment outcomes in the study setting.

title: Matrix Metalloproteinase‐8 Deficiency Alters the Balance Between Viral Clearance and Immunopathology in H1N1 Infection
creator: Xiaoyun Wang, Joselyn Rojas‐Quintero, Duo Zhang, Joaquin Zuñiga, Caroline A. Owen
description: Matrix metalloproteinase‐8 (MMP‐8) regulates inflammatory responses, but its contributions to the pathogenesis of influenza A viral (IAV) disease are not known. Plasma MMP‐8 levels were increased 30‐fold in subjects infected with H1N1 or seasonal IAV and were inversely associated with the PaO2/FiO2 ratio, suggesting potential value as a candidate marker of lung injury severity that requires validation in larger cohorts.

title: Reading profiles in secondary school: concurrent language and cognitive abilities, and retrospective and prospective reading skills
creator: Christian Waldmann, Maria Levlin
description: IntroductionWe examined the concurrent language and cognitive abilities in a group of Swedish students with different reading profiles in secondary school, and the retrospective (primary school) and prospective (upper-secondary school) reading skills of each reading profile.MethodsSeventy-nine students participated in data collections in primary (grade 2: age 8), secondary (grade 8: age 14) and upper-secondary school (year 2: age 17).

title: Structural and functional alterations in postmenopausal women with insomnia: an MRI study of Eight-Section Vajra Exercise intervention effects
creator: Xiangbin Chen, Kun Wang, Xiaoying Xu, Yuxi Li, Yu Gao, Jiamin Yuan, Biyun Xu, Shijun Qiu, Fei Tan, Zhimin Yang
description: BackgroundPostmenopausal women exhibit heightened vulnerability to chronic insomnia due to estrogen decline and age-related neural alterations. While non-pharmacological interventions are preferred for long-term management, the neuroplastic mechanisms underlying exercise-based therapies remain poorly characterized.MethodsThis study examines the effects of Eight-Section Vajra Exercise (ESVE) on brain structure and function in postmenopausal women with insomnia (PMWI) using multimodal MRI.

title: Serum Concentration Relationships of Candesartan in Migraine Prevention
creator: Hedda Skogum Riise, Melanie Simpson, Ketil Arne Espnes, Erling Andreas Tronvik, Andreas Kattem Husøy, Lise R Øie, Anker Stubberud, Emil Kofoed, Aurora Harsvik Alstad, Hedda Hoff Hagen, Maren Guldteig Lien, Marie Larsen Stavseng, Ella Rian Sæther, Tore Wergeland
description: Migraine is a common disabling disorder, and optimising affordable preventive treatments remains highly relevant. Candesartan is an effective and well‐tolerated preventive treatment, but little is known about its dose‐concentration–response relationships. We explored these relationships using data from the MigriNor study, a prospective observational cohort of adults with episodic or chronic migraine initiating oral preventive treatment.

title: Study on the effects of exercise intervention combined with virtual reality technology on emotions and brain networks in secondary school students with depressive symptoms
creator: Ting Peng, Jing Song, Yizhong Ren, Jinghui Yang, Yi Zhang, Aiping Chi
description: BackgroundThis study aimed to investigate the functional connectivity characteristics of brain networks in secondary school students with depressive symptoms and to analyze the effects of exercise combined with virtual reality intervention on improving brain networks and emotional states, providing a neurobiological basis for early identification and precise intervention.

title: Non-coding RNA regulation of Magang geese skeletal muscle maturation via the MAPK signaling pathway
creator: Longsheng Hong, Danning Xu, Wanyan Li, Yifeng Wang, Nan Cao, Xinliang Fu, Yunbo Tian, Yugu Li, Bingxin Li
description: Skeletal muscle is a critical component of goose meat and a significant economic trait of geese. The regulatory roles of miRNAs and lncRNAs in the maturation stage of goose skeletal muscle are still unclear. Therefore, this study conducted experiments on the leg muscles of Magang geese at two stages: 3-day post-hatch (P3) and 3 months (M3).

title: Oxazolidinones in the Clinical Management of Staphylococcal Infection—Linezolid or Tedizolid? A review on behalf of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases (ESCMID) Study Group for Staphylococci and Staphylococcal Diseases (ESGS)
creator: Liana Macpherson, Anne-Grete Martson, Jose L Del Pozo, Cindy Zheng, Anna L Goodman
description: There is limited information in the existing literature regarding the choice of oxazolidinone in clinical practice to treat infections caused by staphylococcal species. As members of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases (ESCMID) Study Group for Staphylococci and Staphylococcal Diseases (ESGS) we have collaborated and written this narrative review aimed at clinicians considering these agents in practice.

title: Pregnancy testing prior to iodine-131 thyroid therapy: a literature review of current recommendations
creator: Stephen J. Sozio, David Cohen, William Y. Raynor, Jeffrey S. Kempf
description: PurposeIodine-131 (I-131) thyroid ablation is strictly contraindicated during pregnancy due to the risk of fetal thyroid damage after 10 weeks of gestation. Current society guidelines lack consistency regarding the best timing and method for pregnancy testing. This review aims to consolidate current recommendations and propose a standardized testing algorithm.

title: Associations between cochlear electrophysiology, emotional health, and sleep quality in adults with tinnitus: a comprehensive analysis
creator: Ye Liu, Lihao Bao, Xiaojiong Mao, Kaixing Shao, Guihua Xia, Shaosheng Liu, Ke Ji
description: IntroductionTinnitus is commonly accompanied by emotional distress and sleep disturbances, yet the extent to which these characteristics relate to cochlear electrophysiologic findings remains unclear. This study examined associations between electrophysiologic measures and emotional and sleep parameters in adults with subjective tinnitus.MethodsThis retrospective study included 120 adults with tinnitus.

title: Inflammatory burden index as a prognostic marker in patients with advanced gastric cancer treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy and immunotherapy
creator: Jiao-Bao Huang, Zhi-Yong Zhou, Jun Lu, Ji-Yun Zhu, Bin Lai, Sheng-Xun Mao, Jia-Qing Cao
description: BackgroundBlood inflammation index has been shown to correlate with the prognosis of patients with gastric cancer. However, few studies have compared the efficacy of existing blood inflammatory markers in predicting the prognosis of patients with locally advanced gastric cancer in combination with neoadjuvant chemotherapy and immunotherapy.

title: Evolution of Outcome Assessment in Chronic Low Back Pain Clinical Trials Throughout the 20th and 21st Centuries: A Scoping Review
creator: Daniel Santos Rocha, Alice Marques Moreira Lima, Ana Clara Chung‐Cardoso, Ana Paula Brito‐de‐Sousa, Anna Lívia Serejo‐da‐Silva, Marcelo Souza de Andrade, André Pontes‐Silva
description: ObjectiveTo identify, map, and synthesise the outcomes reported in patients with Chronic Low Back Pain (CLBP) and describe how these outcomes have changed over time throughout the 20th and 21st centuries.MethodsA scoping review was conducted according to the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and reported following the PRISMA‐ScR guidelines.

title: Exploring the potential mediating role of systemic antibiotics in the association between early-life lower respiratory tract infections and asthma at age 5 in the CHILD study
creator: Maria V. Medeleanu, Myrtha E. Reyna, Darlene L. Y. Dai, Geoffrey L. Winsor, Fiona S. L. Brinkman, Rahul Verma, Ella Nugent, Nashita Riaz, Elinor Simons, Piushkumar J. Mandhane, Meghan B. Azad, Stuart E. Turvey, Theo J. Moraes, Padmaja Subbarao
description: ObjectiveLower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) in early life are one of the strongest risk factors for childhood asthma and are often treated with systemic antibiotics (IV or oral). We aimed to explore the association between early-life LRTIs and systemic antibiotics on asthma development and the potential mediating role of antibiotics in this relationship.

title: Origanum majorana L. polyphenols: in vivo antiepileptic effect, in silico evaluation of their bioavailability, and interaction with the NMDA receptor
creator: Amal Amaghnouje, Mohamed Chebaibi, Saeed M. Aldossari, Hazem K. Ghneim, Fatima Ez-zahra Amrati, Imane Es-Safi, Francesca Di Cristo, Anna Calarco, Sanae Achour, Fabrizio Carta, Yazeed A. Al-Sheikh, Mourad A. M. Aboul-Soud, Dalila Bousta
description: Introduction: Epilepsy is a chronic brain disease characterized by repeated seizures and caused by excessive glutamate receptor activation. Many plants are traditionally used in the treatment of this disease. This study aimed to evaluate the bioavailability of a polyphenolic extract obtained from Origanum majorana L. (OMP) leaves, as well as its antiepileptic activity and its potential mechanism of action.

title: A broad-spectrum SARS-CoV-2 RBD vaccine with selected high-impact mutations and novel adjuvant induces durable T cell response and broad protection in mice
creator: Xianying Chen, Yuzhen Zhang, Shimin Yang, Yan Chen, Shengnan Qian, Zhen Zhang, Qianyun Liu, Chengbao Ma, Weiyi Yu, Jiangpeng Feng, Jiejie Liu, Ming Guo, Zhixiang Huang, Xin Wang, Jie Chen, Haiyan Zhao, Huan Yan, Ke Lan, Yu Chen, Li Zhou
description: IntroductionThe emergence of new SARS-CoV-2 variants with immune evasion capabilities underscores the importance of developing a broad-spectrum and effective vaccine. The receptor binding domain (RBD) of the Spike protein has been widely utilized in vaccine due to its high immunogenicity.

title: MOUD 2.0: a clinical algorithm and implementation evaluation protocol for sublingual and injectable buprenorphine treatment of opioid use disorder
creator: Brandon L. Joa, Eric N. Fung, Michael S. Weinstein, Lara C. Weinstein
description: BackgroundPrimary care is the initial contact point for most patients with opioid use disorder (OUD) but lacks tools for guiding treatment. Only a small fraction of patients access evidence-based care. Long-acting injectable buprenorphine has potential to improve medication adherence and program retention in low-barrier primary care treatment settings.

title: Glucagon‐Like Peptide‐1 Receptor Agonists in Multiple Sclerosis: A Topical Narrative Review
creator: Audrey Y Chang, Farrah J Mateen
description: The glucagon‐like peptide‐1 (GLP‐1) receptor agonists (RAs) are a relatively new class of drugs that were initially approved by the US Food and Drug Administration to improve glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and, subsequently, weight reduction in patients with obesity. Multiple sclerosis (MS) is commonly associated with comorbidities for which GLP‐1RAs are indicated.

title: Correction: Utility of multi-target nested PCR and ELISPOT assays for the detection of paucibacillary leprosy: a possible conclusion of clinical laboratory misdiagnosis
creator: Haiqin Jiang, Ying Shi, Santosh Chokkakula, Wenyue Zhang, Siyu Long, Zhenzhen Wang, Wenming Kong, Heng Long, Limei Wu, Lihua Hu, Qiang Yao, Hongsheng Wang
description:
ng the original, correct data for the groups appears below.

Comparative analysis of IFN-γ expression of ELISPOT in blood samples. Clinically diagnosed PB leprosy (n = 98), clinically diagnosed MB leprosy (n = 202), HHC (n = 150), and HD (n = 150) were detected with IFN-γ expression using ELISPOT (A) and analyzed by GraphPad Prism (B). *p<0.05, **p<0.01.

The original version of this article has been updated.

title: Brentuximab vedotin as a bridge to combination chemotherapy in gray zone lymphoma with severe liver impairment: a case report
creator: Roshan Asrani, Turgot Bora Cengiz, Bruce E. Petersen, Theodora Anagnostou, Joshua D. Brody
description: BackgroundGray zone lymphoma (GZL) is a rare lymphoma subtype characterized by features intermediate between diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) and classic Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL). The optimal first-line treatment for GZL remains undefined, particularly for patients with poor performance status or baseline organ impairment.

title: Ethnobotanical study of medicinal plants used by the people of Mosop, Nandi County in Kenya
creator: Z. C. Maiyo, S. N. Njeru, F. J. Toroitich, S. A. Indieka, M. A. Obonyo
description: Background: Throughout the history, nature has provided mankind with most of their basic needs, which include food, shelter, medicine, clothes, flavours, scents as well as raw materials. Given that they are an integral part of cultural heritage, medicinal plants have played a significant role in human healthcare systems around the world.

title: Common Data Elements for Preclinical High-Frequency Oscillations in Epilepsy
creator: Ziyi Wang, JiaoJiao Guo, Christos Panagiotis Lisgaras
description: Normal brain function relies on coordinated oscillations within and across neural circuits. In epilepsy, disruption of these oscillations may reflect pathological excitability associated with seizure generation and/or the emergence of comorbidities. Among these oscillatory activities, high-frequency oscillations (HFOs, typically within 80-500 Hz) are increasingly considered promising electrophysiological biomarkers of epileptogenicity.

title: Systemic Inflammation and Nutritional Index as a prognostic marker in endometrial cancer
creator: Nagihan Kolkıran, Atike Pınar Erdoğan, Mustafa Şahbazlar, Mustafa Şahin, Ferhat Ekinci
description: The clinical course of endometrial cancer exhibits substantial variability, underscoring the need for additional biomarkers to enhance risk stratification accuracy. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic utility of a novel composite index, integrating systemic inflammatory and nutritional parameters, herein termed the Systemic Inflammation and Nutritional Index (SINI), in patients diagnosed with endometrial cancer.

title: Applying Lifestyle Medicine to Improve Health Outcomes in People With Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities
creator: Theresa Hamlin, Conor Anderson, Johanna F Lantz, Jennifer Franck, Helena le Roux Ohm, Donald W Landry
description: Individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities (I/DD) and autism spectrum disorder experience disproportionately high rates of chronic disease, often exacerbated by systemic care barriers. Despite these concerns, interventions for this population rarely target overall health and wellness and often rely on practices that can contribute to poor health outcomes.

title: Short-term trends in hypertension and high cardiovascular risk at high altitude in Peru
creator: Brando Ortiz-Saavedra, Julio S. Mamani-Castillo, Irmia Paz, Jorge Ballón-Echegaray, Ricardo A. J. Leon-Vasquez
description: ObjectiveThe aim of the present study was to describe short-term trends in the prevalence of high cardiovascular risk and the prevalence, awareness, treatment, and controlled hypertension in the high altitude of Peru, during the years 2017 to 2023, using data from the Demographic and Family Health Survey.

title: Stable isotope‐derived measurements of protein synthesis detect amino acid‐induced anabolism in skeletal muscle microtissues not captured by puromycin labelling
creator: Yekaterina Tiper, Cassidy T. Tinline‐Goodfellow, Penney M. Gilbert, Daniel R. Moore
description: Skeletal muscle microtissues are valuable in vitro models for studying the stimuli regulating muscle protein synthesis (MPS), the key determinant of changes in muscle mass. Differentiated between opposing posts, microtissues contain aligned, contractile myotubes, providing a controlled system for investigating the responses of skeletal muscle to nutrient and contractile stimulation. However, microtissue MPS responses to these stimuli remain under‐characterized.

title: Mechanistic insights into the role of traditional Chinese medicine in treating gastric cancer
creator: Ziqiang Chen, Ting Yu, Yunhe Wang, Jiaxin Li, Bo Zhang, Liya Zhou
description: Gastric cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with advanced stages presenting significant challenges due to metastasis and drug resistance. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) offers a promising complementary approach characterized by holistic treatment principles and minimal side effects. This review comprehensively explores the multifaceted mechanisms by which TCM addresses gastric cancer.

title: Unpacking the Role of Financial Incentives in the Motivation and Individual Performance of Nurses in LMICs: A Scoping Review Protocol
creator: Abdellah Selmi, Diallo Djibrine, Zakaria Belrhiti
description: BackgroundHealth systems in low‐ and middle‐income countries (LMICs) continue to face persistent challenges related to health worker performance and quality of care, exacerbated by a global shortage of nurses. Financial incentive strategies (FIS), which include performance‐based financing, bonuses and allowances, are extensively implemented as mechanisms to enhance the motivation and individual performance of health workers, including nurses.

title: Help, near and far: a systematic review of post-COVID digital mental health solutions for domestic violence victims
creator: Ping Yu, Ping Zhu, Abdulswabul Kudiza, Francis Mungai Kaburu, Mehak Intizar, Chaojun Tong, Ruijie Zhang, Jianlin Jiang, Xin Yu, Qiang Kuang, Ruru Chen, Claudimar Pereira da Veiga, Yu-Tao Xiang, Zhaohui Su
description: IntroductionDomestic violence (DV), as a global pandemic, poses a significant challenge within the field of public health, gravely impacting the mental and physical health of victims. Modern digital technologies have been proposed as promising interventions for DV-related mental health problems. We therefore evaluated their effectiveness.

title: Advanced progress in the genetic modification of the oncolytic HSV-1 virus
creator: Mi Zhou, Zhenyu Shen
description: The use of replication-competent viruses for selective tumor oncolysis while sparing normal cells marks a significant advancement in cancer treatment. HSV-1 presents several advantages that position it as a leading candidate for oncolytic virotherapies. Its large genome can accommodate insertions over 30 kb or deletions of multiple virulence genes without compromising lytic replication in tumor cells.

title: The effect of a web-based lifestyle intervention on nutritional status and physical activity on prevention of COVID-19: a randomized controlled trial in women's empowerment
creator: Farhad Pourfarzi, Aziz Kamran, Maryam Zare, Jafar Mohammadshahi
description: BackgroundHealthy dietary intake and physical activity affect the immune systems. The present study aimed to investigate the effects of a web-based lifestyle intervention on nutritional status, physical activity, and prevention of COVID-19.MethodsThree hundred-three women (30–60 years old), who did not have COVID-19 in the City of Ardabil, participated in this study.

title: Multi‐Omics Integration Reveals Metabolic Reprogramming and EMT‐Driven Metastasis in Triple‐Negative Breast Cancer
creator: Yuheng Pang, Yuefeng Shang, Wenjing Wang, Tong Liu, Xiaolong Zou
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Triple‐negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive subtype with high metastatic potential and poor prognosis, yet the molecular mechanisms driving metastasis remain incompletely understood. Here, we performed integrated transcriptomic, metabolomic, and imaging mass cytometry (IMC) analyses on tumor tissues from 52 TNBC patients stratified into NonMeta (long‐term survival without metastasis, n = 39) and MetaPoor (metastasis‐related death within 36 months after metastatic diagnosis, n = 13) groups.

title: Effect of agarose/gelatin gel addition on the pro-angiogenic potential of polyhydroxybutyrate/chitosan scaffolds
creator: Mária Giretová, Ľubomír Medvecký, Zuzana Demčišáková, Lenka Luptáková, Eva Petrovová, Radoslava Štulajterová
description: The aim of this paper was to evaluate the effect of gel addition to biopolymeric scaffolds on the pro-angiogenic and basic material characteristics of the final composite for use in regenerative medicine. The studied scaffold consisted of natural biopolymers: polyhydroxybutyrate, chitosan, agarose, and gelatin. The final scaffold was characterized by high macroporosity (90%) and wide pore size distribution.

title: The Effect of Training Exercise on Cartilage Zonal Composition and Structure at Two Differently Loaded Sites in the Juvenile Equine Metacarpophalangeal Joint
creator: Michael J. S. Duggan, Margot C. Labberté, René van Weeren, Reinout Stoop, Mika M. Hyttinen, Jarno Rieppo, Jeroen de Groot, Pieter. A. J. Brama
description: BackgroundThe aim of this study was to investigate the depth related spatial distribution of biochemical and structural components in articular cartilage at different topographical sites experiencing different loading within the juvenile equine metacarpophalangeal joint in two groups of foals subjected to different exercise conditions.

title: A task-driven cerebral angiographic imaging based on CT perfusion
creator: Cheng Wang, Siqi Chen, Donghua Mi
description: IntroductionCurrent clinical computed tomography arteriography (cCTA) and clinical computed tomography venography (cCTV) images often display restricted cerebrovascular profiles, incomplete brain tissue segmentation, and incomplete artery-vein segmentation. Especially for vessels associated with diseases, capturing their complete profiles proves challenging.MethodsIn this work, we developed a Task-driven Cerebral Angiographic Imaging (TDCAI) technique using computed tomography perfusion (CTP) images of stroke patients.

title: Subsequent Knee Arthroplasty Does Not Influence Patient-Reported Outcomes Following Lumbar Fusion
creator: Joshua Mathew, Roy Y. Miloh, Mitchell Ng, Emily Berthiaume, Yulia Lee, Gregorio Baek, William Green, Yasmine Eichbaum, Morgan Hitchner, Steven J. Banko, Jonathan Dalton, Dipti Venkatesh, Vinay Bijoor, Paul Gunter, Gus Duininck, Andrew Vanichkachorn, Brandon Martinazzi, Ali Farooqi, Alec Giakas, Jose
description: Study DesignRetrospective Cohort Study.ObjectivesThe impact of knee arthritis and early total knee arthroplasty (TKA) on lumbar fusion recovery remains underexplored. This study aimed to identify demographic differences between lumbar fusion patients that had subsequent TKA and patients with OA without TKA, assess perioperative differences; and compare patient-reported outcomes (PROMs).MethodsRetrospective review was performed at one tertiary care center (2016–2025).

title: Assessing the impact of transcatheter edge-to-edge repair on reverse remodeling in secondary mitral regurgitation: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Adolf Lichtfusz, Nina Galdzytska, Dorottya Gergő, Bence Szabó, Péter Hegyi, Zsolt Molnár, Gábor Duray, Judit Papp
description: Background and aimTranscatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) is a minimally invasive approach to reduce secondary mitral regurgitation (SMR) in patients with heart failure. However, there is limited evidence on its effectiveness in achieving reverse remodeling. Our aim was to assess the effects of TEER over time and to compare the effects of TEER plus GDMT vs. GDMT alone on echocardiographic parameters.

title: An overview of pink eye infection to evaluate its medications: group decision-making approach with 2-tuple linguistic T-spherical fuzzy WASPAS method
creator: M. Waheed Rasheed, Hind Y. Saleh, Areen A. Salih, Jahangeer Karamat, Muhammad Bilal
description: An infectious eye illness known as pink eye results in ocular redness, irritation, and mucus. Schools are an especially vulnerable region for dissemination because they can propagate that contagious disease quickly via direct or indirect interactions. Choosing the right medication to treat pink eye infection is typically thought of as an intricate multi-attribute group decision-making concern.

title: Spin and Methodological Quality in Systematic Reviews of Decompression Timing for Central Cord Syndrome
creator: Marco Napolitano, Andrew Kwon, Aidan Lindgren, Daniel Rusu, Joshua Davood, Clay Beagles, Rajko Vucicevic, Jeffrey C Wang, Raymond J Hah, Ram K Alluri
description: Study DesignMeta-research.ObjectivesTo evaluate the prevalence and types of severe spin and the methodological quality of systematic reviews addressing early versus delayed surgical decompression for central cord syndrome (CCS).MethodsPubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Embase were searched for systematic reviews evaluating decompression timing in CCS.

title: A switch from α5β1 to αvβ3 integrin activity contributes to the development of a profibrotic mesenchymal phenotype in trabecular meshwork cells
creator: Kassidy L. Johns, Jennifer A. Faralli, Mark S. Filla, Nandini Shah, Kate E. Keller, Donna M. Peters
description: PurposeFibrogenic changes in the trabecular meshwork (TM) are considered to be a major cause for the restriction in aqueous humor outflow from the anterior chamber associated with primary open angle glaucoma. In this study, we investigated whether integrin switching from α5β1 to αvβ3 integrin expression could initiate fibrotic-like changes in the TM that could restrict outflow.

title: The role of arbuscular mycorrhizal symbiosis in plant abiotic stress
creator: Qian Wang, Mengmeng Liu, Zhifan Wang, Junrong Li, Ke Liu, Dong Huang
description: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) can penetrate plant root cortical cells, establish a symbiosis with most land plant species, and form branched structures (known as arbuscules) for nutrient exchange. Plants have evolved a complete plant–AMF symbiosis system to sustain their growth and development under various types of abiotic stress.

title: Integrating frailty interventions into existing care models: a comprehensive approach to enhancing patient outcomes in chronic disease management
creator: Izabella Uchmanowicz, Kenneth M. Faulkner, Paolo Iovino, Adrian Kwaśny, Stanisław Surma, Camilla Elena Magi, Grzegorz K. Jakubiak, Yari Longobucco, Dawid Janczak, Alina Rak-Pasikowska, Michał Czapla, Bartosz Uchmanowicz
description: Frailty syndrome (FS) is a complex and multifaceted condition commonly observed in old adults patients with chronic diseases, often accompanied by cognitive impairments. This review explores the integration of frailty interventions into existing care models to improve patient outcomes, focusing on four key areas.

title: Advancing Biotherapeutic Treatment of Ulcerative Colitis Using Lipid Mesophases: Formulation Design and Preclinical Validation
creator: Rafaela Gazzi, Tiziana Cremona, Reto Czekalla, Emily Campbell, Marlene Schwarzfischer, Doris Pöhlmann, Vanessa Dobernig, Gerhard Rogler, Michael Scharl, Alessandra Bergadano, Raffaele Mezzenga, Martin Kuentz, Paola Luciani, Simone Aleandri
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Biotherapeutics are required to achieve high remission rates in patients with severe ulcerative colitis (UC); however, adverse effects, complex dosing regimens, administration routes, and low patient compliance limit their widespread clinical use. Given the localized nature of UC, this study aimed to develop localized delivery strategies for infliximab (IFX), an anti‐tumor necrosis factor‐α (TNF‐α) monoclonal antibody recommended for moderately‐to‐severely active UC.

title: Serum decorin and biglycan levels as predictive biomarkers for lung fibrosis severity and mortality risk in COVID-19 patients
creator: Shaaf Ahmad, Kaleem Maqsood, Farwa Liaqat, Nabila Roohi
description: IntroductionIndividuals experiencing severe symptoms of COVID-19 are at the greatest risk of developing post-COVID lung fibrosis, which significantly impacts long-term health outcomes. This study aims to investigate the predictive potential of serum biomarkers, specifically decorin and biglycan, in assessing the severity and mortality risk among COVID-19 patients.

title: Isolation and Cs+ resistance mechanism of Escherichia coli strain ZX-1
creator: Daiki Kojima, Shunsuke Tanaka, Ayane Kurosaki, Xiong Zhiyu, Masahiro Ito
description: This research aims to elucidate the physiological mechanisms behind the accidental acquisition of high-concentration cesium ions (Cs+) tolerance of Escherichia coli and apply this understanding to develop bioremediation technologies. Bacterial Cs+ resistance has attracted attention, but its physiological mechanism remains largely unknown and poorly understood. In a prior study, we identified the Cs+/H+ antiporter TS_CshA in Microbacterium sp.

title: Optimized Land–Water Management Expands Afforestation Potential Under Land and Human Water‐Use Constraints
creator: Binbin Huang, Fei Lu, Yuebo Su, Xuming Wang, Hua Zheng, Zhiyun Ouyang
description: Afforestation is a low‐cost and high‐potential climate change mitigation strategy, but its feasibility remains highly uncertain because most existing assessments focus primarily on biophysical suitability and land resource constraints, while largely overlooking the critical limitation imposed by human water demand.

title: Case Report: Challenges in the surgical treatment of Marfan-associated aortic aneurysms: a literature review starting from a clinical case
creator: Ombretta Martinelli, Antonio Marzano, Valeria Gonta, Lucio Ferriero, Carola D’Amico, Simone Cuozzo, Maria Irene Bellini
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Marfan syndrome (MFS) is a systemic connective tissue disease severely affecting the cardiovascular system. We present the case of a MFS 55-year-old woman who arrived at the emergency department with increasing chest pain. Over the past 25 years, this patient had undergone mitral valve annuloplasty, subsequent open surgical repair of a ruptured infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm followed by open surgery for a type I thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm.

title: Gonadotropin‐Inhibitory Hormone (GnIH) and Its Receptor GPR147 Mediates Acute Stress‐Induced Activation of the Locus Coeruleus‐SAM Axis
creator: Jiani Zhang, Hongyu Zhu, Wenqi Wang, Bingqian Shen, Yuanyuan Xin, Xingxing Song, Xuanyi Lu, Lixuan Li, Siting Chen, Xiaochen Zhang, Jialing Zeng, Haodong Zheng, Jianlong Lao, Ke Peng, Yixian Wei, Jiaming Zheng, Chuanhuo Hu, Xiaoye Wang, Xun Li
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Gonadotropin‐inhibitory hormone (GnIH, also known as RFamide‐related peptide‐3, RFRP‐3) is a hypothalamic neuropeptide that regulates vertebrate reproduction via its receptor GPR147. Although GnIH is known to mediate stress‐induced reproductive suppression, its role in broader stress responses remains unclear. This study investigated the fuction of GnIH in acute stress and evaluated the mechanisms by which GnIH regulates norepinephrine (NE) release and activates the locus coeruleus‐sympathetic‐adrenal medulla (LC‐SAM) axis in mice.

title: Comparing the effects of laparoscopic radical surgery and traditional open surgery on short-term efficacy and long-term survival in patients with colorectal cancer
creator: Yanhong Lin, Jie Ling, Chuting Liao, Xiangjun Wang, Junfeng Yin
description: AimThis study aimed to compare the impacts of laparoscopic surgery (LS) and open surgery (OS) on the short-term efficacy and long-term survival in patients diagnosed with colorectal cancer (CRC).MethodsSixty CRC patients who underwent LS at our hospital between January 2021 and January 2022 were enrolled as the LS group.

title: An 8-week physical exercise intervention for e'athletes improves physical performance rather than short-term esports performance parameters - a randomized controlled trial
creator: Felix Wachholz, Nicole Gamper, Martin Schnitzer
description: IntroductionEsports have been suggested to enhance hand-eye coordination, fine motor skills, and reaction times. While physical exercise is known to improve these abilities, its impact on short-term esports performance is under-researched. This study aims to evaluate the effects of specific and general physical training on gaming performance, hypothesizing improvements in both physical and gaming-related variables.

title: Diabetes‐Associated Cognitive Impairment: Pathophysiology and Emerging Therapies
creator: Osman Corbali, Priyanka Menon, Halil I. Corbali, Ram Jagannathan, Allan I. Levey
description: Diabetes‐associated cognitive impairment (DACI) is a common yet underrecognized condition, manifesting along a spectrum from mild cognitive impairment to dementia. DACI encompasses patients who develop vascular dementia (VaD) or Alzheimer's disease (AD) with diabetes as a risk factor; however, in certain patients, particularly those lacking clear VaD or AD features, diabetes may act as a primary driver of neurodegeneration.

title: Predicting completion and early dropout in routine-care internet-delivered cognitive behaviour therapy: A temporal validation study
creator: Ram P. Sapkota, Blake F. Dear, Nickolai Titov, Heather D. Hadjistavropoulos
description: BackgroundIn routine-care Internet-delivered cognitive behaviour therapy (ICBT), engagement may be better understood as a staged process (e.g., early discontinuation vs full completion), yet many studies use a single dropout definition and seldom test whether prediction models remain useful as services evolve over time.

title: Comparative analysis of metabolites in different Areca inflorescence tissues based on spatial metabolomics
creator: Xinyu Wen, Panjing Li, Linbi Zhang, Han Li, Fusun Yang
description: In this study, we focused on the spatial distribution of metabolites in areca palm (Areca catechu L.) floral organs. Using spatial metabolomics, the composition and accumulation patterns of active metabolites were delineated to provide a basis for the development and utilization of their bioactive compounds.

title: Segmentation of tobacco shred point cloud and 3-D measurement based on improved PointNet++ network with DTC algorithm
creator: Yihang Wang, Haiwei Zheng, Jie Yang, Yan Wang, Li Wang, Qunfeng Niu
description: IntroductionThe three dimensions of the tobacco silk components (cut stem, tobacco silk, reconstituted tobacco shred, and expanded tobacco silk) of cigarettes directly affect cigarette combustibility; by accurately measuring the dimensions of different tobacco silks in cigarettes, it is possible to optimize combustibility and reduce the production of harmful substances.

title: HeCOG Cancer Biobank and Registry: a nationwide real-world resource for translational oncology research
creator: E. Fountzilas, K. Papadopoulou, G.-A. Koliou, T. Papapavlou, D. Pectasides, C. Christodoulou, E. Samantas, D. Bafaloukos, G. Aravantinos, P.A. Kosmidis, H.P. Kalofonos, J. Sgouros, P. Papakostas, E. Razis, T. Economopoulos, N. Zamboglou, A. Koutras, G. Pentheroudakis, F. Zagouri, H. Linardou, A. Chr
description: BackgroundLong-standing cooperative oncology groups are uniquely positioned to generate high-quality real-world data in diverse tumor types. The Hellenic Cooperative Oncology Group (HeCOG), a nonprofit scientific organization, has established a multi-institutional clinical database and biobank to support translational cancer research and precision oncology initiatives. Our aim was to describe the structure, governance and operation of HeCOG Biobank and patient registry.

title: Expert opinions and clinical experiences with chlormethine gel as maintenance treatment for patients with mycosis fungoides
creator: Larisa Geskin, Christiane Querfeld, Emmilia Hodak, Neda Nikbakht, Evangelia Papadavid, Marco Ardigò, Ulrike Wehkamp, Martine Bagot
description: Maintenance treatment can be recommended for patients with mycosis fungoides (MF) whose disease responds to primary treatment. While positive outcomes have been observed in small studies with maintenance therapy, there is a lack of practical guidelines and agreement on when and how maintenance therapy for MF should be approached.

title: Cryoimmobilized anther analysis reveals new ultrastructural insights into Rhynchospora (Cyperaceae) asymmetrical microsporogenesis
creator: Danilo M. Rocha, Ulla Neumann, Fernanda M. Nogueira, Georgios Tsipas, André L. L. Vanzela, André Marques
description: IntroductionThe Cyperaceae family is distinguished by holocentric chromosomes and a distinctive microsporogenesis process, which includes inverted meiosis, asymmetric tetrad formation, selective cell death, and the formation of pseudomonad pollen. Despite significant advances, the ultrastructural details of these processes remain poorly understood.

title: Graphene-oxide-microfiber aptasensor for dynamic neutrophil monitoring: Bridging cytokine release syndrome and point-of-care sepsis diagnosis
creator: Zhiheng Yu, Heshuang Dong, Xiaolin Chen, Mengjiang Xu, Ren Liu, Jingjing Wang, Cunliang Yang, Ke Wang, Xianyuan Zhao, Hao Jia, Jijun Feng
description: SummaryNeutrophil granule release is critical for host defense, yet its dysregulation underpins cytokine release syndrome (CRS) in both acute (such as sepsis) and sustained inflammatory states. Distinguishing these phases requires real-time monitoring of early markers like neutrophil elastase (ELANE) and lactoferrin (LF), but conventional assays lack requisite sensitivity.

title: Beyond anti-VEGF: expanding the therapeutic horizon and biomarker landscape in retinopathy of prematurity
creator: Yuxin Zhang, Qian Chen, Jianli Lv
description: BackgroundRetinopathy of prematurity (ROP) remains a leading cause of childhood blindness worldwide. While anti-VEGF therapy has revolutionized ROP treatment, concerns regarding systemic absorption, potential neurodevelopmental impacts, and late reactivation have spurred the quest for alternative therapeutic approaches. This mini-review examines emerging therapeutic targets and novel biomarkers that may transform ROP management beyond the anti-VEGF era.

title: Guanidine-quaternary ammonium polymer-derived carbon dots differentially modulate bacterial respiration and osteoblast mitochondria to resolve infection and foster osteointegration
creator: Xinxin Bai, Anhui Qin, Zhenguo Wang, Guang Kong, Menghan Zhang, Hongyu Li, Rui Zhao, Yue Yu, Yongfeng Zhang, Qi Liu, Ziqing Zhu, Bing Xia, Shengyou Li, Yiming Hao, Mingze Qin, Dong Lei, Lingli Guo, Meijia Su, Zhuojing Luo, Shaohuang Weng, Teng Ma, Jinghui Huang
description: Implant-associated infections (IAIs) represent one of the most challenging complications following orthopedic implantation. Current antibacterial strategies struggle to achieve complete pathogen eradication while maintaining sustained osteogenic activity at the implant-bone interface. Leveraging the spatial divergence in energy metabolism between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, we designed and synthesized guanidine-quaternary ammonium polymer-derived carbon dots (GQCDs) with confirmed structure.

title: Whole-genome analysis of a ST45-SCCmec IVa (2B)-t116 methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus strain isolated from the sputum of a 5-year-old child with pneumonia
creator: Lin Huang, Rui Guo, Jingxian Lin, Xiaowei Li, Zhicong Li, Limei Zhang, Wenting Li, Rui Xue, Cheng Zhang, Xiaosan Feng, Xiaobin Li
description: IntroductionMethicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) sequence type (ST) 45 is a major global MRSA lineage with huge strain diversity and a high clinical impact. In Hainan and Guangzhou of China, the ST45-MRSA was mainly associated with t116.MethodsThe MRSA strain SA2107 was isolated from the sputum of a 5-year-old child with pneumonia.

title: Goal-setting mechanisms in educational management: a psychological perspective on student and teacher behavior
creator: Yizhuo Wang, Shuzhu Tang, Yang Meng
description: ObjectiveTo explore the psychological mechanisms and behavioral impacts of goal-setting mechanisms in educational management.MethodsA cross-sectional survey was conducted with 1,247 students and 358 teachers from 15 schools; data were analyzed using structural equation modeling, multilevel regression, and mediation effect testing.ResultsGoal-setting mechanisms positively affected student learning behavior (β = 0.42, p < 0.001) and teacher teaching behavior (β = 0.

title: TPPU, a soluble epoxide hydrolase inhibitor, mitigates Aβ-induced neurotoxicity via dual modulation of mitochondrial stabilization and JNK suppression
creator: Jingfang Song, Ailan He, Shuyu Li, Qiong Wu
description: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive cognitive decline, primarily driven by β-amyloid (Aβ) aggregation and neuronal apoptosis. This study aims to investigate the neuroprotective effects of soluble epoxide hydrolase (sEH) inhibition against Aβ-induced cytotoxicity in PC-12 cells, focusing on cell viability, apoptosis, and the c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) signaling pathway.

title: Botulinum toxin type A for myogenic temporomandibular disorders: A scoping review of injection protocols, clinical outcomes, safety, and evidence gaps
creator: Marines Vega Sanchez, Luis Chauca Bajaña, Francisco Córdova, Maria Rodriguez Tates, Byron Velasquez Ron
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundBotulinum toxin type A (BoNT-A) has been increasingly investigated for persistent myogenic temporomandibular disorders (TMDs), particularly when conservative therapies provide insufficient symptom control. However, variability in patient selection, injection protocols, outcomes, and safety reporting complicates interpretation of its effectiveness.ObjectiveTo map and critically synthesize evidence regarding BoNT-A injection protocols, clinical outcomes, functional and physiological effects, safety, and methodological limitations in adults with myogenic TMD.MethodsThis scoping review followed PRISMA-ScR.

title: The challenges of direct Claisen–Schmidt condensation in the synthesis of polyhydroxylated bischalcones: experimental results supported by DFT calculations
creator: Rui Pereira, Mariela M Nolasco, Vera L M Silva, Eduarda Fernandes, Marine Desage-El Murr
description: The synthesis of chalcones commonly relies on the Claisen–Schmidt condensation, an attractive reaction owing to its operational simplicity and favorable atom economy. However, its application to acetophenones bearing multiple hydroxy substituents can be problematic, often requiring hydroxy protection and subsequent deprotection, thereby diminishing the sustainability advantages of the approach.

title: Cost-effectiveness analysis of toripalimab for metastatic or recurrent triple-negative breast cancer
creator: Jiangbo Shao, Cuiping Zhan, Chunxiang Jin, Ying Jin
description: BackgroundToliparibizumab in combination with nab-paclitaxel (T+N) has excellent efficacy inmetastatic or recurrent triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), but the optimal choice of sequence of therapy is unclear given the trade-offs between quality of life and cost. Cost-effectiveness analyses can quantify these tradeoffs, leading to more informed decisions.

title: Development and validation of machine learning models for MASLD: based on multiple potential screening indicators
creator: Hao Chen, Jingjing Zhang, Xueqin Chen, Ling Luo, Wenjiao Dong, Yongjie Wang, Jiyu Zhou, Canjin Chen, Wenhao Wang, Wenbin Zhang, Zhiyi Zhang, Yongguang Cai, Danli Kong, Yuanlin Ding
description: BackgroundMultifaceted factors play a crucial role in the prevention and treatment of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). This study aimed to utilize multifaceted indicators to construct MASLD risk prediction machine learning models and explore the core factors within these models.

title: Scaling HPV Self-Sampling in Low-Resource Settings: From Evidence to Sustainable Implementation
creator: Federica Inturrisi, Beatriz Serrano, Silvia de Sanjosé
description: Profound global inequities in cervical cancer burden persist, with nearly 90% of deaths occurring in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). High-performance human papillomavirus (HPV) testing is the recommended primary screening method, but its scale-up remains constrained by resource and infrastructure limitations.

title: C-Reactive Protein and Risk of Low Back Pain: A Univariable and Multivariable Mendelian Randomization Study
creator: Shalin Feng, Jun Mou, Xiaoqin Wang, Changping Mu
description: ObjectiveTo investigate the causal associations of genetically predicted C-reactive protein (CRP), major depressive disorder (MDD), body mass index (BMI), and smoking initiation with low back pain (LBP) using Mendelian randomization (MR).MethodsSummary-level GWAS data for exposures and LBP (FinnGen R8) were obtained. Instrumental variables were selected at a strict genome-wide threshold (P < 5×10−8) and harmonized.

title: The immune landscape and viral shedding of Omicron SARS-CoV-2 variants implicate immune escape
creator: Weilong Zhang, Xiaoyan Gai, Zhonghui Duan, Changjian Yan, Chunyuan Huang, Chaoling Wu, Siping Zheng, Zixiang Lin, Qingtao Zhou, Lili Dai, Ping Yang, Fang Bao, Hongmei Jing, Chao Cai, Yingmin Ma, Yongchang Sun
description: BackgroundThree years into the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, the virus continues to mutate despite widespread vaccination, posing ongoing challenges for epidemic prevention and control. The relationship between viral shedding and immune escape remains under investigation. This study aims to examine the association between viral shedding and immune escape in the BA.4/5 and BF.7 variants.

title: Healthcare professionals' communication practices and preparedness in organised human papillomavirus-based cervical Cancer screening: A cross-sectional study in Central Portugal
creator: Rita Sousa, José Alberto Fonseca-Moutinho, Fábio Gomes, Fernanda Loureiro, Ana Rita Goes, Patrícia Soares
description: ObjectiveTo evaluate healthcare professionals' knowledge, attitudes, communication confidence and practices within an organised human papillomavirus (HPV)-based cervical cancer screening programme and identify factors associated with communication practices.MethodsA cross-sectional survey was conducted among 470 general practitioners and nurses involved in organised cervical cancer screening in Portugal's Central Region, January–March 2024. Participants completed a 28-item questionnaire.

title: A pragmatic approach to selective genetic testing in kidney transplant candidates
creator: Pitchaphon Nissaisorakarn, Paul K. Fadakar, Kassem Safa, Andrew L. Lundquist, Cristian V. Riella, Leonardo V. Riella
description: IntroductionAdvances in the field of genetic testing have spurred its use in transplantation. Potential benefits of genetic testing in transplant nephrology include diagnosis, treatment, risk stratification of recurrent disease, and risk stratification in potential donors. However, it is unclear how to best apply genetic testing in this population to maximize its yield.

title: High throughput analysis of contaminants of emerging concern in complex matrices
creator: Tsz Yung (Patrick) Wong, Bent Speksnijder, Gayani R Kapukotuwa, Oksana Golovko
description: Contaminants of emerging concern (CECs) occur across diverse aquatic matrices, but their reliable quantification remains challenging because of large differences in matrix composition. This study developed and validated a rapid online solid-phase extraction coupled with ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (online-SPE-UPLC-MS/MS) method for the simultaneous determination of 46 pharmaceuticals, industrial chemicals, pesticides, and per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS).

title: Legume cover under Camellia oleifera forests enhances understory biomass carbon storage and soil CO2 flux but declines soil inorganic carbon storage on a karst steep slope
creator: Leilei Ding, Hang Sun, Zhongfu Long, Birong Gao, Zhenduan Zhou, Yue Ye, Song Yang, Xia Lei
description: IntroductionLegume cover is a widely used and useful soil management strategy in orchards across the world. However, it remains unclear how the alfalfa cover affects vegetation and soil carbon storage, soil greenhouse gas fluxes, and global warming potential in Camellia oleifera forests.

title: Nasopharyngeal diffuse large b-cell lymphoma in a teenage presenting with cavernous sinus syndrome: A case report
creator: Faiza Afzal, Nadia Nazir, Muhammad Junaid Tahir, Sana Akhtar, Asma Usman, Kashif Siddiqui
description: Primary lymphoma of the nasopharynx is uncommon and is more commonly seen as an association with other primary pathologies. Nasopharyngeal lymphoma is an aggressive tumor and can affect all age groups but is more commonly seen in middle-aged and older individuals. Majority of these tumors belong to the non-Hodgkin’s group.

title: Integrative bulk and single-cell transcriptomics identifies a HERC5-linked immune-attenuated risk program for pulmonary metastasis/relapse in osteosarcoma
creator: Zhangfu Li, Baicheng Yang, Shiqing Liu, Shengji Yu
description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Highlights•A nine-gene PM/R score was developed in the TARGET-OS discovery cohort.•A seven-gene implementation showed cross-cohort discrimination in GSE21257.•High-risk tumors showed reduced antigen presentation and immune activity.•HERC5 was linked to interferon and antigen-presentation programs.•Single-cell analysis suggested SPP1/MIF-centered communication axes.Keywords: Osteosarcoma, Pulmonary metastasis/relapse, HERC5, Antigen presentation, Single-cell RNA sequencing

Introduction

Osteosarcoma is one of the most common primary malignant bone tumors in children, adolescents and young adults, and metastatic progression remains the principal factor associated with poor clinical outcome [1,2].

title: The time has come: integrating vaccination and vector control for Aedes-borne disease prevention
creator: Henry Puerta-Guardo, Pablo Manrique-Saide
description: abundance, vector competence, or transmission potential, thereby reducing population-level exposure. The key question is therefore not whether either approach has value in isolation, but how vaccination, biological vector control, and evidence-based routine vector-control measures can be combined within integrated prevention programs.

title: Protocol for an immunocompetent KPC mouse model of pancreatic cancer resection and recurrence for perioperative treatment studies
creator: Jacob L Léger, Nawal Amhis, Sarah Mansouri, Maria Fernanda Meza Pacheco, Lauren Daniel, Hugo Giguère, Yves Collin, Lee-Hwa Tai
description: SummaryIn mouse models of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, surgical removal of orthotopic tumors typically involves removing the primary tumor along with the spleen. Here, we present a protocol for surgical removal of the tumor in the tail of the pancreas while preserving the spleen.

title: Taichi on the brain: an activation likelihood estimated meta-analysis of functional neuroimaging data
creator: Shengxin Wang, Tianyu Liu, Jingtao Du, Jun Chen, Xiufen Luo, Yujie Meng, Chun Zeng, Xupeng Zhang, Binghua Shao
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionTai Chi Chuan (TCC) is an exercise regimen renowned for its comprehensive benefits to both physical and mental health. The present research endeavor aims to elucidate the neurocognitive impacts of TCC compared to alternative exercise modalities or therapeutic interventions.MethodsA systematic meta-analysis was undertaken, encompassing a rigorous review of diverse datasets, wherein 422 scholarly articles were examined, with a subset of 18 articles meeting the stringent criteria for inclusion in the analytical framework.ResultsThe study cohort comprised 677 participants, characterized by a mean age

title: Development and validation of a nomogram for predicting pulmonary infection in patients receiving immunosuppressive drugs
creator: Chuxuan Luo, Yue Zhang, Jiajie Zhang, Chen Jin, Xiaolan Ye, Yan Ren, Huajuan Shen, Maosheng Chen, Yiwen Li, Qiang He, Guangbiao Xu, Lina Shao
description: Objective: Pulmonary infection (PI), a severe complication of immunosuppressive therapy, affects patients’ prognosis. As part of this study, we aimed to construct a pulmonary infection prediction (PIP) model and validate it in patients receiving immunosuppressive drugs (ISDs). Methods: Totally, 7,977 patients being treated with ISDs were randomised 7:3 to the developing (n = 5,583) versus validation datasets (n = 2,394).

title: Preoperative Thoracic Compensation is Associated With a Lower Risk of Proximal Junctional Kyphosis After Lower Thoracic Fusion for Adult Spinal Deformity
creator: Tae Soo Shin, Jin-Sung Park, Dong-Ho Kang, Jun-Seok Oh, Joon Young Jung, Jae-Won Hur, Se-Jun Park
description: Study DesignRetrospective cohort study.ObjectivesTo determine whether thoracic compensation (TC) assessed against the deformity burden is associated with proximal junctional kyphosis (PJK) after lower thoracic fusion for adult spinal deformity (ASD).MethodsWe reviewed 343 patients fused from T9-L1 to the sacrum or pelvis with a pelvic incidence (PI) minus lumbar lordosis (LL) mismatch above 20°.

title: PBMCs gene expression predicts liver fibrosis regression after successful HCV therapy in HIV/HCV-coinfected patients
creator: Ana Virseda-Berdices, Óscar Brochado-Kith, Juan Berenguer, Juan González-García, Leire Pérez-Latorre, Carmen Busca, Cristina Díez, Rafael Micán, Amanda Fernández-Rodríguez, María Ángeles Jiménez-Sousa, Salvador Resino
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundHCV eradication with antiviral treatment reduces hepatic disease, but some patients remain at risk of progression to cirrhosis despite HCV clearance. We aimed to examine the association between peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) gene expression before HCV therapy and a pronounced decrease in the liver stiffness measurement (LSM) value in HIV/HCV-coinfected patients after HCV treatment and achievement of sustained virological response (SVR).MethodsWe performed a retrospective study in 48 HIV/HCV-coinfected patients who started anti-HCV treatment with at least advanced fibrosis (LSM ≥9.5).

title: Recurrent symmetrical bendings cause dwarfing in Hydrangea through spatial molecular regulation of xylem cell walls
creator: Béra Ley-Ngardigal, Hanaé Roman, Nathalie Brouard, Lydie Huché-Thélier, Vincent Guérin, Nathalie Leduc
description: Environmental prejudices progressively lead to the ban of dwarfing molecules in agriculture, and alternatives are urgently required. Mechanical stimulation (MS) is a promising, eco-friendly, and economical technique, but some responses to mechanical stimulation vary from one plant species to another.

title: Targeting the kynurenine pathway: another therapeutic opportunity in the metabolic crosstalk between cancer and immune cells
creator: Irene Kang, George Theodoropoulos, Medhi Wangpaichitr
description: The pivotal role of metabolic reprogramming in cancer-related drug resistance, through the tryptophan-catabolized kynurenine pathway (KP), has been particularly underscored in recent research. This pathway, driven by indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1), facilitates immune evasion and promotes tumor progression by fostering an immunosuppressive environment.

title: Critical importance of patient-reported outcomes for a comprehensive assessment of psoriatic arthritis patients
creator: Marika Lo Monaco, Raffaella Mallaci Bocchio, Giuseppe Natoli, Annarita Giardina, Ignazio Cangemi, Salvatore Scibetta, Christiano Argano, Salvatore Corrao
description: IntroductionPsoriatic arthritis (PsA) is a heterogeneous, chronic inflammatory disease that negatively impacts patients’ quality of life. Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) are used to capture patient perspectives in disease assessment, and physicians use the Disease Activity Index for Psoriatic Arthritis (DAPSA) to evaluate disease activity in PsA.

title: Dietary inflammatory index and disability among older adults in Guangzhou: a cross-sectional analysis
creator: Junbin Liao, Wenfeng Cai, Danrong Lin, Yuanyun Xiao, Yanxi Liu, Yahui Wang, Yuquan Zhong, Fan Xiao, Heng Fang, Yilu Yao, Yunfeng Lin, Jiewen Su, Siyu Sun, Bo Zhang, Yan Wang, Wei Zhu
description: ObjectiveThis study aims to evaluate factors linked to the degree of disability among older adults and explore the relationship between the dietary inflammatory index (DII) and the degree of disability among older adults in southern China.MethodsConducted in two districts of Guangzhou, China, this cross-sectional study included 262 older adults with mild-to-severe disabilities.

title: Inflammation and poverty as individual and combined predictors of 15-year mortality risk in middle aged and older adults in the US
creator: Arch G. Mainous, Frank A. Orlando, Lu Yin, Pooja Sharma, Velyn Wu, Aaron Saguil
description: BackgroundChronic systemic inflammation and poverty are both linked to an increased mortality risk. The goal of this study was to determine if there is a synergistic effect of the presence of inflammation and poverty on the 15-year risk of all-cause, heart disease and cancer mortality among US adults.

title: Speaker-turn aware diarization for speech-based cognitive assessments
creator: Sean Shensheng Xu, Xiaoquan Ke, Man-Wai Mak, Ka Ho Wong, Helen Meng, Timothy C. Y. Kwok, Jason Gu, Jian Zhang, Wei Tao, Chunqi Chang
description: IntroductionSpeaker diarization is an essential preprocessing step for diagnosing cognitive impairments from speech-based Montreal cognitive assessments (MoCA).MethodsThis paper proposes three enhancements to the conventional speaker diarization methods for such assessments. The enhancements tackle the challenges of diarizing MoCA recordings on two fronts.

title: Exendin-4 affects calcium signalling predominantly during activation and activity of beta cell networks in acute mouse pancreas tissue slices
creator: Eva Paradiž Leitgeb, Jasmina Kerčmar, Lidija Križančić Bombek, Vilijem Pohorec, Maša Skelin Klemen, Marjan Slak Rupnik, Marko Gosak, Jurij Dolenšek, Andraž Stožer
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Tight control of beta cell stimulus-secretion coupling is crucial for maintaining homeostasis of energy-rich nutrients. While glucose serves as a primary regulator of this process, incretins augment beta cell function, partly by enhancing cytosolic [Ca2+] dynamics. However, the details of how precisely they affect beta cell recruitment during activation, their active time, and functional connectivity during plateau activity, and how they influence beta cell deactivation remain to be described.

title: Hexokinase-linked glycolytic overload and unscheduled glycolysis in hyperglycemia-induced pathogenesis of insulin resistance, beta-cell glucotoxicity, and diabetic vascular complications
creator: Naila Rabbani, Paul J. Thornalley
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Hyperglycemia is a risk factor for the development of insulin resistance, beta-cell glucotoxicity, and vascular complications of diabetes. We propose the hypothesis, hexokinase-linked glycolytic overload and unscheduled glycolysis, in explanation. Hexokinases (HKs) catalyze the first step of glucose metabolism. Increased flux of glucose metabolism through glycolysis gated by HKs, when occurring without concomitant increased activity of glycolytic enzymes—unscheduled glycolysis—produces increased levels of glycolytic intermediates with overspill into effector pathways of cell dysfunction and pathogenesis.

title: The quality of selected raw and pasteurized honeys based on their sensory profiles and consumer preferences
creator: Marek Kardas, Wiktoria Staśkiewicz-Bartecka, Katarzyna Sołtys, Lechowsław Dul, Anna-Maria Sapała, Agata Kiciak, Agnieszka Bielaszka, Justyna Kardas
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The purpose of this study was to determine the sensory profile of honeys based on the method of quantitative descriptive analysis and principal component analysis and assess consumer preferences of raw and pasteurized honeys. Samples of multi-floral honeys (from the store and apiary) were subjected to sensory analysis based on the method of ranking for taste preference, the method of scaling based on color, aroma, taste, and texture, and the method of differential descriptive analysis using 11 quality descriptors.

title: CD8⁺ T Cell infiltration and spatial organization in cancer: mechanisms, barriers, and therapeutic strategies
creator: Lylou Milian, Mannon Geindreau, Cassandre Pignol, Frédérique Vegran
description: The infiltration of tumors by CD8⁺ T lymphocytes is a critical determinant of antitumor immunity and response to immunotherapy. However, the presence of tumor-specific CD8⁺ T cells does not necessarily translate into effective tumor control, as multiple biological barriers can prevent their recruitment, spatial distribution, persistence, and functional activity.

title: Managing Dissociation and Somatic Symptoms in Complex PTSD Using a Structural Dissociation-informed Approach: A Case Report
creator: Sanya Kapur, Megha Sharma
description: Chronic interpersonal trauma can lead to complex clinical presentations characterized by dissociation, somatic symptoms, and disturbances in self-organization, particularly when psychosocial stressors remain active. This case report describes a 32-year-old female with prolonged interpersonal trauma who presented with dissociative episodes, somatic symptoms including fainting and jaw locking, recurrent suicidal ideation, and significant functional impairment.

title: Osteo-immunological impact of radon spa treatment: due to radon or spa alone? Results from the prospective, thermal bath placebo-controlled RAD-ON02 trial
creator: Denise Eckert, Megi Evic, Jasmin Schang, Maike Isbruch, Melissa Er, Lea Dörrschuck, Felicitas Rapp, Anna-Jasmina Donaubauer, Udo S. Gaipl, Benjamin Frey, Claudia Fournier
description: Musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) are associated with pain and lead to reduced mobility and quality of life for patients. Radon therapy is used as alternative or complementary to pharmaceutical treatments. According to previous reports, radon spa leads to analgesic and anti-inflammatory effects, but the cellular and molecular mechanisms are widely unknown.

title: YOLOv8s-Longan: a lightweight detection method for the longan fruit-picking UAV
creator: Jun Li, Kaixuan Wu, Meiqi Zhang, Hengxu Chen, Hengyi Lin, Yuju Mai, Linlin Shi
description: IntroductionDue to the limited computing power and fast flight speed of the picking of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), it is important to design a quick and accurate detecting algorithm to obtain the fruit position.MethodsThis paper proposes a lightweight deep learning algorithm, named YOLOv8s-Longan, to improve the detection accuracy and reduce the number of model parameters for fruitpicking UAVs.

title: Osteochondral lesions of the talus in the pediatric population: A practical narrative review
creator: Marco Turati, Simone Daniel Gatti, Monika Thüsing, Matteo Guelfi, Marco Crippa, Jaakko Sinikumpu, Marco Bigoni
description: Osteochondral lesions of the talus (OLTs) in children and adolescents are a clinically important cause of persistent ankle pain after trauma and may also be present without a clear inciting event. Because plain radiographs may fail to detect OLTs or may underestimate their severity, modern pediatric pathways rely on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for characterization.

title: Wearable Health-Tracking Devices and Adherence to Physical Activity Guidelines Among US Adults, Including Those with Elevated Anxiety Symptoms: A Nationally Representative Cross-Sectional Analysis of HINTS 7 (2024)
creator: David Goldman, Laurie Kortowich, Matthew Nagra
description: Physical activity is a pillar of lifestyle medicine, yet most US adults do not meet aerobic guidelines, and inactivity is especially common among people with anxiety. Wearables enable self-monitoring, but population-level evidence linking them to guideline adherence among distressed adults is limited. We analyzed 6686 adults from the nationally representative Health Information National Trends Survey 7 (2024).

title: Lipid metabolism in myeloid cell function and chronic inflammatory diseases
creator: Ayaka Ito, Takayoshi Suganami
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Immune cells adapt their metabolism in response to their differentiation and activation status to meet the energy demands for an appropriate immune response. Recent studies have elucidated that during immune cell metabolic reprogramming, lipid metabolism, including lipid uptake, de novo lipid synthesis and fatty acid oxidation, undergoes significant alteration, resulting in dynamic changes in the quantity and quality of intracellular lipids. Given that lipids serve as an energy source and structural components of cellular membranes, they have important implications for physiological function.

title: Application of CAR-T cell therapy in orthopedics: From bone malignancies to non-malignant musculoskeletal disorders
creator: Yimei Que, Xienilai Xie, Wei Xie, Yunzhou Zuo, Wang Chen, Zedong Xu, Changtian Gong, Xugui Li
description: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy has transformed hematologic oncology, but its application in orthopaedic diseases remains at an early stage. In bone malignancies, including osteosarcoma, chondrosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma, and bone metastases, antigen heterogeneity, limited trafficking and persistence, and the immunosuppressive skeletal microenvironment restrict efficacy.

title: Depression, anxiety and its predictor among internally displaced person in metekel Ethiopia, 2023: using a structural equation model
creator: Solomon Debela Bekeko, Teshome Demis Nimani, Samuel Demissie Darcho, Feyisa Shasho Bayisa
description: IntroductionThese individuals face psychological and physical trauma, loss of jobs, and emotional isolation, which may lead to the development of depression and anxiety. In 2022, 120 countries had over 71 million IDPs, a 20% increase from the previous year. In sub-Saharan Africa, natural disasters accounted for 40% of all new IDPs worldwide.MethodAn institutional-based cross-sectional study was conducted in Ethiopia.

title: Six pragmatic steps to separate medical GenAI’s promise from its inherent dangers
creator: Stephen Gilbert, Max Ostermann, Oscar Freyer
description: GenAI and agentic systems in medicine bring real opportunities for better diagnosis and therapy and for the development of better diagnoses and therapies. It is now increasingly being recognised that the power of these systems for good is inseparable from their power to be used for harm.

title: Decreased influenza activity during the COVID-19 pandemic in Ghana, 2020
creator: Ivy Asantewaa Asante, Stephen Ofori Nyarko, Yaw Awuku-Larbi, Richard Asomadu Obeng, Gifty Mawuli Sarpong, Esinam Aku Apefa Amenuvor, Mildred Adusei-Poku, Linda Boatemaa, Vanessa Magnusen, Jennifer Wutsika, Samuel Ago, Lorreta Kwasah, Juliet Wordui, Roberta Aprilyn Tackie, Dennis Odai Laryea, Frankli
description: IntroductionThe COVID-19 pandemic had a significant effect on influenza activity globally. In this study, we analyzed trends of influenza activity in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic in Ghana.MethodsThis was a cross-sectional study using active prospective influenza surveillance data from 29 sentinel sites.

title: Sustainable Diepoxide Monomers for Polyoxazolidinone‐Based High‐Performance Thermoplastics
creator: Lisa Van Emelen, Friederike Ratsch, Patrick Klein, Sarah Brettschneider, Hans Gildenast, Markus D. Schötz, Mathias Glaßner, Martin Reiher, Elena Dirksen, Felix Niebisch, Kiruthika Periasamy, Ria Ghosh, Sohajl Movahhed, Kai Laemmerhold, Jürgen Klankermayer
description: Owing to their outstanding mechanical, thermal, and chemical properties, polyoxazolidinones, which are accessible from the reaction of diepoxides and diisocyanates, have recently gained interest as a new class of high‐performance thermoplastic materials. However, mainly bisphenol A diglycidyl ether (BADGE) has thus far served as benchmark for the diepoxide part.

title: First record of Alectorobius coniceps (Ixodoidea: Argasidae) and Dermacentor sp. (Ixodoidea: Ixodidae) in Pakistan
creator: Abid Ali, Mehran Khan, Zafar Ullah, Muhammad Numan, Kun-Hsien Tsai, Abdulaziz Alouffi, Mashal M. Almutairi, Tetsuya Tanaka
description: Alectorobius species are soft ticks primarily infesting birds, such as swallows, while Dermacentor species are hard ticks mainly infesting mammals, such as small ruminants. This study for the first time reported on the morphological and molecular bases of two tick species, namely A. coniceps and a Dermacentor sp. in Pakistan.

title: Unraveling the insomnia puzzle: sleep reactivity, attention deficit hyperactivity symptoms, and insomnia severity in ADHD Patients
creator: Hilal Uygur
description: IntroductionInsomnia is the most common sleep problem among adults with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). The severity of insomnia can exacerbate the symptoms of ADHD. Identifying the predictive factors that contribute to insomnia severity may be crucial in treating insomnia among adults with ADHD.

title: Microbial ecology of sandflies—the correlation between nutrition, Phlebotomus papatasi sandfly development and microbiome
creator: Slavica Vaselek, Bulent Alten
description: The role and the impact of the microbial component on the biology, ecology, and development of sandflies is largely unknown. We evaluated the impact of larval nutrition on laboratory-reared sandflies in correlation to the abundance of food, light starvation, and food with/without live microbiome, by monitoring the survival and development of immature stages, and the longevity of adult sandflies.

title: Eco-phenotypic characterization of Candida palmioleophila from poultry litter and marine environments: implications for One Health
creator: Dario Corrêa-Junior, Igor Avellar-Moura, Marcos de Abreu Almeida, Elisa Gonçalves Medeiros, Alessandro F Valdez, Rodrigo Almeida-Paes, Leonardo Nimrichter, Cláudio Ernesto Taveira Parente, Allan Jefferson Guimarães, Susana Frases
description: Candida palmioleophila is an emerging opportunistic yeast frequently misidentified within the Meyerozyma guilliermondii complex, potentially obscuring its clinical and ecological relevance. Although its clinical significance is increasingly recognized, the phenotypic characteristics of environmental isolates remain poorly explored. This study evaluated the eco-phenotypic profiles of 14 C.

title: Association between triglyceride glucose index and adverse clinical outcomes in patients with acute myocardial infarction and LDL-C≤1.8 mmol/L who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention: a prospective cohort study
creator: Hong-wei Zhao, Yong Wang, Cheng-fu Wang, Qing-kun Meng
description: BackgroundRecently, the triglyceride glucose (TyG) index has emerged as a reliable predictive indicator for adverse outcomes of cardiovascular disease. However, the roles of the TyG index in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C)≤1.8 mmol/L after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remain unclear.MethodsA total of 599 patients diagnosed with AMI and LDL-C ≤ 1.

title: The impact of ventilation mode on systemic inflammation and organ dysfunction in a porcine model of abdominal sepsis-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome
creator: James G. Williams, Michaela Kollisch-Singule, Nirmeen Elmadany, Nader M. Habashi, Gary F. Nieman, Brian M. Varisco
description: IntroductionSepsis commonly causes acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and immune hyperactivation may be a causal link. Ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI) is common in ARDS, and VILI may potentiate organ dysfunction in severe sepsis. We used a porcine model of abdominal sepsis-associated ARDS to test whether ventilation strategy could impact systemic inflammation and organ dysfunction.

title: Adaptation and Translation of the Brain Fog Scale into the Indian Psycho-Socio-Cultural Context
creator: Himanshi Khanna, Neeraj Panwar
description: BackgroundBrain fog is a subjective experience characterised by forgetfulness, poor concentration, mental slowness, dissociation and fatigue, with individuals describing experiences such as a ‘mental wall’ over formerly simple tasks. During and after the 2019 pandemic, scientific enquiry into brain fog was revived, explored and studied worldwide.

title: Clonal and plasmidic dissemination of critical antimicrobial resistance genes through clinically relevant ExPEC and APEC-like lineages (ST) in the dairy cattle population of Québec, Canada
creator: Maud de Lagarde, John Morris Fairbrother, Marie Archambault, Simon Dufour, David Francoz, Jonathan Massé, Hélène Lardé, Cécile Aenishaenslin, Marie-Eve Paradis, Yves Terrat, Jean-Philippe Roy
description: Antimicrobial resistance can be effectively limited by improving the judicious use of antimicrobials in food production. However, its effect on the spread of AMR genes in animal populations is not well described. In the province of Québec, Canada, a new legislation implemented in 2019 has led to an unprecedented reduction in the use of critical antimicrobials in dairy production.

title: Family-related Factors Associated With Readmission Among Children and Adolescents With Psychiatric Disorders
creator: Mohammad Sabzi Khoshnami, Mohammad Rajabi, Fardin Alipour, Mohsen Vahedi, Fatemeh Gholami Jam
description: Background:Psychiatric readmission among children and adolescents is a major concern in mental health services and is influenced by clinical, familial, and demographic factors.
