title: Disentangling the effects of terroir, season, and vintage on the grapevine fungal pathobiome
creator: Carla Mota Leal, Adrienn Geiger, Anna Molnár, Kálmán Z. Váczy, Glodia Kgobe, Zsolt Zsófi, József Geml
description: The composition, diversity and dynamics of microbial communities associated with grapevines may be influenced by various environmental factors, including terroir, vintage, and season. Among these factors, terroir stands out as a unique possible determinant of the pathobiome, the community of plant-associated pathogens.

title: Practical applications of photon-counting CT in oncology: an organ-based pictorial review
creator: Yusuke Kawasaki, Kota Yokoyama, Hiroto Hada, Hirofumi Yamada, Junichi Tsuchiya, Kurara Yamamoto, Iichiroh Onishi, Yosuke Ariizumi, Takayuki Honda, Kenichi Okubo, Tomoyuki Aruga, Daisuke Asano, Daisuke Ban, Soichiro Yoshida, Yasuhisa Fujii, Kimio Wakana, Marie Hanaoka, Keisuke Tanaka, Masahide Yamamo
description: Spectral computed tomography (CT) has become an important extension of contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) in oncologic imaging by providing material-specific information beyond conventional morphologic assessment. Dual-energy CT (DECT), implemented on energy-integrating detector CT (EID-CT) platforms, has demonstrated the value of low-keV virtual monoenergetic imaging (VMI), iodine mapping, and material decomposition for improving tumor conspicuity, delineating local extent, and supporting tissue characterization.

title: Case report: Rare benign obstructive disease of the biliary tract—a rare case of eosinophilic cholangitis
creator: Xiao-Ning Huang, Qi-Min Fang, Yu-Feng Zhong, Jing Liu
description: ObjectiveEosinophilic cholangitis (EC) is an uncommon form of benign biliary obstruction. It frequently eludes accurate clinical diagnosis, leading to inappropriate treatment methods. It is our aspiration that this clinical report will impart comprehensive insights into EC and, specifically, the critical role of tomographic examination.

title: Real-time CT/MR fusion imaging-guided core needle biopsy: enhancing diagnostic precision in head and neck lesions
creator: Xing Liang, Ying Wang, Zheng Yuan, Jiliang Ren, Gongxin Yang, Weiqing Tang, Ying Yuan
description: ObjectivesTo establish an intraoperative CT/MR fusion imaging (FI)-guided core needle biopsy (CNB) approach for head and neck lesions and to evaluate its diagnostic performance in comparison with conventional CT-guided biopsy.Material and methodsThis retrospective study included patients undergoing CT-guided or FI-guided CNB for head and neck lesions between January 2020 and December 2024.

title: A computational validation for the health concept maturity levels questionnaire
creator: Arthur Trognon, Islem Habibi, Hamza Altakroury, Loann Mahdar-Recorbet, Alizée Poli, David Servais, Julien Lambert, Mathias Béjean, Denis Abraham
description: BackgroundThe healthcare market is undergoing rapid transformation, requiring the integration of user needs from the earliest stages of product and service design. Living Labs are emerging as a model for the co-creation and evaluation of user-centered innovations. In this work, we developed a Health Concept Maturity Levels grid and questionnaire to assess the maturity of health concepts.

title: Random forest can accurately predict the technique failure of peritoneal dialysis associated peritonitis patients
creator: Zhiyun Zang, Qijiang Xu, Xueli Zhou, Niya Ma, Li Pu, Yi Tang, Zi Li
description: InstructionsPeritoneal dialysis associated peritonitis (PDAP) is a major cause of technique failure in peritoneal dialysis (PD) patients. The purpose of this study is to construct risk prediction models by multiple machine learning (ML) algorithms and select the best one to predict technique failure in PDAP patients accurately.

title: Ultrasensitive SERS detection via hydrodynamic focusing coupled with electric field induced migration
creator: Monika Poonia, Zachary D. Schultz
description: Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) offers a powerful platform for ultrasensitive molecular detection, yet its performance is often limited by inefficient analyte transport to plasmonic hotspots. In this work, we present a hybrid microfluidic-SERS detection platform that integrates hydrodynamic focusing and electric field-induced migration to overcome diffusion limitations and enhance molecular delivery to the sensing interface.

title: Comparing SARS-CoV-2 infections in the US Military Health System and national data: opportunities for future pandemic surveillance
creator: Megan Clare Craig-Kuhn, Laveta Stewart, Erica Sercy, Caryn Stern, Brock Graham, Amber Michel, Edward Parmelee, Stacy Shackelford, Simon Pollett, Timothy Burgess, David R. Tribble
description: BackgroundThe Military Health System offers geographically distributed SARS-CoV-2 incidence estimates to support critical national pandemic surveillance, but this has not been previously assessed. The objective was to identify confirmed, probable, and possible SARS-CoV-2 infections with laboratory and clinical evidence and compare cumulative incidence to the general United States population.

title: Real‐world implementation and acceptability of HPV self‐sampling in routine cervical screening: Addressing methodological considerations
creator: Saara Kyllönen, Satu Saloranta, Saara Kares, Anu Mustila, Karolina Louvanto
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). We agree that the absence of a contemporaneous randomized control group limits causal inference regarding the comparative effect of self‐sampling on screening participation. However, the FALCON study aimed not to compare invitation strategies or estimate the effectiveness of self‐sampling versus standard care, but rather to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of introducing self‐sampling within an established population‐based screening program under routine conditions. Previous studies have shown that direct mailing of self‐sample kits is more effective in increasing screening participation.

title: Latent profiles of resilience and associations with quality of life in head and neck cancer patients undergoing proton and heavy ion therapy
creator: Lina Xiang, Hongwei Wan, Yu Zhu, Shuman Wang, Mimi Zheng
description: BackgroundPsychological resilience is the most important psychological protection factor for cancer patients in the face of tumors and treatment. However, few studies have performed meaningful latent profile analyses of resilience to identify unobserved subgroups of head and neck cancer patients.

title: Study on the path of combining music and digital health technology to promote the health of older adult groups
creator: Chuang Ma, Bo Hu, Shixue Chen, Xiaomei Ma
description: ObjectiveAs the global population ages, non-pharmacological interventions such as personalized music therapy show promise for wellbeing in older adults. We propose the Fusion-Attentive Temporal Network (FAT-Net). This dual-stream model processes minute level heart-rate and music on/off data alongside daily summary features to predict a composite health score.

title: Comparative analysis of select 3D human mesenchymal stromal cell-derived spheroid models for adipogenic differentiation
creator: Bianca Vezzani, Elisa Tamburini, Anna Terenziani, Nadia Ilaria Oliverio, Simonetta Croci, Alessandro Bartolomucci
description: In vitro modelling of adipose tissue (AT) commonly employs 2D systems, which do not fully capture the complexity of AT, lacking cell-cell interactions and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling. Despite the innovations in 3D culture systems offering physiologically relevant AT platforms, the field lacks consensus and cross-protocol method comparison.

title: Forest therapy using virtual reality in the older population: a systematic review
creator: Davide Clemente, Luciano Romano, Elena Zamboni, Giuseppe Carrus, Angelo Panno
description: IntroductionAs life expectancy increases, more attention needs to be paid to their mental and physical condition. Many older patients are also bedridden, which makes some treatments, like in vivo exposure to natural environments, more difficult to be applied. This study aimed to systematically review articles that include interventions combining virtual reality and forest environment, targeting a sample of older people.

title: Early childhood malnutrition impairs adult resting brain function using near-infrared spectroscopy
creator: Kassandra Roger, Phetsamone Vannasing, Julie Tremblay, Maria L. Bringas Vega, Cyralene P. Bryce, Arielle Rabinowitz, Pedro Antonio Valdes-Sosa, Janina R. Galler, Anne Gallagher
description: IntroductionEarly childhood malnutrition affects 200+ million children under 5 years of age worldwide and is associated with persistent cognitive, behavioral and psychiatric impairments in adulthood. However, very few studies have investigated the long-term effects of childhood protein-energy malnutrition (PEM) on brain function using a functional hemodynamic brain imaging technique.

title: Lactylation and exercise: A molecular link to disease alleviation (Review)
creator: Jian Wang, Lei Wu
description: Regular physical activity improves physical capacity and overall health by enhancing cardiopulmonary function and muscle strength, reducing stress, and improving psychological well-being and quality of life. Despite these known benefits, the molecular mechanisms that underlie these effects remain incompletely understood. Lactylation, a modification wherein lactate molecules form ester bonds with proteins, induces functional changes in these proteins.

title: Anti-inflammatory effects of Banisteriopsis caapi and beta-carbolines in neuronal cells: potential implications for neuro-COVID
creator: Laura Seixas Bianco, Tiago Nicoliche, Nelson Francisco Corrêa-Neto, Rafael Lanaro, Ariadiny L. Caetano, Carla Maximo Prado, Rodrigo Portes Ureshino, Iolanda de Fátima Lopes Calvo Tibério, Renato Fraga Righetti, Roberta Sessa Stilhano, Alessandra Linardi
description: BackgroundNeuroinflammation plays a central role in neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s, along with depression, anxiety, and infectious diseases including COVID-19. Harmine and harmaline, β-carboline alkaloids from Banisteriopsis caapi, exhibit immunomodulatory, anti-inflammatory, and neuroprotective properties. In this study, we aimed not only to investigate the anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective effects of β-carbolines and B.

title: Comparing movement-related cortical potential between real and simulated movement tasks from an ecological validity perspective
creator: Kakuya Ogahara, Akira Nakashima, Tomotaka Suzuki, Kenichi Sugawara, Naoshin Yoshida, Arihiro Hatta, Takefumi Moriuchi, Toshio Higashi
description: IntroductionConcerns regarding the ecological validity of movement-related cortical potential (MRCP) experimental tasks that are related to motor learning have recently been growing. Therefore, we compared MRCP during real movement task (RMT) and simulated movement task (SMT) from an ecological validity perspective.MethodsThe participants performed both RMT and SMT, and MRCP were measured using electroencephalogram (EEG).

title: SLC12A7 serves as a prognostic and immunotherapeutic biomarker identified by multi-omics analysis
creator: Haoran Qu, Jun Sun, Guohao Wang, Shuhong Ding, Xiaoming Li
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundSolute carrier family 12 member 7 (SLC12A7) is a membrane transporter implicated in ion homeostasis. Recent studies have suggested its aberrant expression in various malignancies; however, its functional roles and clinical relevance across cancers remain poorly defined.

title: Temporary screw epiphysiodesis for correction of ankle valgus in children with multiple hereditary exostoses
creator: Sarah I Schmitz, Moritz Broja, Anne Andresen, Alexandra Doerell, Luisa Saegebrecht, Martin Rupprecht, Kiril Mladenov, Alexander S Spiro
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). AimsIn patients with multiple hereditary exostosis (MHE), the development of ankle valgus is a common deformity. The aim of this study was to evaluate whether temporary screw epiphysiodesis of the medial distal tibia leads to a correction of the deformity and to provide further information on the timing and duration of the operative treatment, considering sex-specific differences and a concomitant fibular shortening or relevant exostoses.MethodsThe data of 37 MHE patients with a total of 68 ankles, and 35 patients with idiopathic ankle

title: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing enhances diagnosis of fungal infections in kidney transplant recipients: a retrospective study
creator: Qin Wang, Handong Ding, Zongyao Hao, Guiyi Liao
description: BackgroundAlthough fungal infections are relatively rare, they have low detection rates and high mortality rates. The value of metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) in kidney transplant patients with fungal infections remains insufficiently explored, especially regarding diagnosis and antimicrobial stewardship.MethodsFrom September 2021 to August 2023, 234 kidney transplant patients were enrolled, with detailed data collected on 66 patients suspected of fungal infections.

title: Nuclear Wrinkles Result From Geometric Adaptations to Cellular and Nuclear Morphological Changes in Epithelial Cells
creator: Le Minh Khoa, Yohei Kono, Takeshi Shimi, Hiroshi Kimura
description: Mechanical cues influence cell behavior and fate and are frequently accompanied by changes in nuclear shape; however, how epithelial nuclei accommodate such deformations remains incompletely understood. In this article, we investigated the formation and regulation of nuclear wrinkles (NWs), inward folds of the nuclear envelope, in human epithelial cells. Using quantitative confocal imaging in 2.

title: Autonomic neurotransmission in cardiovascular regulation and pathophysiology
creator: Fahimeh Varzideh, Stanislovas S. Jankauskas, Pasquale Mone, Urna Kansakar, Gaetano Santulli
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The autonomic nervous system (ANS) is a central regulator of cardiovascular function, coordinating involuntary control of heart rate, vascular tone, and blood pressure through its sympathetic (SNS) and parasympathetic (PNS) subdivisions. The SNS mediates the “fight or flight” response via catecholamines, increasing heart rate, contractility, and vasoconstriction, whereas the PNS promotes restorative processes through acetylcholine, decreasing heart rate and enhancing vasodilation. Nitric oxide further modulates vascular tone and autonomic balance, serving as a key neuromodulator.

title: The molecular landscape of nodular fasciitis: novel USP6 fusions, genomic stability, and an exploratory clinicopathological model – a 20‐year retrospective study
creator: Kristijan Skok, Maximilian T Buchwald, Maria Anna Smolle, Theresa Godschachner, Andreas Leithner, Christian Viertler, Bernadette Liegl‐Atzwanger
description: Nodular fasciitis (NF) is a benign myofibroblastic neoplasm characterized by rapid growth and recurrent USP6 rearrangements. Despite its benign nature, NF may exhibit worrisome histologic or clinical features that mimic sarcoma, posing diagnostic challenges. The relationship between molecular diversity and morphologic heterogeneity remains incompletely understood.

title: Early vaccination of laying hens with the live bivalent Salmonella vaccine AviPro™ Salmonella DUO results in successful vaccine uptake and increased gut colonization
creator: Shaun A. Cawthraw, Adam Goddard, Tom Huby, Isaac Ring, Louise Chiverton, Doris Mueller-Doblies
description: IntroductionSalmonella Enteritidis and S. Typhimurium are the two most clinically important zoonotic Salmonella serovars and vaccination of breeding and laying hens affords effective Salmonella control. The use of live vaccines has proven beneficial for a number of reasons, including ease of application, protection from the first day of life onwards and initiation of a strong local immune response.

title: Acute trazodone treatment ameliorates behavioral abnormalities and improves subsequent short‐term memory in a lipopolysaccharide‐induced mouse model of acute brain dysfunction
creator: Hideki Matsuoka, Leo Gotoh, Hikaru Hori
description: AimSystemic inflammation‐associated acute brain dysfunction, typified by delirium, is linked to later cognitive impairment. Although trazodone is used clinically for delirium‐related symptoms, its effects on subsequent cognition remain unclear. We examined whether acute‐phase trazodone treatment influences behavioral abnormalities, later cognitive outcomes, and inflammatory/glial‐related changes in an lipopolysaccharide (LPS)‐induced mouse model.MethodsAdult male C57BL/6J mice received saline or LPS (3.0 mg/kg, intraperitoneally).

title: Adrenergic signaling during parasitic infections
creator: Patrycja Gardias, Piotr Bąska
description: Adrenergic signaling plays a critical role in modulating immune and physiological responses during parasitic infections. Catecholamines such as adrenaline and noradrenaline interact with adrenergic receptors (ARs) to regulate immune cell activity, inflammation, and systemic processes. This review highlights the involvement of adrenergic pathways in infections caused by protozoa (Trypanosoma spp., Plasmodium spp., Toxoplasma gondii, Leishmania spp.

title: A randomized controlled trial on the application of a chronic disease management platform based on digital health technology combined with an innovative model of intelligent management for hypertension in patients with hypertension
creator: Keli Liu, Benshan Niu, Xiaoyi Zhang, Lingyuan Zhang, Yuexia Gao, Juying Lu
description: ImportanceDigital health technology (DHT)-based chronic disease management platforms combined with smart hypertension models may improve patient self-management.ObjectiveTo compare the effect of Nantong University Affiliated Hospital's DHT platform combined with an intelligent hypertension management model (providing education, follow-up, evaluation) vs. traditional offline management on patients' systolic blood pressure (SBP).

title: Predicting the Risk of Proteinuria Based on Blood Plasma Fourier‐Transform Infrared Spectroscopy and Machine Learning Algorithms From Pregnant Women and Newborns
creator: Camila Lopes Ferreira, Sara Maria Santos Dias da Silva, Luma Martins Aleixo de Oliveira, Vitórya Carvalho Pádua de Magalhães, Simone Lima Silva, Sheila Cavalca Cortelli, Rodrigo Augusto Silva, Jaqueline Maria Brandão Rizzato, Marcelo Saito Nogueira, Luís Felipe Das Chagas e Silva de Carvalho
description: Proteinuria, defined by an abnormally elevated concentration of proteins in the urine, serves as a critical biomarker for the early detection and diagnosis of preeclampsia. Elevated proteinuria levels adversely affect both maternal and foetal health, increasing the risk of preterm birth and low birth weight.

title: A plasma proteomic signature of the actin-coagulation axis accurately predicts progression to active tuberculosis
creator: Peng Lu, Weiwei Gao, Xiaoyan Ding, Jingjing Pan, Hui Ding, Qiao Liu, Limei Zhu, Xiang Huo
description: BackgroundPredicting progression to active tuberculosis (TB) is a critical unmet need, as current immunological tests only detect infection but cannot discriminate those who will develop active disease. A reliable prognostic biomarker could enable targeted preventive therapy and transform TB control strategies.

title: Effects of probiotics on joint homeostasis and osteoarthritis: Development of microbe-gut-cartilage axis-on-a-chip
creator: Jun Liu, Ning Zhang, Yiting Lei, Xiaoshuai Wang, Xiang Zhang, Wei Huang, Changhai Ding, Denghui Xie, Jun Yu, Rocky S. Tuan, Zhong Alan Li
description: Although emerging evidence implicates gut microbiome-cartilage cross-talk in the pathogenesis of osteoarthritis (OA), the most common joint disease, studying this microbe-gut-joint axis remains challenging due to limitations of animal models and conventional in vitro systems. Here, we report a microbe-gut-cartilage axis-on-a-chip (MGCAoC) that recreates tissue-specific microenvironments with oxygen gradients and physiological fluid shear.

title: Insights into temporal and spatial dynamics of short association fiber formation in the human fetal brain
creator: Bo Li, Željka Krsnik, Lana Pierotich, Ivica Kostović, Simon K. Warfield, P. Ellen Grant, Davood Karimi
description: Short association fibers (SAFs) form the local scaffold of cortical connectivity and support early functional specialization. However, their development before birth remains largely unknown. Using fetal diffusion magnetic resonance imaging from the Developing Human Connectome Project and histology from the Zagreb Collection of human brains, we present an in utero reconstruction of SAF pathways in the human brain.

title: Tolerance to occasional frosts during germination in Chilean Altiplano quinoa (Chenopodium quinoa Willd.) cultivars
creator: Ignacio Delfino Yurin, José Delatorre-Herrera, Juan Pablo Rodríguez, José Pablo Delatorre-Castillo, Isabel Sepúlveda-Soto, Cristopher Low-Pfeng
description: Quinoa (Chenopodium quinoa Willd.) is increasingly cultivated in marginal environments; however, early-season frosts pose a major constraint to successful stand establishment. Despite evidence of genotypic variation in cold tolerance, the effects of short, occasional frost events occurring at specific germination stages remain poorly understood.

title: Influence of plant species, mycorrhizal inoculant, and soil phosphorus level on arbuscular mycorrhizal communities in onion and carrot roots
creator: Umbrin Ilyas, Lindsey J. du Toit, Mehrdad Hajibabaei, Mary Ruth McDonald
description: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) are ancient and ecologically important symbionts that colonize plant roots. These symbionts assist in the uptake of water and nutrients, particularly phosphorus, from the soil. This important role has led to the development of AMF inoculants for use as biofertilizers in agriculture.

title: Detection rate of PSMA PET MRI (18 F-Flotufolastat) at the onset of biochemical recurrence following radical prostatectomy
creator: Herbert Lepor, Hebert Alberto Vargas, Majlinda Tafa, James S Wysock, Wei Phin Tan, Madhur Nayan
description: PurposeThe optimal timing to obtain the initial PET-PSMA imaging study when disease recurrence is suspected following RP is controversial.Methods24 subjects with new onset of BCR following RP were enrolled. The initial PET MRI (study #1) was performed within 2 months of signing informed consent. Salvage treatment was offered only if site(s) of disease recurrence were identified by study #1.

title: Arthroscopic Palmaris Longus Tendon Bridging for Augmented Repair of Bursal‐Sided Partial Thickness Rotator Cuff Tears
creator: Guo Zheng, ZunHan Liu, JunYan Yu, MoLong Chen, YunJiao Wang, ChenKe Zhang, Lin Ma
description: The management of bursal‐sided partial‐thickness rotator cuff tears remains controversial. Both transtendon repair preserving the residual tendon and conversion to full‐thickness repair yield satisfactory outcomes. However, treating bursal‐sided partial‐thickness rotator cuff tears with significant tendon retraction because of delamination is challenging. Direct repair of the retracted bursal layer under high tension results in a high retear rate.

title: Meta-analysis of plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria interaction with host plants: implications for drought stress response gene expression
creator: Roberta Ferrante, Chiara Campagni, Cristina Vettori, Alice Checcucci, Cesare Garosi, Donatella Paffetti
description: IntroductionThe molecular and physiological mechanisms activated in plants during drought stress tolerance are regulated by several key genes with both metabolic and regulatory roles. Studies focusing on crop gene expression following plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) inoculation may help understand which bioinoculant is closely related to the induction of abiotic stress responses.

title: Experience of using anti-CD 20 therapies in multiple sclerosis patients in Kenya
creator: Nyambane Eunice, Tejal Patel, Jacqueline Mavuti, Juzar Hooker, Dilraj Sokhi
description: ObjectiveThe objective of the study was to evaluate the safety and efficacy of ocrelizumab (OCR) and rituximab (RTX) in multiple sclerosis.MethodsThis was a retrospective single-centre study. Ocrelizumab- and rituximab-treated patients were identified through the multiple sclerosis (MS) registry maintained at Aga Khan University Hospital Nairobi (AKUHN), Kenya.

title: Characterizing molecular and behavioral changes arising from ROMK potassium channel deficiency in the cerebellum
creator: Jacopo Agrimi, Aidan J. Dunphy, Justin C. Zhong, Wenxi Zhang, Naeem Sbaiti, Daniel R. Turner, Lucia Bernardele, D. Brian Foster, Brian O’Rourke, Nazareno Paolocci, Kyriakos N. Papanicolaou
description: The cerebellum is critically involved in both motor coordination and affective regulation, and growing evidence suggests that cerebellar dysfunction contributes to neuropsychiatric disorders. While much attention has focused on synaptic signaling and calcium homeostasis, the role of potassium channels in cerebellar function remains relatively understudied.

title: Citron kinase activity controls alternative splicing events that drive prostate cancer growth
creator: Chitra Rawat, Nidhi Singh, Ujjwal R. Dahiya, Qiang Hu, Sarah Ng, Dingxiao Zhang, Shaun R. Stauffer, Amina Zoubeidi, Eva Corey, Jesse McKenney, Christopher J. Weight, Samuel C. Haywood, Song Liu, Tao Liu, Hannelore V. Heemers
description: Prostate cancer (CaP) remains a major cause of cancer death in men, underscoring the need for mechanistically novel therapies. We previously identified the action of the mitotic kinase citron (CIT) kinase as a key driver of CaP progression and promising therapeutic target, but selective CIT inhibitors are not available.

title: Integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomics combined with whole-exome sequencing reveal key hub genes and epithelial heterogeneity in bladder cancer
creator: Lin Li, Qianyue Li, Jiaxin Liu, Yifan Wang, Yanjun Ma, Lei Tang, Yawei Zhao
description: BackgroundBladder cancer (BLCA) is a malignant tumor originating from the urothelial lining, characterized by a complex tumor microenvironment (TME) and heterogeneous tumor mutation burden (TMB). Cancer-associated epithelial cells (EpiCs) exhibit substantial heterogeneity during BLCA initiation and progression. Therefore, elucidating the diversity and functional states of EpiCs is essential for improving future diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

title: Efficacy and safety of PARP inhibitors monotherapy or combination therapy with anti-angiogenics in ovarian cancer: a network meta-analysis
creator: Yuan Liu, Tongtong Ren, Xinchun Wang, Yuqi Wang, Lisha Tang, Wenjiang Cao
description: BackgroundThe incidence of ovarian cancer ranks second only to cervical cancer and uterine cancer, but its mortality rate is the highest. Searching for effective and safe PARP inhibitors - antiangiogenic drugs combined treatment for ovarian cancer is a new approach.

title: Interdisciplinary fetal-neonatal neurology training applies neural exposome perspectives to neurology principles and practice
creator: Mark S. Scher
description: An interdisciplinary fetal-neonatal neurology (FNN) program over the first 1,000 days teaches perspectives of the neural exposome that are applicable across the life span. This curriculum strengthens neonatal neurocritical care, pediatric, and adult neurology training objectives. Teaching at maternal-pediatric hospital centers optimally merges reproductive, pregnancy, and pediatric approaches to healthcare.

title: Hydration channel engineering in Tröger’s base-POP membranes for mono/multivalent cation and anion discrimination
creator: Haopan Sun, Ning Gan, Baolong Wu, Chenglin Liu, Yan Jin, Yuzhu Sun, Jianguo Yu, Zhaoliang Cui, Yuqing Lin, Hideto Matsuyama, Young Moo Lee
description: Sustainable recovery of critical resources from complex aqueous streams is constrained by membranes that fail to combine rapid ion transport with precise mono/multivalent discrimination. Here, we report Tröger’s base-derived porous organic polymer (POP) membranes with rigid, covalently crosslinked microporous frameworks that stabilize angstrom-scale transport channels while suppressing hydration-induced swelling.

title: Surficial carbonates in mantle plume sources revealed by magnesium isotopes
creator: Ze-Zhou Wang, Fang-Zhen Teng, Matthew G. Jackson, Catherine Chauvel, Cédric Hamelin
description: Deep recycling of surficial carbonates into the mantle may play a critical role in shaping Earth’s long-term habitability, yet its contribution to the deep mantle carbon budget remains uncertain. Magnesium isotopes provide a promising tracer for addressing this issue, because of the uniquely light isotopic signatures of sedimentary carbonates.

title: Color‐Bar Bedsheet: Affordable Assistive Tool for Dix‐Hallpike Test in Primary Care
creator: Suwicha Kaewsiri Isaradisaikul, Pitchayanan Namung, Sanathorn Chowsilpa
description: BackgroundBenign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) is a common cause of vertigo encountered in general practice. The definitive diagnosis relies on the Dix‐Hallpike test (DHT), which remains underperformed in primary care due to limited training and unfamiliarity among general practitioners.AimTo develop the color‐bar bedsheet as a simple visual positioning guide for DHT and demonstrate its usefulness.

title: Professional grief experience and psychological detachment of pregnant emergency nurses after the death of pediatric patients: a longitudinal mixed-methods study
creator: Man Zhang, Dongyang Wang
description: BackgroundEmergency nurses are frequently exposed to pediatric death events, which trigger professional grief and impair psychological detachment. Pregnant nurses, due to heightened physiological and psychological sensitivity, may exhibit unique emotional responses, yet evidence remains scarce.MethodsThis study adopted a longitudinal mixed-methods design, combining semi-structured qualitative interviews with quantitative assessment using the DASS-21 scale at three time points.

title: Identifying key performance tests in differentiating starting and substitute women Rugby players: a discriminant function analysis
creator: Cebrail Gençoğlu, Cemre Can Akkaya, Erkan Tortu, Abdulkadir Birol, Osman Ateş, Abdullah Demirli, İzzet İnce, Salih Çabuk, Süleyman Ulupınar, Serhat Özbay
description: Aim/backgroundThis study aims to identify the performance tests with the highest discriminatory power for distinguishing between starting and substitute female rugby players.MethodA total of 24 female rugby players, who regularly participated in official league competitions and engaged in structured training on a regular basis, voluntarily participated in this study. The players were divided into two groups: starting players (age: 25.

title: Solution-processed organic infrared photodetectors operating beyond 1.4 μm for sensitive environmental monitoring
creator: Yifei Geng, Tengfei Li, Zhenzhen Zhang, Huiqing Hou, Yuze Lin
description: Photon energies in the short-wave infrared (SWIR) beyond 1.4 μm enable access to vibrational-overtone signatures of O–H, C–H, and N–H bonds in pollutants and waste materials, offering an imaging-based nondestructive approach for environmental monitoring. However, current SWIR imaging technologies rely on costly epitaxial semiconductors incompatible with monolithic integration, limiting consumer-grade deployment.

title: Case report: Immune pressure on hematopoietic stem cells can drastically expand glycosylphosphatidylinositol-deficient clones in paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria
creator: Naoki Shingai, Hiroki Mizumaki, Yuho Najima, Yuta Yamada, Dung Cao Tran, Kyoko Haraguchi, Takashi Toya, Yoshiki Okuyama, Noriko Doki, Yasuhito Nannya, Seishi Ogawa, Shinji Nakao
description: IntroductionParoxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH) is a rare hematological disease characterized by intravascular hemolysis, thrombosis, and bone marrow (BM) failure. Although PNH is caused by excessive proliferation of hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) clones with loss of function mutations in phosphatidylinositol N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase subunit A (PIGA) genes, what drives PNH clones to expand remains elusive.

title: Analysis of ASMs and male infertility using the FDA adverse event reporting system (FAERS)
creator: Kunyang An, Jingyu Xu, Yujia Xi, Xinfang Cao, Jingqi Wang, Xiaoqin Hu, Xuezhi Liang
description: IntroductionAntiseizure medications (ASMs) are the cornerstone of epilepsy treatment, but their potential reproductive toxicity may impact male fertility. Globally, approximately 15% of couples are affected by infertility, with male factors accounting for 50%. This study aimed to analyze the association between ASMs and male infertility using the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS).

title: Surface temperatures drive strong seasonality in urban reactive carbon emissions
creator: Michael P. Vermeuel, Dylan B. Millet, Róisín Commane, Timothy J. Griffis, Trey A. Maddaleno, Emily B. Franklin, Katelyn L. Richard, Rose K. Rossell, Jeff Peischl, Delphine K. Farmer
description: Urban air quality is affected by diverse volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and prior studies reveal a need to understand their seasonal sources. We combine high-resolution mass spectrometry with eddy covariance to quantify VOC fluxes from an urban/suburban New York site during summer and winter.

title: Exploring antibiotic stewardship interventions within a One Health context: a scoping review
creator: Léo Delpy, Chloe Clifford Astbury, Olivier Kambere Kavulikirwa, Mouhamadou Moustapha Sow, Sandrina Vandenput, Cécile Aenishaenslin, Arne Ruckert, Ria Benko, Mary Wiktorowicz, Tarra L. Penney, A. M. Viens, Marion Bordier
description: Antibiotic resistance (ABR) presents a global threat to human health, animal health, and the environment. While ABR is a natural phenomenon, the overuse and misuse of antibiotics in human health, animal health, and food production is a major driver of ABR.

title: Cloud platform to improve efficiency and coverage of asynchronous multidisciplinary team meetings for patients with digestive tract cancer
creator: Yu Zhang, Jie Li, Min Liao, Yalan Yang, Gang He, Zuhong Zhou, Gang Feng, Feng Gao, Lihua Liu, Xiaojing Xue, Zhongli Liu, Xiaoyan Wang, Qiuling Shi, Xaiobo Du
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundMultidisciplinary team (MDT) meetings are the gold standard of cancer treatment. However, the limited participation of multiple medical experts and the low frequency of MDT meetings reduce the efficiency and coverage rate of MDTs. Herein, we retrospectively report the results of an asynchronous MDT based on a cloud platform (cMDT) to improve the efficiency and coverage rate of MDT meetings for digestive tract cancer.MethodsThe participants and cMDT processes associated with digestive tract cancer were discussed using a cloud platform.

title: Rise and spread of lead-silver metallurgy deciphered from peatland archives
creator: Hugo Delile, André-Marie Dendievel, Laura Chollet, Iscia Codjo, Adrien Barra, Janne Blichert-Toft
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). How mining has shaped long-term economic and political landscapes across Europe and the Mediterranean remains poorly understood, largely because archaeological evidence is spatially fragmented and ore sources are difficult to trace from atmospheric lead (Pb) records. Here, we compile Pb isotope data from environmental archives and introduce the Environmental Match Intensity Index (EMII), a metric applied to peat records to track Pb–silver (Ag) ore-supply patterns and relative changes in the integrated mining-related atmospheric Pb signal over six millennia.

title: Designing integrated early-phase protocols to reduce substantial modifications, including considerations for patient cohorts – a multi-stakeholder consensus view for a practical approach in Germany
creator: R. Schultz-Heienbrok, S. Baumann, R. Böhm, A. Bonertz, K. Breithaupt-Groegler, U. Buckpesch-Heberer, M. Coenen, K. Erb-Zohar, N. Faisst, G. Grass, J. Höchel, A. Kovar, A. Muehlenbroich, J. Rengelshausen, C. Riedel, B. Schug, T. Sudhop, A. Warnke, B. Ziegele
description: • Frequent substantial modifications for initiating new trial parts slow down development and reduce transparency.• Combining healthy volunteers and patients in a single early-phase trial raises safety, feasibility, and regulatory concerns.• A multi-stakeholder consensus in Germany identified regulatory pathways to enable seamless transitions within integrated protocols for non-ATMP (advanced therapy medicinal product), non-oncology trials.

title: The cellular triumvirate: fibroblasts entangled in the crosstalk between cancer cells and immune cells
creator: Adel Fergatova, Nesrine I. Affara
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This review article will focus on subpopulations of fibroblasts that get reprogrammed by tumor cells into cancer-associated fibroblasts. Throughout this article, we will discuss the intricate interactions between fibroblasts, immune cells, and tumor cells. Unravelling complex intercellular crosstalk will pave the way for new insights into cellular mechanisms underlying the reprogramming of the local tumor immune microenvironment and propose novel immunotherapy strategies that might have potential in harnessing and modulating immune system responses.

title: Optimizing DUS testing for Chimonanthus praecox using feature selection based on a genetic algorithm
creator: Ting Zhu, Yaoyao Feng, Xiaoxuan Dong, Ximeng Yang, Bin Liu, Puying Yuan, Xingrong Song, Shanxiong Chen, Shunzhao Sui
description: Chimonanthus praecox is a famous traditional flower in China with high ornamental value. It has numerous varieties, yet its classification is highly disorganized. The distinctness, uniformity, and stability (DUS) test enables the classification and nomenclature of various species; thus, it can be used to classify the Chimonanthus varieties.

title: Strategic intelligence and organizational ambidexterity for strengthening health system performance in a public healthcare network
creator: Mohammad Khalilzadeh, Zahra Rajaei, Sayyid Ali Banihashemi
description: This study examines the association between strategic intelligence (SI) and organizational ambidexterity (OA) in a public healthcare network, with attention to the two dimensions of OA: exploratory innovation (innovation, experimentation, and adaptation) and exploitative innovation (refinement, efficiency, and execution of existing competencies). OA was modeled as a latent variable indicated by the exploratory and exploitative innovation dimension scores.

title: Anti-PLA2R positivity does not exclude malignancy in membranous nephropathy: lessons from the course after tumor treatment
creator: Saide Elif Güllülü Boz, Abdülmecit Yıldız
description: increased before the cancer is found. We report three anti-PLA2R-positive patients whose courses after tumor treatment differed (Table 1). Table 1:Clinical characteristics, treatment, and outcomes of the three patients.CharacteristicPatient 1Patient 2Patient 3Age/sex53/male67/male61/malePresentation: proteinuria; anti-PLA2R9 g/day; 106 RU/ml (760 at relapse)11 g/day; 839 RU/ml7.

title: Soft gripper for small fruits harvesting and pick and place operations
creator: Eduardo Navas, Redmond R. Shamshiri, Volker Dworak, Cornelia Weltzien, Roemi Fernández
description: Agriculture 4.0 presents several challenges for the automation of various operations, including the fundamental task of harvesting. One of the crucial aspects in the automatic harvesting of high value crops is the grip and detachment of delicate fruits without spoiling them or interfering with the environment.

title: An artificial intelligence-assisted PARP-1-targeted PET imaging agent [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-FZPF: From bench to clinic
creator: Mengjing Ji, Chunjuan Jiang, Yue Xi, Shuai Liu, Simin He, Jianping Zhang, Xiaoping Xu, Zhongyi Yang, Xiangwei Wang, Shaoli Song
description: Considering that clinical data for 68Ga-labeled poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP)-targeted probes have not yet been reported and integrated artificial intelligence (AI) workflows for radiotracer development are still lacking, to support radiotracer development and clinical translation, we constructed an AI-assisted multi-stage prioritization workflow and then synthesized two 68Ga-labeled PARP-1-targeted probes, validating their performance through in vitro, in vivo, and clinical evaluations.

title: Myosin inhibitor therapy in Fabry cardiomyopathy with dynamic left ventricular outflow obstruction
creator: Kolja Lau, Nils Petri, Peter Nordbeck
description: A 56-year-old woman with presumed hypertrophic cardiomyopathy was diagnosed with Fabry disease (GLA: p.Glu358del) and a concomitant PLN variant. Imaging revealed advanced Fabry cardiomyopathy with dynamic LVOT obstruction. Despite optimized medical and enzyme replacement therapy, symptoms progressed (NYHA-class III) with a marked increase in LVOT gradient. Mavacamten was initiated and uptitrated under echocardiographic monitoring.

title: Impact of the hypoxic microenvironment on spermatogonial stem cells in culture
creator: A. S. Gille, M. Givelet, D. Pehlic, C. Lapoujade, B. Lassalle, V. Barroca, A. P. Bemelmans, D. Borderie, D. Moison, G. Livera, L. R. Gauthier, F. D. Boussin, N. Thiounn, I. Allemand, C. Peyssonnaux, J. P. Wolf, V. Barraud-Lange, L. Riou, P. Fouchet
description: The stem cell niche plays a crucial role in the decision to either self-renew or differentiate. Recent observations lead to the hypothesis that O2 supply by blood and local O2 tension could be key components of the testicular niche of spermatogonial stem cells (SSCs). In this study, we investigated the impact of different hypoxic conditions (3.5%, 1%, and 0.

title: Loss of the Asn333 high-mannose N-glycan impairs ACP3 folding and drives disease-associated dysfunction
creator: Noriyoshi Manabe, Kazuyoshi Itoh, Shiho Ohno, Ayumi Miura, Aika Miyata, Sora Yashima, Sachiko Komatsu, Tsutomu Fujimura, Hisatoshi Hanamatsu, Jun-ichi Furukawa, Kiyohiko Angata, Akira Togayachi, Kiyoko F. Aoki-Kinoshita, Yoshihiro Akimoto, Tadashi Kaname, Shoko Nishihara, Yoshiki Yamaguchi
description: SummaryMissense mutations disrupting N-glycosylation motifs can perturb protein folding and trafficking, yet the site-specific contributions of individual N-glycans to proteostasis remain poorly defined. Here, we delineated the functional hierarchy of three N-glycosylation sites in human prostatic acid phosphatase (ACP3). Glycoproteomic analysis showed that Asn94 and Asn220 carry predominantly complex-type N-glycans, whereas Asn333 is enriched in high-mannose structures.

title: Building climate-resilient health systems for the displaced: health information systems and the statistical invisibility of climate-related mobility in sub-Saharan Africa
creator: R Leone, Y Ouattara, L Tognaccini, W Ricciardi, MR Gualano
description: BackgroundClimate change is reshaping the populations health systems serve, yet health information systems (HIS) remain blind to one of the fastest-growing groups: people displaced or migrating in the context of climate change. In sub-Saharan Africa this mobility is now counted at scale, but mobility data and health data systems have developed as parallel infrastructures blind to each other's populations.

title: Plasma proteomic analysis identified potential therapeutic targets for pulmonary arterial hypertension
creator: Song Hu, Yuqi Xie, Jiang-Shan Tan, Ting-Ting Guo, Shengsong Zhu, Zhennan Lin, Jian Zhang, Lu Hua
description: SummaryPulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains a progressive disease with high mortality. By integrating the UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project (49,272 participants, 337 incident cases) with drug-target Mendelian randomization, we identified 398 plasma proteins associated with incident PAH and 19 with potential causal relevance, 15 of which are druggable.

title: Alternative splicing of a species- and skeletal muscle-specific microexon diversifies the menu of clathrin heavy chains in mice and rats
creator: R. Eric Blue, Adam J. Black, Jessica L. Cote, Sumaya A. Addish, Archishma Kavalipati, Scott P. Lyons, J. Ashley Ezzell, Steven C. Bremmer, Daniel Dominguez, Jimena Giudice
description: SummaryLittle is known about alternative splicing of microexons in most tissues other than the brain. Humans have two homologous clathrin heavy chains. Ubiquitously expressed, CLTC drives clathrin-mediated endocytosis. Highly expressed in skeletal muscles, CLTCL1 instead regulates glucose metabolism. Previously, we reported that a conserved microexon (exon 31) in the CLTC gene is alternatively spliced during striated muscle development.

title: The chylomicron saga: time to focus on postprandial metabolism
creator: Alejandro Gugliucci
description: Since statins have had such tremendous therapeutic success over the last three decades, the field of atherosclerosis has become somewhat LDL-centric, dismissing the relevance of triglycerides (TG), particularly chylomicrons, in atherogenesis. Nonetheless, 50% of patients who take statins are at risk of developing atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and are unable to achieve their goal LDL-C levels.

title: The role of community engagement toward ensuring healthy lives: a case study of COVID-19 management in two Ghanaian municipalities
creator: Matilda Aberese-Ako, Phidelia Theresa Doegah, Lebene Kpodo, Wisdom Ebelin, Mawulom Kuatewo, Atubiga Alobit Baba, Atsu Godsway Kpordorlor, Samuel Yaw Lissah, Anthony Kolsabilik Kuug, Evelyn Ansah
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionCommunity engagement is one of the important requirements for strengthening health delivery in communities in a bid to achieve sustainable development goal 3, target 3.3 (SDG 3.3). The World Health Organization has strongly encouraged the use the five levels of community engagement, which are informing, consulting, planning, collaborating, and empowering communities in order to build resilience and to enable them contribute to the fight against diseases and for the uptake of health interventions.

title: What is moving where? Infants’ visual attention to dynamic objects may assist with processing of spatial relations
creator: Jihye Choi, Youjeong Park
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionA central question in infant spatial cognition concerns how infants form abstract categories of spatial relations such as support (on) and containment (in). Prior work suggests two different possibilities regarding the role of attention to objects in infants’ formation of abstract categories of spatial relations: Attention to objects may compete with (and thus hamper) attention to the spatial relations between them, or assist with encoding of the spatial relation information.

title: Better understanding the phenotypic effects of drugs through shared targets in genetic disease networks
creator: Elena Díaz-Santiago, Aurelio A. Moya-García, Jesús Pérez-García, Raquel Yahyaoui, Christine Orengo, Florencio Pazos, James R. Perkins, Juan A. G. Ranea
description: IntroductionMost drugs fail during development and there is a clear and unmet need for approaches to better understand mechanistically how drugs exert both their intended and adverse effects. Gaining traction in this field is the use of disease data linking genes with pathological phenotypes and combining this with drugtarget interaction data.

title: Pirfenidone regulates seizures through the HMGB1/TLR4 axis to improve cognitive functions and modulate oxidative stress and neurotransmitters in PTZ-induced kindling in mice
creator: Mansi Dahalia, Sparsh Gupta, Haya Majid, Divya Vohora, Nidhi
description: BackgroundEpilepsy is a neurological disorder characterized by recurrent seizures due to abnormal electrical activity in the brain. Pirfenidone, an antifibrotic drug, has shown anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties in various disease models, including neurological conditions. However, its potential anticonvulsant effects have not been thoroughly explored.

title: Nomogram prediction of overall survival in breast cancer patients post-surgery: integrating SEER database and multi-center evidence from China
creator: Yufen Zheng, Yuan Yuan, Minya Jin, Chunlong Wu
description: PurposeOverall survival (OS) in postoperative breast cancer patients is influenced by various clinicopathological features. Current prognostic methods, such as the 7th edition of AJCC staging, have limitations. This study aims to construct and validate a comprehensive nomogram integrating multiple clinicopathological features to predict OS more accurately in breast cancer patients.MethodsWe identified 60,445 .

title: Feasibility and potential benefits of daily online adaptive radiotherapy for head and neck cancer without margin reduction using an RTT-only workflow
creator: A.M. Lindegaard, K. Håkansson, A. Appelt, M. Bernsdorf, A.B. Gothelf, T.R.B. Jensen, A. Mohammad, C.A. Kristensen, I. Vogelius, J. Friborg
description: IntroductionOnline adaptive radiotherapy (oART) may improve head and neck cancer (HNC) treatment, where anatomical changes during radiotherapy (RT) are common. However, oART is resource-intensive and clinical data are limited. We conducted a prospective feasibility trial implementating an RT technologist (RTT)-led workflow to evaluate dosimetric outcomes, workflow strategies, and intrafractional motion in daily oART.

title: Delayed radiographic diagnosis of distal femoral metastases in breast cancer: A case report from Cocody University Teaching Hospital (Côte d’ivoire)
creator: Yaya Coulibaly, You Nina Carmelle Kpami, Bamba Aboubakar, Hodonou Fourier, Nzima Kevin Kollo, Meité Novanly, Jean Jacques Goua, Abidou Kawélé Coulibaly
description: Bone metastases represent a frequent complication of breast cancer, affecting more than one third of patients. Delayed investigation of persistent focal bone pain in a breast cancer patient can lead to serious consequences. We report a case of delayed radiographic diagnosis of distal femur metastases in a breast cancer patient, where the initial standard X-ray was normal.

title: Neural activity responsiveness by maturation of inhibition underlying critical period plasticity
creator: Ibuki Matsumoto, Sou Nobukawa, Takashi Kanamaru, Yusuke Sakemi, Nina Sviridova, Tomoki Kurikawa, Nobuhiko Wagatsuma, Kazuyuki Aihara
description: IntroductionNeural circuits develop during critical periods (CPs) and exhibit heightened plasticity to adapt to the surrounding environment. Accumulating evidence indicates that the maturation of inhibitory circuits, such as gamma-aminobutyric acid and parvalbumin-positive interneurons, plays a crucial role in CPs and contributes to generating gamma oscillations.

title: Assessment of compression forces in a digitally modified short leg cast for pressure injury risk monitoring in healthy children
creator: Matia Iva Vrankovic, Simon Annaheim, Jana Willibald, Jan Lieber, Hubertus J. A. van Hedel, Anna-Barbara Schlüer, René M. Rossi, Andreas Meyer-Heim
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionCasting is an essential treatment for neuro-orthopedic conditions in children with cognitive, sensory, and communicational disabilities. However, a main side-effect is the development of pressure injuries resulting in additional (wound) therapies and prolongation of the hospital stay. The primary aim of our study was to investigate the potential of objective pressure measurements in casts to assess the risk for pressure injury development.MethodsFive pediatric healthy participants were included in this study.

title: Metagenomic insights into the development of microbial communities of straw and leaf composts
creator: Anastasiia K. Kimeklis, Grigory V. Gladkov, Olga V. Orlova, Tatiana O. Lisina, Alexey M. Afonin, Tatiana S. Aksenova, Arina A. Kichko, Alla L. Lapidus, Evgeny V. Abakumov, Evgeny E. Andronov
description: IntroductionSoil microbiome is a major source of physiologically active microorganisms, which can be potentially mobilized by adding various nutrients. To study this process, a long-term experiment was conducted on the decomposition of oat straw and leaf litter using soil as a microbial inoculum.

title: Navigating the brain: the role of exosomal shuttles in precision therapeutics
creator: Shaheera Fatima, Ariba Qaiser, Saadia Andleeb, Asraf Hussain Hashmi, Sobia Manzoor
description: Brain diseases have become one of the leading roots of mortality and disability worldwide, contributing a significant part of the disease burden on healthcare systems. The blood-brain barrier (BBB) is a primary physical and biological obstacle that allows only small molecules to pass through it.

title: Pathological complete response to neoadjuvant therapy with serplulimab and chemotherapy in stage IIIB small cell lung cancer: a case report and literature review
creator: Ting Mei, Ting Wang, Chuanfen Lei, Dan Jiang, Qinghua Zhou
description: Chemotherapy combined with immunotherapy has significantly improved survival in patients with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC), and neoadjuvant immunotherapy combined with chemotherapy has emerged as the standard treatment for those with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the potential benefits of surgery following neoadjuvant immunotherapy combined with chemotherapy in locally advanced SCLC remain unclear.

title: Exploration of the hypoglycemic mechanism of Fuzhuan brick tea based on integrating global metabolomics and network pharmacology analysis
creator: Xingliang Xiang, Shanqin You, Zhaoxiang Zeng, Jinlin Xu, Yuqi Lin, Yukun Liu, Lijun Zhang, Rongzeng Huang, Chengwu Song, Shuna Jin
description: Introduction: Fuzhuan brick tea (FBT) is a worldwide popular beverage which has the appreciable potential in regulating glycometabolism. However, the reports on the hypoglycemic mechanism of FBT remain limited. Methods: In this study, the hypoglycemic effect of FBT was evaluated in a pharmacological experiment based on Kunming mice.

title: Rat Calvarial Defect Models in Bone Regeneration Research: A Narrative Review of Critical Size and Micro-Computed Tomography Outcome Reporting
creator: Klemen Aleš Pilih, Uroš Kovačič
description: Simple SummaryRat skull defects are widely used to test methods intended to improve bone healing, but researchers need reliable information about which defects heal naturally and how healing should be measured. We reviewed published studies of untreated rat skull defects, focusing on defect size and three-dimensional X-ray imaging used to measure new bone.

title: Diverse clinical manifestations and prognosis in a couple’s mercury poisoning caused by skin-lightening creams: two case reports and literature review
creator: Huixia Ji, Ye Chen, Dandan Liu, Tongzhou Zhou, Yuhua Tang
description: Skin exposure to mercury-containing creams occurs most commonly in young and middle-aged women and, in a few cases, in men. This article presents the symptoms and prognosis of a couple who developed mercury poisoning after cosmetic use of similar duration and dosage.

title: A Two-Tier Patient-Based Real-Time Quality Control Program Integrating K-Means Department Stratification and Inter-Instrument Ratios Improves Detection of Small Systematic Errors in Creatinine Testing
creator: Xuemei Wei, Ziqing Jiang, Jingzhu Nan, Zefeng Yan, Zhu Lin, Rong Li, Jie Feng, Yanhong Gao
description: Background/Objectives: Patient-based real-time quality control (PBRTQC) complements traditional internal quality control. This study validates a ratio-based PBRTQC integrating department clustering with inter-instrument ratio monitoring. Methods: Creatinine data (384,730 cases, 2025) from three measuring systems (A, B, C) were analyzed; conventional PBRTQC on unstratified Instrument A data served as comparator.

title: A Computational Analysis of Diagnostic Misrecognition in Co-Occurring Primary Headache Disorders: Prime Encoding of ICHD3 Criteria Reveals 72 Potentially Spurious Diagnoses
creator: Pengfei Zhang
description: Background/Objectives: In clinical circumstances with more than one headache disorder, misrecognition can occur if each headache disorder is not separately and individually evaluated. For example, consider the case of a patient with baseline tension-type headaches lasting hours who now develops cluster headaches with nausea. Merging the characteristics of both disorders may yield the illusion of migraine.

title: Analysis of the influencing factors in the long-term survival of esophageal cancer
creator: Wang Rui, Congcong Li, Qin Da, Yang Yue, Li Jing, Guo Ruirui, Cui Youbin, Tianyu Lu, Bo Li
description: BackgroundTo analyze the prognosis and diagnostic value of relevant hematological indexes on the survival status of patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma after radical surgery.MethodsThis study included 206 patients with esophageal cancer who underwent surgical R0 resection. The data, including the basic information, preoperative blood routine, albumin, fibrinogen, surgery-related information, postoperative pathology, and overall survival, of the patients were compared.

title: Restricted effects of androgens on glucocorticoid signaling in the mouse prefrontal cortex and midbrain
creator: Jorge Miguel Amaya, Hetty C. M. Sips, Eva M. G. Viho, Jan Kroon, Onno C. Meijer
description: Glucocorticoids are key executors of the physiological response to stress. Previous studies in mice showed that the androgen receptor (AR) influenced the transcriptional outcome of glucocorticoid treatment in white and brown adipocytes and in the liver. In the brain, we observed that chronic hypercorticism induced changes in gene expression that tended to be more pronounced in male mice.

title: Perception of obesity among adults as health-related priority in Saudi Arabia. A cross-sectional survey among Riyadh primary healthcare centers attendees
creator: Mohammed Saad Alqahtani, Badr F. Al-Khateeb, Musab Umair, Raed Aldahash, Awad Alshahrani, Ashraf El-Metwally
description: ObjectiveTo explore perception of obesity as a health priority among primary healthcare attendees in Riyadh.DesignA cross-sectional study was conducted between March and July 2023.SiteForty-eight randomly selected primary health care (PHC) centers in Riyadh.ParticipantsA total of 14,239 adults were recruited through multistage cluster sampling and administered an electronic questionnaire.

title: Refusal of treatment among HER2-positive breast cancer patients in China: a retrospective analysis
creator: Xin Wang, Zhiwei Lian, Qiyou Wu, Fan Wu, Gong Zhang, Jian Liu, Chuanben Chen, Jing Sun
description: BackgroundThere is a need to update the understanding of treatment refusal among cancer patients in China, taking into account recent developments. This study investigated how public insurance coverage of the first breast cancer targeted therapy contributed to the changes in treatment refusal among HER2-positive breast cancer patients in China.

title: Rapid protamine evolution suppresses meiotic drive in Drosophila
creator: Ching-Ho Chang, Aida Flor A. de la Cruz, Hung-Yu Lai, Isabel Mejia Natividad, Alex Noyola, Elian Angelo Magsino Abellanosa, Nicolas D. Lee, Harmit S. Malik
description: Many animal species replace histones with protamines during spermatogenesis. Although essential for sperm function, protamines evolve rapidly for reasons that remain unknown. Using in vivo gene replacement, we examined the causes and consequences of the rapid evolution of Mst77F, a protamine essential for male fertility in Drosophila melanogaster (D. melanogaster).

title: Advances in plant electrostimulation: from cellular and molecular mechanisms to agricultural applications
creator: Yu Dong, Ye Tian, Jingxuan Pan, Weiwen Qiu, Xinyu Zhou, Yangyang Xie, Mei Liu, Juntao Wang, Fengru Gao, Liang Jin, Dan Wei, Yanhong Wang, Qiang Xiao
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Electrical stimulation is an emerging physical strategy for agricultural regulation that applies electric fields or currents with defined parameters to modulate plant growth, development, and rhizosphere processes. Owing to its residue-free nature, environmental compatibility, and high controllability, electrical stimulation has considerable potential to improve crop yield and quality while enhancing tolerance to abiotic and biotic stresses, making it increasingly relevant to sustainable agriculture.

title: The role of Ashwagandha in modulating gut parameters in dogs—a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial
creator: Kala Kumar Bharani, Ashok Kumar Devarasetti, Rajendar Bobbili, Amit Khurana, Donga Durga Veera Hanuman, Roupesh Gudepu, Swapna Guda
description: IntroductionThis study explored the role of Withania somnifera/Ashwagandha root extract (ARE) on important gut–microbiome parameters in healthy geriatric dogs. We hypothesized that ARE might promote a healthy gut by its adaptogenic and anti-inflammatory effects and improve vital parameters for healthy ageing.MethodsA randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial was conducted in Telangana, India. Twelve healthy geriatric Beagle dogs aged 12–15 years were enrolled.

title: Synbiotic supplementation leads to gut microbiome communities with functional capacity linked to better brain white matter development in preterm infants
creator: Anna Voulgari-Kokota, Els Janson, Ineke Heikamp de Jong, Jan Knol, Ruurd van Elburg, Niek E. van der Aa, Lisa M. Hortensius, Jeroen Dudink, Caroline G. M. de Theije, Lidewij Schipper, Marta Kozior, Monique van de Lagemaat, Floris Groenendaal, Frank van Bel, Annemieke Wildt-Grootendorst, Sandra Drost
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Preterm birth, a major cause of brain injury, is often linked to dysregulated gut microbiome development. This association underscores microbial metabolic function as a modifiable target to support neurodevelopment. In this secondary analysis of data derived from a randomized controlled trial (Trial Registration: ISRCTN96620855), we tested whether daily nutritional supplementation with Bifidobacterium breve M-16V, short- and long-chain oligosaccharides, and L-glutamine could steer the gut microbiome of very and extremely preterm infants toward communities that support brain maturation.

title: The effects of an acute Tai Chi on emotional memory and prefrontal cortex activation: a fNIRS study
creator: Haining Wang, Yujiang Guo, Hao Fan, Zhihao Chen, Shumeng Liu, Longfei Zhao, Yonggang Shi
description: ObjectiveAcute exercise has the potential to influence emotional memory and cortical hemodynamics, but the specific effects depend on the type of exercise. This study aimed to determine whether acute Tai Chi practice enhances emotional memory and prefrontal cortex activation compared to cycling and a control condition.

title: Highlight selection of radiochemistry and radiopharmacy developments by editorial board
creator: Sarah Spreckelmeyer, Jean DaSilva, Clemens Decristoforo, Robert H. Mach, Jan Passchier, Giuseppe Carlucci, Adriano Duatti, Bart T. Cornelissen, Antonia Denkova, Jeroen Hendrikx, Yann Seimbille, Xing Yang, Hongmei Jia, Ming-Rong Zhang, Lars Perk, Peter Caravan, Jan Rijn Zeevaart, Julien Leenhardt, Ju
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThe Editorial Board of EJNMMI Radiopharmacy and Chemistry releases a biannual highlight commentary to update the readership on trends in the field of radiopharmaceutical development and application of radiopharmaceuticals.Main BodyThis selection of highlights provides commentary on 23 different topics selected by each co-authoring Editorial Board member addressing a variety of aspects ranging from novel radiochemistry, proof-of-concepts, preclinical and early clinical studies using novel radiopharmaceuticals.ConclusionTrends in radiochemistry and radiopharmacy are highlighted.

title: Technical considerations in interpreting rapid transfusion through a 4.2-Fr Broviac catheter
creator: Keiichiro Mizuno
description: vide useful practical information for anesthesiologists managing sudden major bleeding in small children. To facilitate appropriate interpretation of this experience, several technical details would merit clarification. The authors report that a single-lumen 4.2-Fr Broviac catheter was connected to an SL One rapid infusion device and that the infusion rate was intermittently increased to 150 mL/min.

title: Uric acid to albumin ratio is a novel predictive marker for all-cause and cardiovascular death in diabetic patients: a prospective cohort study
creator: Shengnan Chen, Ming Zhang, Shouye Hu, Xiaolong Shao, Lin Liu, Zhi Yang, Kai Nan
description: BackgroundDiabetes is one of the leading causes of death with an increasing prevalence worldwide. Diabetes-related premature mortality is largely preventable and reversible if identified and managed early. Accordingly, we intend to investigate the predictive value of uric acid to albumin ratio (UAR) for all-cause and cardiovascular death in diabetic patients.

title: A20 Inhibits IFN‐γ Signaling in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Cells by Binding to STAT1, Compromising Anti‐Tumor Immunity
creator: Yanlei Dong, Jing Yi, Ruoxuan Yang, Yingyue Wang, Zelong Ma, Hong Yuan, Meichen Song, Ying Xiao, Chun Guo, Jianing Wang, Xiaoyan Wang, Faliang Zhu, Lining Zhang, Yuchen Fan, Yongyu Shi
description: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has demonstrated efficacy in clinical cancer therapy; however, a significant proportion of cancer patients do not respond to ICB. One contributing factor to this lack of response is the impairment of IFN‐γ signaling within cancer cells. A20 acts as a negative regulator of IFN‐γ signaling.

title: Organization of Interventional Neuroradiology in Belgium: results of a national survey
creator: Adam Dmytriw, Iman Kiani, Luciana Koren, Hamza Salim, Thomas Lefebvre, Matea Prenc, Chiara Brechbühl, Denis Brisbois, Frans Vanden Bergh, Maurits Voormolen, Stephanie Elens, Luca Scarcia, Vivek Yedavalli, Louis Deprez, Yacine Boudiba, Adrien Guenego
description: ObjectivesTo provide a comprehensive national overview of interventional neuroradiology (INR) in Belgium through a structured survey conducted under the auspices of the Belgian Society for Interventional and Therapeutic Neuroradiology (BSITN).Materials and methodsAn anonymized online survey was distributed by email through the BSITN to all known active interventional neuroradiologists.

title: Positive Peer Groups Support Preschoolers’ Word Learning
creator: Elise Breitfeld, Courtney N. Snoberger, Jenny R. Saffran
description: Children learn language from their social partners, and differences in the behavior of these social partners can influence language learning outcomes. The literature largely focuses on adult caregivers; however, there is less clarity regarding the extent to which the social behavior of peers might also impact children's language learning.

title: Interest of luspatercept in treatment of anemia in lower-risk of myelodysplastic syndrome anemia: a single center study of 26 patients
creator: A Elalaoui, C Girault, T Cluzeau
description: BackgroundMyelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) are heterogeneous clonal hematological disorders characterized by ineffective hematopoiesis resulting in peripheral cytopenias. Luspatercept, an erythroid maturation agent, represents a novel therapeutic option for the management of anemia associated with low-risk MDS, particularly in patients with ring sideroblasts and/or SF3B1 mutations.

title: Olanzapine for the Prevention and Treatment of ICU Delirium: Protocol for a Systematic Review With Meta‐Analysis
creator: Benedikte Liebetrau, Andreas Ruhvald Madsen, Sören Möller, Markus Harboe Olsen, Sebastian Wiberg, Simon Mølstrøm
description: BackgroundIntensive care unit (ICU) delirium is a multifactorial acute brain dysfunction associated with prolonged hospitalization, increased morbidity and mortality, and higher healthcare costs. Despite these substantial negative impacts of delirium, the optimal prevention and treatment strategies are unclear. Olanzapine, an atypical antipsychotic drug, is commonly used for delirium management.

title: An osteogenesis mimicking biomineralized bone adhesive for rapid skeletal regeneration
creator: Yuqi Liu, Hao Luo, Bin Guo, Xiangming Chen, Martin J. Stoddart, Wen Chen, Xucheng Yang, Yong Zhu, Jianxi Zhu
description: Osteogenesis is a crucial process in bone injury repair where osteoblasts mineralize collagen to form new bone at the fracture site. For effective bone regeneration in comminuted fractures, it is essential to develop an osteogenic bone adhesive that can be applied at the time of fixation to temporarily immobilize fragmented bone pieces.

title: Better to Be Lucky Than Good: How Clinicians and Patients Frame Medical Outcomes
creator: Eliza Brown, Stefan Timmermans
description: Notions of good or bad luck sit uncomfortably in contemporary medical practice defined by efforts to control life through biomedical knowledge and skilled expertise. Yet, talk about luck is common in healthcare to explain medical courses of action. Framing medical results as fortunate or unfortunate bridges the gap between predicted probabilities and variation in individual cases without undermining scientific neutrality.

title: Endovascular magnetic filters for removing excess chemotherapeutic drugs from blood flow using dimensionless scaling laws
creator: Won‐Seok Heo, Steven W Hetts, Vitaliy L Rayz
description: Intra‐arterial chemotherapy (IAC) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is limited by the escape of chemotherapeutic agents into systemic circulation, causing severe side effects such as heart failure. This study aims to develop and optimize endovascular magnetic filtration devices to enhance IAC efficacy, by targeted removal of excess drug‐coated ultrasmall superparamagnetic iron oxide (USPIO) particles from circulation.

title: Mapping the Tissue Architecture and Endothelial‐PEC Network in HAML Using Single‐Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics
creator: Xinyang Liu, Yang Guo, Xuehong Tie, Yu Liu, Fuyu Li, Jingkai Liu, Xiaohang Sun, Jiajun Zhao, Feng Geng, Yingjian Liang
description: Hepatic angiomyolipoma (HAML) is a rare variant of perivascular epithelioid cell neoplasms (PEComas). Unlike its more common renal angiomyolipoma (RAML), the unique spatial microenvironment of HAML and its specific progression mechanisms remain poorly characterized. Here, we integrated single‐nucleus RNA‐sequencing and spatial transcriptomics from three sporadic HAML cases. We mapped functionally heterogeneous PEComas subpopulations and their localized tissue niches.

title: Short Term Effects of Football Headers on Reaction Time and Symptomology in Males and Females
creator: Yusef Mohammed, Rithik Rajan, Benjamin Tari, Flaminia Ronca
description: IntroductionFootball heading is a form of repetitive head impact linked to cognitive decline. Although the English Football‐Association have implemented heading restrictions, evidence guiding sex‐specific protocols remains limited. This study explored the acute effects of a standardized heading drill on reaction time (RT) and concussion symptomology and whether sex moderates these outcomes.Methods51 participants (25 females; mean age 22.8 ± 4.

title: Gel Immersion Endoscopic Mucosal Resection With Submucosal Injection for Superficial Esophageal Squamous Neoplasms (With Video)
creator: Takahiro Uda, Yuji Urabe, Tomoyuki Gurita, Yoshiki Hatsushika, Satoshi Masuda, Yukiko Sako, Takeo Nakamura, Yuki Kamigaichi, Takeshi Takasago, Hidenori Tanaka, Akiyoshi Tsuboi, Ken Yamashita, Yuichi Hiyama, Yoshihiro Kishida, Hidehiko Takigawa, Akira Ishikawa, Toshio Kuwai, Shinji Mii, Shiro Oka
description: ObjectivesGel immersion can provide a stable immersion environment during endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR). However, its application in superficial esophageal squamous lesions remains limited. In this study, we evaluated a gel immersion EMR (GI‐EMR) technique in which submucosal injection was intentionally performed before snaring for selected small superficial esophageal squamous lesions.

title: The physiology of lived experiences: A hole in the heart and the dive that found it
creator: James E Clark
description: forced hiatus had been its own particular kind of suffering. The dive had been months in the planning and felt, in the way that only truly absorbing things can feel during periods of enforced constriction, like a retrieval of something essential.

title: Sudden unexpected death in epilepsy: An Italian expert consensus statement on risk, mechanisms, prevention, and therapeutic strategies
creator: Vincenzo Belcastro, Fedele Dono, Giovanni Falcicchio, Lorenzo Gigli, Angela La Neve, Sara Matricardi, Barbara Mostacci, Angelo Pascarella, Leandro Pecchia, Emilio Russo, Pasquale Striano
description: ObjectiveSudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP) is a leading cause of premature mortality in people with epilepsy, particularly in those with tonic–clonic seizures (TCSs), developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs), and drug‐resistant epilepsy. Although awareness of SUDEP has increased, major uncertainties remain regarding individualized risk stratification, mechanistic interpretation, and implementation of preventive strategies in routine care.

title: Leiomyosarcoma of the Renal Vein That Enlarged Laterally While Preserving the Structure of the Renal Vein Lumen
creator: Naoki Tashiro, Yume Sakaki, Akito Fujinaga, Takahiro Nagai, Chie Onizuka, Shoichiro Mukai, Yoshiko Umekita, Yuichiro Sato, Toshiyuki Kamoto, Atsuro Sawada
description: IntroductionPrimary renal vein leiomyosarcoma is an extremely rare disease and the tumor often infiltrates the vessel wall. We report a case of primary renal vein leiomyosarcoma that enlarged while preserving the structure of the renal vein lumen.Case PresentationA 64‐year‐old woman underwent a computed tomography scan, which revealed a left renal hilar mass.

title: Efficacy and safety of ketamine for post‐traumatic stress disorder: A systematic review with narrative synthesis and consideration of military and veteran populations
creator: Mary Ivasyutyn, Saajan Bhakta
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Post‐traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a debilitating disorder with limited pharmaceutical treatment options. Ketamine, a noncompetitive N‐methyl‐d‐aspartate (NMDA) receptor antagonist with rapid‐onset effects, has emerged as a potential treatment, particularly for patients who do not respond to first‐line therapies. This systematic review synthesizes the current evidence on the effectiveness and safety of ketamine for PTSD, with a focus on military and veteran populations. Eligible studies included adults with PTSD, who evaluated ketamine or esketamine, and reported efficacy and safety outcomes.

title: Robust helicase loading mechanism underlies diverse architectures of bacterial replication origins
creator: Ryusei Yoshida, Kazutoshi Kasho, Shogo Ozaki, Tsutomu Katayama
description: The Escherichia coli chromosomal origin, oriC, contains a duplex-unwinding element (DUE) flanked by two clusters of the initiator DnaA-binding sites (DnaA boxes). ATP-DnaA oligomerizes to construct Left- and Right–DnaA subcomplexes on these clusters. These complexes coordinately promote DUE unwinding and DnaB helicase loading onto the unwound region for replication initiation.

title: Gut mycobiota dysbiosis and an emergent state of “co-dysbiosis” are associated with IgE sensitization in children with comorbid allergic rhinitis and constipation
creator: Haiying Liu, Liqing Liang, Chunyan Wang, Rongrong Luo, Qiuhua Luo, Congfu Huang
description: BackgroundThe comorbidity of allergic rhinitis (AR) and functional constipation (FC), termed ARFC, implies shared gut–immune pathways. Although bacterial dysbiosis has been implicated, the role of the gut mycobiota (fungal community) in this specific comorbidity remains unexplored.MethodsThis pilot case-control study characterized the gut mycobiota in 19 ARFC and 17 healthy control (HC) children aged 3–6 years using metagenomic sequencing.

title: Exploring the long-term use of ambroxol in Gaucher disease type 2: insights from two pediatric cases
creator: Charlotte Aries, Anja Köhn, Karolin Täuber, Cornelia Rudolph, Tobias Böttcher, Peter Bauer, Steffen Fischer, Nicole Muschol
description: Gaucher disease 2 (GD2) is a rare and rapidly progressive neuropathic lysosomal storage disorder with an average survival of 11–19 months. To date, no approved therapy is available, but the variant-dependent pharmacological chaperone ambroxol (ABX) has emerged as a promising off-label therapy.

title: Working with goals in youth mental health and substance use service: A review of current practice guidelines and recommendations
creator: Madison Nugent, Drew Burchell, Jill Chorney, Sharon Clark, Mick Cooper, Debbie Emberly, Danielle Impey, Jenna Jacob, Anam Khan, Jennifer Lane, Duncan Law, Rebecca Pillai Riddell, Lori Wozney
description: BackgroundWorking with goals is a critical yet often overlooked aspect of youth mental health and addictions care, with the potential to strengthen therapeutic relationships, support shared decision‐making, and improve outcomes. Despite its importance, there is no cohesive, equity‐centered guidance for working with youth on their goals.

title: Preoperative prediction of p53 overexpression in pituitary neuroendocrine tumors using MRI radiomics
creator: Longyuan Gu, Fanghua Zhou, Bin Wu, Jianpin Yang, Bin Li, Yuechao Fan, Peizhi Ji, Qian Wu, Fengda Li, Shuhong Mei
description: BackgroundThe expression of p53 protein is closely related to tumor prognosis and plays an important role in patients with pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs). However, its evaluation currently relies on postoperative histopathological analysis. Developing a non-invasive method to predict p53 overexpression preoperatively may help support clinical judgment and facilitate individualized treatment strategies.

title: Manipulating two-dimensional colloidal crystals using Laguerre–Gaussian beams
creator: Habib Moradi, Sjors Cornielje, Mathieu G. Baltussen, Berend van der Meer, Arran Curran, Roel P. A. Dullens
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Optical tweezing has firmly established itself as a versatile tool in fields ranging from biology to physics. In colloidal systems, optical tweezers are used to e.g. measure small forces or to generate optical potential energy landscapes. More complex and dynamic optical tweezing can be readily achieved using holographic wavefront engineering, though this is typically applied to only a handful of particles.

title: Targeting the blood–brain barrier with phytochemicals to attenuate vascular cognitive impairment: mechanisms and therapeutic potential across etiologies
creator: Zixiang Jin, Xianglong Zhai, Yingfei Bai, Jun Hu, Haolu Yu, Jiajia Sang, Minghua Wu, Feng Hao
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026).
