Vascular cognitive impairment (VCI), a cognitive disorder arising from cerebrovascular pathology, currently lacks effective targeted therapies. Dysfunction of the blood–brain barrier (BBB) represents a pivotal event in VCI pathogenesis, characterized by tight junction degradation, neuroinflammation, and oxidative stress. Phytochemicals—including polyphenols, flavonoids, and polysaccharides—demonstrate promising multi-target potential in ameliorating VCI by preserving BBB integrity, mitigating neuroinflammation and oxidative stress, exerting neuroprotective effects, and modulating the gut–brain axis.

title: Production and characterization of breadfruit flour (Artocarpus altilis): an alternative for the elaboration of flakes for children’s alimentation
creator: Cristina Arteaga, Ruth Arias-Gutiérrez, Adriana Rodríguez, Susana Heredia-Aguirre, Mónica Gozalbo, Jesús Blesa, Renata Alejandra Alvarado-Barba, Cristina Gabriela Ríos-Romero, Dayana Villavicencio Barriga, Jessenia Vásquez, Karol Egas, Elizabeth Quiroga-Torres, Alberto Bustillos, Tannia Valeria Carp
description: IntroductionBreadfruit (Artocarpus altilis) represents a promising tropical crop with high nutritional potential and application in functional food development. This study aimed to produce and characterize gluten-free breadfruit flour (BF) and evaluate its use at 20.7% substitution in corn-based extruded flakes.MethodsPhysiologically mature breadfruit was peeled, cored, cut into 20 × 20 × 10 mm pulp cubes, dipped in 0.

title: Elevated wzc mutation frequency promotes carbapenem resistance evolution in hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae ST23
creator: Tao Chen, Xueting Wang, Luying Xiong, Zhuoqi Lou, Ping Lu, Zhien He, Qi Ge, Haoxing Wu, Qixia Luo, Ping Shen, Yunbo Chen, Hui Ding, Yan Geng, Kunpeng Liang, Baorui Yang, Tingting Xiao, Wei Yu, Yonghong Xiao
description: The worldwide expansion of carbapenemase-producing hypervirulent K. pneumoniae (CP-hvKP) raises serious concerns about potentially untreatable invasive infections. ST23, an archetypal hvKP clone, has been highlighted due to the rising prevalence of carbapenem resistance largely driven by horizontal plasmid transfer. However, the factors facilitating carbapenemase acquisition in this lineage remained unclear.

title: Epidemioclinical profile and psychological experience of women consulting for primary infertility at the university hospital of angre about 160 cases
creator: Gbary-Lagaud Eléonore, Houphouet-Mwandji Carine, Kouakou-Kouraogo Ramata, Effoh Denis, Adjoby Roland
description: BackgroundInfertility is a real public health problem today with clinical and psychological aspects.ObjectiveTo improve the care and monitoring of women with primary infertility at the Angré University Hospital Center.Materials and methodThis was a cross-sectional and descriptive study over a period from January 1, 2021 to December 31, 2023.

title: dbcan-nf: a Nextflow pipeline for accurate CAZyme annotation in metagenomes
creator: Xinpeng Zhang, Haidong Yi, Jinfang Zheng, Yanbin Yin
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). MotivationCarbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes) are crucial for carbohydrate degradation in any ecological environment. However, CAZyme annotation is not easy in whole-genome shotgun (WGS) metagenomes, due to the lack of accurate, scalable, robust, and reproducible workflows.

title: Risk of Hepatocellular Carcinoma or Hepatic Decompensation Associated With Steatotic Liver Disease in People With and Without HIV
creator: Jessie Torgersen, Craig W Newcomb, Melissa Skanderson, Farah Kidwai-Khan, Dean M Carbonari, Janet P Tate, Catherine Mezzacappa, Emily J Cartwright, Debika Bhattacharya, Joseph K Lim, Jennifer C Price, Tamar H Taddei, Amy C Justice, Vincent Lo Re
description: BackgroundSteatotic liver disease (SLD) is highly prevalent in people with HIV (PWH), but factors influencing progression to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and hepatic decompensation (HD) remain unclear. It is unknown if the risk of these outcomes associated with SLD differs by HIV status.

title: Oral hygiene and caries experience in children with down syndrome and autism spectrum disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Nurzhamal Bainazarova, Kuralay Zhumabayeva, Gulzhan Yermukhanova, Yagut H. Hajiyeva, Kulmira Abdykerimova, Lyazat Orakbay, Farida Zhumageldiyeva, Indira Karibayeva, Nurlan Jainakbayev
description: IntroductionChildren with Down syndrome (DS) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) are at increased risk for oral health problems due to anatomical, behavioral, and socioeconomic factors. However, evidence on their caries experience and oral hygiene remains inconsistent. This study systematically reviewed and meta-analyzed case–control and cross-sectional studies comparing oral health indices in children with DS or ASD to neurotypical peers.

title: Exploring the determinants of non-suicidal self-injury among university students in Jordan: a cross-sectional study
creator: Hana Taha, Omar AlHaddad, Suhib Awamleh, Abdallah Shatnawi, Habib Yazan Belkhiria, Yahia Jarosheh, Taher Alhawamdeh, Ayman M. Wahbeh, Abdulla Al-Ani, Linus Jönsson
description: BackgroundDeliberate bodily harm without suicidal intent has become a growing concern among young adults and adolescents. This study aims to explore the determinants of non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) and its correlation with psychological distress and mobile phone addiction (MPA) among university students in Jordan.MethodsA quantitative cross-sectional study targeting university students in Jordan.

title: Metabolomics reveals the effects of different carbon sources on the quality and flavor profile of low-salt shrimp paste
creator: Ping Hong, Meiqi Gu, Chuanhai Tu, Wenxiong Zheng, Shanshan Shui, Jialiang Li, Soottawat Benjakul, Bin Zhang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). To elucidate carbon source effects on low-salt shrimp paste quality and bioactivity, glucose and glutinous rice flour were added pre-fermentation, physicochemical indicators monitored, and flavor and metabolic compound changes analyzed via combined HS-SPME-GC-MS and non-targeted metabolomics. The results showed that the addition of glucose and glutinous rice flour significantly enhanced the quality and flavor of low-salt shrimp paste following 12 days of fermentation. In total, 709 volatile compounds and 2089 non-volatile compounds were putatively annotated.

title: Active elements, effects, and working mechanisms of creative arts therapies in forensic psychiatric care: a realist review
creator: Susan van Hooren, Annemarie Abbing, Wim Waterink
description: IntroductionMental disorders are highly prevalent among forensic detainees, complicating treatment and increasing recidivism risk. Due to limited insight and communication difficulties, experiential approaches, such as creative arts therapies are needed. Creative arts therapies - including art therapy, music therapy, drama therapy, and dance/movement therapy - use psychotherapeutic engagement with art modalities to achieve therapeutic goals.

title: Indications, procedural standards, and training requirements for flexible nasolaryngoscopy in pulmonology – a Delphi study protocol✰
creator: Ajit Nair, Philip G Bardin, Paul Leong
description: Flexible nasolaryngoscopy (FNL) is a well-established, minimally invasive procedure for assessing the nasal passages, nasopharynx, and larynx. Its role in pulmonology is expanding, particularly for evaluating vocal cord dysfunction/inducible laryngeal obstruction, chronic cough, and other upper airway conditions relevant to the “united airways” model of care.

title: Prevalence of ties to industry-funded organizations among patient and consumer representatives on FDA advisory committees
creator: Genevieve P Kanter, Toni Mankowitz
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionFDA advisory committees are primarily composed of scientific experts, but also include a patient representative and a consumer representative providing public perspectives. Although the FDA has enacted policies to curb conflicts of interest common among its scientific members, it has paid less attention to potential conflicts arising from patient and consumer representatives who have ties to organizations financially supported by pharmaceutical companies.MethodsWe analyzed the prevalence of industry funding of advocacy organizations in which patient and consumer representatives were actively involved in the

title: Incidence, predictors, and clinical outcome of patients with undetected aneurysms on initial DSA after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage
creator: Carolin Albrecht, Laura Aberle, Ann-Kathrin Joerger, Hraq Sarkis, Arthur Wagner, Tobias Boeckh-Behrens, Julian Schwarting, Christian Maegerlein, Jan Kirschke, Bernhard Meyer, Maria Wostrack
description: IntroductionDigital subtraction angiography (DSA) is the gold standard for diagnosing ruptured intracranial aneurysms in aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH). However, aneurysms may occasionally remain undetected on initial DSA, potentially delaying treatment and increasing the risk of rebleeding. The primary aim was the incidence of aneurysms missed on initial DSA; secondary aims were characteristics, diagnostic yield and outcome.

title: An intrascrotal bioadhesive nanoplatform for sustained hydrogen delivery ameliorates age-associated testicular dysfunction
creator: Shu Liang, Jiawei Lv, Zun Li, Zheng Li, Jiachun Jiang, Shaoqing Yu, Cheng Wang, Xiongjun Wang, Lingyun Xiao, Guanzhen Yu
description: Testicular aging is characterized by progressive spermatogenic decline. Accumulating oxidative injury and insufficient metabolic support from Sertoli cells may contribute to this process. Although molecular hydrogen has shown antioxidant potential, its therapeutic application in reproductive aging is limited by rapid dissipation after administration. To overcome this barrier, we developed the localized hydrogen-releasing system S-H/B.

title: Pediatric RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection burden in G20 countries in 2023
creator: Yan Guo, Yonghan Luo, Jie Zhang
description: SummaryRespiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of childhood lower respiratory infections, but updated G20 burden estimates are lacking. Using the Global Burden of Disease 2023 database, we analyzed deaths and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) for RSV-associated lower respiratory infections in children aged 0–14 years across G20 members from 1990 to 2023, with stratification by sex, age, and country.

title: Burden and trend of cardiovascular diseases in youths aged 0–19 years in China, Asia, and the world, with forecasts to 2036: a systematic analysis of the global burden of disease study 2021
creator: Jin Yu, Shanshan Zhu, Zeping Wang, Yongyao Shen, Sheng Ji, Yongjin Guo, Liying Jiang
description: ObjectiveTo combat the harmful impacts of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) on public health, it is crucial to understand the epidemiologic features and disease burden. The study aims to identify the trends of CVDs burden in youths aged 0–19 years from 1990 to 2021 across the global, Asian, and Chinese contexts to inform more effective strategies and actions.

title: Gender disparities in childhood vaccination in India: exploring the role of son preference using NFHS-5 data
creator: Soumen Barik, Dewaram A. Nagdeve, Alex Motes Carvalho, Mayank Singh
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundEvery child has the fundamental human right to life-saving healthcare, including vaccination. Yet in India, this right is less accessible to girls in households shaped by son preference, a deep-rooted cultural bias that devalues girl children.

title: Multiomics Insights in Research of Nitric Oxide (NO) Donors in Plants upon Stress
creator: Anastasia Gurina, Anna Margarit, Anastasia Zhikhreva, Nadezhda Frolova, Andrej Frolov
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). It is known that the progressive climate changes and environmental pollution prevalent all over the world lead to increasingly frequent and prolonged episodes of stress, and it challenges plants to adapt to changing adverse conditions. Given the significant crop losses caused by challenging environments, protecting plants from the destructive effects of these factors has become one of the most pressing challenges in modern agricultural biology and plant physiology.

title: Which Clinical, Radiological, Inflammatory, and Lesion-Related Characteristics Are Associated with Early Neurological Decompensation After Intracranial Mass Lesion Surgery?
creator: Fatma Betül Saylak, Burak Bahadır
description: Background: Early neurological decompensation is a clinically relevant concern following intracranial surgery, but factors associated with this early outcome remain incompletely characterized. This study evaluated factors associated with neurological decompensation within 48 h after surgery. Methods: This retrospective, single-center study included 301 surgical episodes involving intracranial mass lesions.

title: When are large language models medical devices? Navigating the MDR and AI Act for healthcare applications
creator: Jessica D Workum, Sade J Krijgsman, Ildiko Vajda, R M Van Stokkum, Jan van de Brand, Diederik Gommers, Ari Ercole, Michel van Genderen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The flexibility of generative artificial intelligence (AI), and specifically large language models (LLMs), holds promise to transform healthcare by offering new tools to improve patient care and enhance clinician efficiency. However, this flexibility introduces new challenges, as LLM applications might inadvertently be used in ways that do not align with the intended purpose of the manufacturer, raising patient safety concerns and liability issues.

title: Acceptability and use determinants of digital health technologies for HIV services: a qualitative study of emergency care patients in Nairobi, Kenya
creator: Joshua Smith-Sreen, Benson Timothy, Beatrice Ngila, John Wamutitu Maina, Sankei Pirirei, John Kinuthia, David Bukusi, Harriet Waweru, Rose Bosire, Carey Farquhar, Michael J. Mello, Adam R. Aluisio
description: Digital health technologies (DHTs) represent a promising strategy to improve access to HTS (HIV testing services), particularly among underserved higher-risk populations often missed by current programming, including young adults under 25 years. In 2017, Kenya's Ministry of Health introduced BeSure™, a DHT providing information on HIV, self-testing, and facility geo-location.

title: Protocol for mapping sister chromatid exchanges and structural variations using sci-L3-strand-seq
creator: Shiyang He, Peter Chovanec, Yi Yin
description: SummaryUnderstanding spontaneous genome rearrangement requires mapping both error-free and mutational repair outcomes, particularly error-free sister chromatid exchanges (SCEs). Here, we present a sci-L3-Strand-seq protocol capturing SCEs across thousands of single cells from 12–16 independent samples in one experiment. We detail steps for cell labeling, sample banking, nucleosome depletion, in situ combinatorial barcoding, enrichment of BrdU-labeled cells, and nascent strand ablation.

title: Effect of bedside comprehensive ability training on teaching and training in operating room
creator: Yi Zhong, Wenjun Bu, Qifan Li, Lili Zheng
description: AimTo assess the effect of bedside comprehensive ability training on teaching and training in operating room.MethodsOne hundred and thirty female clinical nurses who joined our hospital from January 2019 to December 2021 were randomly assigned to a control group and an observation group. The control group adopted problem-based learning (PBL), while the observation group adopted bedside comprehensive ability training.

title: A proteome-based classification of paediatric adrenocortical tumours links functional tumour states to clinical outcome and therapeutic vulnerabilities
creator: Rainer Claus, Andreas Metousis, Victoria E. Fincke, Marina Kunstreich, Stefan A. Wudy, Eva Jüttner, Joern Pons-Kühnemann, Christian Vokuhl, Michael C. Frühwald, Christoph Röcken, Lisa Schweizer, Pascal D. Johann, Antje Redlich, Matthias Mann, Michaela Kuhlen
description: SummaryBackgroundPaediatric adrenocortical tumours (pACT) are rare endocrine neoplasms characterised by marked biological heterogeneity and variable clinical behaviour. Current risk stratification relies largely on histopathology and clinical staging, which incompletely capture underlying tumour biology. We aimed to define proteome-based subtypes of pACT and evaluate their biological, clinical, and therapeutic relevance.

title: Dynamic shifts in pathogen ecology of catheter-related bloodstream infections: temporal trends and ward-specific risk landscapes
creator: Shanfeng Li, Jia Zuo, Yu Xie, Weifen Liu, Hanjie Yi
description: Catheter-related bloodstream infections (CRBSIs) represent a severe clinical complication with high mortality and pose a significant public health challenge due to increasing multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs). This study aimed to systematically analyze the epidemiology, pathogen distribution, and independent predictors of 28-day mortality in CRBSI to support early risk warning and precise intervention.

title: Determining the Causal Effect of Neurotrophic Tropomyosin Receptor Kinase Gene Fusions on Survival Prognosis for Adult Patients With Advanced Cancers
creator: Emanuel Krebs, Nirupama Tamvada, Deirdre Weymann, Howard J Lim, Stephen Chia, Cheryl Ho, Dean A Regier
description: PurposeUncertainty about the prognostic significance of neurotrophic tropomyosin receptor kinase (NTRK) fusions complicates clinical decisions and interpretation of survival outcomes in oncology care. Drawing on the largest cohort of NTRK fusion–positive (NTRK+) patients, we establish the prognostic effect of NTRK fusions in adults with advanced cancers.

title: Minimal-actuation feather star–inspired soft swimmers for multimodal 3D maneuverability
creator: Haitao Qing, Yuanhang Zhu, Jiacheng Guo, Caizhi Zhou, Haoze Sun, Haibo Dong, Daniel Quinn, Jie Yin
description: Complex, three-dimensional (3D) motions typically require actuator arrays and complex control architectures. Here, we present a feather star–inspired soft robotic swimmer that uses only two pneumatic inputs to produce three distinct and switchable swimming modes: jellyfish-like pulsation, fishlike propulsion, and rotor-like reorientation.

title: Sensory receptor expansion and neural accommodation in butterfly color vision
creator: Ke Gao, Julia Ainsworth, Antoine Donati, Yunchong Zhao, Michelle Franc Ragsac, Cara Genduso, Zoie Andre, Andrew Tomlinson, Michael W. Perry
description: The evolution of complex brains required the incorporation of newly evolved neurons into existing circuits, yet the genetic and developmental mechanisms enabling their integration remain poorly understood. Butterflies expanded their color vision by adding a second R7 photoreceptor per ommatidium, a rare departure from the conserved insect eye ground plan.

title: Menstrual blood-derived mesenchymal stromal cell secretome modulates macrophage polarization in a preconditioning-dependent manner
creator: María Ángeles de Pedro, María Pulido, Ana María Marchena, Verónica Álvarez, Francisco Manuel González-Nuño, Witold Szymański, Johanna Pörschke, Silke Reinartz, Johannes Graumann, Elke Pogge von Strandmann, Francisco Miguel Sánchez-Margallo, María Gómez-Serrano, Esther López

This study studied the impact of secretomes from basal MenSCs (S-bMenSCs) and those preconditioned with IFNγ and TNFα (S-pMenSCs) on human monocytes and macrophages in vitro.MethodsS-MenSCs were used to assess their effects on three stages of monocyte-derived cell maturation: i. monocyte differentiation; ii.

creator: Jyoti Madhusoodanan
description: e to receive the vaccine, which protects against the painful rash caused by herpes zoster virus. Studies thus far don’t suggest a causal relationship between some vaccines and dementia, only an association. But the work has led researchers to examine how inflammation, and immunity in the body as a whole, can influence the brain over time. Image credit: Shutterstock/LIAL.

title: Influence of housing retaining materials on fracture resistance of zirconia-reinforced implant overdentures: an in vitro study
creator: Shradha Bhutoria, Thilak Shetty, Shobha J. Rodrigues, Umesh Y. Pai, Sharon Saldanha, Mahesh M, Ann Sales, Sandipan Mukherjee, Vignesh Kamath, Prashant Bajantri
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). AimTo evaluate the influence of zirconium oxide (ZrO₂) nanoparticle reinforcement and housing retaining material on the flexural performance of implant-supported overdenture acrylic resin bases.Materials and methodsThirty-six standardized bar-shaped heat-cured polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) specimens were fabricated in accordance with ISO 20795-1 and divided into six groups (n = 6) based on ZrO₂ nanoparticle concentration (0%, 3%, and 7% by weight) and housing retaining material (autopolymerising PMMA or UfiGel Hard).

title: Advances in Indocyanine Green Near-Infrared Fluorescence for Extrahepatic Biliary Identification in Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy for Acute Cholecystitis: A Narrative Review
creator: Zhihui Jin, Xusheng Yang, Yuntian Liu, Lei Song, Xuewen Chen, Yue Wang, Xiaoping Cheng, Lu Liang, Bihui Yao
description: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy, a minimally invasive procedure with rapid recovery, remains the standard surgical intervention for acute cholecystitis. Acute inflammation of the gallbladder can cause severe edema, dense adhesions, and anatomical distortion within Calot’s triangle, frequently obscuring tissue planes and increasing the risk of iatrogenic bile duct injury, a significant surgical complication.

title: Internet gaming disorder, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and learning in adults: a systematic review
creator: Xiaodeng Zhou, Juntao Chen, Jiahua Yao, Derek Tinyol Chui, Su-Kit Tang
description: The comorbidity between attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and Internet gaming Disorder (IGD) has attracted much attention. The aim of this systematic review was to explore the specific association between ADHD and IGD/GD Adult learning group. Through the literature search of MEDLINE, PUBMED and CINAHL, a total of 14 relevant studies were included.

title: Pan-European Training Program for Robotic Pancreatoduodenectomy (LEARNBOT)
creator: Leia R. Jones, Maurice J.W. Zwart, Felix Nickel, Thilo Hackert, Freek Daams, Bas Groot Koerkamp, Quintus Molenaar, Ugo Boggi, Olivier Saint-Marc, Philip Leenart, Rawin Amiri, Mahsoem Ali, Sebastiaan Festen, Olivier Busch, Paul S. Krohn, Ernesto Sparrelid, Bergthor Björnsson, Christian Toso, Edoardo

Objective:To assess the feasibility of and clinical outcomes after a pan-European training program for robotic pancreatoduodenectomy (RPD).Summary Background Data:The implementation of RPD into clinical practice comes with considerable challenges, leading to concerns about patient safety, oncological outcomes, and costs.

title: Sport-related Concussion Characteristics and Time-loss Among Male and Female Community Rugby Union Players Across 6 Seasons
creator: Laura C Power, Tom M Comyns, Helen Purtill, John JE Mulvihill, Kilian L Bibby, Caithríona Yeomans, Patrick Dolan, Michael W Collins, Anthony P Kontos, Ian C Kenny
description: Background:Sport-related concussion (SRC) is a common injury in Rugby Union. There is currently a paucity of prospective research in SRC specific data in both male and female community Rugby Union players, which may restrict SRC prevention, recognition, and management practices.

title: Reciprocal control of the stomach and intestine by viscerosensory neurons in caudal brainstem
creator: Naz Dundar, Ilayda Alkislar, Brooke C Jarvie, Ho Namkung, Kathryn Xie, Mahekdeep Kaur, Queenie Li, Anagh S Ravi, Alejandro Lopez, Antionette Spina, Longhui Qui, Truong Ly, Jun Oh, Kevin Yackle, Zachary A Knight
description: Digestion requires precisely timed transit of food through the gastrointestinal tract. Here we show that emptying of food from the stomach occurs in discrete pulses, separated by pauses that allow the proximal duodenum to clear before the next bolus arrives.

title: Above- and belowground succession following multiple-tree mortality in Pinus densiflora forests
creator: Seung–Jae Lee, Ah–Rim Lee, Dong–Seok Son, Dong–Bin Shin, Seok Hui Lee, Yeong-Eun Kim, Jun Won Kang, Seung–Hwan Oh
description: Climate-driven tree mortality impacts forest ecosystems, yet studies rarely integrate above- and below-ground processes. Consequently, the temporal dynamics of rhizosphere microbial communities following mortality and their link to vegetation changes remain unclear. This study examined coupled shifts in species composition and rhizosphere microbial communities following multiple-tree mortality events in Pinus densiflora stands.

title: Prospective evaluation of uterine artery embolization using diluted NBCA-lipiodol mixture for uterine fibroids: preliminary treatment outcomes
creator: Nguyen Thi Bich Van, Nguyen Thanh Khiem, Nguyen Ngoc Cuong, Phan Hoang Giang, Nguyen Quang Trung, Thieu Thi Tra My, Bui Thi Phuong Thao, Tran Quoc Hoa
description: BackgroundThis study aimed to determine the safety and effectiveness of uterine artery embolization using NBCA – lipiodol mixture via radial artery access for the treatment of uterine fibroids.MethodsForty patients underwent uterine artery embolization with NBCA mixed with lipiodol (1:10). The uterine fibroid volumes were determined on magnetic resonance imaging before and 3–6 months after the procedure.

title: Comparative analysis of morphological traits and photosynthetic parameters as well as carbon accumulation characteristics of six typical shrub species in the Qilian Mountains
creator: Rong Zhou, Na Wei, Yaoyao Shangguan, Hu Zhao, Bin Chen, Yin Miao, Hongmei Liu, Xiaobin Xie, Gang Chen, Jingzhong Zhao, Dong Lv
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionShrubs are key components of arid ecosystems, and their functional traits directly influence ecological adaptability and productivity. Current research pays insufficient attention to the synergistic relationship between the overall morphological structure and leaf physiological functions of shrubs.

title: Allele-resolved monosome and polysome sequencing identifies cis-variants affecting mRNA translation
creator: Laura Alunno, Ilaria Massignani, Meriem Hadjer Hamadou, Fabio Mazza, Daniele Peroni, Romina Belli, Erik Dassi, Alessandro Romanel, Alberto Inga
description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Allele-specific profiling of ribosome-associated mRNAs reveals widespread cis-regulatory effects on translation and shows that 80S monosome analysis improves detection sensitivity. Introduction

The relevance of the posttranscriptional and translational controls in modulating gene expression has recently been emphasized (Mata et al, 2005; Ruggero, 2013; Zhao et al, 2016; Robichaud et al, 2019; Jia et al, 2020; Mitschka & Mayr, 2022; Orellana et al, 2022; Wu & Bazzini, 2023; Biffo et al, 2024).

title: Machine vision-based detection method for key phenotypic information of shiitake mushroom stipes
creator: Jiuxiao Zhao, Mingfei Wang, Zuolin Li, Qiuxiao Song, Cheng Chen, Guoqiang Guo, Jing Dong, Feifei Shan, Ruixue Xu, Wei Liu, Xin Zhang, Wengang Zheng
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionIn the field of shiitake mushroom breeding, the difficulty and inaccuracy in measuring key stipe traits severely limit improvements in breeding efficiency and product quality. This study aims to address this technical challenge.MethodsA key trait detection method for mushroom stipes based on integrated image processing technology was proposed: 1) Developed the ACmix-ADown-YOLOv11n stipe detection model; 2) Input the detection bounding box into the EfficientSAM network for precise segmentation,then used OpenCV-based techniques to calculate 12 key phenotypic features; 3) Constructed the CoTAttention-YOLOv11n-Ghost-pose algorithm

title: Mesenchymal Stem Cell (MSC)-based therapies for neonatal lung and brain injury – one size fits all?
creator: U. Felderhoff-Müser, J. Herz, I. Bendix, J. Behnke, Y. Dong, H. Ehrhardt
description: MSC-based therapies have emerged as a highly promising approach for two of the most devastating consequences of perinatal insults such as extreme prematurity and perinatal asphyxia: bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) and neonatal brain injury. Both conditions share a common pathophysiological basis of inflammation, oxidative stress, and disrupted progenitor cell function in critical windows of organ development.

title: Characterization of the Middle Ear Microbiome in Meniere's Disease by 16S rRNA Gene Sequencing Compared to Chronic Suppurative Otitis Media
creator: Yu‐Ting Tao, Lin Wang, Hong‐wei Zheng, Li‐Sheng Yu

title: Cold‐adapted Ligninolytic Nanozyme Unveiling New Horizons in Black Liquor Treatment Under Mild Condition
creator: Qing Tian, Huile Liu, Yao Chen, Xiaohe Miao, Rong Yang, Yangjun Guo, Mato Knez, Xiyun Yan, Kelong Fan, Lianbing Zhang
description: Kraft black liquor, characterised by high lignin content, poses significant challenges for efficient treatment under mild conditions. This study unveils a pioneering solution via a novel cold‐adapted ligninolytic nanozyme constructed from an amorphous manganese‐containing metal‐organic framework (aMnMOF). The aMnMOF features low‐coordination Mn within mixed‐valence trinuclear Mn‐O clusters integrated with a long‐range disordered MOF architecture.

title: Fine mapping and candidate gene mining of major QTL QSL.caas-6BL.1 for spike length in bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L.)

This study focused on fine‑mapping a major SL‑regulating quantitative trait locus (QTL), QSL.caas‑6BL.1, previously identified in a Doumai (DM) × Shi 4185 population.MethodsHigh‑density molecular markers were developed and used to screen recombinant families derived from the cross.

title: Association Between Trust in Healthcare Providers and Readiness to Deprescribe in Older Adults: A Cross‐Sectional Comparative Study in the United States and Japan
creator: Kenya Ie, Amy M Linsky, Xinran Liu, Melina B Martin, Rie Oyama, Steven M Albert
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundUnderstanding how patient trust in healthcare providers is related to readiness to deprescribe is essential for optimizing deprescribing. This study examined this association among older adults with polypharmacy in the U.S. and Japan.MethodsWe conducted cross‐sectional surveys involving Japanese older adults receiving care from a community hospital and primary care clinic (Kawasaki City, n = 185) and American older adults recruited to a research registry within a university hospital system (Pittsburgh, n = 107).

title: The effect of Bartholin gland diseases on female sexual function, sexual distress, and genital self-image: a prospective cohort study

description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionBartholin gland disease impairs sexual function, yet most studies focus on surgical technique rather than the broader sexual health burden, and none has systematically examined sexual distress or genital self-image in this population.

title: Categorizing differences in postpartum hemorrhage management and associated clinical factors
creator: Moeun Son, Lisbet Lundsberg, Caitlin Partridge, Danna Tortal, Heather Burris, Leyla Sahin, Robert Whetsel, Kevin Dysart, Jennifer Culhane
description: ObjectiveTo examine whether there is variation in postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) management and whether differences are associated with patient‐level factors and delivery hospital.MethodsThis is a retrospective cohort study of patients delivered at ≥20 weeks of gestation at any of four hospitals within one Connecticut healthcare system, with evidence of PPH, and receipt of intervention from 2012 to 2023.

title: A case series exploring the human milk polyclonal IgA1 response to repeated SARS-CoV-2 vaccinations by LC–MS based fab profiling
creator: Sebastiaan C. de Graaf, Albert Bondt, Danique M. H. van Rijswijck, Hannah G. Juncker, Sien J. Mulleners, Mirjam J. A. Damen, Max Hoek, Britt J. van Keulen, Johannes B. van Goudoever, Albert J. R. Heck, Kelly A. Dingess
description: IntroductionUpon vaccination against severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) humans will start to produce antibodies targeting virus specific antigens that will end up in circulation. In lactating women such antibodies will also end up in breastmilk, primarily in the form of secretory immunoglobulin A1 (SIgA1), the most abundant immunoglobulin (Ig) in human milk.

title: Unique circulating miRNAome signatures captured with distinct molecular states in Lynch syndrome and sporadic colorectal cancer
creator: Ramadhani Salum Chambuso, Md Shohel Ul Islam, Rosa M Xicola, Raj Ramesar, Xavier Llor, Sinclair Steele
description: Hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer (HNPCC), usually termed Lynch syndrome (LS), is the most prevalent hereditary colorectal cancer syndrome, yet molecular biomarkers to differentiate nonmalignant from malignant LS cases remain limited. We performed a secondary analysis of the circulating miRNAome in 155 individuals, including healthy controls (CTRL), nonmalignant LS (H‐LS), cancer‐associated LS (C‐LS), and sporadic colorectal cancer (CRC).

title: Quality of life, stress, anxiety and depression and associated factors among people with type 2 diabetes mellitus in Western region Saudi Arabia

title: Tropism of Plasmodium malariae for young red blood cells and the bone marrow
creator: Barbara Mouyama, Vivienne Fey, Dorenda J.A. Schoorl, Malika Serra-Hassoun, Fidelis Ambinintsoa, Barclaye Ngossanga, Leticia Hartmann, Ayola A. Adegnika, Artur Scherf, Mario Recker, Rolf Fendel, Steffen Borrmann, Sylvie Garcia
description: Fundamental aspects of the biology of the third most prevalent human malaria species Plasmodium malariae, including the basis for its capacity to establish chronic, low-density infections associated with debilitating quartan fevers, remain poorly characterized, hampering control efforts. Here, we combined ex vivo flowcytometric profiling of P. malariae isolates with infection studies in a recently developed humanized mouse model.

title: Baseline risk factors of in-hospital mortality after surgery for acute type A aortic dissection: an ERTAAD study

description: This study was part of an in vivo investigation of methane (CH4) abatement feed on local Menz breed sheep in Ethiopia, conducted over 90 days period using a randomized complete block design. Sheep were subjected to four dietary treatments: Control, Acacia (Acacia nilotica), BSG (Brewer's Spent Grain), and Ziziphus (Ziziphus spina-christi).

title: Modeling the effect of climatic conditions and topography on malaria incidence using Poisson regression: a Retrospective study in Bannu, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan

description: BackgroundMalaria has been identified as a crucial vector-borne disease around the globe. The primary aim of this study was to investigate the incidence of malaria in the district of Bannu and its relationship with climatic conditions such as temperature, rainfall, relative humidity, and topography.

In the thermal industry, the operational characteristics of heating equipment are often controlled by artificial connections, assess the efficiency of radiator systems and accelerate the boiling and investigation procedures.

title: Psychological drivers of electric vehicle battery recycling: the impact of place attachment and sustainable attitudes
creator: Jie Cheng, Tian Gao, Yi-Cheng Zhang, Noor Ullah Khan, Ke-Bin Lu
description: IntroductionThe rapid expansion of electric‑vehicle adoption in China has intensified concerns about end‑of‑life management of power batteries. Despite increasing apprehensions about economic, social, and environmental sustainability 2021-2035, there has been a noticeable surge in scholarly interest directed towards formal power battery recycling.

title: Goat and cow milk merits distinct nutritional and functional properties based on simulated gastrointestinal digestion of infant
creator: Jiaxin Chen, Ruikai Zhu, Linjun Wu, Jian Kuang, Xiangyu Bian, Xiaoqiong Li, Weiwei Wang, Wenjie Kang, Shanbo Mu, Bryan Yanwen Liu, Ke Zhao, Jinjun Li
description: The nutritional and functional properties of goat and cow milk in digestive tract of infant is unclear. Applying simulated infant gastrointestinal digestion method, this study aims to systematically compare digestibility, peptide profiling, and immunomodulatory role of goat and cow milk, and further characterize their role in regulating homeostasis of gut microbiota and metabolism.

title: Sequential 2.5 mg letrozole/FSH therapy is more effective for promoting pregnancy in infertile women with PCOS: a pragmatic randomized controlled trial
creator: Li-Juan Chen, Yi Liu, Ling Zhang, Jing-Yi Li, Wen-Qian Xiong, Tao Li, Hui Ding, Bing-Jie Li

title: Natural products targeting the MAPK signaling pathway: potential options for ulcerative colitis treatment
creator: Canglin Li, Zuoqiang Li, Ya Zheng
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). As a chronic, recurrent inflammatory bowel disease, ulcerative colitis (UC) poses significant clinical challenges due to its progressive intestinal mucosal damage, recurrent exacerbations of abdominal pain and diarrhea, and increased risk of colorectal cancer conversion with disease duration. Conventional medications such as aminosalicylates and glucocorticoids can control inflammation in the short term, but long-term use often leads to issues like drug resistance, gastrointestinal adverse reactions, and immunosuppression, failing to meet patients’ demand for safe, long-lasting treatment.

title: Long-Term Mortality and Morbidity After Pediatric Sepsis
creator: Erik Edholm, Adam Linder, Malin Inghammar, Anton Nilsson, Sara Jesperson, Lisa Mellhammar
description: BackgroundAdults experience sustained disease burden in the years following sepsis, but data regarding long-term prognosis after pediatric sepsis are still limited. The objective of this study was to determine long-term outcomes after sepsis in children, in terms of mortality, morbidity, and socioeconomic factors.

title: GRAYU: graph-based database integrating Ayurvedic formulations, medicinal plants, phytochemicals and diseases
creator: Sarthak Joshi, Aditi Pathak, Dheemanth Reddy Regati, Revathy Menon, Deepthi S. Ajith, Aditya Sheshadri, Neerja Viswanathan, Poulomi Ray, Vimarishi Koul, Pratishruti Panda, Shriya Anand Bhambore, Shailya Verma, Ananya Sinha, K. Mohamed Shafi, Murugavel Pavalam, Ramanathan Sowdhamini
description: IntroductionThe translation of India's extensive traditional knowledge on indigenous medicinal plants into modern therapeutic solutions is contingent upon a systematic framework. While traditional Indian medicine offers a rich source of therapeutic leads, this knowledge is often not structured for modern computational analysis, creating a barrier to systematic drug discovery.

title: From a visible health problem to an actionable research priority: Development and demonstration of the VISIBLE-to-ACTION framework
creator: Gilbert C. Magulod, Jamaica Castillo-Pedro
description: PurposeTo develop and demonstrate the VISIBLE-to-ACTION framework as a transparent method for moving from a documented health problem to a defensible research priority, while distinguishing research, evidence, decision, and implementation gaps. The framework addresses the limitation of conventional gap statements that rely primarily on claims that few studies exist without establishing why additional evidence is necessary.

title: Robotics total knee arthroplasty: is an image-based the only solution?

While traditional robotic systems rely on preoperative imaging, imageless technology has emerged as a viable alternative, leading to a reduction in costs, radiation exposure, and logistical challenges. This narrative review aims to evaluate the efficacy and reliability of imageless robotic-assisted TKA, specifically assessing its accuracy in component positioning, functional outcomes, and potential advantages over image-based systems.

title: Weekend admissions and outcomes in patients with pneumonia: a systematic review and meta-analysis

creator: Tzu-Yi Chia, Leah K. Billingham, Lauren Boland, Joshua L. Katz, Victor A. Arrieta, Jack Shireman, Aurora-Lopez Rosas, Susan L. DeLay, Kaylee Zillinger, Yuheng Geng, Jeandre Kruger, Caylee Silvers, Hanxiang Wang, Gustavo Ignacio Vazquez Cervantes, David Hou, Si Wang, Hanxiao Wan, Adam Sonabend, Peng
description: IntroductionGlioblastoma multiforme (GBM) pathobiology is characterized by its significant induction of immunosuppression within the tumor microenvironment, predominantly mediated by immunosuppressive tumor-associated myeloid cells (TAMCs). Myeloid cells play a pivotal role in shaping the GBM microenvironment and influencing immune responses, with direct interactions with effector immune cells critically impacting these processes.

title: Cerebrospinal fluid C-reactive protein to diagnose healthcare-associated meningitis after neurosurgical procedures: An exploratory retrospective diagnostic accuracy study
creator: M Foppen, IO Kommers, SE Olie, HHM Schotman, D Verbaan, MC Brouwer
description: IntroductionNeurosurgical procedures are frequently complicated by postoperative meningitis. Current diagnostic methods are insufficient and time-consuming. Cerebrospinal fluid C-reactive protein (CSF CRP) has shown excellent diagnostic accuracy for patients with a community-acquired meningitis and can be determined quickly.Research questionThis study investigates the diagnostic accuracy of CSF CRP for detecting postoperative meningitis.

title: Treatment of metastatic bladder paraganglioma with cadonilimab plus radiotherapy: a case report and literature review
creator: RiHan Wu, ZiRui Wang, YuanRui Bai, Yihui Liu, Chunhui Dong, Ling Chen
description: BackgroundBladder paraganglioma (PPGL) is a rare neuroendocrine tumor associated with a lower survival rate compared to paragangliomas originating in other anatomical locations. Surgical resection is still the primary treatment modality for bladder paraganglioma; however, this approach carries a significant risk of malignant metastasis. Once metastasis occurs, therapeutic options become notably limited.

title: Percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion versus oral anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation: A pragmatic meta-analysis of randomized trials within the DOAC era
creator: Gabriel Moraes Kuniyoshi, Rafael Zoppi Campane, Nikita Patil, Ana Clara Vitorino de Oliveira, Beatriz Araújo, Ricardo Ryoshim Kuniyoshi
description: BackgroundPercutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is an established alternative to oral anticoagulation (OAC). However, its safety and efficacy boundaries remain incompletely defined in dedicated comparisons against direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs).ObjectiveThis study applied a pragmatic framework to evaluate the comparative efficacy and safety of LAAO versus OAC in a DOAC-predominant setting.

title: Synergistic PVA/zein electrospun nanofiber array with curcumin-alizarin: a water-resistant, sensitive colorimetric platform for graded pork freshness monitoring
creator: Bingcan Liu, Siling Zhang, Honghui Geng, Can Hu, An Zhou, Zeyu Wu
description: In this work, a synergistic polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)/zein electrospun nanofiber array was fabricated using curcumin and alizarin as dual responsive pigments for visual pork freshness monitoring. The water solubility of the PVA/zein composite reduced from 100.00% to 31.74%–35.42% (P < 0.05), exhibiting remarkably enhanced water resistance. The dual-pigment array displayed continuous color transitions from pH 4.0 to 11.

title: Influence of an oregano-based essential oil on growth performance and carcass traits of beef steers
creator: Bergin M DeBruin, Christina E Bakker, Keith R Underwood, Judson K Grubbs, Warren C Rusche, Zachary K Smith, Amanda D Blair
description: The objective of this study was to determine the influence of an oregano-based essential oil on growth performance, health outcomes, and carcass characteristics of yearling beef steers finished in an all-natural program. Single-sourced yearling steers (N = 128; initial body weight [BW] = 335 ± 7.9 kg) were allotted to 16 pens (n = 8 pens/treatment with 8 steers/pen).

title: POLB 001, a p38 MAPK inhibitor, decreases local and systemic inflammatory responses following in vivo LPS administration in healthy volunteers: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study
creator: Digna T. de Bruin, Manon A. A. Jansen, Diana R. Pereira, Lisa van Schijndel, Erica S. Klaassen, Marije E. Otto, Jeremy Skillington, Paula Maguire, Liam Tremble, Alan Bell, Laura Maher, Katsuhiro Mihara, Mark Sumeray, Derek W. Gilroy, Naomi B. Klarenbeek, Matthijs Moerland
description: Background and aimPOLB 001 is an oral p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) inhibitor in development for the prevention of cancer immunotherapy-induced cytokine release syndrome (CRS). It has previously been shown to be well tolerated and capable of decreasing ex vivo lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced tumour necrosis factor (TNF) secretion in a phase 1 first-in-human trial.

title: Earth-observation variables identify temperature-centered protein-family covariation across macroalgal genomes
creator: Alexandra Mystikou, David R. Nelson, Diana C. El Assal, Ashish K. Jaiswal, Mehar Sultana, Cecilia Rad-Menendez, Noura Al-Mansoori, Sewar T. Elias, Ma-sum Abdul-Hamid, Layanne Nayfeh, Nizar Drou, John A. Burt, David H. Green, Kourosh Salehi-Ashtiani
description: SummaryMacroalgal genome-environment associations are difficult to separate from lineage, geography, and uneven genome quality. We describe nine Arabian Gulf genomes and analyze them with 117 published genomes (126 total). We tested protein family (Pfam) profiles against 13 Google Earth Engine variables. Of 87,123 tests, 84 met global Benjamini-Hochberg q < 0.

title: Non-human primate preclinical model revealed the feasibility and short-term safety of iPSC-derived innate-like T cells in autologous transplantation
creator: Yasuyuki Miyake, Shoichi Iriguchi, Ai Kawana-Tachikawa, Shuichi Kitayama, Eri Imai, Kahoru Taya, Hiroshi Ishii, Tomoyuki Miura, Hiromi Sakawaki, Tetsuro Matano, Shin Kaneko
description: BackgroundT cells derived from gene-edited induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) are a promising alternative cell source for universal T-cell immunotherapy. However, current preclinical evaluations of iPSC-derived T cells (iPSC-T cells) rely on immunodeficient mouse models, which limit the assessment of immune-related adverse events and in vivo immune cell interactions.

title: Dengue infection in kidney transplant recipients during a major epidemic and the implementation of systematic donor screening: a cohort study
creator: José Medina Pestana, Débora Fonseca Raimundo, Caio Leite Albuquerque, Telma Raduan, Natália Ferreira de Oliveira, Carolinna Marques da Silva, Haryanne de Souza Goulart, Elisabeth Lucena Franca, Renato Demarchi Foresto, Celso F Hernandes Granato, Lúcio Requião-Moura
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryBackgroundDuring Brazil's unprecedented dengue epidemic in 2023–2025, we develop a rationale for organ donor screening to mitigate the risk of donor derived transmission using rapid, widely available, and low-cost tests. Here we aimed to describe the epidemiology, clinical presentation, and outcomes among kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) who developed different routes of dengue infection and establish a policy for mitigating the risk of donor transmission.MethodsThis study conducted at a large kidney transplant center in Brazil—Hospital do Rim (HRIM) examined dengue in KTRs through

title: Deep-STP: a deep learning-based approach to predict snake toxin proteins by using word embeddings
creator: Hasan Zulfiqar, Zhiling Guo, Ramala Masood Ahmad, Zahoor Ahmed, Peiling Cai, Xiang Chen, Yang Zhang, Hao Lin, Zheng Shi
description: Snake venom contains many toxic proteins that can destroy the circulatory system or nervous system of prey. Studies have found that these snake venom proteins have the potential to treat cardiovascular and nervous system diseases. Therefore, the study of snake venom protein is conducive to the development of related drugs.

title: Organ-Specific Phenolic Specialization and Antioxidant Responses in Crocus cancellatus: LC–MS/MS and Multivariate Analysis
creator: Bedrettin Selvi
description: Organ-specific allocation of phenolic metabolites may shape antioxidant responses in Crocus species. This study characterized stamen, pistil, tepal, perigon tube, and corm of Crocus cancellatus Herb. using ultrasound-assisted methanolic extraction, liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry with 30 authentic standards, six antioxidant assays, a relative antioxidant capacity index, Pearson correlation analysis, and principal component analysis. Twenty phenolic compounds were quantified.

title: Editorial: Non-cutaneous melanoma: new therapeutic insights
creator: Ernesto Rossi, Richard D. Carvajal
description: s frequent in terms of incidence compared to cutaneous disease, are less commonly the focus of large-scale research efforts, and are associated with inferior clinical outcomes. Uveal melanoma is a rare neoplasm, but is the most common primary malignancy of the eye, occurring in about 5.2 patients/million/year (1, 2). Mucosal melanoma arises from mucosal tissue of head and neck (eg.

title: Complementary Molecular and Spectroscopic Approaches for Meat Authentication: Real-Time PCR Detection of Porcine DNA and FT-NIR Analysis of Slaughter-Related Biochemical Changes
creator: Diyas Myrzakozha, Elmira Karlova, Saule Meldebekova, Tolkyn Issabekova, Nurgali Rakhymbayev, Nyshanbay Konash, Aliya Yermekkyzy
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Food adulteration and species mislabeling represent important challenges for food safety, regulatory control, and consumer protection, particularly for products requiring species-specific authentication. This study investigated two complementary analytical approaches relevant to meat authentication: species-specific real-time polymerase chain reaction (real-time PCR) for the molecular detection of porcine mitochondrial deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) and Fourier-transform near-infrared (FT-NIR) spectroscopy combined with chemometric analysis for exploratory assessment of slaughter-related compositional changes in a controlled murine proof-of-concept model.

title: Low Nephron Number and Kidney Disease
creator: Samaneh Goorani, John D. Imig
description: Reduced nephron endowment and acquired nephron loss increase susceptibility to hypertension and chronic kidney disease (CKD). Low birth weight, prematurity, genetic factors, and adverse prenatal exposures can limit nephron development, whereas aging and kidney injury reduce the number of functioning nephrons after birth.

title: The link of universalism, transformational leadership, innovativeness, and leader effectiveness: a multivariate dataset
creator: Sunu Widianto, Budi Harsanto, Arviansyah Arviansyah
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). g practitioners and academia (Newstead et al., 2021). De Hoogh and Den Hartog (2008) investigated the relationship between leaders' social responsibility and the ethical aspects of leadership, such as morality and fairness, role clarification, and power sharing. De Hoogh and Den Hartog (2008) found that leaders with high social responsibility have a high level of ethical values and ethical conduct (Banks et al., 2016; Gardner and Wickramasinghe, 2023).

title: Nicarbazin-Based Fertility Control for Urban Pigeon Management: A Review of Experimental, Regulatory and Operational Evidence
creator: Marco Pellizzari, Paolo Pietro Albonetti, Yassine Hankaz
description: Simple SummaryFeral pigeons are common in cities worldwide, where large populations can damage buildings, create health concerns, and cause conflict between residents and local authorities. Removing or culling pigeons rarely solves the problem for long, because new birds quickly move in to replace those that are taken away.

title: Prognosis and Therapies in Non-Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinomas
creator: Trilok Shrivastava, Yusra Medik, Nikhila Sampath Kumar, Shi-Ming Tu, Anuradha Kunthur
description: Simple SummaryNon-clear cell renal cell carcinomas (nccRCCs) comprise a heterogeneous group of kidney cancers with distinct biological features and clinical outcomes. Prognosis varies substantially according to histology and molecular drivers. Historically, outcomes have been inferior to those of clear cell RCC because subtype-specific evidence has been limited.

title: VEGF-A isoforms induce the expression of APLN in endothelial cells during human prenatal lung development
creator: Antony Hoarau, Andrew Frauenpreis, Randa Belgacemi, Emma Loeffler, Osshaya Maalouf, Ian A. Glass, Denise Al Alam, Soula Danopoulos
description: IntroductionSingle-cell RNA-sequencing analyses have revealed the existence of two distinct capillary cell populations in the human lung: general capillary cells (CAP1) and alveolar capillary cells (CAP2). Studies in mouse have shown that the splicing of Vegf-a evolves during embryonic development, creating a temporal pattern of expression for different isoforms, which contributes to the formation of pulmonary capillaries.

title: The effects of metabolic indicators and immune biomarkers on pregnancy outcomes in women with recurrent spontaneous abortion: a retrospective study
creator: Jie Zhang, Zhan Song, Hui Yuan, Zhu-Hua Cai
description: BackgroundThe etiology of recurrent spontaneous abortion (RSA) remains elusive despite specific investigations affirming the association between RSA and thyroid autoimmunity (TAI). This study explores the immunological and metabolic profiles of RSA patients exhibiting positive thyroid antibodies and their connection with the rates of first-trimester miscarriage and live births. The aim is to provide further guidance for clinical interventions.

title: Phase-targeted erythropoietin derivatives for traumatic brain injury: bridging mechanisms to precision therapy
creator: Yujin Sun, Bo Song, Yonglei Zhang, Yan Zhang, Lu Zhou
description: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) unfolds through a well-defined chronology—hyperacute excitotoxic and inflammasome bursts, acute apoptotic and blood–brain-barrier failure, and subacute neurovascular remodeling—that no single-pathway drug can adequately cover. Recombinant erythropoietin (EPO) limits secondary damage in animals, yet its erythropoietic drive and thrombotic liability have stalled clinical adoption.

title: The Adipovascular Unit in Lipedema: A Framework for Regional Adipose Tissue Dysregulation
creator: Jörg Faulhaber, C. William Hanke, Martin Barsch, Matthias Sandhofer
description: Highlights What are the main findings? The adipovascular unit (AVU) is proposed as a system-level framework linking progenitor, vascular, immune, extracellular matrix, and adipocyte compartments in lipedema.The framework integrates regional susceptibility and reciprocal multicellular signaling while distinguishing lipedema-specific evidence from mechanisms inferred from general adipose-tissue biology. What are the implications of the main findings?

title: Burnout and Perceived Stress Among Female Health Sciences Faculty Members at a University in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study
creator: Zeinab A. Abusabeib
description: Highlights What are the main findings? Emotional exhaustion was the most prominent dimension of burnout among faculty members across five health sciences colleges at a university in Riyadh.In multivariable analyses using continuous outcome scores, younger age and working more than 50 h per week were associated with higher emotional exhaustion and perceived stress.

title: Harnessing filamentous phages for enhanced stroke recovery
creator: Yang Li, Kai-di Yang, De-cai Kong, Xiao-meng Li, Hao-yu Duan, Jun-feng Ye
description: Stroke poses a critical global health challenge, leading to substantial morbidity and mortality. Existing treatments often miss vital timeframes and encounter limitations due to adverse effects, prompting the pursuit of innovative approaches to restore compromised brain function. This review explores the potential of filamentous phages in enhancing stroke recovery. Initially antimicrobial-centric, bacteriophage therapy has evolved into a regenerative solution.

title: Decompressive craniectomy in adults with moderate to severe traumatic brain injury: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
creator: Marwan Bouras, Frédérique Lamothe-Boucher, Jihad Abou Jamous, Paule Lessard Bonaventure, Antoine Ouellet, Olivier Costerousse, Charles Francoeur, Ryan Zarychanski, Shane W English, Michael Verret, François Lauzier, Alexis F Turgeon
description: ObjectiveThe aim of this study was to evaluate the impact of decompressive craniectomy (DC) on functional outcomes, mortality, and quality of life in adults with moderate to severe traumatic brain injury (TBI).DesignSystematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials (RCTs).Data sourcesWe searched MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.

title: Lymphocytic interstitial non-HIV-related pneumonia in pediatrics: a case report
creator: Andrea Dionelly Murillo Casas, Diana María Duarte Dorado, Manuela Olaya Hernández
description: Lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia (LIP) in pediatric patients without human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection remains a poorly characterized and enigmatic disease. Immunological dysregulation, mutations in the COPA gene, and increased morbidity and mortality have been reported in these patients. We present a case of LIP in a pediatric patient without HIV infection.

title: Protocol for high-throughput identification of genes involved in pyroptotic cell death by live microscopy
creator: Aleksandra Bajger, Lukasz S. Borowski, Roman J. Szczesny, Michal P. Wandel
description: SummaryIntracellular lipopolysaccharide activates caspase-4/5 triggering pyroptotic cell death. We present a protocol for a high-throughput loss-of-function screening approach to identify interferon-gamma-stimulated genes regulating this pathway. We detail procedures for cell reverse-transfection with a custom-made small interfering RNA (siRNA) library in 384-well plates and priming with interferon-gamma.

title: Retraction Note: NR1B2 suppress kidney renal clear cell carcinoma (KIRC) progression by regulation of LATS 1/2-YAP signaling
creator: Lei Yin, Wenjia Li, Guangchun Wang, Heng Shi, Keyi Wang, Huan Yang, Bo Peng
description: d the lower right section of PLKO/Invasion panel appear to overlap; Figure 3I: the upper left section of PLKO/Migration panel and the lower right section of PLKO/Invasion panel appear to overlap; Figure 5B: the 786-O: SH-NR1B2 band of NR1B2 and the SW839: OE-NR1B2 band of P-YAP appear to overlap when flipped; Figure 5B: the 786-O: SH-NR1B2 band of NR1B2 and

title: Criterion validity of brief, comprehensive, and latent measures of intrinsic capacity against frailty, disability, and mortality in older adults
creator: Sunyoung Kim, Lan Luo, Sandra M. Shi, Chan Mi Park, Kevin T. Pritchard, Miji Kim, Chang Won Won, Dae Hyun Kim
description: BackgroundIntrinsic capacity (IC), the composite of physical and mental capacities, underpins the WHO Integrated Care for Older People (ICOPE) program. IC may be measured as a brief screen, a comprehensive assessment, or a latent factor score; whether the simpler measures retain the prognostic information of the complex ones remains untested within a single population.

title: Integrating RNA-sequencing and network analysis to explore the mechanism of topical Pien Tze Huang treatment on diabetic wounds
creator: Guang-Zhao Cao, Liang-Liang Tian, Jing-Yi Hou, Yi Zhang, He Xu, Hong-Jun Yang, Jing-Jing Zhang
description: Introduction: Diabetic ulcers have become one of the major complications of diabetes mellitus (DM) and are a leading cause of death and disabling disease. However, current therapies are not effective enough to meet clinical needs. A traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formula, Pien Tze Huang (PZH), is known as a medicine that is used to treat diabetic ulcers.

title: A narrative review of functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) applications in hearing loss, tinnitus and vestibular disorders
creator: Davide Brotto, Gaia Lucarini, Valeria Del Vecchio, Nicole Galoforo, Elisa Lovato, Benedetta Colavolpe, Giusy Melcarne, Gino Marioni, Judit Gervain, Anna Rita Fetoni, Patrizia Trevisi
description: IntroductionFunctional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) has emerged as a promising neuroimaging modality for investigating cortical activity in auditory and vestibular domains. Its portability, device compatibility, and motion tolerance make it particularly suited for use in populations that are challenging to study with conventional neuroimaging techniques, such as infants and cochlear implant (CI) users.

title: Exposure route, not dose, is the primary driver of infection patterns for a respiratory virus
creator: Celine E. Snedden, Dylan H. Morris, Thomas C. Friedrich, James O. Lloyd-Smith
description: Infectious disease severity, shedding, and within-host kinetics can vary substantially with exposure dose, inoculation route, and host factors. However, the relative contributions of these variables to infection heterogeneity remain poorly quantified because small sample sizes in controlled in vivo experiments limit their statistical power and scientific scope.

title: Eugenol improves salt tolerance via enhancing antioxidant capacity and regulating ionic balance in tobacco seedlings
creator: Jiaxin Xu, Tingting Wang, Changwei Sun, Peng Liu, Jian Chen, Xin Hou, Tao Yu, Yun Gao, Zhiguo Liu, Long Yang, Li Zhang
description: Salt stress inhibits plant growth by disturbing plant intrinsic physiology. The application of exogenous plant growth regulators to improve the plant tolerance against salt stress has become one of the promising approaches to promote plant growth in saline environment. Eugenol (4-allyl-2- methoxyphenol) is the main ingredient in clove oil and it is known for its strong antioxidant and anti-microbial activities.

title: Detection of a bibenzyl core scaffold in 28 common mangrove and associate species of the Indian Sundarbans: potential signature molecule for mangrove salinity stress acclimation
creator: Bhanumati Sarkar, Hemendra Nath Kotal, Chayan Kumar Giri, Anup Mandal, Nandagopal Hudait, Nithar Ranjan Madhu, Subhajit Saha, Sandip Kumar Basak, Jhimli Sengupta, Krishna Ray
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Bibenzyl derivatives comprising two benzene rings are secondary plant metabolites with significant therapeutic value. To date, bibenzyl derivatives in the Plant kingdom have been primarily identified in bryophytes, orchids, and Cannabis sativa. The metabolic cost investment by plant species for the synthesis of these bioactive secondary metabolites is rationalized as a mechanism of plant defense in response to oxidative stress induced by biotic/abiotic factors. Bibenzyl derivatives are synthesized from core phenylpropanoid biosynthetic pathway offshoots in plant species.

title: How much can reticulate evolution entangle plant systematics? Revisiting subfamilial classification of the Malvatheca clade (Malvaceae) on the basis of phylogenomics
creator: Gustavo Luna, Lucas Costa, Flávia Fonseca Pezzini, Nisa Karimi, Joeri Sergej Strijk, Jefferson Carvalho-Sobrinho, Matheus Colli-Silva, André Marques, Gustavo Souza
description: Reticulate evolution (RE), involving hybridization and related processes, generates network-like rather than strictly bifurcating relationships among lineages and can obscure phylogenetic relationships. Detecting ancient hybridization is particularly challenging, as genomic signals may erode over time. The Malvatheca clade (Malvaceae), marked by multiple paleopolyploidy events since it’s estimated origin 66 my, offers a useful model for examining RE.

title: Potential health impacts and costs of active case finding guided by Mycobacterium tuberculosis immunoreactivity survey results in Blantyre, Malawi: A mathematical modeling study
creator: Sun Kim, Melike Hazal Can, Hannah M. Rickman, Mphatso D. Phiri, Marriott Nliwasa, Tisungane E. Mwenyenkulu, Kuzani Mbendera, Stéphane Verguet, Marcia C. Castro, Elizabeth L. Corbett, Peter MacPherson, Ted Cohen, Nicolas A. Menzies, Heather Van Epps, Andreia Cunha, Andreia Cunha, Andreia Cunha, Andre
description: BackgroundActive case finding (ACF) for tuberculosis (TB) can reduce transmission, yet efficient targeting requires high-quality surveillance data. We investigated the potential costs and impact of targeted ACF, guided by local estimates of the annual risk of TB infection (ARTI) derived from Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) immunoreactivity survey data in children aged <5 years.

title: Case report: abemaciclib-induced syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone (SIADH) without underlying kidney injury in a patient with early-stage estrogen receptor (ER)+ breast cancer
creator: Neil Carleton, Julia Foldi
description: The CDK4/6 inhibitor, abemaciclib, is now the standard of care adjuvant therapy for patients with estrogen receptor-positive (ER+)/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HER2-) tumors at high risk of recurrence. Real-world usage uncovers emerging side effects that may have been previously unreported in clinical trials.

title: Prevalence of Strongyloides stercoralis infection among African children: A systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Tadesse Hailu, Arancha Amor, Getaneh Alemu, Hiwot Tadesse, Veeranoot Nissapatorn, Hesham M. Al-Mekhlafi, Uriel Koziol, Eduardo José Lopes-Torres, Uriel Koziol, Eduardo José Lopes-Torres, Uriel Koziol, Eduardo José Lopes-Torres
description: Strongyloides stercoralis is a neglected parasite that causes strongyloidiasis. However, the true prevalence of strongyloidiasis is underreported due to low-sensitivity diagnostic methods. This systematic review assessed the prevalence of S. stercoralis among African children and its variation by diagnostic methods, countries, and study settings. All studies published in African countries on S.

title: The perception of surgical valve disease patients on quality of life improvement through the care line model: a longitudinal study
creator: Sirlei Pereira Nunes, Vitor Emer Egypto Rosa, Danielle Misumi Watanabe, Bellkiss Wilma Romano, Flávio Tarasoutchi
description: ObjectivesTo evaluate the improvement in the quality of life of surgical cardiac valve disease patients based on their perceptions at three distinct points: preoperative, immediate postoperative, and late postoperative.BackgroundQuality of life has been increasingly recognized as a central outcome in cardiovascular care, especially in valvular diseases.

title: Myeloid cell reprogramming drives enhanced defense against Streptococcus pneumoniae lung infection following exposure to commensal Prevotella
creator: Sara N. Stoner, Eric D. Larson, Sam Fulte, Steven C. Shaw, Erin R. Fish, Edward N. Janoff, Matthias Mack, Sarah E. Clark
description: SignificanceEven though Streptococcus pneumoniae is the most common cause of bacterial lung infections, most people who are exposed to this bacterium can successfully defend against infection. We investigated a mechanism for this natural resilience against infection by exploring how the immune system is educated by lung exposures to a common airway bacterium, Prevotella.

title: A systematic review of the barriers and facilitators to lived experience involvement in mental health services
creator: Selina Shaw, Louisa Shirley, Emma Schroeder, Grace Thompson, Kirsty Watt, Katrina Forsyth
description: IntroductionIndividuals with lived experience of mental health conditions provide a unique perspective to mental health services. In this systematic review, a broad definition of ‘involvement in mental health services’ was used, which included peer support, peer mentors, and peer specialists.

title: The core functions and forms paradigm throughout EPIS: designing and implementing an evidence-based practice with function fidelity
creator: Alec Terrana, Clare Viglione, Kyung Rhee, Borsika Rabin, Job Godino, Gregory A. Aarons, Jessica Chapman, Blanca Melendrez, Margarita Holguin, Liliana Osorio, Pradeep Gidwani, Cynthia Juarez Nunez, Gary Firestein, Eric Hekler
description: There are numerous frameworks for implementing evidence-based practices (EBPs) in novel settings to achieve “fidelity.” However, identifying appropriate referents for fidelity poses a challenge. The Core Functions and Forms paradigm offers a model that can inform adaptation decisions throughout all phases of the Exploration, Preparation, Implementation, Sustainment (EPIS) framework.

title: Protocol for isolation and cryopreservation of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells for high-resolution respirometry
creator: Alejandra Romero, Alba Timón-Gómez, Jaime R Willis, Anja Perfler, Theresa Lindlbauer, Michael Knoflach, Erich Gnaiger
description: SummaryHigh-resolution respirometry (HRR) of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) relies on controlled preanalytical procedures. Here, we present an optimized workflow for PBMC isolation from human whole blood, followed by short-term cryopreservation at −80°C. The protocol includes rapid thawing to preserve cell viability, washing steps to minimize platelet contamination, and quality-control assessment of PBMC number, viability, and composition before HRR measurements.

title: Comparative analysis of energy transfer mechanisms for neural implants
creator: Sols Miziev, Wiktoria Agata Pawlak, Newton Howard
description: As neural implant technologies advance rapidly, a nuanced understanding of their powering mechanisms becomes indispensable, especially given the long-term biocompatibility risks like oxidative stress and inflammation, which can be aggravated by recurrent surgeries, including battery replacements. This review delves into a comprehensive analysis, starting with biocompatibility considerations for both energy storage units and transfer methods.

title: Determining biocide efficacy for treating established sulfate-reducing biofilms using flow cell systems
creator: Gloria N. Okpala, Anna L. Walker, Craig Brideau, Pina Colarusso, Lisa M. Gieg
description: Sulfate-reducing microorganisms (SRM) can contribute to souring and to the corrosion of infrastructure built to support many industrial operations, including in aquatic environments. While chemicals such as biocides can effectively treat planktonic cells, less is known about biocide efficacy for treating established biofilms potentially plaguing infrastructure.

title: From gut colonization to recurrence: E. coli secretion systems at the host-microbiota interface
creator: Marcin Równicki, Maciej Obrębski, Jakub P. Piwowarski
description: Escherichia coli occupies a unique position between commensal colonization and infection. It is a common member of the intestinal microbiota, yet selected pathogenic or opportunistic lineages can persist in mucosal niches, interact with resident microbial communities, and in some cases seed recurrent extraintestinal diseases.

title: Illegitimate tasks, knowledge hiding, and performance erosion: a four-wave latent change score investigation
creator: Honghong Zhu, Xuan Gu, Daokui Jiang, Yaru Liu
description: This four-wave longitudinal study reframes unnecessary and unreasonable tasks as relational stimuli. Latent change score modeling on 250 employees (1 month intervals) showed that within-person increases in unnecessary tasks heightened knowledge hiding (β = 0.30-0.32), which subsequently eroded task performance (indirect effect = −0.12 to−0.14). Unreasonable tasks exerted comparable indirect harm (indirect = −0.11 to−0.

title: Cranial anatomy of the Middle Eocene Egyptian crocodylian Herugavialis cairensis provides new insights into gavialoid diversity in the Mediterranean region
creator: Paul M J Burke, Stephan N F Spiekman, Belal S Salem, Sara Saber, Hesham M Sallam, Philip D Mannion
description: Gavialoidea is presently composed of only two extant crocodylian species, the Indian gharial Gavialis gangeticus, and the false gharial Tomistoma schlegelii, both from southeast Asia. However, Gavialoidea displays a rich and near-cosmopolitan diversity in the fossil record, with over 40 species currently recognized.

title: Identification of RNAi hypoallergic bread wheat lines for wheat-dependent exercise-induced anaphylaxis patients
creator: María H. Guzmán-López, Violeta Ruipérez, Miriam Marín-Sanz, Isabel Ojeda-Fernández, Pedro Ojeda-Fernández, José Antonio Garrote-Adrados, Eduardo Arranz-Sanz, Francisco Barro
description: Wheat-dependent exercise-induced anaphylaxis (WDEIA) is one of the most severe forms of wheat allergy. It occurs in patients when they exercise after ingesting wheat-containing foods. Nowadays, the only possible alternative for WDEIA patients is to avoid such foods. This study investigated the potential of six RNA of interference (RNAi) wheat lines with low-prolamin content as alternatives for WDEIA patients.

title: Association between socioeconomic status and dental caries in adolescents – a systematic review of cohort studies
creator: Marit Slåttelid Skeie, Kristin Solveig Klock, Göran Dahllöf, Hedda Høvik, Ida Sofie Karlsen Sletten, Tone Natland Fagerhaug, Abhijit Sen
description: IntroductionEarly adolescence is a critical period for caries initiation, underlining the need for updated knowledge on effective caries indicators. This systematic review of cohort studies aimed to assess the association between socioeconomic status (SES), involving a wide range of indicators, and dental caries in adolescents aged 12–19.

title: Optimising ovarian cancer care: An embedded mixed methods evaluation of a national nurse-led telehealth program
creator: Patsy Yates, Wei-Hong Liu, Vanissa Ong, Sue Hegarty, Cyril Dixon, Anna Tart, Natalie Williams, Bridget Bradhurst
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeA nationwide nurse-led telehealth case management program was established providing personalised supportive care to individuals and families experiencing ovarian cancer. The program was evaluated using the RE-AIM framework. This paper focuses on the effectiveness findings of the evaluation.MethodsUsing mixed methods design, participants completed four surveys over 12 months assessing symptom burden, psychological distress, supportive care needs, quality of life, and self-efficacy. Service experiences were further explored through interviews.ResultsOf the 652 individuals enrolled in the program, 112 (17%) participated in the evaluation.

title: Psychological wellbeing in Chinese university students: insights into the influences of academic self-concept, teacher support, and student engagement
creator: Hua Zhang
description: ObjectiveThis study investigates the complex interplay between academic self-concept, teacher support, student engagement, and psychological wellbeing among Chinese university students. We aimed to elucidate the mediating role of student engagement in these relationships.MethodsA sample of 597 Chinese undergraduate students from diverse universities participated in the study.

title: Comment on: “Technical considerations in interpreting rapid transfusion through a 4.2-Fr Broviac catheter”—a reply
creator: Shoko Fujioka, Yusuke Miyazaki, Hinako Furuya, Chika Miyazaki, Nobuyuki Katori, Yoshie Taniguchi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ultidisciplinary meeting was held in advance, as described in our case report. In addition to the various healthcare professionals from the departments listed in the case report, representatives from our hospital’s Patient Safety Committee participated in the preoperative conference. The conference addressed not only strategies for rapid transfusion but also the overall safety management of the anticipated acute hemorrhage, including alternative surgical approaches.

title: Randomized prenatal and postnatal nutrient supplementation shows no long-term impact on cortical gray matter in Ghanaian children
creator: Fatimah B. Ayete Labi, Ludmila Midrigan-Ciochina, Elizabeth L. Prado, Seth Adu-Afarwuah, Kathryn G. Dewey, Charles D. Arnold, Adom Manu, Seth Kwadjo Angmorterh, John Arko-Mensah, Mavis Osipi Mensah, Helena Nti, Lois M. Donkor Aryee, Yaw Boateng Mensah, Becky Amponsaa Appiah, David Atawone, Norbert A
description: IntroductionMaternal and child undernutrition are linked to atypical brain development in children. Provision of pre- and post-natal small-quantity lipid-based nutrient supplements (SQ-LNS) has been shown to positively impact children’s growth and development. It is unknown, however, whether SQ-LNS affects child brain morphology.MethodsThe present study used data from the International Lipid-based Nutrient Supplements randomized controlled trial in Ghana.

title: Dysferlin promotes inflammatory macrophage responses and modulates Ca2+-dependent STAT1 signaling
creator: Kana Tominaga, Naoomi Tominaga
description: This study links macrophage dysferlin to Ca²⁺-dependent STAT1-associated inflammatory responses and impaired myogenic differentiation in cellular models. Introduction Dysferlin (DYSF) is a Ca2+-binding transmembrane protein characterized by multiple C2 domains that enable rapid responses to change in intracellular Ca2+ levels (Bansal & Campbell, 2004; Cai et al, 2009).

title: Single-cell transcriptomics reveals keratinocyte dynamic processes associated with S100a4 expression in psoriasiform dermatitis
creator: Huiqin Wang, Yuan Ding, Shirong Yu, Tingting Li, Dezhi Zhang, Zhenqun Weng, Caying Wu, Zhenrui Wang, Yiqi Wang, Yaqin Ma, Weidong Wu
description: BackgroundPsoriasis is a common autoimmune skin disease with high morbidity and associated complications, characterized by epidermal hyperplasia and cutaneous infiltration of immune cells. The role of S100A4, a key antimicrobial peptide, is highly expressed in psoriatic skin and has aroused considerable interest in recent years, yet its specific function and associated molecular mechanisms remain elusive.

title: Utilizing exosomes as sparking clinical biomarkers and therapeutic response in acute myeloid leukemia
creator: Wandi Wang, Xiaofang Wu, Jiamian Zheng, Ran Yin, Yangqiu Li, Xiuli Wu, Ling Xu, Zhenyi Jin
description: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a malignant clonal tumor originating from immature myeloid hematopoietic cells in the bone marrow with rapid progression and poor prognosis. Therefore, an in-depth exploration of the pathogenesis of AML can provide new ideas for the treatment of AML.

title: Analyzing the Ratio Between Prenatal Consultations and Live Births in Brazil: Spatial and Professional Patterns, 2008–2023
