This study aims to evaluate the detection efficiencies of different exome-based sequencing techniques.MethodsExome-based epilepsy panel tests, clinical exome sequencing (CES), and whole exome sequencing (WES) were conducted on 259 pediatric patients diagnosed with epilepsy.

title: The multiple sclerosis exposome: environmental determinants, immunological convergence, and the Gulf Region as a natural test case
creator: Eslam Shosha, Najeeb Qadi
description: BackgroundThe multiple sclerosis (MS) exposome is widely invoked but rarely measured; grouping environmental exposures together obscures large differences in evidence quality. Much of the existing gene–environment evidence originates from genetically and environmentally homogeneous northern European cohorts, leaving open whether it generalizes elsewhere.

title: Characterization of Listeria monocytogenes strains isolated from soil under organic carrot farming
creator: Maciej Nowak, Zbigniew Paluszak, Natalia Wiktorczyk-Kapischke, Katarzyna Grudlewska-Buda, Anna Budzyńska, Joanna Skonieczna-Kurpiel, Ewa Wałecka-Zacharska, Monika Huse-Kutowska, Krzysztof Skowron
description: IntroductionListeria monocytogenes are Gram-positive, non-spore-producing rods that are the etiological agent of listeriosis. L. monocytogenes is isolated from soil, water, sewage, rotting vegetation, and the main source of these rods for humans is food (fish, unpasteurized dairy products, or raw fruits and vegetables). In recent years, there has been an increase in consumer interest in healthy food, especially organically grown.

title: Early recognition of eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis in outpatient settings: musculoskeletal and gastrointestinal clues beyond respiratory disease
creator: Ernesto Aitella, Massimo De Martinis, Lia Ginaldi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is a multisystem immune-mediated disease characterized by adult-onset asthma, eosinophilic inflammation, and necrotizing vasculitis of small-to-medium-sized vessels. Diagnosis is frequently prompted by clinically overt neurological, cardiac, renal, cutaneous, or gastrointestinal involvement. However, potentially informative manifestations may already be recognizable earlier, particularly when asthma, chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps, and blood eosinophilia coexist with otherwise nonspecific extrapulmonary findings.

title: Clinical correlates for fluconazole resistance in Candida bloodstream infections
creator: Zihuan Li, Tian Wang, Mengdie Zhang, Shu Cao, Baohong Liu, Cuiqiong Fan, Guanwen Lin, Yanfen Ming
description: BackgroundCandidemia poses a growing global health threat, with rising fluconazole resistance complicating clinical management. This study aimed to investigate the species distribution and fluconazole resistance profiles of Candida bloodstream infections and identify risk factors associated with fluconazole resistance.MethodsA retrospective study was conducted at a tertiary care hospital in Guangzhou, China, from 2023 to 2025.

title: The global burden of otitis media in 204 countries and territories from 1992 to 2021: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease study 2021
creator: Guan-Jiang Huang, Bao-Rui Lin, Pei-Shan Li, Na Tang, Zhi-Jun Fan, Biao-Qing Lu
description: ObjectivesThis study aims to analyze the global burden of otitis media and predict future trends using data from the Global Burden of Disease 2021 (GBD 2021).Study designA cross-sectional analysis of GBD 2021 results was conducted.MethodsAge-standardized incidence rates (ASIR), age-standardized prevalence rates (ASPR), and age-standardized disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) rates (ASDR) were calculated.

title: Shenshuaikang enema restores the intestinal barrier and microbiota-gut-kidney axis balance to alleviate chronic kidney disease via NF-κB pathway
creator: Yan Ye, Xiaopeng Huang, Xueying Li, Fei Gao, Wenzhen Zhong, Anqi Tang, Liangbin Zhao, Dengpiao Xie, Naijing Ye
description: IntroductionChronic kidney disease (CKD) is a chronic progressive disease characterized by abnormalities in kidney structure or function caused by variousfactors. It has become a significant public health problem, posing a threat to human health worldwide. Shenshuaikang enema (SSKE) has demonstrated notable efficacy and safety in treating CKD, although its mechanism of action remains unclear.

title: Assessment of hypoxia status in a rat chronic liver disease model using IVIM and T1 mapping
creator: Wenlu Dong, Longyang Xiao, Ziwei Luo, Haiyang Yu, Lili Wang, Yuanxiang Gao, Zhiming Li
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectivesThis study was aimed to assess the diagnostic performance of intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and T1 mapping in detecting hypoxia status of chronic liver disease using a carbon tetrachloride (CCl4)-induced rat model.Materials and methodsThe hypoxia group of chronic liver disease consisted of eight rats induced by injection of CCl4 and the control group consisted of nine rats injected with pure olive oil. All 17 rats underwent MRI examination at week 13 after injection, using T1 mapping and IVIM.

title: Use of amantadine in traumatic brain injury: an updated meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
creator: João Félix, Luísa Araújo, Antônio Henriques, Ana Pereira, Saul Carneiro
description: IntroductionAmantadine has been shown to accelerate cognitive and functional brain recovery after cerebrovascular accidents. However, the efficacy of this drug in TBI patients remains poorly defined.MethodsWe performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials (RCTs) evaluating the effects of amantadine in TBI patients.

title: Integrating cotyledon-based virus-induced gene silencing with visual marker promises a rapid, highly effective validation of gene functions in Nepeta cataria
creator: Zongxia Yu, Ruo Lv, Bo Hong, Lei Yang
description: Nepeta spp. generate volatile nepetalactone iridoids that have cat-attractant and insect-repellent activities. They differ from typical mint family (Lamiaceae) iridoids, which are non-volatile glucosides, and also vary from other species in the Nepetoideae sub-family, which do not generate iridoids. The chemistry and evolution of Nepeta make it suitable for further investigation.

title: Incidence and Predictors of QTC Prolongation Among Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis Patients Receiving Bedaquiline-Based TB Regimens in Uganda: A Countrywide Retrospective Cohort Study
creator: Marble Nasasira, Kevin Ouma Ojiambo, Daniel Iraguha, Joseph Baruch Baluku
description: BackgroundBedaquiline improves culture conversion in drug-resistant tuberculosis (DR-TB) treatment; its main safety concern is QTc prolongation, particularly when combined with other anti-TB drugs. This study assessed the incidence and predictors of QTc prolongation among DR-TB patients receiving bedaquiline under programmatic conditions in Uganda.

title: Associations between subjective and objective measures of stress and load: an insight from 45-week prospective study in 189 elite athletes
creator: Kristina Drole, Mojca Doupona, Kathrin Steffen, Aleš Jerin, Armin Paravlic
description: IntroductionThe aim of this study was to investigate the associations between subjective and objective measures of stress and load in elite male handball players at both the group and individual levels.MethodsIn this 45-week prospective cohort study, 189 elite male handball players weekly reported their perceived stress and load across training, competition, academic, and work domains.

title: Unsaturated fatty acids as immunometabolic modulators in high-risk pregnancies: mechanisms, clinical evidence, and translational perspectives
creator: Edmarcio Olinto da Fonseca, Jocilda Carvalho de Faria, Regiane Penaforte Santos, Julia Vieira Carvalho, Caroline Maria Oliveira Volpe
description: High-risk pregnancies (HRPs) are characterized by the convergence of metabolic dysfunction, chronic low-grade inflammation, and placental maladaptation, leading to increased maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality. Emerging evidence indicates that these conditions are driven by a tightly integrated immunometabolic axis, in which metabolic stress activates innate immune pathways, amplifying systemic and placental inflammation.

title: An acetophenone carboxylase homolog from Rhodococcus aetherivorans initiates acetone rather than acetophenone catabolism
creator: Katharina Müller, Jörg Kahnt, Nicole Paczia, Johann Heider
description: Ketones such as acetone and acetophenone are chemically inert and must be activated prior to microbial degradation. In aerobic bacteria such as Rhodococcus, ketone activation is accomplished either by oxygenation or carboxylation reactions. Acetone and acetophenone carboxylases are homologous enzymes, but have different subunit compositions.

title: Molecular characterization and pathogenicity stratification of YWHAG missense variants in developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
creator: Wen-Hui Liu, Juan Zhou, Zhong-Yan Zhu, Qian-Ru Wen, Si-Qi Zhang, Yan Ding, Heng Meng
description: BackgroundVariants in YWHAG cause severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) with early-onset seizures. Rapid and precise clinical classification of its missense variants presents a substantial challenge. This study sought to explore YWHAG spatiotemporal expression-pathogenicity correlation and reliable pathogenicity indicators for its variants to promote clinical genetic diagnosis.

title: An interpretable machine learning model for MRI-based morphological classification of lumbar disc herniation using functional biomechanical features
creator: Guanghui Yuan, Can Cui, Yong Xu, Bin Xue
description: IntroductionLumbar disc herniation (LDH) is commonly assessed using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), although disc morphology does not necessarily correspond to pain intensity, functional impairment, neurological findings, or prognosis. This retrospective single-center exploratory study examined whether functional biomechanical indicators were associated with MRI-based morphological classification of LDH.

title: Effects of dance-based physical activity on cognitive and psychological health across age groups: a systematic review
creator: Yingying Fan, Xutao Liu
description: BackgroundDance-based physical activity is a multimodal intervention integrating motor, cognitive, emotional, and social components, and has been increasingly recognized for its potential to enhance cognitive function and mental health. However, evidence regarding its effectiveness across different age groups remains fragmented.

title: The spillover effects of fairness events in competitive sports events on audience social trust: a quasi natural experimental analysis
creator: Chuanyong Zhang, Meiling Zhou
description: IntroductionHow fairness incidents in sports events cross the boundary of entertainment and spill over onto spectators’ social trust has been a continuing controversy in existing research. This paper proposes the framework of “surrogate institutional signals,” which treats the arena, with its explicit rules, public enforcement, and verifiable outcomes, as a low cost diagnostic window on which spectators perform Bayesian updating.

title: Novel quantitative trait loci identified for bean rust and the fuscan subspecies of common bacterial blight in an F2 tepary bean population
creator: Santos Barrera, Giseli Valentini, Jorge C. Berny Mier y Teran, Tatiana Garcia, Jon Turkus, Marcial A. Pastor-Corrales, Timothy Porch, Carlos A. Urrea
description: Bean rust, caused by Uromyces appendiculatus, is one of the most critical diseases affecting common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris L.) worldwide. Similarly, common bacterial blight, caused by Xanthomonas fuscans subsp. fuscans (Xff) and Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. phaseoli (Xap), poses major threats to common bean production globally. While common bean exhibits limited natural resistance to these pathogens, tepary bean (Phaseolus acutifolius A.

title: Preoperative nutritional status defined by GLIM criteria and postoperative delirium in older patients receiving general anesthesia
creator: Yuan Tian, Ming-Rui Song, Jian-Feng Jiang, Jia-Teng Wu, Yun-Fei Yan, Yan-Yuan Sun
description: BackgroundPreoperative malnutrition may reflect reduced physiological reserve and increased vulnerability to postoperative delirium (POD) in older surgical patients. However, evidence based on standardized diagnostic criteria remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the association between Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition (GLIM)-defined malnutrition and POD among older patients undergoing surgery under general anesthesia.

title: Machine learning-based CT texture analysis in the differentiation of testicular masses
creator: Can Hu, Xiaomeng Qiao, Zhenyu Xu, Zhiyu Zhang, Xuefeng Zhang
description: PurposeTo evaluate the ability of texture features for distinguishing between benign and malignant testicular masses, and furthermore, for identifying primary testicular lymphoma in malignant tumors and identifying seminoma in testicular germ cell tumors, respectively.MethodsWe retrospectively collected 77 patients with an abdominal and pelvic enhanced computed tomography (CT) examination and a histopathologically confirmed testicular mass from a single center.

title: Development and validation of a structured questionnaire for assessing risk factors of medication non-adherence among pulmonary tuberculosis patients in Indonesia
creator: Leonov Rianto, Ika Agustina, Sofa D. Alfian, Aulia Iskandarsyah, Ivan Surya Pradipta, Rizky Abdulah
description: Background: Medication non-adherence is a significant concern in tuberculosis (TB) treatment, requiring a precise understanding of the associated risk factors. However, there is a lack of appropriate means to assess the risk factors among TB patients in Indonesia, leading to the development and validation of a structured questionnaire for this purpose.

title: Furosemide in pediatric intensive care: a retrospective cohort analysis
creator: Melany Gaetani, Christopher S. Parshuram, Donald A. Redelmeier
description: IntroductionFurosemide is the most commonly used medication in pediatric intensive care. Growing data indicates improved hemodynamic stability and efficacy of furosemide infusions compared to intermittent injections, thereby suggesting furosemide infusions might be considered as first line therapy in critically ill, paediatric patients.

title: The use of the ratio of C-reactive protein to albumin for the diagnosis of pediatric septic arthritis
creator: Chong Ren, Quanwen Yuan, Chunhua Yin, Feng Yao, Wentao Yu, Fuyong Zhang, Xiaodong Wang
description: PurposeThis study aimed to investigate the relationship between the ratio of c-reactive protein to albumin (CAR) and pediatric septic arthritis (PSA).MethodsClinical and laboratory data were collected. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to evaluate the predictive ability of CAR in identifying PSA.

title: Yield and nutrient composition of forage crops and their effects on soil characteristics of winter fallow paddy in South China
creator: Liuxing Xu, Guojian Tang, Dan Wu, Jianguo Zhang
description: In terms of providing additional feeds and improving the soil fertility, planting forage crops during the fallow seasons is an effective strategy to promote resource utilization. The objective of this research was to compare the effects of planting different forage crops on the yields and nutritive compositions of forage and soil properties of winter fallow paddy in southern China.

title: Association of childhood meat consumption with late-life cognitive function: mediation by adult education and moderation by parental literacy
creator: Zhihao Chai, Rao Dai, Baijing Zhou, Chaoqiang Jiang, Yali Jin, Feng Zhu, Tai Hing Lam, Lin Xu, Weisen Zhang
description: BackgroundResults on the associations of childhood nutrition with late-life cognitive function are inconsistent, and little is known about whether family educational resources modify this association or whether adult education lies on the life-course pathway. We examined the associations of childhood meat consumption (CMC), used as an indicator of childhood nutrition, with late-life cognitive function and mild cognitive impairment (MCI).

title: AIPFusion-Net: an interaction-fusion framework for anti-inflammatory peptide prediction using protein language model embeddings, local sequence patterns, and handcrafted descriptors
creator: Wentao Wang, Weidong Yang, Hongmei Li, Zhenyu Cui, Dan Shen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionAnti-inflammatory peptides (AIPs) are promising candidates for treating inflammatory diseases. However, experimental identification is time-consuming and costly, creating a need for accurate computational prediction methods.MethodsWe developed AIPFusion-Net, an interaction-fusion framework that integrates three complementary sources of peptide information: global contextual embeddings generated by the ESM2 protein language model, local sequence patterns extracted from biologically relevant subsequences, and handcrafted physicochemical and sequence descriptors.

title: Advancing stone treatment: the transformative impact of flexible navigable suction ureteral access sheath (fans) for inferior calyx calculi (<2 cm)
creator: Xiang yun Xu, Hong jian Tu, Qing hua Luo, Wen Wei, Fan qi Cheng, Lei hua Cao
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveThis study aimed to assess the efficacy, safety, and stone-free rates (SFR) of the application of a flexible navigable suction ureteral access sheath (FANS) in patients undergoing retrograde intrarenal surgery (RIRS) for inferior calyx calculi (<2 cm).MethodsA retrospective analysis of the clinical data of 111 patients who underwent treatment for inferior calyx calculi at Nanchang People’s Hospital between January 2023 and October 2024 was performed.

title: The NERD model: reflex circuit dysfunction as a systems-level driver of persistent post-concussion symptoms
creator: Matthew M. Antonucci, Kenneth Jay
description: Persistent post-concussive symptoms are often attributed to diffuse cortical dysfunction, yet this perspective may overlook key systems-level mechanisms. We propose a conceptual framework in which dysfunction arises from the dynamic interplay among five functional nodes: the sensory interface, reflex-brain stem hub, cerebellar module, basal ganglia–thalamic modulator, and cerebral cortex.

title: Association between birthweight discordance and extrauterine growth restriction among preterm twins: a national multi-center study in China
creator: Qian Chen, Bijun Shi, Lizi Lin, Danfang Lu, Jiayi Zhang, Shuhua Ren, Kang Huang, Wei Shen, Zhifeng Chen, Jin Liu, Chunming You, Guifang Li, Hong Jiang, Hongping Rao, Jianwu Qiu, Xian Wei, Yayu Zhang, Xiaobo Lin, Haiyan Jiang, Shasha Han, Fan Wang, Weixing Zhang, Xiufang Yang, Yitong Wang, Niyang Lin
description: BackgroundThis multicenter study investigated the association between birthweight discordance (BWD) and extrauterine growth restriction (EUGR) in preterm twins, and evaluated the modifying role of small for gestational age (SGA).MethodsData from 2,496 infants (1,248 twin pairs) admitted to 22 Chinese NICUs (2018–2020) were analyzed.

title: Adaptive gait transition in trekking pole-assisted hiking due to fatigue and staircase height elevation
creator: Yusuke Koshimizu, Akira Fukuhara, Yuji Yamamoto, Akifumi Kijima
description: Humans adapt their gait patterns in response to both internal (e.g., fatigue) and external (e.g., terrain) constraints. Although bipedal locomotion is generally efficient, its stability is reduced on steep or uneven surfaces. Under such conditions, adult hikers often use trekking poles to enhance stability and reduce physical load.

title: Glucocorticoids do not cause a clinically relevant elevation in the urine protein-to-creatinine ratio in dogs with inflammatory protein-losing enteropathy
creator: Cameron J. Wood, Peter S. Chapman, Cara Horowitz
description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to document changes in the urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPC) in dogs with inflammatory protein-losing enteropathy (iPLE) undergoing glucocorticoid therapy and with no overt evidence of concurrent renal disease.MethodsDogs with histologically confirmed iPLE, a serum albumin level of <2.

title: Comparison of the effects of clear aligners and fixed appliances on the oral microbiota and reactive oxygen species: a prospective study
creator: Min Xu, Guiding Li, Jingjun Tian, Feifei Xie, Jingpeng Zuo, Jiangtian Hu, Kang Yin, Wei Wang
description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to compare the effects of clear aligners (CA) and fixed appliances (FA) on periodontal indices, oral microbiota, and oxidative stress markers. Potential associations between microbial changes, oxidative stress, and periodontal health were also explored.MethodsTwenty-four orthodontic patients matched at baseline were randomly allocated to the CA (n = 12) and FA (n = 12) groups.

title: Development and internal validation of a CatBoost–SHAP-guided nomogram for significant liver fibrosis in children with chronic hepatitis B
creator: Yuanzhen Zhang, Tingting Wu, Yunan Chang, Xiaorong Peng, Kai Zhu, Yijing Liu, Tingting Shang, Tao Qin, Jing Zhu, Jiao Tian, Ruiqiu Zhao, Hongmei Xu
description: BackgroundSignificant liver fibrosis can develop in children with chronic hepatitis B (CHB), yet liver biopsy is invasive and unsuitable for repeated assessment. We developed an interpretable, non-invasive prediction model for significant fibrosis in pediatric CHB and evaluated whether baseline risk stratification was associated with subsequent treatment outcomes.

title: Explainable machine learning model to predict refeeding syndrome in patients with severe acute pancreatitis
creator: Cui Wu, Shuangshuang Jing, Dinghui Guo, Congcong Cheng, Sujuan Fei
description: ObjectiveTo construct and validate a risk prediction model for refeeding syndrome (RFS) in patients with severe acute pancreatitis (SAP), identify high-risk individuals before overt electrolyte abnormalities occur, and provide decision support for the timing of enteral nutrition initiation and early personalized intervention.

title: Efficacy and safety of zuranolone in the treatment of major depressive disorder: a meta-analysis
creator: Shuyu Wang, Wenxing Zhang, Zhang Liu, Tian Zhang, Yi Wang, Weihong Li
description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to systematically review zuranolone’s efficacy and safety in treating major depressive disorder (MDD).MethodsWe conducted electronic searches in databases like PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, and Web of Science to identify randomized controlled trials using zuranolone for severe depression from study inception to September 15, 2023. Two independent reviewers screened studies, extracted data, and assessed study quality.

title: Clinical cure induced by pegylated interferon α-2b in the advantaged population of chronic hepatitis B virus infection: a retrospective cohort study
creator: Chaojing Wen, Yixuan Wang, Haoyue Tian, Yu Lei, Zhiyi Wang, Dachuan Cai, Zhi Zhou, Xiaofeng Shi
description: BackgroundAmong the advantaged population with clinical cure of chronic hepatitis B, chronic inactive hepatitis B virus carriers (IHCs) and nucleoside analog-experienced patients have similar serological manifestations. This study established non-interferon-treated groups as controls to compare the efficacy of pegylated interferon α-2b (Peg-IFNα-2b) in achieving clinical cure between IHCs and nucleoside analog (NA)-experienced patients.

title: Periovulatory neurohormone dynamics reveal an association between secretoneurin and GnRH across the mouse estrous cycle
creator: Chunyu Lu, Di Peng, Kevin B. Smith, Chinelo Uju, Suraj Unniappan, Paula Duarte-Guterman, Nafissa Ismail, Vance L. Trudeau
description: IntroductionSurge release of luteinizing hormone (LH) from the pituitary is essential for fertility, as it triggers ovulation. Secretoneurin (SN), a conserved peptide derived from secretogranin-2, stimulates LH release, but its relationship to periovulatory changes in classical reproductive hormones remains unclear.

title: Maternal obesity induced metabolic disorders in offspring and myeloid reprogramming by epigenetic regulation
creator: Joo Young Kweon, Hyeonji Mun, Myeong Ryeol Choi, Hong Seok Kim, Yong Joo Ahn
description: Maternal obesity and gestational diabetes are associated with childhood obesity and increased cardiovascular risk. In this review, we will discuss and summarize extensive clinical and experimental studies that metabolically imbalanced environment exposure in early life plays a critical role in influencing later susceptibility to chronic inflammatory diseases and metabolic syndrome.

title: Associations of gestational diabetes and proton density fat fraction of vertebral bone marrow and paraspinal musculature in premenopausal women
creator: Saori Harada, Alexandra S. Gersing, Yannick Stohldreier, Olaf Dietrich, Andreas Lechner, Jochen Seissler, Uta Ferrari, Eleni Pappa, Nina Hesse
description: Background and objectiveFat content in bones and muscles, quantified by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) as a proton density fat fraction (PDFF) value, is an emerging non-invasive biomarker. PDFF has been proposed to indicate bone and metabolic health among postmenopausal women.

title: Ferroptosis-associated candidate genes in aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: evidence from human peripheral blood and mouse brain
creator: Jia Li, Cong Wang, Hongwen Li, Yafan Liu, Chunchao Cheng, Zilin Zhao, Guifang Jiang, Xiaopeng Cui, Ben Chat Fong Ng, Yan Zhao, Zhuolin Wu, Xinyu Yang
description: BackgroundAneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) has high morbidity and mortality. Ferroptosis may contribute to aSAH-related brain injury, but its peripheral and brain-associated signatures remain unclear.MethodsHuman peripheral-blood dataset GSE36791 (43 aSAH, 18 controls) was analyzed using limma, FerrDb intersection, WGCNA, GO/KEGG enrichment, and PPI-based prioritization.

title: Effects of intensive insulin therapy combined with non-insulin antihyperglycemic agents on glycemic control, variability, and metabolic outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Zixuan Shen, Jiawei Li, Ziyun Zhao, Ziang Chen, Xiaosen Ma, Jing Zhou, Lijing Jiao, Jing Wang
description: BackgroundIntensive insulin therapy (IIT) induces clinical remission in newly diagnosed or poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), but is limited by hypoglycemia risk and weight gain. Combining IIT with non-insulin antihyperglycemic agents may mitigate these drawbacks while improving glycemic variability.MethodsThis review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD42024582974). We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, Web of Science, ClinicalTrials.

title: Clinical predictors of short-term treatment response in stupor: a retrospective study
creator: Xin Zong, Zhiqian Liu, Zhimeng Yang, Chenchen Zhang, Rui Li, Kun Li, Baohua Li
description: BackgroundStupor is a severe psychomotor syndrome with motor retardation and speech inhibition, that adversely affects outcomes. Benzodiazepines and electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) are standard treatments, yet individual responses vary considerably, highlighting the need for effective clinical predictors.ObjectiveThis study aimed to identify clinical predictors of therapeutic response in patients with stupor to facilitate individualized treatment.

title: Vedolizumab treatment in adults with immunodeficiency-associated enteropathy: a case series
creator: Ernestina Angarola, María Josefina Etchevers, Juan Andres De Paula, Maria Florencia Sanchez, Juan Pablo Santino, Diana Liberatore
description: BackgroundInflammatory gastrointestinal disease is a common manifestation of inborn errors of immunity (IEI) and may affect any segment of the gastrointestinal tract. Vedolizumab, a gut-selective anti-integrin approved for inflammatory bowel disease, has been scarcely studied in IEI. We describe our experience with vedolizumab in adults with immunodeficiency-associated enteropathy.

title: Development and validation of the Chinese family environment influencing physical activity habits scale
creator: Xulin Zhang, Jingfei Yan, Weiqiang Zhu, Xiaoya Fu
description: IntroductionAdolescence represents a pivotal stage in the development of healthy behaviors, where establishing positive physical activity habits can have enduring effects on an individual's overall wellbeing. The ecological model highlights the influence of environmental factors on human behavior, with the family environment playing a significant role in shaping the physical activity habits of adolescents.

title: Editorial: Novel insights in insect immunity: regulators, signaling, and mechanisms
creator: Xin Hu, Aneta Strachecka, Fei Wang, Hong Zhou, Kui Zhang, Ioannis Eleftherianos, Amr Mohamed
description: athogen recognition with intracellular signalling and cellular defences, including antimicrobial peptide production, phagocytosis, encapsulation and melanization. The Toll, immune deficiency (IMD), JAK/STAT, JNK and STING signalling pathways contribute to this regulatory network, with their respective roles varying among insect species, tissues and infection contexts (Figure 1).

title: Evaluating NetMHCpan performance on non-European HLA alleles not present in training data
creator: Thomas Karl Atkins, Arnav Solanki, George Vasmatzis, James Cornette, Marc Riedel
description: Bias in neural network model training datasets has been observed to decrease prediction accuracy for groups underrepresented in training data. Thus, investigating the composition of training datasets used in machine learning models with healthcare applications is vital to ensure equity. Two such machine learning models are NetMHCpan-4.1 and NetMHCIIpan-4.

title: Fetal and neonatal outcomes of pregnancies complicated by maternal sleep-disordered breathing: a systematic review
creator: Mayu Niisaka, Jun Hosomichi, Sakina Mitsuishi, Shiho Kino, Takashi Ono
description: IntroductionMaternal obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and the broader spectrum of sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) during pregnancy may be associated with fetal and neonatal outcomes, but the literature is heterogeneous and uses clinically distinct exposure definitions. This systematic review aimed to evaluate associations between maternal SDB and fetal/neonatal outcomes while preserving differences in exposure ascertainment.

title: Tumor cell metabolic reprogramming and hypoxic immunosuppression: driving carcinogenesis to metastatic colonization
creator: Theodora Katopodi, Savvas Petanidis, Doxakis Anestakis, Charalampos Charalampidis, Ioanna Chatziprodromidou, George Floros, Panagiotis Eskitzis, Paul Zarogoulidis, Charilaos Koulouris, Christina Sevva, Konstantinos Papadopoulos, Marios Dagher, Vasileios Alexandros Karakousis, Nikolaos Varsamis, Vasi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). A significant factor in the antitumor immune response is the increased metabolic reprogramming of immunological and malignant cells. Increasing data points to the fact that cancer metabolism affects not just cancer signaling, which is essential for maintaining carcinogenesis and survival, but also the expression of immune cells and immune-related factors such as lactate, PGE2, arginine, IDO, which regulate the antitumor immune signaling mechanism.

title: Gut microbiota, circulating metabolites, and pancreatic cancer risk: a multi-method causal inference study with cross-population validation
creator: Shicheng Lin, Enze Shi, Yuxin Zhang, Xiaofan Wang, Zhen Tian, Jing Han, Quanwang Li
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Pancreatic cancer (PC) is a lethal malignancy with limited early detection strategies and poor therapeutic response. Emerging evidence implicates the gut microbiota in carcinogenesis, yet whether microbial alterations are causal or secondary remains uncertain. In this study, we integrated cross-sectional 16S rDNA sequencing, two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR), and mediation analysis to investigate the causal role of gut microbiota in PC risk.

title: Instillation timing as the main determinant of aqueous humor nepafenac exposure
creator: Angelo Macri, Annalisa Salis, Margherita Tarallo, Michele Iester, Gianluca Damonte, Francesca Mattioli
description: PurposeTo evaluate aqueous humor concentrations of nepafenac following topical administration of 0.3% and 0.1% formulations, to assess the influence of timing of instillation on intraocular exposure.MethodsAqueous humor samples collected during anterior segment surgery were analyzed. Nepafenac concentrations were quantified in 151 samples (0.3% instilled once daily: n = 73; 0.1% instilled three times daily: n = 78).

title: Comparison of hepatitis B and SARS-CoV2 vaccination rates in people who attended Drugs and Addiction Centres
creator: Diana Corona-Mata, Antonio Rivero-Juárez, Ángela Camacho, Laura Ruiz-Torres, Inmaculada Ruiz-Cáceres, Ana Belén Pérez, Bartolomé de la Fuente Darder, David Cáceres-Anillo, María de Guía Castro-Granados, María Lizaur-Barbudo, María Victoria Cabrera-Gisbert, Justa Redondo-Écija, Ana Aparicio-Aparicio,
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background and aimsPersons with substance use disorder are at increased risk for hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. Although most of them are attached to social health centers, the vaccination rate in this group is low.

title: A reliability generalization meta-analysis of self-report measures of statistics anxiety
creator: Emine Ören Özdemir, Ibrahim Yildirim
description: Objective and MethodIn this study, it was aimed to obtain a general reliability coefficient for each of the statistics anxiety scales. For this purpose, Web of Science, ERIC and Scopus databases and Google Scholar search engine were searched according to certain criteria and 84 Cronbach’s alpha coefficients reported for the whole scale were reached.

title: Efficacy, safety, and strategy-modifying factors of pulsed field ablation for persistent and long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Yuanlin Zhou, Jianhua Xie, Mingliang Fang, Shipeng Wang, Xiaohong Bin, Qingyao Liao

title: Cinnamic acid and magnetized water: A novel nutritional strategy to enhance lamb productivity and meat quality
creator: Mohsen Kazemi, Reza Valizadeh, Abbas Khashei-Siuki
description: Highlights•Cinnamic acid improved growth performance and nutrient digestibility in lambs.•Magnetized water enhanced antioxidant status and meat quality traits.•Combined supplementation reduced lipid oxidation and improved meat color.•Cinnamic acid shifted ruminal fermentation toward greater propionate production.•The combination of cinnamic acid and 6000 Gauss water produced the best responses.

title: Phenotypic characterization of patients with ANCA-associated vasculitis and diffuse alveolar hemorrhage: a data-driven analysis of a multicentre, retrospective, nationwide cohort
creator: Segolene Gendreau, Anne-Claire Sanna, Cyrielle Desnos, Romain Lombardi, Jolan Malherbe, Dimitri Titeca-Beauport, Florian Reizine, Raphael Porcher, Benjamin Terrier, Nicolas de Prost
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundSevere diffuse alveolar hemorrhage (DAH) is a potentially fatal complication of ANCA-associated vasculitides (AAV). This study aimed to identify distinct clinical phenotypes among patients to the ICU, and to examine their association with mortality.MethodsWe conducted an ancillary analysis of the national multicenter retrospective PLEXHIA cohort, including 197 patients with severe AAV-related DAH, defined by respiratory symptoms with new infiltrates consistent with alveolar hemorrhage, along with oxygen saturation ≤85%, high-flow oxygen or mechanical ventilation requirement.

title: Use of lorazepam for analgosedation during mechanical ventilation in pediatric intensive care
creator: Paul Healy, Marco Marano, Marcello Montibeller, Bianca Maria Goffredo, Giuseppe Pontrelli, Oscar Della Pasqua
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionLorazepam has been used off-label for analgosedation in pediatric intensive care units (PICU) as an alternative to midazolam. While its intermediate duration of action makes it suitable for continuous sedation, there is limited evidence to guide dosing in children.

title: Concentrated growth factor in oral bone regeneration: A narrative review
creator: Qi Yang, Yinghua Fu, Zhixin Zhang, Xiaoping Tang, Jiangling Su
description: IntroductionConcentrated growth factor (CGF), a third-generation autologous platelet concentrate, has been increasingly used in oral bone regeneration. This review summarizes its preparation, biological mechanisms, and clinical efficacy, and discusses current limitations and future directions.MethodsWe comprehensively reviewed the literature on CGF preparation, structural features, and bioactive components, and synthesized clinical evidence across various oral bone defect scenarios.

title: Cardiometabolic medicine in China: Burden, challenges, and strategic priorities
creator: Rui-Xiang Zeng, Sha Li, Xiao Wang, Ke-Fei Dou, Jian-Jun Li
description: The development of cardiometabolic medicine (CMM) reflects a shift in cardiovascular disease (CVD) management from organ-based care toward greater cross-system integration. CMM integrates cardiovascular, endocrine, renal, and public health domains to address the bidirectional interplay between metabolic dysfunction and CVD.

title: A new three-layer metapopulation networks model coupling online-offline social interactions with epidemic spread

However, information dissemination through multiple channels, including both online and offline sources, and the dynamics of information dissemination across these channels are influenced by individual mobility.

title: Benzothiazole-Derived Compounds as Potential Drugs for the Treatment of Type 2 Diabetes: A Descriptive Review
creator: Ana María Correa-Basurto, Miguel Valdes, Laura Cristina Cabrera-Pérez, Natalia Reyes Vallejo, Alejandro Cruz, Martha Cecilia Rosales-Hernández, Juan Andres Alvarado-Salazar, Jessica Elena Mendieta-Wejebe

The structural versatility of the benzothiazole scaffold has enabled the development of a diverse array of preclinical compounds capable of modulating multiple diabetes-relevant targets.

title: Extended Reality for Image-Guided Small Animal Surgery: Current Evidence, Clinical Applications, and Future Directions
creator: Domenico Caivano, Federica Valeri, Andrea Corda, Antonello Bufalari
description: Simple SummaryModern veterinary surgery increasingly relies on advanced imaging techniques to better understand patient anatomy and improve surgical planning. Extended reality (XR) offers innovative approaches by allowing to visualize three-dimensional anatomical structures and interact with patient-specific models. This review summarizes the current use of XR technologies in small animal surgery and evaluates their potential benefits and limitations.

title: Vascular Invasion and Survival in Extremity Leiomyosarcoma: An Exploratory Single-Center Cohort Study from the Oxford Sarcoma Service
creator: Seva N. S. Gill, Tanjot S. Kurala, Serkan Bayram, Jennifer M. Brown, Muhammad Riaz, Muhammad A. Siddiqi, Thomas D. A. Cosker
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Simple SummaryLeiomyosarcoma is an uncommon smooth muscle cancer. When it arises in an arm or leg, it generally behaves less aggressively than at other sites, but predicting which patients will do badly remains difficult. Vascular invasion—tumor cells growing inside blood vessels—can be seen when the tumor is examined under a microscope, but it is currently an optional item in pathology reports and has rarely been studied in limb leiomyosarcoma. We reviewed 62 patients treated at our specialist center over ten years.

title: Integrative transcriptomic analysis reveals tissue associated molecular responses to heat stress in chickens

Although RNA-seq has been widely used to investigate heat stress responses, individual studies are constrained by small sample sizes, experimental heterogeneity, and discordant differential expression signatures, limiting the identification of conserved molecular responses across tissues.

title: Stability of curved chain-like bubble structures and transport behavior of gas nuclei in localized turbulent Flows☆

However, their weak acidic character contributes to microbial toxicity. At lower pH values, VFAs predominantly occur in their undissociated form, which can permeate the cell membrane, disturb intracellular metabolism and increase the cellular energy burden.

title: Biotechnological upgrading of palm kernel meal for poultry nutrition: Challenges and opportunities
creator: Ahmed Mijiyawa, Elham Ghashghaei, Uchechukwu Edna Obianwuna, Okasha Hamada, Yendouhamtchié Nadiedjoa, Maxwell Ansong Okai, Lijing Sun, Muhammad Faisal Riaz, Felix Kwame Amevor, Dossêh Jean Apôtre Afayibo, Were Pitala, Hai Lin

title: Dual Antiglutamate Therapy in Super-Refractory Status Epilepticus After Cardiac Arrest (SUPER-CAT Study)
creator: Simone Beretta, Matteo Pozzi, Simone Tagliabue, Elisa Bianchi, Emanuela Rossi, Francesco Pasini, Angela Giglio, Giulia Sofia Cereda, Carlo Morotti Colleoni, Giulia Pederzoli, Giada Giovannini, Niccolò Orlandi, Stefano Meletti, Alessandra Gaiani, Stefania Filipponi, Alberto Cucino, Marco Normanno, Il

title: Protocol for confocal microscopy-based localization of chorismate mutase protein of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in trans-Golgi compartment
creator: Vandana Maurya, Sangita Mukhopadhyay
description: SummaryHere, we present a confocal microscopy protocol to determine the localization of Mycobacterium tuberculosis chorismate mutase (MtbCM) in trans-Golgi compartment. We co-transfect HEK293 cells with either pEGFP-C1-MtbCM and mCherry-TGOLN2 (trans-Golgi marker) or pEGFP-C1 and mCherry-TGOLN2 as a control, using Lipofectamine 2000. We describe steps for constructing pEGFP-C1-MtbCM and performing co-transfection and image acquisition using confocal microscopy.

title: First evidence of Tahyna virus in Central Italy and seasonal dynamics of its putative vector, Aedes caspius
creator: Federico Romiti, Silvia Tofani, Antonella Cersini, Irene Del Lesto, Maria Teresa Scicluna, Gaetana Anita Marcario, Davide La Rocca, Silvia Rondón, Adele Magliano, Claudio De Liberato

title: Influence of the type of facial pattern on the outcome of treatment of patients with obstructive sleep-disordered breathing with an intraoral appliance
creator: Henrique Cabrini Moreira, Rafael de Andrade Balsalobre, Maximiana Cristina de Souza Maliska, Milena de Almeida Torres Campanholo, Renato Prescinotto, Danilo Anunciatto Sguillar, Fernanda Louise Martinho Haddad

title: RESONANCE: Protocol for a Nationwide Cohort Study of Chronic Liver Diseases Using the French National Health Data System
creator: Aurore Baron, Laure Tron, Frédéric Balusson, Vaele Zannou, Victoria Mignot, Anne Ego, Anna Borowick, Thomas Decaens, Emmanuel Oger, Sébastien Bailly, Charlotte Costentin

title: Explainable Machine Learning–Based Prediction of Progression-Free Survival in Prostate Cancer: Retrospective Cohort Study
creator: Hein Minn Tun, Lin Naing, Owais Ahmed Malik, Muhammad Syafiq Abdullah, Thu Ta, Hanif Abdul Rahman

title: The effects, mechanisms, and influencing factors of concurrent strength and endurance training with different sequences: a semi-systematic review
creator: Zhang Feng, Wang Ying, Wang Jun

title: Disconnection syndromes and injury to neural systems after ischemic stroke

title: HED-Net: a hybrid ensemble deep learning framework for breast ultrasound image classification
creator: Soumya Sara Koshy, L. Jani Anbarasi, Modigari Narendra, Rabindra Kumar Singh
description: IntroductionBreast cancer, one of the most life-threatening diseases that commonly affects women, can be effectively diagnosed using breast ultrasound imaging. A hybrid deep learning based ensemble framework combining the effectiveness of different convolutional neural network models has been proposed for breast ultrasound image classification.

title: Biosecurity perspectives of equestrian competition organizers in Ontario, Canada
creator: Gabrielle K. Turcotte, Terri L. O’Sullivan, Kelsey L. Spence, Charlotte B. Winder, Amy L. Greer
description: BackgroundBiosecurity plays an important role in the prevention and control of infectious disease outbreaks in the equine population. With competition organizers responsible for implementing and upholding biosecurity requirements at competitions, it is important to understand the biosecurity landscape at these locations where Ontario horses commonly travel and interact in large group settings.

title: Green-synthesized natural antioxidants in poultry and livestock feed: enhancing oxidative stability and animal welfare
creator: Khaoula Nefzi, Ikram BenSouf, Mariem Saidani, Cyrine Darej, Bochra Bejaoui, Manel Ben Larbi, Naceur M’Hamdi, Vincent Lequart, Nicolas Joly, Patrick Martin
description: Oxidative stress, caused by an imbalance between reactive oxygen species and antioxidant defenses, significantly impacts livestock health, welfare, and productivity. Green synthesis has emerged as a sustainable approach for enhancing the stability and bioavailability of natural antioxidants in animal feed.

title: Potential role of glucagon like peptide 1 in taste receptors
